*Why both Minkowski space and Hilbert space conceal the quantum: they are the two frozen integrals of the one advance.* The relation of the previous paragraph has a consequence that unifies the two arenas and identifies precisely what each hides. The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is a *rate* — a wavefront cycling at the rate $ic$, carrying one action quantum $\hbar$ per Compton cycle. Minkowski space and Hilbert space are each obtained from this rate by an operation that removes the cycling and retains a static residue, and they conceal the quantum for the same reason: both are integrate-and-freeze projections of the one cycling advance.

Minkowski space is the coordinate integral. Integrating the rate over coordinate time, $\int ic\,dt = ict = x_4$, returns the static Minkowski coordinate; the manifold $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is the space of these finished coordinate labels (Lemma 2.5). The integration is a smoothing: the coordinate integral $x_4 = ict$ records the total advance and retains no trace of the $\hbar$-sized cycles that composed it, which is why special and general relativity, built on $x_4 = ict$, are not manifestly quantum-mechanical although the oscillatory content persists at every point. The block manifold is smooth because integration is a smoothing operation; it is the record of the expansion after it has occurred, not the expansion.

Hilbert space freezes the same advance by a different operation, and this symmetry is the point. The stationary states that furnish the standard basis of $\mathcal{H}$ carry their time dependence in the phase $e^{-iEt/\hbar}$; a stationary state is by definition one whose observable content is time-independent, so that $|\psi|^2$ is constant. The phase $e^{-iEt/\hbar}$ *is* the $x_4$-advance cycling — $E/\hbar$ is the Compton-scale angular rate of the wavefront — but in a stationary state that cycling is factored out of every measurable quantity, and the Born rule $P = |\psi|^2$ removes it explicitly: forming the modulus squared annihilates the phase $e^{-iEt/\hbar}(e^{-iEt/\hbar})^{*} = 1$, discarding exactly the factor that carries the tick. Hilbert space, as the space of states under this inner product, is therefore frozen in the same sense Minkowski space is: its static structure is the residue left after the advance is integrated away, here by the modulus-square rather than by the coordinate integral. Minkowski integrates the advance into a coordinate; Hilbert squares the advance out of the probability. Both are integrate-and-freeze operations on the one cycling wavefront.

*The imaginary unit is the fossil of the motion; $\hbar$ is the motion.* This explains, in one stroke, why both arenas carry the imaginary unit and why both nonetheless conceal the quantum. The $i$ in $x_4 = ict$ and the $i$ in $e^{-iEt/\hbar}$ are the same $i$: the signature that the $x_4$-advance is a rotation, a cycling at $90^\circ$ to the observable directions (the geometry of $dx_4/dt = ic$, §2.3). Under integration into Minkowski space the rotation becomes the perpendicularity of the fourth axis, and the $i$ survives as the sign structure of the metric $(-,+,+,+)$ — the *fact* of the perpendicular rotation is retained while its *rate*, the tick, is integrated away. Under the modulus-square into Hilbert space the rotation becomes the state’s phase circulation, and the $i$ survives in the Schrödinger equation and the inner product — again the fact of the rotation retained, its rate squared away. Each space keeps $i$ because $i$ is the fossil of a rotation; each loses $\hbar$ because integration and squaring erase the rate of that rotation. The imaginary unit is the imprint the motion leaves in its static record; $\hbar$ is the living rate that the record does not contain.

*How the quantum is recovered: $\hbar$ re-enters exactly where the advance is restored.* A bare complex vector space contains no $\hbar$; $\hbar$ enters quantum mechanics only through the dynamics, and its placement is diagnostic. In the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial_t \psi = \hat{H}\psi$ and in the canonical commutator $[\hat q,\hat p] = i\hbar$, the constant $\hbar$ stands next to the time derivative and inside the commutator — precisely the operations that reintroduce the advance the static Hilbert space had frozen out. The time derivative un-freezes the stationary phase; restoring it forces $\hbar$ to appear as the constant relating the cycling rate to the energy, because $\hbar$ is the action per cycle of the $x_4$-advance (§2.3). The discreteness returns by the same route: the spectrum of $\hat H$ is discrete for bound states because the cycling must close on itself in an integer number of Compton cycles — the standing-wave closure condition of configuration (1) of the four-fold ontology — a condition on the cycling that the static space suppresses and the dynamics restores. Neither $\hbar$ nor the discreteness resides in the static space of states; both reside in the advance the space is the frozen record of, and both reappear the instant the record is differentiated back into the process. This is the exact sense in which $dx_4/dt = ic$ is prior to both Minkowski space and Hilbert space: the derivative is the physical process, and the two spaces are its two static integrals, each faithful in form (the $i$) and each silent about the motion (the $\hbar$) until the advance is restored.

The quantum-mechanical formalism generates general relativity because every quantum-mechanical structure contains dx₄/dt = ic at every point (Theorem 10.5), and dx₄/dt = ic generates the general-relativistic formalism (corpus \[54–57\]). The mutual generation is not metaphorical: each side’s foundational structures literally contain the foundational principle of the other side at every point, in one of four derivationally distinct senses corresponding to the four types of mathematical structure (manifold, function space, scalar density, operator equation). This is the unification at the foundational-derivation level that the twentieth century could not produce: mutual generativity through pointwise constitutive content — GR and QM as reciprocally generated structures, each containing the other’s foundational principle at every point of its own foundational structures.

The four-sense distinction (literal/constructive/evaluative/operatorial) is a observation about what kind of foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic is: a recurring fact at every level of its descendant structures. The principle is irreversibly constitutive of every derived structure (stripping it destroys the structure) and recoverable from any derived structure (the McGucken Principle is locally readable at every point). No prior foundational program for quantum mechanics has this pointwise-instantiation property; the Dirac–von Neumann axioms and every other prior axiomatization (von Neumann, Mackey, Piron–Solèr, Jordan–von Neumann–Wigner, Hardy, Chiribella–D’Ariano–Perinotti) operate as upstream postulates that do not appear “in” the theorems they entail. The pointwise-instantiation property is what makes the mutual generativity of GR and QM possible: because the McGucken Principle is present at every point of every foundational structure of both theories, the McGucken Principle is recoverable from either side and generates the other.

*Architectural priority and the cogeneration of QM and GR.* dx₄/dt = ic is the foundational physical principle: a foundational, physical statement that the fourth dimension is expanding at rate c from every spacetime event, with each oscillatory step carrying action ℏ. *The methodological standard: unification from the fewest premises.* The programme of this paper is the programme Einstein named the physicist’s supreme task, and it is the shared methodology of the tradition. Einstein, in the Herbert Spencer Lecture of 1933: *“It can scarcely be denied that the supreme goal of all theory is to make the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible without having to surrender the adequate representation of a single datum of experience”*; and, for Max Planck’s sixtieth birthday in 1918: *“The supreme task of the physicist is to arrive at those universal elementary laws from which the cosmos can be built up by pure deduction.”* The standard is older than Einstein and outlasts him. Newton, in the *Principia*: *“Nature is pleased with simplicity, and affects not the pomp of superfluous causes”* — three laws of motion and one of gravitation for both the falling apple and the planets. Maxwell unified electricity, magnetism, and light in four equations. Dirac: *“It is more important to have beauty in one’s equations than to have them fit experiment”* — and predicted antimatter from the elegance of a single equation. Weinberg, in *Dreams of a Final Theory*, located a theory’s beauty in its inevitability, the sense that no premise could be altered without destroying the whole. Wheeler — under whom the present principle was first formulated at Princeton (Historical Note) — went further: *“Behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, so compelling that when … we grasp it, we will all say to each other, ‘Oh, how could it have been otherwise!’”*

Against this standard a foundation is judged not by whether its arena can be written down formally — any consistent mathematics can be — but by how much of the cosmos it builds by pure deduction from how few premises. The present paper offers dx₄/dt = ic as one such universal elementary law: a single physical statement — the fourth dimension expanding at c in a spherically symmetric manner from every event — from which the Lorentzian metric, the Hilbert space, the Born rule, the canonical commutator, the uncertainty principle, the Schrödinger equation, the arrow of time, the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy, and the cosmological record are derived as theorems, with the derivations given in full. The reader schooled in this tradition is asked to judge the paper by its terms: not whether one may posit the arenas independently — one may, as mathematics — but whether they follow by pure deduction from the one premise, which is the only question the tradition of Newton, Maxwell, Einstein, Dirac, Weinberg, and Wheeler considers decisive. The reply to the objection that certain correspondence rules must be posited by hand rather than derived is given in §10.12octies; the sense in which the framework realises the fewest-premises standard against every prior Born-rule and Hilbert-space programme is quantified in §7.7 and §6.3.

### 1.1 The four-pillar problem: Hilbert space 𝓗, Born rule P = \|ψ\|², canonical commutator \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ, and Heisenberg uncertainty principle σ_x σ_p ≥ ℏ/2 as a century of axiomatic postulation rather than derivation from any upstream physical principle

The mathematical structure of quantum mechanics rests on four pillars: the Hilbert space 𝓗, the Born rule, the canonical commutation relation, and the Heisenberg uncertainty principle. The Schrödinger equation governs the dynamics on this foundation. For a century these have been axiomatized rather than derived. Born stated the rule in 1926 with no derivation; Heisenberg and Born and Jordan stated the canonical commutator in 1925 with no derivation; von Neumann axiomatized the Hilbert space in 1932 with no derivation; Robertson’s 1929 inequality derived the uncertainty principle from these axioms but inherited them as postulates; Schrödinger’s 1926 equation was written down by analogy from Hamilton–Jacobi theory and confirmed empirically.

Meanwhile, special relativity supplied a geometric framework — the Lorentzian spacetime metric ds² = −c²dt² + dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃², together with the four-velocity normalization u\^μ u_μ = −c² — that was empirically validated to extraordinary precision across the same century. Yet for a century these two foundational pillars of physics — the Lorentzian metric of relativity and the Hilbert-space formalism of quantum mechanics — were treated as separate axiomatic systems requiring independent justification. The deepest question in the foundations of physics, asked explicitly by Einstein, Wheeler, and many others across a century, was whether the second could be derived from the first.

Every twentieth-century attempt at foundational derivation of QM operated *inside* the axiomatized Hilbert-space formalism. Gleason (1957) derived the form of the Born rule from non-contextuality and probability measures on subspaces, but presupposed the Hilbert space; Mackey (1957), Piron (1964), and Solèr (1995) attempted to derive the Hilbert-space structure from lattice axioms but could not narrow the field of scalars beyond ℝ/ℂ/ℍ; Jordan–von Neumann–Wigner (1934) classified the algebras of observables and reached the same three-way ambiguity; Hardy (2001) and Chiribella–D’Ariano–Perinotti (2010s) reconstructed the formalism from operational or informational axioms whose physical origin remained unexplained; Stueckelberg (1960) showed real quantum mechanics with J²=−1 is equivalent to complex quantum mechanics; Adler (1995, 2004) developed quaternionic quantum mechanics and trace dynamics; Renou et al. (2021) experimentally excluded real quantum mechanics; Deutsch (1999), Wallace (2012), Zurek (2003), Sebens–Carroll (2018), Masanes–Galley–Müller (2019), Saunders (2021), Bohm (1952), and the QBists (2010s) each proposed derivations of the Born rule that imported one further axiom — rationality, environment-induced symmetry, self-locating uncertainty, state-estimation, branch-counting, equivariance, or coherence — sufficient to do the derivational work.

Not one of these programs derived any of the four pillars from the Lorentzian metric of special relativity, or from any physical principle upstream of the Hilbert-space formalism. Each operated within the formalism, importing supplementary axioms to do the lifting. The pattern is uniform: the arena is taken as primitive, and the question is which axioms inside the arena force the rule.

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic of the present paper states that the fourth dimension is expanding from every spacetime event as a *spherically symmetric wavefront* at velocity c. A wavefront expanding at c carries **wavelength, frequency, phase, and therefore action** — it is a dynamical, oscillatory, phase-bearing geometric flow, not a static coordinate label. The two fundamental constants of quantum mechanics are therefore not independent inputs that enter the formalism separately; they are **twin properties of the one advance**: c is the wavefront’s rate, ℏ is the action carried per Planck-frequency oscillation. The spinor of relativistic quantum mechanics is not a free-floating algebraic object attached to a static spacetime by external axiom; **the spinor lives on a wavefront that already has the Compton frequency** ν_C = mc²/h built into the fundamental structure. And the dynamical content of quantum mechanics — Schrödinger evolution, canonical commutator, unitary time evolution, oscillatory phase, Feynman path-integral exp(iS/ℏ), spin precession — was not bolted on as supplementary axioms on top of a static background; **the dynamics were in the premise**. Every dynamical structure of QM is the cascade-level reading of the wavefront-character of the active x₄-expansion that the McGucken Principle names. This reading — *the active spherically symmetric expansion at velocity c, with action ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation, the dynamics in the premise* — is the central content of the present paper, recurring as the upstream physics of every derivation in §§2–14 and made formally explicit in the inset following Principle 2.1 in §2.1 below.

### 1.1bis Two foundational identifications never previously stated as theorems anywhere in physics

Two identifications, to our knowledge, appear nowhere else in the physics literature as labeled theorems with formal proofs. Both identifications resolve century-old foundational puzzles by establishing that what the orthodox tradition treated as separate axiomatic structures — relativity’s locality and quantum mechanics’s nonlocality, the Hilbert-space arena and the Born-rule probability postulate — are in fact cascade-level expressions of the same upstream geometry supplied by dx₄/dt = ic. The two identifications are:

Stated as Theorem 6.6.8.1 (Bidirectional Identity Theorem; importing Theorem 13.1 of \[PQR/2026\]) with formal proof: the Lorentzian signature, the null cone, the McGucken Sphere as null-separated surface, frame-invariance of $c$, and the Lorentz group are biconditionally tied to one another, and the McGucken Sphere — *which is also the null-separated surface that produces quantum nonlocality in three-dimensional observations* — is the common object underlying all of them.

Stated as Theorem 6.6.7.4 (Born rule presupposes nonlocal inner-product structure) with formal proof, with the closing implication chain in the proof being *Born rule ⟸ nonlocality ⟸ null vectors ⟸ Lorentzian metric ⟸ dx₄/dt = ic*. The Born rule is a downstream theorem of the Lorentzian null structure, equivalently of the McGucken Principle.

These identifications dissolve the longest-running puzzles in foundations of physics. The orthodox view treats quantum nonlocality as a *puzzle* requiring reconciliation with relativistic locality — Einstein’s *spukhafte Fernwirkung* preserved as live tension for a century, with the Bell-inequality empirical record forcing the existence of nonlocality but no foundational program identifying its source. The two identifications above replace the puzzle with a identity: the Lorentzian metric of relativity and the quantum nonlocality of entanglement / Bell-violation are the same null-separated structure; quantum probability is the cascade-level reading of this structure on the spatial slice.

None moved one cascade level *upstream* of both the metric and the Hilbert space — to the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic at every event — where the identifications become forced theorems. The Lorentzian metric is then the *integrated coordinate shadow* of dx₄/dt = ic (Lemma 2.5); the Hilbert space is the *function-space rendering* of the same constraint surface (Theorem 10.6); the Born rule is the *probability-density cascade level* of the Sphere geometry (Theorem 7.4); the nonlocality of entanglement / Bell-violation is the *correlation cascade level* of the same Sphere geometry (Theorems 6.6.7.6, 6.6.7.7); and the identifications (I)–(II) follow as derived theorems with formal proofs.

#### 1.1bis.3 The profundity of identifications (I) and (II)

The profundity of these identifications is best seen by considering what they replace.

*Identification (I) replaces the century-long “locality vs nonlocality” tension* — the central puzzle of foundations of quantum mechanics since EPR 1935 — with a identity. The orthodox tradition treated the Lorentzian metric as the source of *locality* (light cones forbid superluminal influence; spacelike separation defines noninfluence) and quantum entanglement as the source of *nonlocality* (Bell-violation requires correlations between spacelike-separated events). The two were treated as separate phenomena requiring reconciliation, with one century’s worth of literature attempting that reconciliation (Bohr-Einstein debates, EPR 1935, Bohm 1952, Bell 1964, Aspect 1982, Hardy 1992, Maudlin’s *Quantum Non-Locality and Relativity* 1994/2011, Norsen’s *Foundations of Quantum Mechanics* 2017). Identification (I) shows that the reconciliation was malformed from the outset: the Lorentzian metric *is* the null-separated surface that produces quantum nonlocality. There is no tension to resolve because the metric and the nonlocality are the same object read at two cascade levels — the metric reading at the manifold level (the null cone as causal-structure separator), the nonlocality reading at the correlational level (the null cone as null-wavefront on which entangled subsystems share locality in $x_4$). The bidirectional closure of Theorem 6.6.8.1 makes this identity rigorous.

*Identification (II) replaces the century-long “Born rule as independent postulate” framing* — the central feature of every quantum-mechanics textbook from Dirac 1930 through the present — with the Born rule as a downstream theorem of the nonlocality. The orthodox tradition treated the Born rule as one of the foundational postulates of QM (Born 1926; Dirac–von Neumann axioms; standard QM textbooks), with derivations of the Born rule from other axioms (Gleason 1957, Deutsch 1999, Zurek 2003, Wallace 2012, Saunders 2021) all running through derivationally distinct upstream axioms (probability measures on lattices, rationality, environment-symmetry, branch-counting, equivariance) that are themselves not derived from any deeper physical principle. Identification (II) supplies the deeper principle: the Born rule’s bilinear structure is the cascade-level expression of the nonlocal inner-product coupling between spacelike-separated wavefunction values, which in turn is the cascade-level expression of the McGucken Sphere null wavefront propagating from the source event. The Born rule is no longer one of the QM postulates; it is a downstream theorem of dx₄/dt = ic via the cascade Sphere → Hilbert → inner product → Born rule (Theorem 6.6.7.6).

*The combined profundity of (I) and (II) is that the Lorentzian metric, quantum nonlocality, the Hilbert space, and the Born rule are not four separate structures requiring separate axiomatic treatments.* They are four cascade-level presentations of the same Sphere-geometry generated by dx₄/dt = ic at every event of $\mathbb{M}_G$. This is the deepest unification result that the McGucken corpus establishes: the central foundational objects of relativity and quantum mechanics — which the twentieth century treated as belonging to separate mathematical universes — are revealed as four cascade-level renderings of one principle, with each rendering instantiating dx₄/dt = ic in its own derivationally distinct way (Theorem 10.5: literally in Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, constructively in Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, evaluatively in $P = |\psi|^2$, correlationally in entanglement / Bell-violation).

#### 1.1bis.4 The static-light-cone tradition vs. the active-Sphere reading: the categorical distinction

The historical-comparison table in §1.1bis.1 catalogues a wide range of prior programs that have engaged with the null cone, locality, Lorentz invariance, or nonlocality in various combinations. The framing in v36 (this paper’s earlier version) characterized the Sorkin–Dowker causal-set lineage as the “closest near-miss” to identification (I), and identified the trinity-conflict-vs-biconditional distinction as the axis. On closer examination — with the verified primary sources read in full (Bombelli–Lee–Meyer–Sorkin 1987, Sorkin 1991, Sorkin 2009, Dowker–Glaser 2013, Belenchia–Benincasa–Dowker 2015, Boguñá–Krioukov 2025) — that framing is correct in detail but mis-located in level. The deeper distinction is between **the entire static-light-cone tradition of orthodox physics** and **the active-Sphere reading of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework**. This subsection develops the deeper distinction with verbatim primary-source content.

*The static-light-cone tradition.* Across twentieth-century and early-twenty-first-century physics, the null cone of the Lorentzian metric is treated as a **frozen, passive, kinematical surface** in a pre-given Lorentzian manifold. Penrose’s twistor program (1967 and subsequent decades) constructs twistors as complex coordinates parameterizing the existing null structure of an existing Minkowski spacetime; the null cone is given, the twistors are built from it. Reeh–Schlieder’s theorem \[*Nuovo Cimento* 22, 1051 (1961)\] establishes the cyclic-vector property of local QFT algebras on regions of an existing Lorentzian manifold; the metric and its null structure are background, the QFT algebra is layered on top. The Bombelli–Lee–Meyer–Sorkin 1987 \[PRL 59, 521\] founding paper of causal-set theory proposes spacetime as a locally finite partial order, with the partial order encoding the causal structure of an *approximating* Lorentzian manifold — *“the metric must be Lorentzian, because no other signature than $(-,+,...,+)$ has the two-napped light cones from which the continuum’s causal order is derived”* — treating the existence of light cones as the geometric fact that justifies the partial-order discretization. The Sorkin–Dowker causal-set lineage (Sorkin 1991, 2007, 2009; Dowker–Glaser 2013; Belenchia–Benincasa–Dowker 2015; Boguñá–Krioukov 2025) Poisson-sprinkles discrete points into a pre-existing Lorentzian manifold whose light cones are taken as the kinematical given; the hyperboloid Belenchia–Benincasa–Dowker 2015 identify as the locus of $L_1(x)$ near $\partial J^-(x)$ is a region of the static, pre-existing light cone, populated by discrete points. Jacobson’s null-thermodynamics derivation of Einstein’s equations \[PRL 75, 1260 (1995); PRL 116, 201101 (2015)\] treats Rindler horizons as pre-existing null surfaces at which equilibrium conditions are imposed; the null structure is given, the thermodynamic argument is applied on it. Maldacena’s holographic correspondence \[Adv. Theor. Math. Phys. 2, 231 (1998)\] and the broader AdS/CFT literature treat bulk and boundary Lorentzian/conformal metrics as fixed inputs; the holographic identification operates between QFTs defined on these pre-given backgrounds. Light-front quantization, conformal compactification (Penrose 1965), Bondi–Metzner–Sachs (BMS) symmetries at null infinity, Strominger’s “null asymptotic” celestial-amplitude program — every one of these orthodox approaches treats the null cone as a frozen kinematical structure, a passive object that physics happens on or near or across, but not itself dynamical.

*The active-Sphere reading of the McGucken framework.* The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic of the present paper makes a derivationally distinct claim: the null cone of the Lorentzian metric is **not** a primitive object in its own right; it is the *integrated coordinate shadow* of an active spherically symmetric wavefront — the McGucken Sphere $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ — propagating from every event $E \in \mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at velocity $c$ in the $x_4$-direction. The McGucken Sphere is an *active* geometric primitive carrying wavelength, frequency $\omega = E/\hbar$, phase, and action $\hbar$ per Planck-frequency oscillation built into its propagation. The static light cone $\partial J^{\pm}(E)$ of the orthodox tradition is the *locus traced* as the McGucken Sphere has propagated outward; the null cone is the geometric record of where the active wavefront has been, not a primitive in its own right. *The dynamics are in the premise.* (See the central content paragraph of §1.1, the inset following Principle 2.1 of §2.1, and the cascade derivation of §§2–9, packaged in Theorem 6.6.7.6.) This distinction is foundational: every static-light-cone program treats geometric kinematics as the primitive input and must add the quantum-mechanical formalism (Hilbert space, Born rule, entanglement, Bell-violation correlations) as separate structure layered on top of the static metric. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework treats the active wavefront — and the dynamical content built into it — as the primitive, and derives BOTH the quantum-mechanical formalism AND the Lorentzian spacetime formalism of relativity as cascade-level theorems from this dynamical premise. The static null cone of orthodox physics and the active McGucken Sphere are **not the same geometric object**: the former is a passive locus, the latter is a propagating wavefront with frequency, phase, and action content built in. They share a region of spacetime, in the way that the trail of a moving particle shares a region of spacetime with the particle’s trajectory, but the trail is not the particle.

*The two senses of locality, disambiguated.* The locality discussion in the static-light-cone tradition refers to **local-Lagrangian locality**: the form of action $S = \int \mathcal{L}(x) d^4x$ where $\mathcal{L}(x)$ depends on field values and finitely many derivatives at the single point $x$. The Einstein–Hilbert action of GR, the Yang–Mills action of QFT, the Klein–Gordon and Dirac Lagrangians, and the continuum d’Alembertian $\Box$ all have this property; the action is an integral over the spacetime manifold of a density that depends only on infinitesimally-nearby field content at each point. **Bell-violation locality**, by contrast, is the no-spacelike-correlation property: measurements at spacelike-separated events have factorizable joint probabilities, the property $P(A,B|a,b,\lambda) = P(A|a,\lambda) P(B|b,\lambda)$ for some hidden variable $\lambda$. The two senses are derivationally distinct: standard continuum QFT on Minkowski spacetime has local-Lagrangian locality (every QFT textbook builds the Lagrangian to satisfy this) but lacks Bell-violation locality (the empirical record of nonlocality, falsifying Bell-CHSH inequalities, has been confirmed by Aspect 1982, Tittel et al. 1998, Hensen et al. 2015 loophole-free, Big Bell Test Collaboration 2018, and every Bell test since). Standard physics is local in sense (1) and nonlocal in sense (2), simultaneously, with no formal contradiction within the orthodox treatment.

*Which sense the Sorkin–Dowker lineage addresses.* The Sorkin–Dowker causal-set lineage addresses **local-Lagrangian locality at the operator level**. Their concern is that the Poisson-sprinkling discretization scheme — which is required to preserve Lorentz invariance — produces discrete d’Alembertians whose kernels depend on infinitely many discrete events distributed on the past-light-cone hyperboloid. The discrete operator $B^{(d)}\phi(x)$ does not have the local-Lagrangian form (it does not depend only on field values at infinitesimally-nearby events to $x$); it depends on field values at an infinite set of events one Planck unit of proper time in the past. The 18-year engineering arc — Sorkin 2007 \[“Does locality fail at intermediate length-scales?”, arXiv:gr-qc/0703099\], Benincasa–Dowker 2010, Dowker–Glaser 2013, Belenchia–Benincasa–Dowker 2015, Boguñá–Krioukov 2025 — is the construction project of finding discrete operators that *behave nonlocally on the discrete substrate* but *converge to the local-Lagrangian continuum d’Alembertian* $\Box$ in the right limit. Boguñá–Krioukov 2025 \[arXiv:2506.18745\] state the engineering goal verbatim: *“This approach thus reconciles locality with Lorentz invariance, and paves a way toward defining converging discrete approximations to locality-based differential operators even in theories that are inherently nonlocal.”* The phrase “Lorentzian nonlocality” in this lineage refers to this operator-kernel nonlocality, treated as a discretization artifact to be tamed so that the continuum limit recovers standard local-Lagrangian physics. The lineage does *not* address Bell-violation nonlocality, does not offer a physical explanation of EPR correlations, and does not engage with the quantum-mechanical nonlocality of standard QM at any level — the quantum-mechanical formalism is treated as a separate framework layered on the causet background (Sorkin 2011 “Scalar Field Theory on a Causal Set in Histories Form” J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 306, 012017; Johnston 2008 “Particle propagators on discrete spacetime” Class. Quant. Grav. 25, 202001; Albertini et al. 2024 in-in correlators Phys. Rev. D 109.106014).

*Which sense McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1 addresses.* McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1 addresses **Bell-violation locality** — the source of the no-spacelike-correlation property that empirical Bell tests have falsified. The theorem identifies the null cone of the continuous Lorentzian metric — *not* a discretization artifact, *not* an operator-kernel property — as the geometric source of the Bell-violation correlations of standard quantum mechanics. The McGucken Sphere wavefront $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ from event $E$ propagates at null on the light cone $\partial J^+(E)$; correlations between measurements at spacelike-separated events $E_1, E_2$ in the chronological future of a common-source event $E_I$ are present in the Sphere wavefront from $E_I$ onward (Theorem 6.6.7.7 no-signaling theorem); the same null structure that the static-light-cone tradition treats as locality-supplying is in fact the nonlocality-source of the empirical Bell-violation record. The McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1 biconditional content (null vectors ⇔ Sphere ⇔ Lorentzian signature ⇔ nonlocality) is a statement about sense (2) — Bell-violation locality — and the geometric source of its failure in nature.

*The two programs are addressing different phenomena that share a word.* The Sorkin–Dowker lineage works on local-Lagrangian operator-kernel locality (sense 1) as a continuum-recovery engineering problem; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework works on Bell-violation locality (sense 2) as a geometric identification. Both use the word “locality” and both invoke the null cone; the geometric objects, the physics, and the claims are different. The Sorkin–Dowker “Lorentzian nonlocality” terminology is not a near-miss to the McGucken claim because the two phrases denote different physical phenomena. A near-miss would require sharing the physical phenomenon being addressed; sharing vocabulary is necessary but not sufficient.

*Why no published near-miss exists to McGucken Theorem 6.6.8.1.* The categorical reason is now clear: **every published program engaging with the null cone treats it as static kinematics, not as the integrated trail of an active wavefront.** A static null cone cannot be the source of Bell-violation correlations because it has no dynamical content — no wavefront, no oscillation, no frequency, no phase, no action quantum, nothing that could carry the information required to *produce* the correlations rather than merely *be the kinematic stage* on which the correlations are observed. To identify the metric’s null structure as the physical source of Bell-violation nonlocality, one needs the null cone to be dynamical — to have wavefront built in. The static-light-cone tradition cannot, by construction, make this identification. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework can, and does, via Theorem 6.6.8.1, precisely because the active McGucken Sphere wavefront carries the dynamical content built into the geometric primitive itself. To our knowledge, no published physics theorem prior to the McGucken corpus offers a physical-geometric explanation of Bell-violation nonlocality as the content of the Lorentzian metric — because the framework required to ask the question (active wavefront as geometric primitive) is the categorical break the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework introduces.

*Categorical novelty of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic programme.* The novelty established by Theorems 6.6.7.4, 6.6.7.6, and 6.6.8.1 is therefore a break with the entire orthodox tradition. *(a) Dynamical premise.* dx₄/dt = ic is an active dynamical principle — every event has an active spherically symmetric expansion in $x_4$ at velocity $c$, with action $\hbar$ per Planck-frequency oscillation — not added separately at a later stage. *(b) Active wavefront as geometric primitive.* The McGucken Sphere $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ is the geometric primitive; the static null cone of the orthodox tradition is the integrated coordinate shadow. The relationship is one-way: the active Sphere generates the static null cone as its trail, but the static null cone does not generate the active Sphere. *(c) Biconditional identity.* Theorem 6.6.8.1 establishes that null vectors, McGucken Sphere, Lorentzian signature, frame-invariance of $c$, Lorentz group structure, and Bell-violation nonlocality are biconditionally tied to one another — they are aspects of one structure, not separate axiomatic ingredients. *(d) Cascade derivation of QM as forced theorem chain.* Quantum mechanics is not added as separate structure; the cascade Sphere → Hilbert → inner product → Born rule → Bell-violation correlations runs as a sequence of forced theorems from the active wavefront of dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 6.6.7.6, packaged with proof-level audit). *(e) Physical explanation of quantum nonlocality.* The Lorentzian metric’s null structure is identified as the geometric source of the empirical Bell-violation record. This is the foundational answer to the EPR question Einstein, Podolsky, Rosen posed in 1935 and that Bell sharpened in 1964: the source of the spooky action at a distance is the active McGucken Sphere wavefront, identical to the null cone of the same Lorentzian metric that produces relativistic locality at the local-Lagrangian level.

The static-light-cone tradition, taken as a whole, was the right framework to investigate within the kinematical paradigm of twentieth-century physics — and it produced enormous results (twistor theory, causal sets, holography, BMS symmetries, null infinity, conformal field theory at null asymptotic boundaries). The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework operates one level upstream, treating the null cone as the integrated shadow of an active wavefront whose dynamical content is what generates the quantum-mechanical structure of nature. This is the categorical distinction. McGucken Theorems 6.6.7.4, 6.6.7.6, and 6.6.8.1 do not extend, sharpen, or near-miss any prior theorem; they state new content made possible by the categorical break with the static-light-cone tradition.

The remainder of §1 develops the architectural inversion (§1.2 below) that supplies the upstream physical principle, the four-step cogeneration cascade $\mathcal{M}_G \to \mathbb{M}_{1,3} \to \mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{H}$ implementing the four-level architecture, and the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s distinctions from the prior literature cataloged in Table 1.A above.

#### 1.1bis.5 Foundational austerity of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic programme

The foregoing sections have established what the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework derives and what its categorical novelty consists in. The property that makes the breadth of these derivations possible is the *foundational austerity* of dx₄/dt = ic: the minimality of the ingredients posited as primitive, set against the volume of downstream physics cascading from them. This subsection itemizes the foundational data of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework with the discipline of identifying precisely what is, and is not, postulated as primitive.

*Two ingredients suffice.* The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework rests on exactly two foundational ingredients:

1.  **A four-dimensional Euclidean coordinate structure** $\mathbb{R}^4$ with four mutually perpendicular axes $(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$ — the McGucken Space $\mathcal{M}_G$ of §1.2 below — with its standard Euclidean line element $ds_E^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2$.

2.  **The McGucken Principle**: at every event $E \in \mathcal{M}_G$, the fourth perpendicular coordinate $x_4$ is advancing at rate $c$ with action $\hbar$ per Planck-frequency oscillation, expressed by dx₄/dt = ic. The Principle is one ingredient bundling two clauses — the *rate clause* (the rate of $x_4$-advance is $c$, giving the constant $c$) and the *action-quantization clause* (the advance carries action $\hbar$ per Planck-frequency oscillation, giving the constant $\hbar$) — as twin properties of a single dynamical advance. The framing as one ingredient is consistent with Proposition 2.2 of §2.2, where $c$ and $\hbar$ are derived as the twin constants of one geometric flow; the framing as two clauses is the unbundling that Proposition 2.2 supplies for readers who wish to name the rate reading and the action reading of dx₄/dt = ic separately, both carried by the one advance.

No further ingredients are posited as primitive. The cascade of §§2–9 derives everything else.

*The imaginary unit $i$ is not a separate primitive.* The imaginary unit appearing in dx₄/dt = ic is the algebraic marker of $x_4$’s perpendicularity to the 3D spatial subspace, not an additional ingredient. The generator of $90°$ rotation in a 2D Euclidean plane is, by elementary algebra, the imaginary unit: if $(x, y)$ are perpendicular axes and one writes $z = x + iy$, then $i$ encodes the rotation that maps $x$ into $y$, and $i^2 = -1$ encodes the $180°$ flip. Perpendicularity *is* $i$, expressed algebraically. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework does not postulate $i$ separately from the geometric perpendicular structure; once one has four mutually perpendicular axes, the algebra of $i$ is forced as the algebraic expression of that perpendicularity. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is therefore properly read as “the active advance along the fourth perpendicular direction at every event proceeds at rate $c$, with $i$ marking the perpendicularity algebraically.” The imaginary unit is the perpendicularity already present in the geometric setup, expressed in algebraic language.

*The evolution parameter $t$ is not a primitive.* The coordinate $t$ appearing in dx₄/dt = ic and in the integrated coordinate $x_4 = ict$ is not a pre-existing evolution parameter. It is the integrated parameterization of the active $x_4$-expansion. The active expansion at every event is what physically occurs; the coordinate $t$ is its mere integrated shadow. *Every theorem of the dx₄/dt = ic framework traces to the active expansion; the coordinate label is its mere integrated shadow.* The principle dx₄/dt = ic is therefore not to be read in the orthodox manner — “the rate of change of $x_4$ with respect to a pre-existing $t$ is $ic$” — because that reading takes both $t$ and $x_4$ as pre-existing coordinates and reduces the principle to a relationship between them. The correct McGucken reading is: at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$, an active perpendicular advance proceeds at rate $c$; the coordinate $t$ is the parameterization that measures how much advance has occurred, and the coordinate $x_4 = ict$ is the integrated label of where the advance has gone in the perpendicular direction. *The dynamics are in the premise.* The advance is primary; the coordinates are its trace.

### 1.2 The architectural inversion: replacing the orthodox Hilbert-space-as-primitive-arena framework with dx₄/dt = ic as upstream physical principle generating 𝓗 + Born rule + CCR + uncertainty + Schrödinger as theorems

The four pillars of quantum mechanics, and the Schrödinger equation governing their dynamics, derive directly from the Lorentzian spacetime metric of special relativity. The starting point is the empirically established Minkowski metric ds² = −c²dt² + dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃². The first observation (Lemma 2.0) is that this metric contains, at every point, the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic as the rest-frame statement of the four-velocity normalization u\^μ u_μ = −c². The McGucken Principle is the rest-frame differential statement of the Lorentzian four-velocity normalization, mathematically equivalent to the metric itself.

*Architectural-priority note.* dx₄/dt = ic is the foundational physical principle of the McGucken framework. The Lorentzian metric is itself a forced consequence of this principle (Lemma 2.5: integration gives x₄ = ict, squaring gives dx₄² = −c²dt², substitution into the four-dimensional Euclidean line element yields the Minkowski signature). Across the McGucken corpus, both quantum mechanics and general relativity (\[54–57\]) are cogenerated as sibling outputs of dx₄/dt = ic, with the Lorentzian metric the first shared downstream waypoint. The framing as a derivation starting from the Lorentzian metric is a presentational choice for accessibility — the metric is the empirically established entry point every physicist accepts — with the architectural priority being the McGucken Principle as foundational and the metric as derived. See §2.0 for the full architectural-priority discussion and the equivalence in both directions.

The orthodox Minkowski treatment writes x₄ = ict as a formal coordinate device — a notational trick to give the Lorentzian signature — and denies x₄ physics beyond that bookkeeping role. dx₄/dt = ic asserts the opposite: x₄ is a physical, geometric, nonlocal direction — the radius of a spherical wavefront expanding from every spacetime event at velocity c, with each oscillatory step carrying a quantum of action ℏ. The imaginary unit i marks geometric perpendicularity to the spatial slice, not imaginary unreality. Orthodoxy and the McGucken Principle agree on the mathematics; they disagree on what is happening in nature. Only the physical-expansion ontology produces the cogenerative cascade through which the Hilbert space, the Born rule, the canonical commutation relation, the uncertainty principle, and the Schrödinger equation are derived. The formal-coordinate treatment produces no foundational quantum-mechanical content; the physical-expansion ontology produces all of it. The empirical productivity of the physical-expansion ontology is the case for the reinterpretation.

The Principle is a *two-constant* statement about a single geometric flow. The velocity of x₄-advance defines c; the foundational wavelength of x₄-advance defines ℏ. These are twin properties of one geometric flow — c its rate, ℏ its action quantum per Planck-frequency oscillation. The principle is a two-constant statement about a single dynamical fact.

This is the dynamical content. The relation x₄ = ict is its integrated coordinate shadow — the algebraic expression of the velocity part of the McGucken Principle in coordinates anchored at x₄ = 0 when t = 0. The relationship between the two forms is that of Newton’s F = ma to x(t) = (1/2)at²: the dynamical law is the physics, the integrated trajectory is its coordinate expression. Obtaining x₄ = ict by integration of dx₄/dt = ic is one small step for math; recognizing that the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric manner, carrying action ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation — with all the derivational consequences this has across quantum mechanics, general relativity, thermodynamics, spacetime, symmetry, action, and cosmology — is one giant leap for physics.

The fourth dimension x₄ is the physical, dynamical, geometric direction that expands at the velocity of light from every spacetime event, oscillating at the Planck frequency and carrying ℏ per cycle. The imaginary unit i in the integrated form x₄ = ict is the algebraic marker for the orthogonality of x₄ to the three spatial dimensions x₁, x₂, x₃ — the same i whose square gives the minus sign of the Lorentzian signature via (ict)² = −c² t².

dx₄/dt = ic forces all four pillars of quantum mechanics and the Schrödinger equation governing their dynamics. The two foundational constants c and ℏ are the two natural dimensional parameters of the one expansion — c as its rate, ℏ as the action it carries per Planck-frequency oscillation — both properties of the same geometric flow rather than independent constants of independent theories. The argument is upstream of the mainstream menu: rather than starting from a vector ψ ∈ 𝓗 and trying to motivate the inner product, the rule, the commutator, the uncertainty, and the dynamics from supplementary axioms inside 𝓗, we *construct* ψ as the projection of x₄-advance onto x₁x₂x₃ on the McGucken Sphere, and then prove that the entire formalism is the unique structure forced by the Lorentzian metric’s rest-frame content.

Once the inversion is accomplished, the central architectural fact of the dx₄/dt = ic framework becomes visible: the Hilbert space of quantum mechanics and the Minkowski spacetime manifold of special relativity are the same geometric object — the constraint surface where dx₄/dt = ic holds locally — represented at two cascade levels. Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is the point-set / manifold-level rendering of the constraint surface; 𝓗 = L²(Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, η_μν) is the function-space rendering of the same constraint surface, with the Lorentzian metric becoming the sesquilinear inner product by the canonical L²-functional construction. The spatial points of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at parameter time t and the position-eigenstate basis of 𝓗 at parameter time t are in canonical bijection, with each spatial point x₀ ∈ ℝ³ corresponding to the position eigenstate \|x₀⟩ = δ³(x − x₀). The complex character of ψ is the algebraic record of x_4’s perpendicularity (Theorem 3.1); the rank-2 sesquilinear inner product is the L²-rendering of the rank-2 Lorentzian metric (Lemma 7.1); the non-commutative operator algebra \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ is the operator-level expression of the geometric perpendicularity x₁x₂x₃ ⊥ x_4 (Proposition 12.10); the infinite-dimensionality of 𝓗 is the continuum cardinality of perpendicular x_4-radii from McGucken Spheres at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (Proposition 10.7) — with each “dimension” of 𝓗 a specific perpendicular x_4-radius from a McGucken Sphere, and the Feynman path-integral sum that constructs ψ being the sum over arriving x_4-radii at the target spatial point; the dx₄/dt = ic framework provides both geometric continuity (continuous spacetime, continuous spectra, exact Lorentz invariance) and action discreteness (one ℏ-quantum per Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance, with the de Broglie / Compton / Planck wavelength hierarchy supplying the natural scale at every regime) simultaneously, at different cascade-level aspects of dx₄/dt = ic (Proposition 10.8), dissolving the century-long discrete-vs-continuous spacetime debate between causal sets / loop quantum gravity / Regge calculus / spin foams on one side and standard QFT / Lorentz invariance / Wielandt–Wintner on the other. There is no separate Hilbert space “where quantum mechanics lives” connected by postulated bridges to a separate spacetime “where relativity lives.” There is one geometric structure — Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ — and 𝓗 is Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ in its function-valued representation, with both representations pointwise instantiated by dx₄/dt = ic. The orthodox “4-dimensional vs infinite-dimensional” contrast (Dirac 1930, von Neumann 1932, Reed-Simon 1972-1980) resolves into same geometric structure, two cascade-level countings: 4 at the manifold level, 2\^ℵ₀ at the function-space level, both counting the same continuum of perpendicular x_4-radii from McGucken Spheres throughout Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. The full theorem-level statements (Theorem 10.6, Proposition 10.7, and Proposition 10.8) are developed in §10.6 of the present paper as the central corollaries of Theorem 10.5’s pointwise-instantiation property. This is the dissolution of the foundations-of-quantum-mechanics problem at its root: the Hilbert space did not require an axiomatization of its own because it is the function-space rendering of the spacetime manifold of relativity, with the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplying both at every point — and the continuum and the discreteness as complementary cascade-level aspects of that one principle.

This work sits within the *McGucken Quantum Formalism* developed in the companion paper \[114\], which establishes the dual-channel quantum-theoretical framework underlying dx₄/dt = ic as a categorically novel mathematical structure (formal three-definition / four-proposition / four-proof argument in \[114, §7.5\]) not reducible to any single-channel framework (algebraic-symmetry or geometric-propagation), nor to standard formulations of spectral-triple (Connes) or categorical-QFT (Atiyah–Segal–Lurie). The defining feature of the McGucken Quantum Formalism is its *dual-channel* content: the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic simultaneously specifies an algebraic-symmetry channel (invariance of x₄’s advance under time translation, space translation, rotation, and Lorentz boost) and a geometric-propagation channel (the spherical symmetry of x₄’s expansion as Huygens-wavefront propagation from every spacetime event), with the canonical commutation relation \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ derivable through two disjoint routes — the Hamiltonian route via Stone’s theorem (\[114, Propositions H.1–H.5\]) and the Lagrangian route via Huygens-wavefront path summation (\[114, Propositions L.1–L.6\]). This is the *convergent overdetermination* of the McGucken Quantum Formalism (\[114, Lemma 15.1\]). §§5–7 below realize the Hamiltonian-channel, §§3, 7.4, 9 realize the Lagrangian-channel, §10 exhibits the cogenerative cascade in which both channels meet, and §11 is the axiomatic-corollary content of the McGucken Quantum Formalism’s quantum layer (Q1)–(Q4) of \[114, Definition 9.1\].

*What convergent overdetermination means, and why it matters.* Throughout this paper, a single result — the Lorentzian metric, the canonical commutator, the Born rule, the Schrödinger equation — is reached repeatedly by derivational pathways that share no machinery except the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic itself. One begins from the one physical fact that the fourth dimension expands at the rate $c$, proceeds along separate and logically independent routes — one through the metric, another through a symmetry group, another through a wavefront collision, another through a reflection — and arrives, along each, at the very same end result. That the same downstream fact is fixed independently by several upstream properties of the same structure is what we call convergent overdetermination. It is not redundancy and not a single argument told several times: each route uses different premises, so any one of them alone would establish the result, and their agreement is therefore evidence about the source rather than about the routes. When many independent derivations converge on one conclusion, the conclusion’s robustness testifies to the foundational nature of their common origin. Here that common origin is dx₄/dt = ic: the recurrence of convergent overdetermination across the metric, the commutator, the Born rule, and the Schrödinger equation is the paper’s central evidence that the Principle is foundational — that these structures are not independently postulated but descend, by multiple confirming paths, from the one physical expansion.

### 1.3 The four prerequisites that blocked everyone else: physical principle upstream of Hilbert space, derivation of both i (perpendicularity marker) and ℏ (action quantization) from the principle, dynamical content built into the premise, and integration of relativistic + quantum structure into one cascade

The McGucken Principle is, on its face, simple. Why did the twentieth century’s foundational physicists — Einstein, Bohr, Dirac, Heisenberg, Wheeler, Feynman — not write it down? The answer is that four conceptual blocks had to be simultaneously rejected for the McGucken Principle to become writable:

1.  **The block-universe reading of relativity**. After Minkowski’s 1908 lecture, the dominant reading of relativity treated spacetime as a static four-dimensional manifold. Past, present, and future were taken to coexist in the block; the flow of time was relegated to psychology. Einstein himself wrote in 1955 that “the distinction between past, present and future is only a stubbornly persistent illusion.” Once spacetime was static, the question “what is the rate of change of x₄?” was treated as malformed. Coordinates do not have rates of change; they are labels.

2.  **The formalist reading of i**. The imaginary unit i entered quantum mechanics through Schrödinger’s 1926 wave equation, the canonical commutator, and the path-integral weight. In each case it appeared as a formal device with no geometry. Hestenes (1966, 1979) made the strongest pre-McGucken case for geometry for i, identifying it with a unit bivector iσ₃ = γ₂γ₁ in spacetime algebra Cl(1,3), but Hestenes’s bivector was static, attached to a fixed Minkowski background, not connected to a rate of change.

3.  **The disciplinary separation of quantum mechanics and relativity**. Twentieth-century physics separated quantum mechanics from relativity at the foundational-derivation level. Quantum field theory unified them at the operator level, but the foundational constants ℏ and c remained separately measured empirical inputs. No major program asked whether the imaginary unit in \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ and the imaginary unit in x₄ = ict are the same i.

4.  **The interpretation industry**. By the 1990s the foundations of quantum mechanics had become an “interpretation industry.” Each interpretation — Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, Bohmian, QBist, relational — took the Hilbert-space formalism as inviolable and proposed a story about what it means. None asked whether the formalism itself could be derived from something deeper.

All four had to fail simultaneously to block the discovery of dx₄/dt = ic. They failed simultaneously at Princeton in 1989–1990, in conversations with John Archibald Wheeler, in the lineage of a physicist who took seriously Wheeler’s question about deriving the time part of the Schwarzschild metric by poor-man’s reasoning from first principles — a question that contained the unfashionable commitments that foundational mathematical structures should have direct geometric meanings and that derivation from one geometric fact is preferable to axiomatization from many.

### 1.5 The dual-channel architecture within the McGucken Quantum Formalism

The dual-channel architecture — dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation channel) and dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry channel) derivations of every quantum-theoretical structure, with both channels descending from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic through derivationally distinct intermediate machinery — is a formal development of the **McGucken Quantum Formalism (MQF)** established as the categorically novel quantum-theoretical structure underlying the McGucken Principle in \[MG-MQF, 2026\] (the comprehensive prior-art survey and formal categorical-novelty propositions) and \[MG-Foundations, 2026\] (the dual-route Hamiltonian-Lagrangian derivation of the canonical commutator). The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel derivations correspond to the **Lagrangian route Propositions L.1–L.6** of \[MG-Foundations\]: the geometric-propagation route through Huygens-wavefront propagation on the McGucken Sphere, path-space generation by iterated Huygens expansions, the x₄-phase identification with classical action, the Feynman path integral as sum over paths weighted by x₄-phase, and short-time Gaussian integration recovering the Schrödinger equation. The Algebraic Channel derivations correspond to the **Hamiltonian route Propositions H.1–H.5** of \[MG-Foundations\]: the algebraic-symmetry route through translation invariance, Stone’s theorem on strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups, the configuration representation, and Stone–von Neumann uniqueness. **The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel is the more foundational channel**: it carries the full content of the McGucken Principle including its +ic orientation, with the McGucken Sphere expanding at +ic from every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ being the physical-spatiotemporal content of the dx₄/dt = ic framework. The Algebraic Channel is the T-invariant projection of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel (the projection theorem ΠA of §16), with the orientation +ic algebraically projected away into the sign-blind operator algebra. The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel is foundationally primary; the Algebraic Channel is the algebraic shadow.

The relation between the two channels is known as the **McGucken Duality** (equivalently the **dx₄/dt=ic Duality** or the **McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Duality**): the foundational Geometric Channel carries the +ic-oriented McGucken Sphere expansion at every spacetime event, and the Algebraic Channel is its T-invariant algebraic shadow. The convergence of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel and the Algebraic Channel on the same result through disjoint intermediate machinery is the **convergent-overdetermination property** of MQF, formalized as Lemma 15.1 of \[MG-MQF\] and Theorem VII.1 of \[MG-Foundations\]: the two routes share no intermediate machinery except the starting principle dx₄/dt = ic and the final algebraic identity. Stone’s theorem does not appear in the Lagrangian route; Huygens-wavefront propagation does not appear in the Hamiltonian route; configuration representation and Gaussian path-integration are disjoint operations. The same canonical commutation relation \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ is reached by two independent chains from the same starting principle, with no shared intermediate steps. This is the formal-mathematical signature of the dual-channel commitment of MQF, and it is the property that distinguishes MQF from every prior single-channel framework of quantum theory.

The companion paper \[MG-Geometry, 2026\] establishes the analogous categorical-novelty result on the geometric side: moving-dimension geometry is a categorically novel geometric category not equivalent to any prior framework of dynamical geometry from 1915 to 2026. Together, the two companion papers position the McGucken Principle as the foundational geometric postulate from which two categorically novel mathematical structures descend: moving-dimension geometry on the geometric side, dual-channel quantum theory on the quantum-theoretical side, with the dual-channel of dx₄/dt = ic as the formal signature of the deeper unity.
