The §10.9 audit table catalogs the convergent-overdetermination property across every derivation in the cascade. Each dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel convergence is an instance of the convergent-overdetermination property of MQF.

The categorical novelty of dual-channel quantum theory is established formally in \[MG-MQF, Propositions 7.5.1–7.5.4\]: the McGucken Quantum Formalism is not reducible to single-channel algebraic-symmetry frameworks (the Heisenberg–Stone–von Neumann apparatus, Wightman axiomatic QFT, Haag–Kastler algebraic QFT, the Wigner–Coleman–Mandula–Weinberg representation-theoretic apparatus, Adler’s trace dynamics), not reducible to single-channel geometric-propagation frameworks (Feynman’s path integral, Dirac’s 1933 Lagrangian formulation, Bohmian mechanics, Nelson’s stochastic mechanics, Lindgren–Liukkonen optimal control, ’t Hooft’s cellular automaton, Hestenes’s spacetime algebra, Schuller’s constructive gravity), and not reducible in standard formulation to spectral-triple frameworks (Connes’s noncommutative geometry) or categorical-QFT frameworks (Atiyah–Segal–Lurie cobordism categories, Lurie’s cobordism hypothesis). The categorical-novelty result is established as a formal mathematical fact via four propositions with proofs, not as a philosophical interpretation. §13 of the present paper revisits the categorical-novelty result in the QM-derivation context with explicit cross-reference.

The MQF framework is summarized as a sextuple **(M, F, V; H, A, ψ)** in \[MG-MQF, Definition 9.2\]: the first three components (M, F, V) constitute the moving-dimension manifold from \[MG-Geometry, Definition 9.3\] (a smooth four-manifold with Lorentzian metric, a codimension-one timelike foliation, and a privileged active timelike vector field whose flow is x₄’s expansion at rate ic); the next three (H, A, ψ) constitute the quantum layer (a separable complex Hilbert space, a \*-algebra of operators satisfying the canonical commutation relations, a wavefunction satisfying the Schrödinger equation), with the additional commitment that the dual-channel is the defining feature: both the algebraic structure (H, A) and the wavefunction evolution ψ are derived from dx₄/dt = ic as parallel sibling theorems through Hamiltonian and Lagrangian routes with convergent overdetermination at every identity. §§3–9 supply the QM-derivation content of this sextuple at depth: §§3–9 derive the Hilbert space, canonical commutator, Born rule, uncertainty principle, Schrödinger equation, and Klein–Gordon equation with both channels of MQF realized for each; §§10–12 develop the cogenerative cascade structure (Theorem 10.5), the Hilbert-Minkowski identity (Theorem 10.6), the Dirac–von Neumann axioms as corollaries (§11), and measurement as physical Wick rotation (Theorem 12.2). The corpus citations \[MG-PathInt\], \[MG-Born\], \[MG-Commut\], \[MG-HLA\], \[MG-Uncertainty\], \[MG-Wick\], \[MG-Constants\], \[MG-deBroglie\], \[MG-Noether\], and the broader McGucken corpus supply the foundational derivations on which §§3–9 build.

### 1.6 The Wheeler-Taylor “soar through spacetime” epigraph of 1966 as pedagogical precursor, dx₄/dt = ic as its dynamical completion, and the Wheeler-Princeton pedagogical lineage from *Spacetime Physics* through *A Journey into Gravity and Spacetime* through *Exploring Black Holes* to the present cascade

The reading of dx₄/dt = ic as the foundational geometric principle of physics is that tradition’s dynamical completion. The direct pedagogical ancestor is not Brian Greene’s *The Elegant Universe* (1999) or *The Fabric of the Cosmos* (2004) — the popular expositions that a generation of readers now associate with the “everything moves through spacetime at c” heuristic — but Edwin F. Taylor and John Archibald Wheeler’s *Spacetime Physics* (W. H. Freeman, 1st edition 1966; 2nd edition 1992) \[191\], the introductory special-relativity text through which the previous three generations of physicists first encountered the four-dimensional formalism in an undergraduate physics education. *Spacetime Physics* opens Chapter 4 (“Trip to Canopus”) with an epigraph, in Wheeler’s characteristic voice, that compresses the whole book’s pedagogical apparatus into eight words: *“Move or stand still; in either case we soar through spacetime.”*

This is the seed of the pedagogy that Greene later popularized. Wheeler wrote it (with Taylor as coauthor) thirty-three to thirty-eight years before Greene, and continued to develop the framing in his single-author popular book *A Journey into Gravity and Spacetime* (Scientific American Library, 1990) \[193\] — which antedates *The Fabric of the Cosmos* by fourteen years — and in the Taylor-Wheeler general-relativity sequel *Exploring Black Holes: Introduction to General Relativity* (Addison-Wesley, 2000) \[194\], which extends the same pedagogical style to four-velocity for both massive and massless particles in curved spacetime. The “everything moves through spacetime at c” reading of relativity, insofar as it can be attributed to any single expositor, is Wheeler’s — with Taylor as coauthor of its first published statement in 1966 — not Greene’s. Greene’s version is downstream of the Wheeler-Taylor pedagogical lineage, not upstream of it.

What the Wheeler-Taylor 1966 epigraph asserts is that soaring through spacetime — whether or not one is at spatial rest — is a primitive fact about physics. The book’s mathematical machinery then supports this framing with the metric-identity content of the invariant four-velocity magnitude, u\^μ u_μ = -c² in the (-, +, +, +) signature convention that Taylor-Wheeler used in the second edition. What the epigraph did not do, and what the Taylor-Wheeler 1966 formal apparatus did not do, is give this soaring-through-spacetime a *dynamical* form as a scalar equation at every event. It left the four-velocity magnitude identity as a metric identity — a static coordinate fact about the Lorentzian signature — rather than promoting the primitive to a dynamical statement about *what x₄ is doing* at every event of spacetime. Wheeler and Taylor’s pedagogical instinct — that we are soaring through spacetime whether we move or stand still — was, in 1966, rhetorical, not scalar-equation; aphoristic, not dynamical.

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies the missing dynamical form. What the Wheeler-Taylor 1966 epigraph stated as a rhetorical framing — that we soar through spacetime whether we move or stand still — the McGucken Principle states as a scalar equation valid at every event of the McGucken Space 𝓜_G: the fourth dimension x₄ is expanding at velocity c from every spacetime point, and this dynamical expansion is precisely the “soaring through spacetime” that Wheeler and Taylor’s epigraph named. The reading is the identification of the geometric object that the apparatus was implicitly describing. Under dx₄/dt = ic:

-   A massive particle at spatial rest has its full four-velocity budget in x₄-advance, dx₄/dt = ic pointwise. This is the Wheeler-pedagogical “moves through time at c” made scalar-equation explicit.
-   A photon has zero share in the x₄-advance, its Sphere-tangent share vanishing, $v_{x_4} = 0$ pointwise (while the Principle dx₄/dt = ic holds at its events): the photon rides the wavefront rather than advancing across it. This is the Wheeler-pedagogical “puts all c into space, and none into time” made scalar-equation explicit.
-   A moving massive particle apportions its budget between x₁, x₂, x₃-motion and x₄-advance via the Lorentz-invariant rapidity content (Theorem 2.4.5 of the present paper), with the total four-velocity budget preserved as a scalar invariant at every event.

Every one of these three cases is the Wheeler-pedagogical framing made dynamically explicit. The “we soar through spacetime” epigraph and the dx₄/dt = ic scalar equation say the same thing about the same geometric object; the second is the first made rigorous. The invariant four-velocity magnitude u\^μ u_μ = -c² of the Taylor-Wheeler 1966 apparatus is the coordinate-integrated shadow of the pointwise dynamical statement dx₄/dt = ic; the metric identity is the label, the dynamical expansion at ic is the geometric object doing the soaring.

The author of the present paper studied physics at Princeton University in the late 1980s under John Archibald Wheeler’s mentorship as an undergraduate, and Wheeler’s recommendation letter written on the author’s behalf (a matter of institutional record; see the biographical preface of this paper and the priority record of §6.6.10) placed the author in the pedagogical tradition of Newton, Euclid, and Wheeler’s own call for nobility in physics — noting, among other things, that the author had played Prospero in a production of Shakespeare’s *The Tempest*. The 1998-1999 UNC Chapel Hill dissertation Appendix B and the 2003-2006 Moving-Dimensions Theory (MDT) preprints developed dx₄/dt = ic as the dynamical formalization of Wheeler’s pedagogical instinct. The five FQXi essays of 2008-2013 extended the treatment. The corpus papers of 2016-2026 (see refs \[50\]–\[57\], \[113\]–\[114\], \[144\], \[182\]–\[186\]) systematized it. The present paper of 2026 supplies the QM-derivation cascade from dx₄/dt = ic to the Hilbert space (Theorem 6.1), the Born rule (Theorems 7.4, 7.7, 7.11), the canonical commutator (Theorem 5.1), the uncertainty principle (Theorem 8.2), the Schrödinger equation (Theorem 9.1), and the Einstein field equations (Theorem 6.6.9.6) as theorems descending from a single dynamical postulate. Wheeler’s *“we soar through spacetime”* was the rhetorical seed of 1966; dx₄/dt = ic is the geometric object doing the soaring; the present paper’s Theorems 6.1, 7.4, 10.5, 10.6 are the cascade of QM-structure that descends from that geometric object once its rate of expansion is written down explicitly as a pointwise scalar equation at every event of 𝓜_G.

The Wheeler pedagogical lineage carries a further feature that the McGucken Principle preserves and makes explicit. Wheeler wrote the epigraph of Chapter 4 of *Spacetime Physics* as an aphorism — a rhetorical framing at the pedagogical opening of the chapter, in the tradition of *Gravitation* (Misner-Thorne-Wheeler 1973 \[192\])’s chapter-opening literary epigraphs from Homer’s *Odyssey*, Shakespeare’s *The Tempest*, Dante’s *Commedia*, William Blake, and the other sources that Wheeler and his coauthors chose for their evocation of the heroic and the eternal in the human tradition. Wheeler’s pedagogy was continuous with the humanist tradition that treats physics as one strand of the highest human aspirations, alongside literature, music, and the visual arts — a tradition that stretches from Newton’s classical apparatus through Euclid’s *Elements* through Kepler’s *Harmonice Mundi* to Wheeler’s own call for nobility in physics research. The present paper is offered in that tradition and cites it explicitly at the moment of highest claim in §1.7 below: that dx₄/dt = ic is the light beyond Plato’s Cave, and Minkowski spacetime and Hilbert space are the shadows dancing on the cave’s walls that the McGucken Space 𝓜_G projects.

### 1.7 The photon-through-x₄ diagnostic — questions Q1, Q2, Q3 — the pre-1973 clarity, the Misner-Thorne-Wheeler 1973 abandonment of x₄ = ict, the post-1973 bifurcation of orthodox pedagogy, the “undefined” verdict of the current rigorous literature, Plato’s Cave as the century-long predicament of physicists chained in the coordinate-label reading of x₄, and the resolution of the diagnostic under the pointwise scalar dynamical reading dx₄/dt = ic

The question that most sharply exposes the pedagogical fracture of the twentieth-century orthodox treatment of relativity is one that appears, on its surface, to admit an immediate kinematic answer. Consider the following triad of questions, which any working physicist could be asked in a single interview:

**Q1.** What is the velocity of a photon through the three spatial dimensions x₁, x₂, x₃?

**Q2.** What is the velocity of a photon through the four dimensions of spacetime x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄?

**Q3.** What is the velocity of a photon through the fourth dimension x₄?

Q1 admits a universal answer. Every physicist trained since Einstein 1905 gives the same answer without hesitation: **c**, the invariant speed of light in vacuum. This is the second postulate of special relativity, the operational quantity that Michelson-Morley registered in 1887 and that every inertial frame agrees on. It is a testable, unambiguous, coordinate-invariant fact. No pedagogical camp splits on Q1.

Q2 admits three answers that mutually contradict one another within orthodox pedagogy, and physicists switch between them depending on audience without generally noticing that they have done so.

*Camp A* — the Wheeler-Taylor-Greene pedagogical answer — states that everything moves at c through spacetime; that the photon’s motion is entirely through the spatial directions with none through time; and that the four-velocity budget is filled at c. The Pythagorean form of the identity, √(v_space² + v_time²) = c, works cleanly for a massive particle at spatial rest (0 + c·1 = c) and is stated as if it also works for the photon (√(c² + 0²) = c). This is the reading inherited from the Wheeler-Taylor 1966 epigraph and popularized by Greene 1999.

*Camp B* — the rigorous general-relativity textbook answer of Wald 1984, Carroll 2004, and Misner-Thorne-Wheeler 1973 \[192\] — states that the four-velocity magnitude is c (equivalently u\^μ u_μ = -c²) for massive particles, but *undefined* for photons because proper-time parametrization fails along null worldlines. Standard rigorous move across the current graduate-level literature.

*Camp C* — the null-vector formalism — states that the tangent vector to a photon’s worldline satisfies η_μν k\^μ k\^ν = 0, so that the photon’s “spacetime velocity magnitude” is *zero*, not c.

Camp A and Camp C mutually contradict at the level of numerical value: Camp A gives c, Camp C gives 0. Both are asserted in the same textbook chapters and the same lecture courses depending on which pedagogical point the exposition is currently making. Neither camp is retracted. A graduate student asked “is the photon four-velocity’s magnitude c or 0?” typically pauses, notices the discrepancy, and reaches for whichever answer they think the questioner wants — Camp A if the questioner appears to be testing pedagogical intuition, Camp B or Camp C if the questioner appears to be testing formal rigor.

The answers documented in the current literature and in graduate-student consensus include no fewer than five distinct claims:

*(i) Zero, in the Wheeler-Taylor pedagogical reading.* “Time freezes for photons; a photon’s clock does not tick; a photon emitted at recombination and absorbed by our eye today experiences zero elapsed time.” Widely taught in undergraduate SR and popular physics exposition. Treats the photon’s motion through x₄ as *definite and equal to zero* — a specific numerical claim.

*(ii) Undefined, in the post-Misner-Thorne-Wheeler rigorous formalism.* “dt/dτ diverges along a null worldline; the ratio is not meaningful.” Standard rigorous position across the current GR-textbook literature. Treats the concept as *not applicable to the photon* — a categorically different claim from (i), which treats the value as zero.

*(iii) c, from the coordinate-slope reading.* If x₄ = ct, then dx₄/dt = c trivially — for everything, not just photons. Some careful pedagogues supply this answer, but it collapses into a triviality that says nothing about the photon that would not equally apply to a stone at spatial rest.

*(iv) dx₄/dt = ic, in the pre-1973 imaginary-coordinate convention.* Standard from Minkowski 1908 through the 1960s. Every relativity textbook of that period carried x₄ = ict and derived dx₄/dt = ic as a coordinate consequence. After 1973 (see below), this answer largely disappeared from the orthodox pedagogical apparatus, and physicists trained after 1975 often do not know it was ever the standard convention.

*(v) The block-universe / eternalist dodge.* The question presupposes time-passage, which is illusory; the photon’s worldline is a static geometric object with no “velocity through” any dimension. Rovelli, Barbour, and philosophy-of-physics-adjacent physicists sometimes give this answer.

Five different answers to a single kinematic question about the paradigmatic object of physics. The situation of Q3 is one of elementary kinematics that the orthodox pedagogical tradition cannot answer itself. The kinematic question that Q1 answers trivially and universally becomes, when the same question is asked about x₄, a locus of pedagogical fracture with five mutually distinct answer-types coexisting in the current literature. This is the predicament that the present subsection names and diagnoses.

Before Charles W. Misner, Kip S. Thorne, and John Archibald Wheeler’s *Gravitation* (W. H. Freeman, 1973 — hereafter MTW \[192\]), the standard convention across the international relativity literature was x₄ = ict, with i = √(-1). This convention traces to Hermann Minkowski’s 1908 paper *Die Grundgleichungen für die elektromagnetischen Vorgänge in bewegten Körpern* (submitted 21 February 1908), where Minkowski’s four-position vector carried an imaginary fourth component and the four-velocity’s magnitude was invariant under Lorentz transformations because it was rotation-invariant in the effectively-Euclidean complex geometry, with (ic)² = -c² supplying the effective Lorentzian signature. Under this convention, the answer to Q3 was clean: dx₄/dt = ic. The photon had a definite (imaginary) rate through x₄. Squared, this gave (dx₄/dt)² = (ic)² = -c², which exactly zeroed the null-vector budget of the photon when added to the spatial +c² of Q1:

$$
(ic)^2 + c^2 = -c^2 + c^2 = 0.
$$

The three questions Q1, Q2, Q3 admitted mutually consistent answers under the pre-1973 convention. Q1 gave c; Q2 gave the null-vector condition u\^μ u_μ = 0 by direct algebraic consequence of (ic)² + c² = 0; Q3 gave ic. Camp A’s “moves at c through spacetime” reading and Camp C’s “null-vector budget of zero” reading were the *same statement* under i² = -1: they said the same thing about the same geometric object, with the imaginary factor making the Pythagorean sum work out to zero. The mutual-contradiction of Camps A and C was a *notation artifact* generated by the abandonment of the imaginary-coordinate convention, not a genuine incompatibility between the pedagogical and formal readings.

**Misner-Thorne-Wheeler’s 1973 abandonment of x₄ = ict.** *Gravitation* (MTW) abandoned the x₄ = ict convention. The stated objection was that the imaginary-fourth-coordinate reading cannot extend to curved spacetime — that in a general curved geometry, one cannot maintain the convention that one coordinate is intrinsically imaginary while the other three are intrinsically real, since general coordinate transformations of general relativity mix them. MTW replaced the convention with the real Lorentzian signature (-, +, +, +), and the whole downstream tradition of general-relativity textbooks (Wald 1984, Carroll 2004, and every modern GR text) followed. Even Taylor and Wheeler’s own *Spacetime Physics* second edition of 1992 switched to the real-signature convention in the general-relativity treatment.

The consequence of the MTW abandonment was that the answer to Q3 bifurcated. Wheeler-pedagogical readers of *Spacetime Physics* (1966) continued to give answer (i) at the undergraduate SR level — the photon’s velocity through x₄ is zero, its clock frozen. Post-MTW rigorous readers of *Gravitation* (1973) gave answer (ii) at the graduate GR level — the concept is undefined, proper time is not defined along null worldlines. Both traditions are taught in the same physics departments to the same students at successive stages of their training, and the discrepancy between them is rarely made explicit in the classroom. The dodge that the pedagogy inherited from this bifurcation — reaching for the poetic (“we soar through spacetime”) in the undergraduate context and for the technical (“proper time is not defined for photons”) in the graduate context — is the instability that the present subsection names.

The consensus rigorous position — that the photon’s four-velocity, proper time, and hence “velocity through x₄” are undefined — is documented verbatim across multiple recent arxiv publications. Barak Shoshany’s 2019 SciPost lecture notes on faster-than-light travel and time travel \[187\] supply the most explicit contemporary statement:

> *“The worldline of a massless particle… is a null path. For a null path we cannot define a proper time, since by definition its tangent is a null vector, so \|ẋ(λ)\|² = 0 for any choice of parameter λ… This is why we sometimes say that massless particles, such as photons, ‘do not experience the passage of time’; the proper time along their worldlines vanishes… massless particles do not have a well-defined 4-velocity, since the definition of 4-velocity makes use of the proper time.”* — Shoshany 2019, arXiv:1907.04178.

J. O. Shipley’s PhD thesis on strong-field gravitational lensing by black holes \[188\] casts the same conclusion as a formal statement:

> *“For null geodesics, there is no invariant notion of proper time or proper length: a null geodesic can be said to have zero proper time and proper length.”* — Shipley 2019, arXiv:1909.04691.

Kajari, Buser, Feiler, and Schleich’s 2009 lecture notes on rotation in relativity and the propagation of light \[189\] spell out why one falls back on an affine parameter:

> *“Light… evolves on lightlike curves x\^μ(λ), also called ‘null curves’, corresponding to the line element ds² = 0. Therefore, it is not possible to define a proper time for light in the same way as for massive particles. Instead, we consider the evolution parameter λ just as a label for the spacetime point of the light ray with no deeper physical meaning.”* — Kajari, Buser, Feiler, Schleich 2009, arXiv:0905.0765.

Asgari and Saffari’s 2021 paper on spacetime expansion in the presence of a background velocity field \[190\] states it briefly:

> *“A null geodesic is a path taken by a massless particle like a photon. It is named null since its interval is equal to zero, ds² = 0, and it does not have a proper time connected with it.”* — Asgari and Saffari 2021, arXiv:2111.09647.

Four independent recent publications, converging on the same rigorous verdict: the photon does not have a well-defined four-velocity, its proper time is not defined, its “velocity through x₄” is *not a physical quantity in the orthodox post-MTW framework*. This is the modern orthodoxy of the rigorous graduate-level literature. The graduate-student consensus, as visible on Physics Forums and equivalent venues, matches this rigorous orthodoxy verbatim.

The specific 1973 objection that killed the x₄ = ict convention — that the imaginary coordinate cannot extend to curved spacetime — dissolves under the dynamical reading of the McGucken Principle. dx₄/dt = ic is not a global coordinate identity claiming that one spacetime axis is intrinsically imaginary and the other three are intrinsically real. It is a pointwise scalar equation at every event of the McGucken Space 𝓜_G, stating the rate of expansion of the x₄-direction from that event. The scalar equation transports trivially to curved spacetime as a statement about the rest frame at each spacetime point, because the “rest frame” is a *local* geometric object defined pointwise at each event of the Lorentzian manifold, and Lemma 2.0 of the present paper establishes that at every spacetime point of any Lorentzian manifold (M, g) satisfying Einstein’s equations, the rest-frame statement of the four-velocity normalization u\^μ u_μ = -c² is the pointwise statement dx₄/dt = ic. Misner-Thorne-Wheeler’s global-chart-oriented objection to the imaginary-coordinate convention does not apply to the pointwise scalar reading. The dynamical form of dx₄/dt = ic thus recovers the pre-1973 clarity of Q3’s answer while satisfying MTW’s own extensibility requirement to curved spacetime — the objection MTW raised in 1973 is answered by the promotion of the coordinate identity to a pointwise dynamical statement, which the 1973 apparatus did not consider.

Under dx₄/dt = ic read as a pointwise dynamical principle rather than as a static coordinate identity, the triad Q1, Q2, Q3 admits mutually consistent answers:

-   **Q1** — photon velocity through x₁, x₂, x₃: c. Same as every physicist agrees.
-   **Q2** — photon velocity through spacetime: the four-velocity budget satisfies u\^μ u_μ = (ic)² + c² = -c² + c² = 0, the null-vector condition falling out algebraically from the McGucken Principle’s imaginary factor. Camp A’s “moves at c through spacetime” reading and Camp C’s “null-vector budget of zero” reading become the *same statement* under i² = -1; the standard incompatibility between the pedagogical and formal readings dissolves as a notation artifact of the abandoned imaginary-coordinate convention.
-   **Q3** — photon share in x₄: the Sphere-tangent share vanishes, $v_{x_4} = 0$ *for the photon*, since the photon rides the wavefront rather than advancing across it, while dx₄/dt = ic is the *rate of the wavefront’s advance* that the massive particle at spatial rest fully rides. The photon’s coordinate is stationary in x₄; the wavefront itself is expanding at ic; the photon rides the leading edge and does not advance beyond it. This is neither zero-because-undefined (which contradicts the well-defined post-MTW answer (ii)), nor zero-because-time-freezes (which conflates coordinate rate and proper-time rate), but zero-because-the-wavefront-is-the-null-cone-and-the-photon-rides-it — a definite geometric fact that follows from the four-fold ontology of §2.4 (massive particle at spatial rest = full budget into +ic; photon at v = c = rides the null cone with vanishing share $v_{x_4} = 0$ (the Principle dx₄/dt = ic still holding); absolute motion = x₄’s active expansion at ic from every event; CMB frame = isotropic cosmological x₄-expansion). The massive particle at spatial rest, in the same framework, has dx₄/dt = ic at every point of its worldline; the moving massive particle apportions its budget between spatial motion and x₄-advance via the Lorentz-invariant rapidity content (Theorem 2.4.5 of the present paper); all cases are pointwise well-defined without appeal to proper-time parametrization.

The pedagogical instability of the orthodox treatment of Q3 — Wheeler-pedagogical answer of zero versus post-MTW rigorous answer of undefined — is a symptom of a specific historical event: the 1973 abandonment of the dynamical form of the x₄-coordinate. Before 1973, the answer was clean; after 1973, physicists reached for the poetic (“we soar through spacetime” in Wheeler-Taylor 1966 \[191\]; “moves at c through spacetime” in Greene 1999; the space-proper-time diagrams of Lewis Carroll Epstein’s *Relativity Visualized* of 1981) or for the technical dodge (“the concept is not defined for photons; use an affine parameter” in Wald, Carroll, MTW) because the dynamical statement of what x₄ is *doing* had been abandoned as a static coordinate identity. The century-long inability of orthodox physics to answer Q3 with a single clean geometric statement is the direct trace of a specific pedagogical decision taken in 1973 and never reversed.

The predicament can be named directly, in the Platonic image whose force Wheeler himself understood and honored throughout his career. Physicists chained in the coordinate-label reading of x₄ inherited from post-MTW pedagogy mistook the coordinate shadows on the wall of the cave for the substance of physics. They feared to turn their heads toward the fire, and above all they feared to venture out to the light beyond the cave. They feared to look into the light — to look the photon in the eye — and to ask what the photon, the very object made of light, was doing relative to the fourth dimension. The question *“what is a photon doing relative to x₄?”* was the question that would have unchained them, and it was the question they most consistently declined to answer. The dodges — proper-time-freezes, four-velocity-undefined, use-an-affine-parameter, block-universe-eternal, coordinate-slope-trivial — are the shadow-play by which the chained physicists explained to themselves why the question could not be answered, while the light that would have answered it played unwatched beyond the cave.

*dx₄/dt = ic is the light beyond the cave.* It is the generator of the McGucken Space 𝓜_G, the source space from which all other geometric structures descend. Minkowski spacetime 𝕄\_{1,3} and Hilbert space 𝓗 are the shadows dancing on the walls of the cave — cascade-level projections of 𝓜_G, the second and fourth cascade levels of the source (Theorem 10.6 of the present paper establishes explicitly that Hilbert space and Minkowski space are *one geometric object at two cascade levels*, both descending from 𝓜_G, each containing dx₄/dt = ic pointwise at every point). The coordinate identities that orthodox physics has taken as the substance of relativity and quantum mechanics — the Lorentzian metric η_μν, the wavefunction ψ, the four-velocity u\^μ, the Born density \|ψ\|² — are shadows of the dynamical expansion of x₄ that is generating them all. To ask *“what is a photon doing relative to x₄?”* and to insist on a definite kinematic answer is to unchain oneself from the coordinate-label reading; to answer *“the photon’s Sphere-tangent share is $v_{x_4} = 0$ at every event, because the photon rides the wavefront that is expanding at dx₄/dt = ic from every event of 𝓜_G, and the massive particle at spatial rest has dx₄/dt = ic because it advances with the wavefront”* is to leave the cave entirely, walk out into the light, and see the source that has been casting the shadows all along.

The photon — the object physicists have most feared to look at directly — is the object that most sharply exposes the shadow-character of the coordinate reading of x₄. Q1 is answered universally because x₁, x₂, x₃ are dynamical dimensions in orthodox physics: things move through them, and the pedagogical apparatus knows how to describe that motion. Q3 fractures orthodox pedagogy because x₄ was demoted to a coordinate label in 1973 and has not been restored. The McGucken Principle restores it. Under dx₄/dt = ic, the fourth dimension is once again the sort of thing photons and massive particles have well-defined kinematic relationships with; the century-long predicament of Q3 dissolves; the dodges are recognized as coordinate-label shadow-play; the geometric substance of x₄ is named for what it is — an expanding dimension carrying the wavefront that generates all downstream structure of physics.

The present paper’s project is to unchain the century, to look the photon in the eye, and to name the light beyond the cave that has been generating the shadows all along. The Wheeler pedagogical instinct that spacetime is soared through, not merely inhabited, was correct; what was missing was the scalar-equation statement of what the soaring is a *rate of*. The scalar-equation statement is dx₄/dt = ic, the light beyond the cave.

### 1.8 The six Wightman axioms of relativistic quantum field theory (W1 Hilbert space, W2 Poincaré covariance, W3 microcausality, W4 field-operator distributions, W5 unique Poincaré-invariant vacuum, W6 Spectrum Condition) as forced theorems of dx₄/dt = ic, and the sixty-eight-year-unexplained W6 (Wightman 1956 through 2026) supplied by the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework

The six Wightman axioms of relativistic quantum field theory — first laid down by Arthur Wightman in 1956 and codified in Streater-Wightman 1964 *PCT, Spin and Statistics, and All That* — have served as the canonical foundational system for axiomatic quantum field theory for seventy years (1956–2026). They are:

-   **W1** — the system’s states form a separable complex Hilbert space, i.e. **the Hilbert space** $\mathcal{H}$ of relativistic QFT.
-   **W2** — the Poincaré group $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$ acts unitarily on Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ via a strongly continuous representation $U(a, \Lambda)$, i.e. **Poincaré covariance**.
-   **W3** — field operators at spacelike-separated points of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ commute for bosonic statistics or anticommute for fermionic statistics, i.e. **microcausality**, also called **locality** or **local commutativity**.
-   **W4** — the field operators $\hat{\phi}(x)$ are operator-valued distributions on a dense domain $\mathcal{D} \subset$ Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$, smeared against Schwartz test functions on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, i.e. **operator-valued distributions on a dense domain**.

-   **W6** — the joint spectrum of the energy-momentum operators $P^\mu$ is contained in the closed forward light cone $\overline{V_+}$ in momentum space, i.e. **the Spectrum Condition** (positive-energy support).

### 2.0 The McGucken Principle and the Lorentzian Metric: cogeneration architecture and equivalence in both directions

*The QM-cogeneration cascade isolates with the Lorentzian metric as the empirically established entry point.* Starting from the Lorentzian metric — empirically validated since 1905 by every accelerator experiment, every GPS timing correction, every Michelson–Morley test, every muon-decay measurement, every Hafele–Keating clock comparison, and accepted by every physicist — the Hilbert space, the Born rule, the canonical commutation relation, the uncertainty principle, and the Schrödinger equation all follow as forced theorems. The Minkowski line element in the (−, +, +, +) signature is

$ds² = −c² dt² + dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃²,$

equivalently ds² = η_μν dx\^μ dx\^ν with η = diag(−1, +1, +1, +1) and the convention x⁰ = ct. The metric is the empirically established geometric setting that mainstream physics accepts; in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, it is a forced consequence of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic (Lemma 2.5).

The McGucken framework relates the McGucken Principle and the metric through two complementary statements:

-   *Foundational direction (Lemma 2.5, principle → metric):* dx₄/dt = ic integrates to x₄ = ict; squaring gives (ic)² = −c² and dx₄² = −c²dt²; substitution into the four-dimensional Euclidean line element ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄² yields the Lorentzian metric ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c²dt² with signature (−, +, +, +). The Lorentzian metric is therefore derived; the McGucken Principle is foundational.

-   *Reverse-reading equivalence (Lemma 2.0 below, metric → principle):* given the Lorentzian metric as established physics, the rest-frame four-velocity normalization u\^μu_μ = −c² for any massive particle reads off, when the temporal direction is expressed in Minkowski’s 1908 coordinate x₄ = ict, as dx₄/dτ = ic in the rest frame. This is the reverse-reading direction, allowing mainstream physicists to enter the dx₄/dt = ic framework from territory they already accept.

The two directions together establish that dx₄/dt = ic and the rest-frame Lorentzian four-velocity normalization are mathematically equivalent statements: the McGucken Principle is the foundational physics, and the Lorentzian metric is its empirically anchored integrated form. The QM derivations downstream of the Lorentzian metric apply identically under either reading.

**Lemma 2.0 (Reverse-reading equivalence: the rest-frame Lorentzian four-velocity normalization expressed in the x₄ = ict coordinate equals dx₄/dt = ic).** *Let Minkowski space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ be Minkowski spacetime equipped with the Lorentzian metric ds² = −c²dt² + dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃², regarded for the purposes of this Lemma as the given empirical starting point of special relativity (the foundational direction principle → metric is established in Lemma 2.5 below). For any massive particle at any point p ∈ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, the rest-frame four-velocity normalization u\^μu_μ = −c², expressed in the Minkowski coordinate x₄ = ict, reads*

$dx_4/d\tau = ic \quad (\text{rest frame, } d\tau = dt),$

*which is the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. Equivalently: the rest-frame Lorentzian four-velocity normalization and the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic are the same statement, with x₄ = ict the integrated form of the McGucken Principle (Lemma 2.5) and equivalently the Minkowski 1908 coordinate for the temporal direction.*

*Proof.* By the standard relativistic definition of proper time for a massive particle, the proper time τ along the particle’s worldline is defined by ds² = −c²dτ² along the worldline (dτ ≥ 0 the line element along the worldline divided by c, with τ increasing in the forward time direction). Substituting the Minkowski line element ds² = −c²dt² + dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² along the worldline and dividing through by dt² yields the four-velocity normalization

$-c²(dτ/dt)² = -c² + ∑_{i=1}^{3}(dx_i/dt)²,$

equivalently u\^μu_μ = −c² for the four-velocity u\^μ := dx\^μ/dτ. The physics of this normalization is that every massive particle’s four-velocity has invariant magnitude c, partitioned between the temporal component u⁰ = dx⁰/dτ (where x⁰ := ct) and the spatial components u\^i = dx\^i/dτ.

In the rest frame of the particle at p, the spatial coordinate velocities vanish: dx_i/dt = 0 for i = 1, 2, 3. The normalization collapses to (dτ/dt)² = 1; taking the positive root since proper time advances forward along the worldline (dτ \> 0 with t increasing), dτ/dt = +1. The four-velocity in the rest frame has its full magnitude c carried by the temporal component: u⁰ = c.

Now express the temporal direction in Minkowski’s 1908 complex coordinate x₄ := ict. *In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, x₄ = ict is the integrated form of the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic, obtained by integrating with the anchor x₄(t=0) = 0 (Principle 2.1; Lemma 2.5 establishes the foundational direction). In the present Lemma — which establishes the reverse-reading equivalence — x₄ = ict is taken as Minkowski’s coordinate substitution applied to the temporal direction, and the Lemma’s content is that this substitution makes the rest-frame Lorentzian four-velocity normalization read as dx₄/dτ = ic.* The temporal four-velocity expressed in the x₄ coordinate is

$\frac{dx_4}{d\tau} = \frac{d(ict)}{d\tau} = ic \cdot \frac{dt}{d\tau} = ic \cdot 1 = ic \quad (\text{rest frame}),$

using dt/dτ = 1 established in the rest frame above. Since dt = dτ in the rest frame, this is equivalently dx₄/dt = ic.

The Lemma’s content is therefore not that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is derived from the Lorentzian metric (the foundational direction is principle → metric, established in Lemma 2.5), but that the McGucken Principle and the rest-frame Lorentzian four-velocity normalization — when the temporal direction is expressed in the Minkowski coordinate x₄ = ict — are the *same statement*. In an arbitrary frame F’ with time coordinate t’ and fourth coordinate x₄’ := ict’, the same construction applies: the rest-frame four-velocity normalization for any massive particle at any event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (in the rest frame of that particle, the frame-invariant Lorentz-covariant statement) reads dx₄/dτ = ic at every event. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is therefore the rest-frame content of the Lorentzian four-velocity normalization at every point of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, equivalently the differential form of x₄ = ict. ∎

The Lemma establishes the equivalence in the reverse-reading direction: dx₄/dt = ic and the rest-frame Lorentzian four-velocity normalization are the same statement, with x₄ = ict the integrated form of the McGucken Principle and equivalently the Minkowski 1908 coordinate for the temporal direction. *The foundational direction is the opposite one:* the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic generates the Lorentzian metric via integration and squaring (Lemma 2.5 below), and across the McGucken corpus the same principle cogenerates general relativity (\[54–57\]) and the entire QM cascade developed in this paper. The reverse-reading equivalence (Lemma 2.0) allows the present paper to be entered from the Lorentzian-metric side — the empirically established starting point that every physicist accepts; the foundational direction (Lemma 2.5) establishes that the metric is itself a consequence of the McGucken Principle, with both QM and GR as sibling outputs of dx₄/dt = ic cogenerated through the metric as their first shared downstream waypoint.

The orthodox Lorentzian treatment writes x₄ = ict as a formal coordinate device — a notational trick that gives the Lorentzian signature by making the metric look Euclidean under the substitution. In orthodoxy, x₄ is not a physical direction; the four-velocity normalization u\^μ u_μ = −c² is kinematic bookkeeping for how proper time relates to coordinate time across frames. dx₄/dt = ic asserts the opposite ontology: x₄ is a *physical, geometric, nonlocal direction* — the radius of a spherical wavefront expanding from every spacetime event at velocity c, with the imaginary unit i marking geometric perpendicularity to the spatial slice (not imaginary unreality). ### 2.2 The two dimensional parameters of the McGucken Principle’s expansion: c as its rate, ℏ as its action per Planck-frequency oscillation — both properties of one geometric flow

**Proposition 2.2 (The two dimensional parameters of the x₄-expansion).** *The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic has two natural dimensional parameters, and both fundamental constants of quantum mechanics — c and ℏ — are wired into the framework as these two parameters of the one expansion. ### 2.2.bis The substrate-tick invariants of dx₄/dt = ic: $\Delta t_C = 2\pi\hbar/(mc^2)$, $\Delta x_4 = i\lambda_C$, $\Delta S = h$, and the Lorentz-invariance of $\hbar$ as the Lorentz-invariance of $c$ expressed at the Compton substrate-tick scale

Section 2.2 established $c$ and $\hbar$ as twin dimensional parameters of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic: $c$ is the rate of $x_4$-advance perpendicular to the spatial slice, $\hbar$ is the action carried per Planck-frequency oscillation of that advance. The twin-parameter framing leaves one fact implicit: at what scale does $\hbar$ enter as an invariant, and how is the invariance of $\hbar$ related to the invariance of $c$? This subsection makes both explicit with exact identifications at the Compton substrate-tick scale of the wavefront expansion.

**Definition 2.2.bis.1 (Compton substrate tick).** *At every event $p \in$ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and every massive particle of rest mass $m$ at $p$, the Compton substrate tick is the period $\Delta t_C = 2\pi/\omega_C$ where $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is the Compton angular frequency of the particle. Explicitly,*
$$\Delta t_C = \frac{2\pi\hbar}{mc^2}.$$

**Proposition 2.2.bis.1 (Three exact substrate-tick identifications).** *During one Compton substrate tick of a massive particle of rest mass $m$ at event $p \in$ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, the following three quantities are given exactly:*

*(i) The fourth-dimensional advance:*
$$\Delta x_4 = ic \cdot \Delta t_C = i\lambda_C, \quad \text{where } \lambda_C = \frac{h}{mc} \text{ is the Compton wavelength.}$$

*(ii) The action accumulation:*
$$\Delta S = E \cdot \Delta t_C = mc^2 \cdot \frac{2\pi\hbar}{mc^2} = 2\pi\hbar = h.$$

*(iii) The oscillation phase advance:*
$$\omega_C \cdot \Delta t_C = \frac{mc^2}{\hbar} \cdot \frac{2\pi\hbar}{mc^2} = 2\pi \quad \text{(one full cycle)}.$$

*Proof.* Direct calculation from Definition 2.2.bis.1:

*(i)* $\Delta x_4 = ic \cdot \Delta t_C = ic \cdot \frac{2\pi\hbar}{mc^2} = \frac{2\pi i\hbar}{mc} = i \cdot \frac{h}{mc} = i\lambda_C$.

*(ii)* $\Delta S = E \cdot \Delta t_C = mc^2 \cdot \frac{2\pi\hbar}{mc^2}$; the $mc^2$ factors cancel exactly, leaving $\Delta S = 2\pi\hbar = h$.

The cancellation is exact — not approximate, not up to numerical factors of order unity, not up to logarithms — the two $mc^2$ factors are algebraically identical and cancel to give $\Delta S = h$ independent of $m$. $\blacksquare$

**Theorem 2.2.bis.1 (Lorentz-invariance of $\hbar$ as Lorentz-invariance of $c$ at the substrate scale).** *The Lorentz-invariance of Planck’s constant $\hbar$ across all inertial frames and all massive quantum systems is the same physical fact as the Lorentz-invariance of the speed of light $c$ across all inertial frames, expressed at the Compton substrate-tick scale of the dx₄/dt = ic wavefront expansion. #### 2.4.4 The McGucken Sphere and the light-sphere tradition: covariance, the Einstein–Poincaré dispute, and absolute rest and absolute motion without a detectable frame

The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ stands in the line of the light sphere that Einstein introduced in 1905, and its exact relation to that tradition sharpens both what the framework preserves and what it adds.

*The light-sphere tradition (Einstein 1905, Poincaré’s ellipsoid, Minkowski’s cone).* Einstein’s 1905 relativity paper introduced the form-invariance of the equation of a light sphere: the wavefront $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = c^2 t^2$ emitted from an event keeps the same form $x'^2 + y'^2 + z'^2 = c^2 t'^2$ under a Lorentz transformation, so that the light sphere remains a light sphere expanding at the one speed $c$ for every inertial observer \[Walter 2018\]. Historically this form-invariance was first used to derive the Lorentz transformation in 1907 and became the cornerstone of Einstein’s relativity by 1911. Poincaré promoted a rival figure, the light *ellipsoid*: for an observer in motion relative to the source, he held, the emitted spheres appear as elongated ellipsoids on account of the contraction, with the undistorted sphere reserved for the ether rest frame \[Walter 2018\]. Minkowski then recast Einstein’s light sphere geometrically, the one-parameter family of expanding fronts over all emission events forming the light cone of spacetime.

*The Sphere is covariant, and the family is invariant — stated precisely.* The McGucken Sphere is this light sphere, reinterpreted ontologically: not the locus a light signal has reached, but the geometric expression of the $x_4$-expansion at $c$ from the event (§2.3), with light tracing the Sphere because both are that one expansion. The exact transformation property must be stated with care. An *individual* McGucken Sphere is Lorentz *covariant* (form-invariant): under a boost it maps to another McGucken Sphere of the same form, and every inertial observer agrees the wavefront is a sphere expanding at $c$. It is not Lorentz *invariant* in the sense of being the numerically identical instantaneous 2-surface for all observers — different observers slice the expansion on different simultaneity surfaces and read different instantaneous radii, which is Poincaré’s ellipsoid recovered as the frame-dependent spatial *projection* of §10.12bis. What is Lorentz *invariant* is the *family* of McGucken Spheres — the null cone they envelope — and the interval $ds^2 = 0$ the wavefront satisfies. The framework thus supports the tradition exactly (Einstein’s form-invariance holds, and the cone is recovered as the envelope) and moves beyond it: sphericity is not postulated (Einstein) nor treated as an ether-frame truth distorted into an ellipsoid elsewhere (Poincaré), but derived from the isotropy of the $x_4$-expansion, so the wavefront is spherical at every event because the expansion is isotropic at every event. Einstein’s instinct that the sphere stays a sphere for all observers, which distinguished his account from Lorentz’s dynamical contraction and from Poincaré’s ellipsoid with its retained ether frame, is here vindicated with a mechanism: the isotropic $x_4$-expansion is why the light sphere is universally spherical, and Poincaré’s ellipsoid is exactly the projection an observer reads on a boosted slice.

*Absolute rest and absolute motion, without a detectable frame.* The four-fold ontology (§2.4) carries a structure that at first appears to contradict special relativity and, on inspection, is what makes the framework’s compatibility with it precise. The three spatial dimensions $x_1, x_2, x_3$ are the seat of **absolute rest**: they do not themselves advance, but are stationary and stretchable in response to mass-energy (configuration 1 of §2.4). The fourth dimension is the seat of **absolute motion**: it expands at $ic$ from every event, independent of any single worldline (configuration 3). There is, therefore, an absolute rest structure (the spatial three) and an absolute motion structure (the $x_4$-advance), and there is a distinguished foliation — the cosmic-comoving frame, operationally the CMB rest frame (configuration 4) — on which the expansion proceeds isotropically. This does not conflict with the relativity of inertial frames, for a definite reason: **absolute velocity is not detectable from within any inertial frame**. The reason is the mutual dependence of the instruments of measurement. Every clock is calibrated by light — a rate of $x_4$-advance read against the expansion at $c$ — and every ruler is calibrated by a clock and the speed of light (the metre is defined as the distance light travels in a fixed fraction of a second). Rulers rest on clocks and clocks rest on rulers, and both rest on $c$, which is the rate of the very expansion whose absolute motion one would attempt to detect. An apparatus built entirely from $c$ cannot measure its own velocity against the structure that defines $c$: the measuring rods and the measuring clocks co-adjust under a boost in exactly the proportion that cancels any read-off of absolute velocity. The absolute rest of the spatial three and the absolute motion of the fourth are real geometric facts of the framework, and they are jointly *cloaked* from local metrology (the Dual-Cloaking Theorem 6.6.8.2): local rulers and clocks report the same physics in every inertial frame, so the distinguished foliation on which the expansion rides is not locally detectable. This is the same conclusion Einstein reached by eliminating the ether, reached here by a different route — the ether frame is replaced by a real but cloaked cosmological foliation, and the impossibility of detecting absolute velocity follows from the fact that the dance of the stationary spatial rulers and the expanding $x_4$-clocks is built entirely from the one invariant rate $c$.
\### 2.4.5 The two postulates of special relativity as theorems descending from dx₄/dt = ic

Einstein’s 1905 special relativity is built on two foundational postulates: the *principle of relativity* (the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames) and the *constancy of the speed of light* (c is the same in all inertial frames). In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework both postulates are theorems — derived consequences of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic — not independent foundational inputs.

**Theorem 2.4.5 (Both postulates of special relativity descend from the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic).** *Let* (P1) *denote the principle of relativity (the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames) and let* (P2) *denote the constancy of the speed of light (c has the same value in all inertial frames). Both (P1) and (P2) are forced theorems of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, with (P1) descending from the universality clause of Principle 2.1 (the McGucken Principle holds at every event identically) and (P2) descending from the rate clause of Proposition 2.2(i) (\|dx₄/dt\| = c is the same scalar at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$).*

**Proof of (P1) — Principle of relativity from universality of the McGucken Principle.**

By Principle 2.1, the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic holds at every spacetime event identically. The rate ic is the same scalar at every event; the direction of x₄-advance is perpendicular to x₁x₂x₃ at every event; the action quantization (Proposition 2.2(ii)) is the same ℏ at every event. There is no privileged event; the McGucken Principle is invariant under translation across events of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (the translation symmetry used in Theorem 5.1 to derive the canonical commutator).

The Minkowski metric ds² = −c²dt² + dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² is the integrated coordinate expression of dx₄/dt = ic (Lemma 2.5: (ict)² = −c²t²). The Lorentz transformations are the linear coordinate transformations preserving this metric, equivalently the linear transformations preserving the constraint surface where dx₄/dt = ic holds. Under any Lorentz transformation, the McGucken Principle takes the same form in the transformed frame: the rate of x₄-advance is still \|ic\| = c, the perpendicularity of x₄ to the new spatial axes is preserved (Lorentz transformations preserve the (−,+,+,+) signature), and the action quantization is unchanged. Every law derived from the McGucken Principle — the Hilbert space (Theorem 6.1), the canonical commutator (Theorem 5.1), the Born rule (Theorem 7.2), the uncertainty principle (Theorem 8.2), the Schrödinger equation (Theorem 9.1), and the corresponding general-relativistic theorems of \[54–57\] — therefore takes the same form in every inertial frame.

The principle of relativity (P1) is the statement that the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames. Since every law of physics derived in the McGucken framework descends from dx₄/dt = ic, and dx₄/dt = ic takes the same form in every inertial frame, the laws are the same in every inertial frame. (P1) follows.

The content: (P1) is the universality clause of the McGucken Principle expressed at the level of derived laws. The McGucken Principle is universal across events of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, hence laws derived from it are universal across inertial frames at Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. ∎

**Proof of (P2) — Constancy of c from the rate clause of the McGucken Principle.**

By Proposition 2.2(i), the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic has \|dx₄/dt\| = c, with c the modulus of the rate ic. By the universality clause of Principle 2.1, this rate is the same scalar at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$: c is a frame-independent constant of the McGucken Principle’s geometric flow, not an empirical rate that happens to coincide across frames.

The photon configuration of the four-fold ontology (§2.4 configuration 2) has vanishing Sphere-tangent share $v_{x_4} = 0$ along the photon’s null worldline (Principle dx₄/dt = ic holding), with the four-velocity budget u\^μ u_μ = −c² (§2.3) forcing the spatial speed to saturate at v_spatial = c. By Lemma 2.5, the null cone of the Minkowski metric has slope c at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, with null worldlines being the locus of u\^μ u_μ = 0 = (dx_spatial/dt)² − c²(dt/dt)², equivalently dx_spatial/dt = c. The photon’s worldline lies on this null cone, hence the photon’s spatial speed is c at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$.

Under any Lorentz transformation, the null cone is preserved as a geometric object (Lorentz transformations preserve the metric, hence preserve the locus where ds² = 0). The slope c of the null cone is therefore the same in every inertial frame. The photon’s spatial speed — read off the null worldline as the slope of the null cone — is therefore c in every inertial frame.

### 2.6 Theorem 2.4: space-operator cogeneration — the McGucken Principle simultaneously generates the source-space 𝓜_G (geometric setup) and the McGucken operator 𝓕_p = ∂*t + ic·∂*{x₄}\|\_p (dynamical content)

The architectural foundation of the McGucken framework is that dx₄/dt = ic is *simultaneously* a statement about a coordinate (x₄ expanding at rate ic) and a statement about an operator (D_M = ∂\_t + ic ∂\_x₄, the differential expression of the same statement). Asserting the McGucken Principle asserts both.

**Theorem 2.4 (Space-Operator Cogeneration).** *The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic generates simultaneously the source-space*

𝓜_G = (E₄, Φ_M, D_M, Σ_M)

*and the source operator D_M from the same primitive law. Specifically, dx₄/dt = ic asserts*

(i) *the ambient four-dimensional space E₄ in which x₄ is a coordinate;*

(ii) *the constraint Φ_M = x₄ - ict whose vanishing locus is the physical sector;*

(iii) \*the source operator D_M = ∂\_t + ic ∂\_x₄, the differential expression of the McGucken Principle;\*

(iv) *the McGucken measure Σ_M on the constraint surface, inherited from the Lebesgue measure on x₁x₂x₃ and the proper-time measure on t-slices.*

*All four components of 𝓜_G descend from the single principle.*

*Proof.* The proof separates into two parts: **constructive existence** (parts (i)–(iv) of the statement, derived directly from dx₄/dt = ic within the present paper), and **uniqueness** (the cogeneration claim that 𝓜_G is the unique four-tuple forced by the Principle, depending on the Reciprocal Generation and Containment-Generation theorems of the McGucken Category McG paper \[186\] and the Reciprocal-Generation / Huygens-Principle paper \[185\], not derived in-session in the present paper).

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic involves the coordinates t and x₄ as independent variables; these are coordinates on the ambient carrier E₄ := ℝ³ × ℂ (with the ℂ-component carrying $x_4$ as an algebraic-perpendicularity-marked coordinate per Theorem 4.6.1; equivalently E₄ is the real four-manifold $\mathbb{R}^4$ with the fourth axis algebraically marked by $i$). Part (i) is therefore the natural setting for the Principle. The integrated form $x_4 = ict$ is established by direct integration of $dx_4/dt = ic$ from the source-event convention $x_4(t_E) = 0$ (Lemma 2.5 of §2.7 below):

$$x_4(t) = x_4(t_E) + \int_{t_E}^t ic \, dt' = ic(t - t_E),$$

and after fixing the origin via $t_E = 0$ this is $x_4 = ict$. The constraint function $\Phi_M(t, x_4) := x_4 - ict$ has vanishing locus $\Phi_M^{-1}(0) = \mathcal{C}_M$ — the physical sector where the integrated McGucken Principle holds. Part (ii) is established by direct construction.

For part (iii) (the source operator $D_M = \partial_t + ic \, \partial_{x_4}$), the chain-rule total-derivative identity along any smooth curve $\gamma(t) = (t, x_4(t))$ satisfying $dx_4/dt = ic$ gives, for any differentiable function $\Psi(t, x_4)$,

$$\frac{d}{dt}\bigg|_\gamma \Psi(t, x_4(t)) = \frac{\partial \Psi}{\partial t} + \frac{dx_4}{dt} \cdot \frac{\partial \Psi}{\partial x_4} = \frac{\partial \Psi}{\partial t} + ic \cdot \frac{\partial \Psi}{\partial x_4} = D_M \Psi.$$

This is the v40-internal **Generator Equivalence**: the McGucken Principle as a curve-condition $dx_4/dt = ic$ and the McGucken Operator $D_M$ as a differential operator are two presentations of the same content — the curve-condition gives the integral curves of $D_M$, and $D_M$ acting on functions yields the chain-rule total derivative along those curves. The argument runs by direct computation and requires nothing beyond standard multivariable calculus.

The tangency of $D_M$ to $\mathcal{C}_M$ is direct: $D_M \Phi_M = \partial_t (x_4 - ict) + ic \, \partial_{x_4}(x_4 - ict) = -ic + ic \cdot 1 = 0$. Hence $D_M$ is tangent to the constraint surface everywhere on $\mathcal{C}_M$.

The characteristic-invariance property — that functions $\Psi$ satisfying $D_M \Psi = 0$ depend on $(t, x_4)$ only through the first integral $u := x_4 - ict$ — is a standard fact of first-order linear PDE theory: $D_M$ is a first-order linear operator with constant coefficients on $\mathbb{R}^2 \times \mathbb{C}$, and its kernel consists exactly of functions of the conserved quantity along characteristics, which here is $u = x_4 - ict$ (the characteristic curves are precisely the curves $x_4 - ict = \mathrm{const}$). ## 3. The complex character of amplitudes: Theorem 3.1 — the McGucken wavefunction ψ is intrinsically complex-valued, with phase generated by the factor i appearing in the integrated form x₄ = ict descended from dx₄/dt = ic

The first forced theorem of dx₄/dt = ic is the complex character of the wavefunction. This is the substrate on which every subsequent derivation rests.

**Theorem 3.1 (Complex amplitudes from dx₄/dt = ic).** *Let ψ be the McGucken wavefunction of Definition 2.6 constructed under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. Then ψ is intrinsically complex-valued, with phase generated by the factor i that appears in the integrated form x₄ = ict (descended from dx₄/dt = ic by integration).*

*Proof.* The proof has two parts. **Part 1 (Kinematic).** The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic integrates to x₄ = ict (Lemma 5 of \[30\]; integration anchored at x₄ = 0 when t = 0). The factor i in the integrated form is the algebraic signature of the geometric fact that x₄ is perpendicular to the spatial three-axes x₁x₂x₃: multiplication by i is the canonical representation of a quarter-rotation in the complex plane, and it encodes here the orthogonality of the fourth axis to ordinary space. The Minkowski signature of the constraint surface is the algebraic shadow of this perpendicularity, (ict)² = −c² t² (Lemma 2.5), and the minus sign in ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² - c² dt² records orthogonality, not unreality.

Consider an event E from which the McGucken expansion proceeds. A spatial point x ∈ ℝ³ at parameter time t = \|x\|/c lies on the McGucken Sphere 𝓜_E(t). The four-displacement from E to this point has spatial component x (magnitude ct) and x₄-component Δ x₄ = ict. The four-displacement vector is

$Δ X = (x, ict), ‖Δ X‖² = |x|² + (ict)² = c² t² - c² t² = 0,$

confirming the null character of the McGucken Sphere. *The x₄-component of every displacement to a point on the wavefront is purely imaginary.* This is the kinematic fact from which the complex character of ψ descends: any spatial-slice projection σ: ℝ³ → 𝓜_E(t) of an x₄-propagating excitation must record both the in-slice content (real part) and the perpendicular-to-slice content (imaginary part). The wavefunction $\psi(\mathbf{x}, t)$ is therefore a ℂ-valued field with a real and an imaginary part forced by the kinematic structure of the McGucken Sphere. The selection of ℂ specifically — rather than ℝ² as an unstructured direct sum, or ℍ as the next associative real division algebra — is forced by the Frobenius theorem on associative real division algebras (1877): one perpendicular axis x₄ yields exactly one independent imaginary unit i, uniquely selecting ℂ from the Frobenius candidates {ℝ, ℂ, ℍ} (zero / one / three perpendicular axes). The Frobenius selection is developed in §4.1 (the algebra of perpendicularity) and applied formally in the construction of Theorem 6.1 (Hilbert space).

The kinematic complex character of Part 1 establishes that ψ takes values in ℂ but does not yet determine the *form* of the phase. The dynamical content comes from the action-quantization clause of the Principle (Proposition 2.2, clause ii): the x₄-advance carries one quantum of action ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation, its wavelength setting h. We translate this into the phase carried by an arbitrary path from E to a point on the null wavefront 𝓜_E(t).

Let γ be a path from E to B, where B ∈ 𝓜_E(t) lies on the null wavefront of the x₄-expansion from E (the McGucken Sphere of Definition 2.3), with proper time Δ τ_γ elapsed along γ. By Proposition 2.3 of \[54\] (proper time as x₄-arc-length), the accumulated x₄-displacement along γ has modulus \|Δ x₄\|\_γ = c Δ τ_γ. The action carried by the propagating excitation along γ is, in the standard relativistic form,

$S[γ] = -mc² Δ τ_γ$

for a massive excitation of mass m (or the analogous Planck-quantum expression for a photon; the absolute magnitude \|S\[γ\]\| enters the phase). Because the x₄-advance carries one quantum of action ℏ per oscillation, each unit of action ℏ corresponds to one *radian* of phase rotation in the complex plane spanned by (real spatial component, imaginary x₄-component); a full 2π rotation of phase corresponds to action h = 2πℏ, the standard relation between the reduced Planck constant ℏ and Planck’s constant h. The phase rotation accumulated along γ is therefore S\[γ\]/ℏ radians, and the phase contributed by this rotation is:

$phase[γ] = exp \left((i S[γ])/(ℏ)\right).$

The factor i in the exponent is the *same* perpendicularity marker that appears in x₄ = ict: each oscillation is a quarter-rotation in the (spatial, x₄) plane four times around, with the imaginary unit recording the perpendicular direction of advance. The factor ℏ in the denominator is the action-quantization scale of Proposition 2.2.

The McGucken wavefunction is the sum over all paths from E to B ∈ 𝓜_E(t) (B on the null wavefront) of these phase contributions (Definition 2.6):

$ψ(B) = ∑_γ : E → B exp \left((i S[γ])/(ℏ)\right) ∈ ℂ.$

Both the perpendicularity of x₄ (Part 1) and its action-per-oscillation (Part 2) are required for the full complex-amplitude content: perpendicularity without the action gives a static imaginary coordinate without phase accumulation; the action without perpendicularity gives an action quantum without a perpendicular axis to rotate around. The Principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies both, as its two clauses (Proposition 2.2).

If x₄ were real — x₄ = ct without the i — the path weights would be exp(S/ℏ), real and (for S \> 0) divergent or decaying. This is precisely the Wick-rotated Euclidean theory (\[1, §9\]; corpus paper \[Wick/2026\]), which is classical statistical mechanics, not quantum mechanics. The Wick rotation t → -iτ that connects the two is, in McGucken terms, the coordinate identification τ = x₄/c (\[1, Theorem 9.1\] and the dedicated companion paper \[Wick/2026\], which develops the McGucken–Wick rotation as a real coordinate identity on the McGucken manifold). The i in x₄ = ict is what marks the genuine perpendicularity of x₄ to ordinary space, and that perpendicularity is what makes the path weights complex phases rather than real exponentials. Removing the i removes the perpendicularity and collapses quantum mechanics to its Euclidean shadow. ∎

The complex character established here is the prerequisite for the entire formalism that follows. The Hilbert space requires complex amplitudes; the canonical commutator requires the factor i; the Born rule requires the modulus structure; the uncertainty principle and Schrödinger equation require the complex inner-product space on which the operators act. Theorem 3.1 supplies the underlying complex structure from which all five subsequent derivations descend.
