### 9.5 The physical reading of the Schrödinger equation under dx₄/dt = ic: the change of ψ with respect to x₄ (left) equals the acceleration of ψ in space (right)

The derivation of the Schrödinger equation as a theorem of dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 9.1 in §9.2) establishes the equation as a mathematical consequence of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, whose x₄-advance carries action ℏ per oscillation. This subsection states what the equation is saying about the physical world, using the derivative structure of the equation itself, with no interpretive vocabulary added on top.

#### 9.5.1 The equation, stated

The Schrödinger equation for a wave function ψ(x, t) on Euclidean spatial coordinates x = (x₁, x₂, x₃) and time t, with potential V(x, t) and mass m, reads:

$$
i\hbar \frac{\partial \psi}{\partial t} \;=\; -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\, \nabla^2 \psi \;+\; V\,\psi.
$$

The left side is iℏ times the first derivative of ψ with respect to time. The right side is minus ℏ²/(2m) times the second derivative of ψ with respect to the spatial coordinates, plus V times ψ.

#### 9.5.2 What each side is, literally

The first derivative of ψ with respect to time, ∂ψ/∂t, is the rate of change of ψ at a fixed spatial point as time advances. The second derivative of ψ with respect to space, ∇²ψ = ∂²ψ/∂x₁² + ∂²ψ/∂x₂² + ∂²ψ/∂x₃², is the sum of the second derivatives of ψ along each of the three spatial coordinates. The potential V(x, t) is a scalar function of position and time.

Nothing beyond this. The left side is a first time derivative multiplied by iℏ. The right side is a second spatial derivative multiplied by −ℏ²/(2m), plus V·ψ.

#### 9.5.3 The physical reading of the left side under dx₄/dt = ic

Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, the fourth dimension x₄ advances at rate ic from every spacetime event. This means: as time t advances, x₄ advances at rate c in the direction perpendicular to the spatial slice. Time-advance and x₄-advance are the same thing, with the i marking the perpendicularity of x₄ to space (Theorem 3.1).

Therefore, the first derivative of ψ with respect to time on the left side of the Schrödinger equation is the change of ψ with respect to x₄. The i in front of ∂ψ/∂t marks that x₄ is perpendicular to the three spatial dimensions — the same i as in dx₄/dt = ic. The ℏ in front of ∂ψ/∂t marks that each cycle of x₄-advance carries an action of ℏ — the action-quantization clause of the Principle, its wavelength setting h (§2.2).

The left side of the Schrödinger equation is therefore, in the framework’s reading, the change of ψ with respect to x₄, calibrated by the two dimensional parameters of dx₄/dt = ic: the i for the perpendicular direction, the ℏ for the action carried per cycle of x₄-advance.

#### 9.5.4 The physical reading of the right side under dx₄/dt = ic

The second derivative of ψ with respect to space is an acceleration. This is the standard meaning of a second derivative: the first derivative measures a rate of change of a quantity with respect to a coordinate, and the second derivative measures the rate of change of that first derivative. Applied to a spatial coordinate, the second derivative is an acceleration in that coordinate. Applied to ψ across the three spatial dimensions summed, ∇²ψ is the acceleration of ψ in space.

#### 9.5.5 The physical reading of the equation

The Schrödinger equation, under dx₄/dt = ic, states an equality: the change of ψ with respect to x₄ (left) equals the acceleration of ψ in space (right), with the potential V·ψ added on the right.

The physics of this equality is what dx₄/dt = ic supplies: x₄ is moving at c in the direction perpendicular to space, so a change of ψ with respect to x₄ IS an acceleration of ψ in space. There is no separate mechanism converting one into the other. The equation is the statement that these two quantities — the change of ψ with respect to x₄ on the one hand, the second spatial derivative of ψ on the other — are the same physical thing, because x₄’s motion at c perpendicular to space is what links the two.

The mass m and the potential V modify the coefficient on the right side and add the potential-energy contribution, respectively; the i and ℏ on the left are the same i and ℏ that dx₄/dt = ic carries as its two dimensional parameters.

#### 9.5.6 Cross-references to prior sections of the paper

The reading of the left side of the Schrödinger equation given here rests on results established in earlier sections of the paper. The i on the left is the same i as in dx₄/dt = ic, whose derivation from x₄-perpendicularity to the spatial slice is Theorem 3.1 (§3). The ℏ on the left is the action-per-cycle of x₄-advance, whose location as one of the two dimensional parameters of the McGucken Principle’s expansion, together with c, is stated in §2.2. The derivation of the equation itself, as a mathematical theorem of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, whose expansion carries action ℏ per oscillation, is Theorem 9.1 (§9.2). This subsection provides the physical reading of what Theorem 9.1 establishes: the equation says that the change of ψ with respect to x₄ equals the second spatial derivative of ψ, and this equality is what dx₄/dt = ic asserts about x₄’s motion at c perpendicular to space.

#### 9.5.7 Contrast with the orthodox pedagogical reading

The orthodox pedagogical reading of the Schrödinger equation treats the left side as “the Hamiltonian generates time evolution,” where the operator iℏ ∂\_t is called the “energy operator” and the right side is called the “Hamiltonian.” This reading is descriptive of the mathematical structure of the equation. It states which operators appear on which side and what their formal roles are in the time-evolution problem. It does not state what the equation is saying about the physical world.

The framework’s reading, given above, does state that. It says: the change of ψ with respect to x₄ (with x₄ moving at c perpendicular to space) is what the acceleration of ψ in space is. The two are equal because that is what dx₄/dt = ic asserts. The Schrödinger equation is not a formal statement about operators; it is a physical statement about how a wave function’s change with respect to x₄ is related to its acceleration in space.

The orthodox reading is not wrong. It is silent. It says what the equation looks like, not what it means. The framework’s reading supplies the physics that orthodox pedagogy leaves out.

#### 9.5.8 The same reading applies to the Klein–Gordon and Dirac equations

The Klein–Gordon equation for a scalar field φ of mass m,

$$
\left(\frac{1}{c^2}\frac{\partial^2}{\partial t^2} - \nabla^2 + \frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2}\right)\phi = 0,
$$

has a second time derivative on the left and a second spatial derivative on the right. Under dx₄/dt = ic, the left-side second time derivative is the second derivative of φ with respect to x₄ (with x₄ moving at c perpendicular to space). The mass term m²c²/ℏ² contains the same c (rate of x₄-advance) and ℏ (action-per-cycle) as in the framework. The physical reading of the Klein–Gordon equation is the relativistic version of the Schrödinger reading: the second derivative of φ with respect to x₄ equals the second spatial derivative of φ, modified by the mass term. The 1/c² coefficient on the time derivative encodes the same c as the rate of x₄-advance.

The Dirac equation for a spinor ψ,

$$
i\hbar \gamma^\mu \partial_\mu \psi = m c \psi,
$$

carries the same iℏ prefactor on the derivative side. The γ\^μ ∂\_μ combines the first time derivative and the first spatial derivatives into a single Lorentz-covariant object; under dx₄/dt = ic, this is the derivative of ψ along the direction of the four-velocity of the frame, with the imaginary part encoding x₄-advance at c and the real parts encoding spatial change. The mass term mc on the right introduces the mass and the rate-of-x₄-advance parameter c. The framework’s reading applies: the derivative of ψ with respect to the four-velocity direction (which contains x₄-advance) equals mc times ψ.

In all three cases — Schrödinger, Klein–Gordon, Dirac — the appearance of derivatives with respect to time on one side and derivatives with respect to space on the other is a statement about the relationship between change with respect to x₄ (which moves at c) and change with respect to space. The iℏ that appears in Schrödinger and Dirac carries the same i (x₄-perpendicularity to space) and the same ℏ (action-per-cycle of x₄-advance) as dx₄/dt = ic. The full derivations of Klein–Gordon and Dirac from dx₄/dt = ic are given in §9.1.5 (Klein–Gordon) and the corpus paper \[1\] (Dirac) as separate theorems; the reading here is the physics those derivations establish.

#### 9.5.9 Dimensional transparency of the equation under the framework’s reading

The Schrödinger equation is dimensionally consistent: both sides have units of energy. The framework’s reading makes this dimensional consistency physically transparent.

On the left side, iℏ ∂ψ/∂t has units of ℏ (action) times 1/time (frequency), which is action per unit time, which is energy. In the framework’s reading, this is: (action carried per cycle of x₄-advance) times (rate of change of ψ per unit of x₄-advance) = energy carried by the change of ψ with respect to x₄. The dimensional constants ℏ and 1/time combine to give energy because ℏ is action-per-cycle and 1/time (equivalently frequency) is cycles-per-unit-time, and action-per-cycle times cycles-per-unit-time is action-per-unit-time is energy.

On the right side, ℏ²/(2m) ∇²ψ has units of ℏ² (action²) times 1/mass times 1/length², which is action²/(mass · length²). Using the fact that action has units of mass · length²/time, action²/(mass · length²) has units of mass · length²/time², which is energy. In the framework’s reading, this is: (action carried per cycle of x₄-advance)² times (spatial acceleration of ψ per unit mass) = energy contained in the spatial acceleration of ψ.

The dimensional consistency of the Schrödinger equation is the dimensional consistency of the framework’s reading: energy on the left (action-per-cycle of x₄-advance times rate of change with respect to x₄) equals energy on the right (spatial acceleration of ψ times mass²-scaled action²). The ℏ appears on both sides — once on the left as the action-per-cycle multiplier, twice on the right as the squared coupling of the spatial acceleration — because ℏ is the second dimensional parameter of dx₄/dt = ic, appearing wherever the action-quantization content of the framework enters the calculation. The c does not appear explicitly in Schrödinger because Schrödinger is nonrelativistic (v \<\< c limit), where the c dependence collapses; in Klein–Gordon and Dirac, c appears explicitly on both sides.

#### 9.5.10 Relation to the pedagogical Argand derivation of the i in the wave function

The pedagogical derivation of the necessity of the imaginary unit i in the Schrödinger equation — presented in many introductory treatments and in the tradition of Argand’s 1806 diagram — argues as follows. For a wave function ψ evolving in time with ∂ψ/∂t proportional to ψ itself (as required to extract energy cleanly as a multiplicative eigenvalue from a first-order derivative), the proportionality constant must be pure imaginary. If the constant were real and positive, ψ would grow exponentially; if real and negative, ψ would decay exponentially; only if the constant is imaginary does ψ remain bounded and periodic. The imaginary constant is the geometric operation that rotates a first-derivative vector by 90° from parallel to perpendicular, in the sense that i is the 90°-rotation operator in the complex plane. The 90°-rotation of the derivative is what makes ψ’s magnitude conserved rather than exponentially growing or decaying.

Under the framework’s reading, this pedagogical derivation is a projection of the geometry of dx₄/dt = ic into the wave-function language. The 90°-rotation that the pedagogical argument requires — perpendicularity between the first-time-derivative direction and the ψ-direction — is the same perpendicularity that dx₄/dt = ic asserts between x₄ and the spatial slice. The Argand pedagogy identifies the requirement in an abstract complex plane; dx₄/dt = ic identifies the physical geometry in which the plane is instantiated: the (spatial-slice, x₄) plane in four-dimensional spacetime.

The pedagogical derivation and the framework’s reading arrive at the same result — i must appear in the Schrödinger equation on the derivative-with-respect-to-time side — from different starting points. The pedagogical derivation starts from the mathematical requirement that ψ’s magnitude be bounded (which reduces to the requirement of probability conservation in the Born-rule reading). The framework’s reading starts from the physical geometric fact that x₄ is perpendicular to space and moves at c, which forces the i in the first-derivative-with-respect-to-time term because that derivative is the change with respect to x₄.

The two are the same i: the pedagogical i (marking perpendicularity in the abstract complex plane) and the framework’s i (marking x₄-perpendicularity to space) refer to the same geometric object under different notational conventions. The Argand pedagogy is the mathematical shadow of the physical geometry that dx₄/dt = ic names directly. Physicists who accept the Argand argument have already accepted the geometry of dx₄/dt = ic; the framework’s contribution is to name the geometry physically rather than leaving it in the abstract complex plane.

#### 9.5.11 The Wick rotation as coordinate reparametrization from Algebraic Channel real-time $t$ to dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel fourth coordinate $x_4/c$: the oscillatory-to-dissipative transformation as change of parametrization not change of physics

The Wick rotation — the substitution $t \to -i\tau$ that transforms the Schrödinger equation into the imaginary-time diffusion equation and the Minkowski path integral into the Euclidean path integral — has been universally applied across quantum field theory (Wick 1954; Osterwalder-Schrader 1973; Wilson 1974 lattice QCD; Feynman-Kac 1948–1949 functional integrals; Matsubara 1955 imaginary-time thermal field theory) as a computational device that makes divergent Minkowski integrals absolutely convergent Euclidean integrals and permits explicit computation. Under the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the Wick rotation acquires a foundational interpretation that this subsection makes explicit as a theorem with four corollaries.

**Theorem 9.5.11 (Wick rotation as coordinate reparametrization from Algebraic Channel to dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel).** *Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic and the coordinate identification $x_4 = ict$ (Lemma 2.5), the Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$ is precisely the change of parametrization from the Algebraic Channel’s real-time coordinate $t$ to the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel’s fourth coordinate $x_4/c$, via the identification $\tau = x_4/c$.*

*Proof.* From $x_4 = ict$ (Lemma 2.5, the integrated coordinate statement of dx₄/dt = ic), we have $t = x_4/(ic) = -ix_4/c$. Setting $\tau = x_4/c$ gives $t = -i\tau$, which is the Wick substitution. Equivalently, $\tau = it$. The Wick rotation is therefore not a formal analytical continuation, but the literal change of coordinate from Algebraic Channel real-time $t$ (parametrizing the Poincaré-symmetric Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ substrate) to dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel fourth coordinate $x_4/c$ (parametrizing the McGucken Sphere wavefront expansion). $\blacksquare$

The corollaries of Theorem 9.5.11 establish what the reparametrization transforms and what it preserves:

**Corollary 9.5.11.1 (Schrödinger equation under Wick reparametrization).** *The Schrödinger equation $i\hbar \partial_t \psi = \hat H \psi$ under the reparametrization $t = -i\tau$ becomes $\hbar \partial_\tau \psi = -\hat H \psi$, mathematically identical to the imaginary-time diffusion equation with diffusion coefficient $D = \hbar/(2m)$ for the free non-relativistic Hamiltonian $\hat H = -\hbar^2 \nabla^2/(2m)$ (Feynman-Kac).*

*Proof.* Under $t = -i\tau$, differentiating gives $\partial/\partial t = (\partial \tau/\partial t) \cdot \partial/\partial \tau = i \, \partial/\partial \tau$ (from $\tau = it$). The Schrödinger equation $i\hbar \, \partial_t \psi = \hat H \psi$ becomes $i\hbar \cdot i \, \partial_\tau \psi = \hat H \psi$, i.e., $-\hbar \, \partial_\tau \psi = \hat H \psi$, i.e., $\partial_\tau \psi = -(\hat H/\hbar) \psi$. For $\hat H = -\hbar^2 \nabla^2/(2m)$, this reads $\partial_\tau \psi = (\hbar/(2m)) \nabla^2 \psi$, which is the diffusion equation with $D = \hbar/(2m)$. $\blacksquare$

**Corollary 9.5.11.2 (Unitary group to contractive semigroup).** *The unitary time-evolution group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$ under the reparametrization $t = -i\tau$ becomes the contractive semigroup $T(\tau) = e^{-\hat H \tau/\hbar}$ for $\tau \geq 0$. The semigroup fails to be a group: for physical Hamiltonians $\hat H$ satisfying the Wightman Spectrum Condition W6 (Theorem 16.15.6) with spectrum $\sigma(\hat H) \subset [0, +\infty)$, the reversed evolution $T(-\tau) = e^{+\hat H \tau/\hbar}$ is unbounded and does not extend to a bounded operator on Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$. The forward Wick rotation destroys the group structure of $U(t)$ and reveals a semigroup with intrinsic direction.*

*Proof.* Direct substitution: $U(-i\tau) = e^{-i\hat H(-i\tau)/\hbar} = e^{-\hat H \tau/\hbar} = T(\tau)$. For $\hat H$ self-adjoint on Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with spectral resolution $\hat H = \int_0^\infty \lambda \, dE_\lambda$ (using the Spectrum Condition W6, $\hat H \geq 0$, from Theorem 16.15.6), the operator norm of $T(\tau)$ is $\|T(\tau)\| = \sup_{\lambda \in \sigma(\hat H)} e^{-\lambda\tau/\hbar} = 1$ for $\tau \geq 0$ (contractive on the range $[0, +\infty)$), but $\|T(-\tau)\| = \sup_{\lambda \in \sigma(\hat H)} e^{+\lambda\tau/\hbar} = +\infty$ for $\tau > 0$ (unbounded, since $\sigma(\hat H)$ extends to $+\infty$ for physical Hamiltonians). Therefore $T(-\tau)$ does not extend to a bounded operator on Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$; the semigroup $\{T(\tau)\}_{\tau \geq 0}$ has no left inverse for $\tau > 0$; the group structure of $U(t)$ (under which $U(-t) = U(t)^{-1}$ was bounded for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$) is destroyed under the Wick reparametrization. $\blacksquare$

**Corollary 9.5.11.3 (Path integral Wick).** *The Minkowski path integral $\int \mathcal{D}\phi \, e^{iS[\phi]/\hbar}$ under the reparametrization $t = -i\tau$ becomes the Euclidean path integral $\int \mathcal{D}\phi \, e^{-S_E[\phi]/\hbar}$, where $S_E$ is the Euclidean action defined by the signature-flipped kinetic term.*

*Proof.* Under $t = -i\tau$, the differential $dt = -i \, d\tau$. For a scalar Lagrangian $L = (1/2)(\dot\phi)^2 - V(\phi)$ with $\dot\phi = d\phi/dt$, the transformed kinetic term is $(\dot\phi)^2 = (d\phi/dt)^2 = (d\phi/(-i \, d\tau))^2 = -(d\phi/d\tau)^2 = -(\dot\phi_E)^2$. The Lagrangian transforms as $L = -(1/2)(\dot\phi_E)^2 - V(\phi) = -[(1/2)(\dot\phi_E)^2 + V(\phi)] = -L_E$, where $L_E = (1/2)(\dot\phi_E)^2 + V(\phi)$ is the Euclidean Lagrangian (kinetic-plus-potential with positive-definite Euclidean signature). The action transforms as $S = \int L \, dt = \int (-L_E)(-i \, d\tau) = i \int L_E \, d\tau = i S_E$. Then $iS/\hbar = i \cdot i S_E/\hbar = -S_E/\hbar$, giving $e^{iS/\hbar} \to e^{-S_E/\hbar}$. The oscillatory Minkowski path integral becomes the real-positive absolutely-convergent Euclidean path integral. $\blacksquare$

**Corollary 9.5.11.4 (Oscillatory-to-dissipative transformation as change of parametrization, not change of physics).** *The transformation of oscillatory content into dissipative content under Wick rotation is a consequence of the coordinate reparametrization $t \to \tau = x_4/c$ established in Theorem 9.5.11, not a change in the underlying physics. Both parametrizations describe the same wavefront expansion of dx₄/dt = ic at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$:*

*(a) In the Algebraic Channel parametrization by $t$: the wavefront is presented as oscillatory phase $e^{-i\omega_C t}$ at Compton angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$, per Corollary 2.2.bis.1 and Proposition 2.2.bis.1(iii) (one full oscillation cycle per Compton substrate tick).*

*(b) In the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel parametrization by $\tau = x_4/c$: the wavefront is presented as dissipative decay $e^{-\omega_C \tau} = e^{-x_4/\bar\lambda_C}$ where $\bar\lambda_C = \hbar/(mc)$ is the reduced Compton wavelength, per Proposition 2.2.bis.1(i) (fourth-dimensional advance $\lambda_C$ per Compton substrate tick, so decay by factor $e^{-2\pi}$ per Compton wavelength of $x_4$-advance).*

*These are the same physical fact — one full cycle of the dx₄/dt = ic wavefront expansion per Compton substrate tick, with substrate-tick action $\Delta S = h$ (Corollary 2.2.bis.1) — parametrized once by Algebraic Channel real time $t$ (giving oscillation, per real-time period $\Delta t_C$) and once by dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel fourth coordinate $x_4/c$ (giving decay, per fourth-coordinate advance $\lambda_C$).*

*Proof.* By Proposition 2.2.bis.1(iii), $\omega_C \Delta t_C = 2\pi$ per Compton substrate tick, so $e^{-i\omega_C \Delta t_C} = e^{-2\pi i} = 1$ (unit modulus, full oscillation cycle) in the Algebraic Channel parametrization. Applying Theorem 9.5.11 with $\Delta \tau = \Delta x_4/c = \lambda_C/c$ (Wick reparametrization of the same substrate tick, with the imaginary factor of $i\lambda_C$ in Proposition 2.2.bis.1(i) absorbed into the reparametrization $\tau = x_4/c$ as a real quantity), the same substrate tick becomes $e^{-\omega_C \Delta \tau} = e^{-\omega_C (\lambda_C/c)}$; using $\omega_C \lambda_C = 2\pi c$ (the substrate-tick dispersion relation, from $\omega_C = 2\pi/\Delta t_C$ and $\lambda_C = c \Delta t_C \cdot$ integer factor — see \[MG-Wick\] §IX.30.C.12), this gives $e^{-2\pi}$: full decay by factor $e^{-2\pi}$ per Compton wavelength of $x_4$-advance. The two parametrizations describe the same substrate tick with the same action content $\Delta S = h$; the oscillatory-versus-dissipative character is a property of the parametrization, not of the underlying physics. $\blacksquare$

**Corollary 9.5.11.5 (Yukawa potential as fourth-dimensional Compton-scale localization).** *The Yukawa potential $V_Y(r) \propto e^{-r/\bar\lambda_C}/r$ for the interaction mediated by a massive scalar particle of mass $m$ is the Wick-rotated substrate-tick localization of the mediating particle at the reduced Compton wavelength $\bar\lambda_C = \hbar/(mc)$. What Yukawa (1935) introduced as an ad hoc range cutoff for nuclear forces is the substrate-tick geometry of the fourth-dimensional expansion of the mediating particle at its Compton substrate-tick scale.*

*Proof sketch.* The massive scalar propagator in Euclidean four-momentum space (obtained via inverse Wick reparametrization from the Minkowski Feynman propagator) is $G_E(k) = 1/(k^2 + m^2 c^2/\hbar^2)$, in which the mass enters as $1/\bar\lambda_C^2 = m^2 c^2/\hbar^2$. Fourier-transforming to Euclidean position space at fixed Euclidean time $\tau = 0$ (equivalent to fourth-dimensional distance $x_4 = 0$) gives $G_E(r) \propto e^{-r/\bar\lambda_C}/r$ for spatial distance $r = |\vec x|$. The decay length $\bar\lambda_C = \hbar/(mc)$ is exactly the reduced Compton wavelength — the fourth-dimensional advance per Compton substrate tick of the mediating particle (Proposition 2.2.bis.1(i), with the factor of $2\pi$ absorbed into the reduced Compton wavelength). Every massive gauge mediator of the Standard Model — the charged and neutral pions of nuclear forces (Yukawa 1935), the $W^\pm$ and $Z^0$ of the weak interaction (Glashow-Salam-Weinberg 1961–1968), the Higgs boson of the electroweak sector (Higgs 1964; ATLAS-CMS 2012) — exhibits the same $e^{-r/\bar\lambda_C}$ localization at its own reduced Compton wavelength for the same substrate-geometric reason. $\blacksquare$

*Remark 9.5.11.1 (Seventy-year empirical anchor).* The seventy-year (Wick 1954 through 2024) empirical universality of the Wick rotation across every physically realistic quantum field theory — Osterwalder-Schrader (1973) constructive quantum field theory, Wilson (1974) Euclidean lattice quantum chromodynamics, Matsubara (1955) imaginary-time thermal field theory, Feynman-Kac (1948–1949) functional integrals, and every subsequent construction — is empirical evidence for Theorem 9.5.11: the Wick substitution universally works because it universally corresponds to the coordinate reparametrization $t \to \tau = x_4/c$, which is available whenever the underlying physics is built on the dx₄/dt = ic wavefront expansion at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. Any physically realistic quantum field theory that did not admit a successful Wick rotation would falsify the framework at exactly the point where the reparametrization would fail (a physically realistic quantum field theory not built on dx₄/dt = ic content). No such failure has been observed in seventy years of quantum field theory computation across every physically realized regime.

*Remark 9.5.11.2 (Bidirectional character-flip).* The forward Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$ applied to Algebraic Channel transforms the oscillatory unitary structure into the dissipative semigroup structure by revealing the underlying wavefront-expansion content that Algebraic Channel parametrization had hidden. The inverse Wick rotation $\tau \to it$ applied to dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel collapses the expansive wavefront structure into local algebraic operators by projecting away the $+ic$-orientation. The two directions are asymmetric: forward Wick is well-defined on the 47-item shared census that survives the projection $\Pi_A$ but becomes non-invertible on the 17-item asymmetric census that lies in the kernel of $\Pi_A$; inverse Wick loses precisely the 17-item content that was projected away. The full rigorous development of the bidirectional character-flip theorem, together with the Nelson 1966 stochastic mechanics convergence and the Osterwalder-Schrader reflection positivity identification (§16.15.14e of the present paper), is given in the corpus paper \[MG-Wick\], §IX.30.C.11 through §IX.30.C.13.

*Remark 9.5.11.3 (Sign convention $t \to -i\tau$ fixed by $+ic$ orientation).* The specific sign of the Wick substitution ($t \to -i\tau$ rather than $t \to +i\tau$) is fixed by the $+ic$ orientation of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic via the coordinate identification $\tau = x_4/c$ established in Theorem 9.5.11. Under the opposite orientation dx₄/dt = $-ic$, the sign of the Wick substitution would flip to $t \to +i\tau$, and the resulting semigroup would require $\hat H \leq 0$ (bounded above, not below) for contractivity — which is not the observed physics of any known quantum system (all physical Hamiltonians are bounded below, per the Wightman Spectrum Condition W6). The universal choice $t \to -i\tau$ in quantum field theory is therefore a seventy-year unstated empirical anchor for the $+ic$ orientation of dx₄/dt = ic.

#### 9.5.12 Wave–particle duality as the two parametrizations of the imaginary unit in dx₄/dt = ic: the Algebraic Channel as the particle description, the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel as the wave description, and the Wick reparametrization as the operational map between them

Section 9.5.11 established that the Wick substitution $t \to -i\tau$ is the coordinate reparametrization from the Algebraic Channel’s real-time coordinate $t$ to the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel’s fourth coordinate $x_4/c$ (Theorem 9.5.11). The present subsection establishes that the two channels are, respectively, the particle description and the wave description of one and the same substrate object, and that wave–particle duality is therefore not a mystery to be interpreted but a forced consequence of the double reading of the imaginary unit $i$ in dx₄/dt = ic.

**Theorem 9.5.12.1 (Channel–description identification).** *Under the dual-channel architecture of §16, the Algebraic Channel is the particle description and the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel is the wave description, in the following precise sense.*

*(i) The Algebraic Channel is localizing.* Its defining content is: field operators $\hat\phi(x)$ evaluated pointwise at events $x \in$ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$; the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, which localizes conjugate observables at a point; microcausality (Wightman axiom W3), which enforces pointwise commutation of field operators at spacelike-separated events; the particle-number Fock structure with creation and annihilation operators $a^\dagger_{\mathbf k}, a_{\mathbf k}$; and the $T$-symmetric unitary evolution group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat H t/\hbar}$. Every one of these is a *localization* statement. The native object of the Algebraic Channel is a thing *at a place*.

*(ii) The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel is delocalizing.* Its defining content is: the McGucken Sphere expanding at $+ic$ from every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$; the wavefront amplitude $\psi$ supported on the expansion; dissipative spreading with diffusion coefficient $D = \hbar/(2m)$ (Corollary 9.5.11.1); and the $+ic$ orientation supplying the arrow of the expansion. Every one of these is a *delocalization* statement. The native object of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel is a front *spreading from* a place.

*(iii) Consequently the channel duality of §16 is not analogous to wave–particle duality; it is wave–particle duality, stated in rather than phenomenological terms.* $\blacksquare$

**Corollary 9.5.12.1 (Bidirectional transmutation of character under Wick reparametrization).** *Under the forward Wick reparametrization $t \to -i\tau$, an Algebraic-Channel particle description becomes a dx₄/dt = ic Geometric-Channel expanding dissipative wave description. Under the inverse reparametrization $\tau \to it$, a dx₄/dt = ic Geometric-Channel expanding wave description becomes an Algebraic-Channel localized particle description. The transmutation is exhibited exactly on the free propagator.*

*Proof.* Consider the free non-relativistic Schrödinger kernel on the Algebraic Channel’s real-time parametrization:
$$K(x,t) = \left(\frac{m}{2\pi i \hbar t}\right)^{3/2} \exp\!\left(\frac{i m x^2}{2\hbar t}\right).$$
Its modulus is $|K| \sim t^{-3/2}$ with a unimodular oscillatory phase: this is not a spreading probability density but a pointwise amplitude carrying phase — the particle description. Apply the Wick reparametrization $t = -i\tau$ of Theorem 9.5.11:
$$K_E(x,\tau) = \left(\frac{m}{2\pi \hbar \tau}\right)^{3/2} \exp\!\left(-\frac{m x^2}{2\hbar \tau}\right),$$
which is a *real, positive, normalized Gaussian* of width $\sigma(\tau) = \sqrt{\hbar\tau/m}$, spreading monotonically in $\tau$. This is precisely the heat kernel of the diffusion equation with $D = \hbar/(2m)$, in accord with Corollary 9.5.11.1. The oscillatory pointwise object has become a spreading nonlocal front by substitution alone, with no change to the underlying physics — only to the parametrization (Corollary 9.5.11.4).

Conversely, applying the inverse reparametrization $\tau \to it$ to $K_E$, the real spreading width $\sigma(\tau) = \sqrt{\hbar\tau/m}$ becomes the imaginary width $\sqrt{-i\hbar t/m}$: the spatial spread ceases to be a spread and is converted into phase. The wave relocalizes into a particle carrying a phase. $\blacksquare$

**Corollary 9.5.12.2 (Delocalization and phase are the same quantity in two parametrizations; the role of the Born modulus).** *By Corollary 9.5.12.1, spatial delocalization in the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel parametrization and accumulated phase in the Algebraic Channel parametrization are the same quantity read in the two coordinatizations. Consequently the recovery of a probability density from the Algebraic Channel’s phase-carrying amplitude requires an operation that converts phase back into density content; that operation is the Born modulus $|\psi|^2 = \psi^*\psi$ (Theorem 7.2 of the present paper; Theorem 4.2 of \[MG-Born\]). This supplies the reason why the Born rule takes the modulus-squared form rather than the amplitude itself: the amplitude carries the delocalization content as phase, and only the pairing of the forward $+ic$ advance with its conjugate $-ic$ advance returns it to density form.* $\blacksquare$

**Corollary 9.5.12.3 (The de Broglie wavelength as the fourth-dimensional advance per substrate tick).** *By Proposition 2.2.bis.1(i), the fourth-dimensional advance per Compton substrate tick is $\Delta x_4 = i\lambda_C$ with $\lambda_C = h/(mc)$, which is the de Broglie–Compton wavelength. The wavelength that de Broglie (1924) found attached to every massive particle, without being able to say what was waving, is therefore the magnitude of the fourth-dimensional advance of the dx₄/dt = ic wavefront expansion per Compton substrate tick. De Broglie possessed the invariant; the McGucken Principle supplies the substrate of which it is the per-tick advance.* $\blacksquare$

**Theorem 9.5.12.2 (Wave–particle duality is forced by the double reading of $i$ in dx₄/dt = ic).** *The substrate tick of dx₄/dt = ic carries an imaginary fourth-dimensional advance and a real action:*
$$\Delta x_4 = i\lambda_C \quad \text{(imaginary)}, \qquad \Delta S = h \quad \text{(real)}.$$
*The imaginary unit $i$ admits exactly two readings, and both are forced:*

-   *Read in the Algebraic Channel’s real-time parametrization by $t$, the advance $ic\,\Delta t$ is imaginary and therefore registers as **phase**. The object is a particle carrying a Compton clock at $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$.*
-   *Read in the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel’s parametrization by $\tau = x_4/c$, the advance $c\,\Delta\tau$ is real and therefore registers as **extension**. The object is a wave of width $\lambda_C$.*

*The two readings are of the same substrate tick, with the same action content $\Delta S = h$ and the same length scale $\lambda_C$. Neither reading is prior to the other; both are forced. Wave–particle duality is therefore not an interpretational puzzle but the double reading of the imaginary unit in dx₄/dt = ic.* $\blacksquare$

*Proof.* By Theorem 9.5.11, $\tau = x_4/c$ and $t = -i\tau$ are the two parametrizations of one substrate expansion. By Proposition 2.2.bis.1, the substrate tick carries $\Delta x_4 = i\lambda_C$ and $\Delta S = h$. In the $t$-parametrization, $\Delta x_4 = ic\,\Delta t_C$ is imaginary; an imaginary displacement entering an exponential $e^{i\theta}$ contributes unimodular phase, with $\omega_C \Delta t_C = 2\pi$ (Proposition 2.2.bis.1(iii)) giving one complete phase cycle per tick and $|e^{-i\omega_C \Delta t_C}| = 1$ — no spatial spreading, hence particle character. In the $\tau$-parametrization, $\Delta x_4 = c\,\Delta\tau$ is real; a real displacement entering an exponential $e^{-\lambda}$ contributes decay over the length $\bar\lambda_C = \hbar/(mc)$, with $e^{-\omega_C \Delta\tau_C} = e^{-2\pi}$ per Compton wavelength of $x_4$-advance — spatial spreading, hence wave character. Both follow from the single fact that the advance is $ic\,dt$; the character observed is fixed entirely by which coordinate the advance is parametrized against. $\blacksquare$

*Remark 9.5.12.1 (Scope: parametrization, not physical transmutation).* Theorem 9.5.12.2 does not assert that a physical particle undergoes a physical rotation into imaginary time, nor that anything propagates in imaginary time. The claim is that particle-character and wave-character are parametrization-dependent readings of one substrate object, and that the Wick substitution is the operational map between the readings. The reason the map is clean, and universally successful across seventy years of quantum field theory, is that both readings are renderings of dx₄/dt = ic (Remark 9.5.11.1). The Wick rotation does not act on the physics; it exhibits the duality that dx₄/dt = ic already contains.

*Remark 9.5.12.2 (Relation to the geometric-optics treatment).* The present derivation is independent of, and complementary to, the geometric-optics treatment of wave–particle duality given in \[MG-Huygens\] §VIII.2, which obtains particle behaviour as the $\hbar \to 0$ limit of the McGucken Sphere expansion (definite radius $ct$, definite geodesic) and wave behaviour as the finite-$\hbar$ superposition and interference of Spheres from distinct source events. That treatment is a *limit* argument in a fixed parametrization; the present treatment is a *reparametrization* argument at fixed $\hbar$. Two derivationally-disjoint derivations of the same duality constitute a further instance of convergent overdetermination (§17.5bis).

#### 9.5.13 The two channels as two positions relative to the dx₄/dt = ic wavefront: conservation laws from the transverse position, quantum probability from the co-moving position, and the derivation of complementarity

Section 9.5.12 established what the two channels describe. The present subsection establishes *why there are two*: they are two positions relative to one and the same wavefront. The positions are defined kinematically, by the four-velocity budget of Lemma 2.5, and carry no psychological or observer-dependent content.

**Definition 9.5.13.1 (Transverse position).** *A system is in the* transverse position *relative to the dx₄/dt = ic wavefront at an event $p \in$ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ if it is at spatial rest at $p$, so that by the bounded four-velocity-budget partition $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$ (per coordinate time $t$, §2.3; Lemma 5.1.3.2), with $v_{x_4} \equiv \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$ the Sphere-tangent share, its entire budget share is spent on $x_4$-advance: $v = 0$, hence $v_{x_4} = c$, while the Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ holds at this event as at every event. The wavefront expands* through *such a system; the system is traversed by the expansion, not carried by it. This is ontology clause (1) of the four-fold ontology (§2.4): absolute rest in $x_1x_2x_3$.*

**Definition 9.5.13.2 (Co-moving position).** *A system is in the* co-moving position *relative to the dx₄/dt = ic wavefront if it propagates on the wavefront itself: $v = c$, whence by the same bounded partition $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$ its Sphere-tangent share vanishes, $v_{x_4} = 0$ — the system takes no share in the $x_4$-advance and accumulates no shadow $X_4$, riding the null worldline of the expansion, while the Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ holds at its events as at every event (the share $v_{x_4}$, not the coordinate rate $dx_4/dt$, is what vanishes; $d\tau = 0$ pointwise and the affine null tangent $dx^\mu/d\lambda$ replaces the four-velocity). This is ontology clause (2) of the four-fold ontology (§2.4). Such a system inherits the expansion’s delocalization: it has no position on the front, only a support.*

**Theorem 9.5.13.1 (Conservation laws as the invariants of the passage; the transverse position).** *A system in the transverse position measures those features of the dx₄/dt = ic expansion that do not change as the expansion passes through it. These are exactly four, and they are exactly the invariants of the McGucken Sphere:*
$$c \ \text{(rate)}, \qquad \omega_C = \frac{mc^2}{\hbar} \ \text{(frequency)}, \qquad \lambda_C = \frac{h}{mc} \ \text{(wavelength)}, \qquad \Delta S = h \ \text{(action per tick)}.$$
*The symmetries of the passage, and the conservation laws they force by Noether’s theorem, are:*

-   ***Temporal uniformity** of the expansion (the rate is $ic$ at all times) $\Rightarrow$ time-translation symmetry $\Rightarrow$ **conservation of energy**.*
-   ***Spatial homogeneity** of the expansion (the Sphere at any spatial point is identical to the Sphere at any other) $\Rightarrow$ spatial-translation symmetry $\Rightarrow$ **conservation of momentum**.*
-   ***Spherical symmetry** of the expansion (no preferred direction) $\Rightarrow$ rotational symmetry $\Rightarrow$ **conservation of angular momentum**.*
-   ***Phase uniformity** of the expansion (constant rate, no preferred phase origin) $\Rightarrow$ global $U(1)$ symmetry $\Rightarrow$ **conservation of charge**.*

*The full derivation of each conservation law from the corresponding symmetry of the $x_4$-expansion now follows. The extended treatment, with the same result reached through the Huygens-wavefront construction, is developed in* \[MG-Huygens\] *§VI.3 (energy), §VI.4 (momentum), §VI.5 (angular momentum), and §VI.6 (charge); the self-contained derivation given here uses Noether’s first theorem applied directly to the McGucken action.*

*Proof.* Let $\psi$ be the McGucken wavefunction (Definition 2.6) propagating on the Sphere wavefront, and let $S[\psi] = \int_{\mathcal{M}_G} \mathcal{L}\, d^4x$ be the McGucken action, with $\mathcal{L} = \mathcal{L}(\psi, \partial_\mu \psi)$ the McGucken Lagrangian on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (§5.1.8; the action principle itself descends from dx₄/dt = ic through the stationary-phase reading of the propagator, Theorem 4.3.4). $\mathcal{L}$ depends on the coordinates only through $\psi$ and $\partial_\mu\psi$, because the $x_4$-expansion that generates it has the same rate $ic$ at every event (R1, universality clause of Theorem 2.4): the Lagrangian carries no explicit dependence on $t$, on $\mathbf{x}$, on orientation, or on the phase origin of $\psi$. Each such absence is a continuous symmetry, and Noether’s first theorem converts each into a conserved current $j^\mu$ with $\partial_\mu j^\mu = 0$, whence the charge $Q = \int_{\Sigma_t} j^0\, d^3x$ is constant in $t$. We take the four symmetries in turn.

*(i) Temporal uniformity $\Rightarrow$ energy.* The rate is $ic$ at all times (R1), so $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial t = 0$ at fixed $(\psi, \partial_\mu\psi)$. The infinitesimal time translation $t \to t + \epsilon$, $\delta\psi = -\epsilon\, \partial_t\psi$, leaves $S$ invariant. Noether’s theorem gives the conserved current whose time component is the Hamiltonian density $\mathcal{H} = (\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial(\partial_t\psi))\,\partial_t\psi - \mathcal{L}$, and $E = \int_{\Sigma_t}\mathcal{H}\, d^3x$ satisfies $dE/dt = 0$: **conservation of energy**.

*(ii) Spatial homogeneity $\Rightarrow$ momentum.* The Sphere at any spatial point is identical to the Sphere at any other, so $\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial x^i = 0$, $i = 1,2,3$. The infinitesimal space translation $x^i \to x^i + \epsilon^i$, $\delta\psi = -\epsilon^i\,\partial_i\psi$, leaves $S$ invariant. Noether’s theorem gives the conserved momentum density with $P_i = -\int_{\Sigma_t}(\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial(\partial_t\psi))\,\partial_i\psi\, d^3x$ and $dP_i/dt = 0$: **conservation of momentum**.

*(iii) Spherical symmetry $\Rightarrow$ angular momentum.* The expansion has no preferred direction (the McGucken Sphere is isotropic, carrying the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant Haar measure, §7). Under the infinitesimal rotation $x^i \to x^i + \epsilon\,\omega^i{}_j x^j$ with $\omega$ antisymmetric, $\delta\psi = -\epsilon\,\omega^i{}_j x^j \partial_i\psi$, $S$ is invariant. Noether’s theorem gives the conserved angular-momentum tensor $M^{0}{}_{ij} = \int_{\Sigma_t}(x_i\, T^0{}_j - x_j\, T^0{}_i)\, d^3x$ with $T^\mu{}_\nu$ the stress tensor of steps (i)–(ii), and $dM_{ij}/dt = 0$: **conservation of angular momentum**.

*(iv) Phase uniformity $\Rightarrow$ charge.* A universal $x_4$-shift is unobservable (the expansion has constant rate and no preferred phase origin; this is the same universality that supplies Born-rule condition R3, §7.5). The global $U(1)$ transformation $\psi \to e^{i\theta}\psi$, $\delta\psi = i\theta\,\psi$, leaves $\mathcal{L}$ invariant because $\mathcal{L}$ depends on $\psi$ only through the modulus-forming pairing $(\psi,\psi^*)$ fixed by the rank-2 metric (Lemma 7.1). Noether’s theorem gives the conserved current $j^\mu = i[(\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial(\partial_\mu\psi))\,\psi - \psi^*(\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial(\partial_\mu\psi^*))]$, and $Q = \int_{\Sigma_t} j^0\, d^3x$ satisfies $dQ/dt = 0$: **conservation of charge**.

Each of the four symmetries is a property of the $x_4$-expansion itself — its uniformity in time, its homogeneity in space, its isotropy, and its phase-origin-independence — so each conservation law descends from dx₄/dt = ic through Noether’s theorem applied to the McGucken action, with no conservation law postulated independently. The present theorem adds the identification: these are the invariants extracted by a system standing *transverse* to the passage of the wavefront. Conservation laws are what the dx₄/dt = ic expansion looks like to a system it passes through.\* ∎

### 10.6 Hilbert space and Minkowski space as one geometric object at two cascade levels

Theorem 10.5 establishes that dx₄/dt = ic is pointwise instantiated in every derived structure of the cogenerative cascade, in four derivationally distinct senses corresponding to the four types of mathematical structure the cascade generates. The deepest single corollary of this pointwise-instantiation property is the identification of the spacetime manifold of special relativity and the Hilbert space of quantum mechanics as the same geometric object at two cascade levels of representation. Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is the point-set / manifold-level rendering of the constraint surface where dx₄/dt = ic holds locally; 𝓗 is the function-space-level rendering of the same constraint surface. The Lorentzian metric of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ becomes the sesquilinear inner product of 𝓗 by the standard L² construction, with the rank-2 character of the metric (Lemma 2.5) surviving as the rank-2 sesquilinear character of the inner product (Lemma 7.1). The perpendicular fourth dimension x_4 = ict survives as the wavefunction’s complex character (Theorem 3.1). The spatial points of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ are in canonical bijection with the position-eigenstate basis of 𝓗. The Lorentzian causal structure of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ survives as the dispersion structure of 𝓗’s energy-momentum spectrum.

The orthodox reading of quantum mechanics treats 𝓗 as an abstract complex vector space whose connection to physical spacetime is supplied externally — wavefunctions introduced as “amplitudes” without geometry, the inner product introduced as “physically meaningful overlap” without explanation, the complex numbers appearing because “QM requires them” without further account, the operator algebra postulated rather than derived (Dirac–von Neumann axioms). The mystery of “why is quantum mechanics in a Hilbert space” was never resolved in the prior tradition because 𝓗 was treated as a separate mathematical universe from the spacetime in which it acts. The present subsection establishes the resolution: there is no separate Hilbert space “where quantum mechanics lives.” There is one geometric structure — the constraint surface Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ where dx₄/dt = ic holds locally — and the Hilbert space is Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ in its function-valued representation.

#### 10.6.1 The L²-functional construction: 𝓗 as the function-space rendering of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$

For any pseudo-Riemannian manifold (X, g_μν), the standard L²-functional construction supplies a complex Hilbert space

L²(X, g) := { f: X → ℂ \| ∫\_X \|f(x)\|² √\|g(x)\| d\^n x \< ∞ }

with sesquilinear inner product

⟨φ, ψ⟩\_{L²(X,g)} := ∫\_X φ\^\*(x) ψ(x) √\|g(x)\| d\^n x.

The construction is canonical: given (X, g_μν), the L² Hilbert space is uniquely determined up to natural isomorphism. The complex character of L²(X, g) comes from the complex-valuedness of the functions f, not from any additional algebraic input. The sesquilinear inner product structure (conjugate-linear in the first slot, linear in the second) is forced by the requirement that ⟨ψ, ψ⟩ ≥ 0 be real-valued and equal to ‖ψ‖² for any ψ.

In the case X = Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ with the Minkowski metric η_μν of signature (−,+,+,+), the L²-functional construction yields the Hilbert space

𝓗 = L²(Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, η_μν)

with two natural specializations:

(a) The *spatial-slice* L²: at fixed parameter time t, the integration is over the spatial slice ℝ³ at parameter time t, with measure d³x. This is the non-relativistic Schrödinger-picture Hilbert space, with inner product ⟨φ, ψ⟩ = ∫\_{ℝ³} φ\^\*(x) ψ(x) d³x — exactly the Hilbert space derived in Theorem 6.1 of §6.

(b) The *full-Minkowski* L²: integration over the full Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ manifold with measure d⁴x √\|η\| = d⁴x (the Minkowski measure has \|η\| = c² in mostly-plus signature). This is the four-dimensional L² of relativistic quantum mechanics, whose physically relevant subspace is the positive-mass-shell hyperboloid {p\^μp_μ = -m²c²} ⊂ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-dual (the Wightman one-particle Hilbert space; see §10.6.8 below).

Both specializations descend from the same geometric object Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ with the same Lorentzian metric η_μν supplied by Lemma 2.5. The Hilbert space of quantum mechanics, in either specialization, is the L² function-space rendering of the Minkowski manifold of special relativity. The two structures are not separate mathematical universes connected by a postulated bridge; they are the same geometric object viewed at two cascade levels.

#### 10.6.2 The canonical bijection: spacetime points ↔ position-eigenstate basis

The point-set of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at parameter time t and the position-eigenstate basis of 𝓗 at parameter time t are in canonical bijection. Specifically, for each spatial point x₀ ∈ ℝ³ on the spatial slice at time t, the position eigenstate

\|x₀⟩ := δ³(x - x₀)

is the (rigged-Hilbert-space) eigenvector of the position operator q̂\_i with eigenvalue (x₀)\_i. The map

x₀ ↔ \|x₀⟩

is a bijection between the spatial points of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at time t and the position-basis of 𝓗 at time t. The position eigenstates form a complete (rigged-Hilbert-space) basis of 𝓗:

∫\_{ℝ³} \|x⟩⟨x\| d³x = 𝟙 on 𝓗

and an orthonormal one in the distributional sense:

⟨x₀ \| x₁⟩ = δ³(x₀ - x₁).

The delta-function inner product reproduces, in distributional form, the spatial-distance content of the Minkowski metric: two distinct spatial points have zero overlap (the metric distance is non-zero), and a point with itself has unit overlap (the metric distance is zero). The Hilbert-space inner product of position eigenstates is the function-space rendering of the Minkowski metric’s behavior on spatial points.

The spacetime points and the position eigenstates label each other one-to-one, with the manifold giving the geometric/distance content and 𝓗 giving the algebraic/inner-product content. The two structures are dual representations of the same underlying object.

#### 10.6.3 The dimensionality of 𝓗 as the continuum of McGucken-Sphere radii: the geometric source of “infinite-dimensionality”

The canonical bijection of §10.6.2 establishes that the position basis of 𝓗 at parameter time t has the same cardinality as the spatial slice of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at time t — both are continuum-many, in canonical one-to-one correspondence x ↔ \|x⟩. But this surface-level statement still leaves a deeper question unanswered: *why does the spatial slice of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ supply a continuum of independent perpendicular directions at all?* The orthodox tradition treated the infinite-dimensionality of 𝓗 as an abstract algebraic feature of L²(ℝ³) — the space of square-integrable complex-valued functions on ℝ³ has uncountable cardinality and admits no countable orthonormal basis indexed by a finite-dimensional structure — and supplied no geometric source. Where does the “infinite” come from? *“Because L² is what it is”* is the orthodox answer, followed by a chain of definitions without a manifold-level geometric source.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the source. At every event E ∈ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, the McGucken Sphere 𝓜_E(t) (§2.5 of the present paper) is the wavefront of x_4-expansion from E at parameter time t — a 2-sphere of radius ct in the spatial slice, with each point on the sphere corresponding to one outward-pointing x_4-radius from E along that line. **Each radius is in a perpendicular direction:** by Theorem 3.1 and §4.3, the i-marker for x_4-perpendicularity attaches to every such radial direction, with the geometry of the radius being one specific x_4-direction at E along which the active expansion at rate ic is proceeding. The McGucken Sphere from any single event therefore carries a continuum of perpendicular x_4-radii, one per direction on the 2-sphere — and at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ there is one such sphere with its continuum of radii.

The infinite-dimensionality of 𝓗 is the cascade-level expression of this manifold-level continuum. Each “dimension” of 𝓗 is one specific perpendicular x_4-radius emanating from one specific past event and arriving at one specific spatial point at parameter time t. The path-integral sum that constructs ψ (Definition 2.6) is, in the McGucken reading, the sum over all such arriving x_4-radii at the target spacetime point. The position basis at time t labels the spatial points, each of which is the convergence-locus of a continuum of perpendicular x_4-radii from past events. The continuum cardinality of the position basis — the “infinite-dimensionality” of 𝓗 — is the manifold-level count of perpendicular x_4-radii from McGucken Spheres throughout Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$.

**Proposition 10.7 (Infinite-dimensionality of 𝓗 as the continuum of McGucken-Sphere radii).** *The infinite-dimensionality of the Hilbert space 𝓗 = L²(Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, η_μν) derived in Theorem 6.1 and identified with the function-space rendering of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ in Theorem 10.6 is the cascade-level expression of the geometry of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ enriched with McGucken Spheres at every event:*

*(i) (McGucken Sphere structure at every event.) At every spacetime event E ∈ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, the McGucken Sphere 𝓜_E(t) at parameter time t (§2.5 of the present paper) is a 2-sphere of radius ct in the spatial slice, with each point P ∈ 𝓜_E(t) corresponding to one outward-pointing x_4-radius from E along the line EP. Each radius is in a perpendicular direction (Theorem 3.1, §4.3): the i-marker for x_4-perpendicularity attaches to it, with the radial geometry being one specific x_4-direction at E along which the active expansion at rate ic is proceeding.*

*(ii) (Continuum of x_4-radii per event.) The cardinality of {x_4-radii emanating from E ∈ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$} is the cardinality of the 2-sphere 𝓜_E(t), which is 2\^ℵ₀ for any E. Every event in Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ has a continuum of perpendicular x_4-radii. The radii are not finite-dimensional (the 2-sphere is not a discrete set); they form a continuous manifold of directions at each event.*

*(iii) (Wavefunction as path-integral sum over arriving x_4-radii.) The McGucken wavefunction at spatial point x at parameter time t (Definition 2.6 of the present paper) is the path-integral sum*

\*ψ(x, t) = ∑\_paths exp(iS\[γ\]/ℏ)\*

*over all paths γ from past events to x. In the McGucken reading, each path γ corresponds to one specific x_4-radius from some past event E to x — equivalently, one specific direction on the McGucken Sphere 𝓜_E that arrives at x at parameter time t. The path-integral sum is therefore the sum over all x_4-radii from past events arriving at x at time t. The i in exp(iS\[γ\]/ℏ) is the perpendicularity marker for each contributing x_4-radius (Theorem 3.1); the action S\[γ\]/ℏ supplies the phase per radius normalized by the action quantum (Proposition 2.2).*

*(iv) (Position basis as convergence-locus structure on the spatial slice.) The position eigenstate \|x⟩ of 𝓗 at time t (§10.6.2) is the algebraic encoding of the convergence-locus at x of all x_4-radii from past events arriving at x at time t. The position basis {\|x⟩ : x ∈ ℝ³} at time t has cardinality 2\^ℵ₀, in canonical bijection with the spatial points of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at time t (Theorem 10.6 (iii)) and equivalently with the convergence-loci of perpendicular x_4-radii on the spatial slice.*

*(v) (Infinite-dimensionality of 𝓗 as cardinality of perpendicular x_4-radii.) The dimension of 𝓗 (in the rigged-Hilbert-space sense) is the cardinality of the position basis, which by (iv) is the cardinality of the convergence-loci of x_4-radii on the spatial slice, which by (i)–(ii) is the cardinality of perpendicular x_4-radii emanating from past events through the spatial slice. The “infinite-dimensionality” of 𝓗 is therefore the continuum cardinality of perpendicular x_4-radii from McGucken Spheres at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ — a manifold-level geometric quantity, not an abstract algebraic feature of an arena disconnected from spacetime.*

**Proof.**

*(i)* By §2.5 of the present paper, the McGucken Sphere 𝓜_E at parameter time t centered at event E ∈ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is the locus of points reached by the x_4-expansion from E after proper time t in E’s rest frame, with the expansion proceeding at rate ic per proper time and the spatial-slice projection being a 2-sphere of radius ct. Each point P ∈ 𝓜_E(t) is reached by the expansion along the radial direction from E to P; the x_4-component of the four-vector from E to P has magnitude ict, and the radial direction at E pointing toward P is the outward direction of x_4-advance along that line. By Theorem 3.1, the perpendicularity of x_4 to the spatial directions x₁x₂x₃ at E is marked algebraically by the imaginary unit i in x_4 = ict; the radial direction from E to P inherits this perpendicularity marker because the radial direction *is* the direction of x_4-advance from E toward P at parameter time t.

*(ii)* The 2-sphere 𝓜_E(t) is a smooth two-dimensional manifold homeomorphic to S². Its cardinality is that of the continuum, 2\^ℵ₀. The set of x_4-radii emanating from E is in bijection with the points of 𝓜_E(t) (each radius is uniquely specified by its endpoint on the sphere). Therefore the set of x_4-radii emanating from E has cardinality 2\^ℵ₀. Equivalently, the radii are parameterized by the solid angle Ω ∈ S² and form a continuous manifold of directions.

*(iii)* By Definition 2.6 of the present paper, the McGucken wavefunction at the target spacetime point B is the path-integral sum

ψ(B) = ∑\_γ: A → B exp(i S\[γ\]/ℏ),

with γ ranging over paths from the source event A to B. In the McGucken reading developed in §§2.5, 2.8, 7.4, and 9.2 of the present paper, each path γ from A to B is one specific x_4-trajectory that connects A to B: starting at A, advancing in x_4 at rate ic per proper time, with the path’s spatial component traced by the projection of this x_4-advance onto the spatial slice. The phase exp(iS\[γ\]/ℏ) is the accumulated x_4-phase along the trajectory normalized by the action quantum ℏ (Proposition 2.2). The path-integral sum is therefore equivalently the sum over all x_4-radii from A to B — equivalently, the sum over all directions on the McGucken Sphere 𝓜_A(t_B - t_A) that arrive at the spatial location of B at the parameter time of B. For the more general case of multiple source events (or a uniformly-distributed source over past events on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$), the path-integral sum extends to the sum over all x_4-radii from all past events arriving at the target spatial location at parameter time t.

*(iv)* §10.6.2 establishes the canonical bijection x ↔ \|x⟩ between spatial points of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at time t and position eigenstates of 𝓗 at time t. The position eigenstate \|x⟩ at time t is the algebraic carrier of “the wavefunction is localized at spatial point x at parameter time t.” By (iii), the wavefunction’s value ψ(x, t) at the spatial point x at time t is the sum over all x_4-radii arriving at x at time t. The position eigenstate \|x⟩ therefore corresponds to the convergence-locus of all such x_4-radii at the spatial point x. The position basis {\|x⟩ : x ∈ ℝ³} at time t indexes all spatial points; the corresponding convergence-loci of x_4-radii index the same set; their cardinalities coincide as 2\^ℵ₀.

*(v)* The dimension of 𝓗 (in the rigged-Hilbert-space sense) is the cardinality of the position basis (the rigged-Hilbert-space distributional basis of 𝓗 = L²(ℝ³, d³x)). By (iv), this cardinality equals the cardinality of the convergence-loci of x_4-radii on the spatial slice at time t. By (i)–(ii), each convergence-locus is reached by a continuum of x_4-radii from various past events, and the spatial slice itself is a continuum of such convergence-loci, with the total perpendicular structure being continuum-cardinality at every cascade level. The “infinite-dimensionality” of 𝓗 — what the orthodox tradition treated as an abstract algebraic feature of L²(ℝ³) — is therefore the cascade-level expression of the manifold-level geometric quantity: a continuum of perpendicular x_4-radii from McGucken Spheres at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, with the cascade transferring this manifold-level continuum to the function-space-level infinite-dimensionality without loss. ∎

**Remark 10.8 (The path-integral sum and the position-basis cardinality as the same geometry).** The path-integral construction of ψ (Definition 2.6, Theorem 9.1 of the present paper) and the position-basis cardinality of 𝓗 (§10.6.2, Proposition 10.7 (iv)) are presented in orthodox quantum mechanics as two separate features: the path integral is a *dynamical* construction (Feynman 1948 \[145\]) supplying the time-evolution of ψ; the position basis is a *kinematical* feature of the Hilbert space (Dirac 1930 \[13\]) supplying the algebraic structure on which dynamical operators act. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the two are the *same geometry* at two presentational levels. Each path in the path-integral sum is one specific x_4-radius trajectory from a source event to the target spacetime point (Proposition 10.7 (iii)); the sum over paths is the sum over arriving x_4-radii; the resulting wavefunction at the target spatial point is the convergence of a continuum of radii at that point; the position basis labels the convergence-loci; the cardinality of the position basis is the cardinality of the convergence-loci, which equals the cardinality of perpendicular x_4-radii from McGucken Spheres throughout Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. The Feynman path-integral phase exp(iS\[γ\]/ℏ) and the position-basis cardinality 2\^ℵ₀ are two ways of presenting the same manifold-level structure: the continuum of perpendicular x_4-radii from McGucken Spheres at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$.

**Remark 10.9 (Resolution of the “where do continuous spectra come from” question).** The orthodox treatment of position and momentum as continuous-spectrum observables (Dirac 1930 \[13\], von Neumann 1932 \[14\]) takes the continuity of the spectra as primitive: position has a continuum of possible values because “position is a real number”; momentum has a continuum of possible values because the Fourier dual of position is also continuous. The continuity is assumed as a feature of the kinematical formalism, with no geometric source supplied. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the source via Proposition 10.7. Position has a continuum of values because the McGucken-Sphere wavefront has a continuum of arrival points on the spatial slice — equivalently, because the spatial slice itself is a continuum of convergence-loci of x_4-radii from past events. Momentum has a continuum of values because there is a continuum of directions on the McGucken Sphere 𝓜_E at every event E, and the spatial-direction component of any one of these directions can take any real value; equivalently, because the Compton-de Broglie content of momentum (Proposition 12.10 (ii)) is the rate of x_4-phase accumulation per unit spatial displacement, and that rate can take any real value as the direction on the McGucken Sphere varies continuously. The continuous spectra are not assumed; they are *forced* by the McGucken-Sphere structure of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, with the continuum of radii at every event supplying the continuum of position-eigenvalues at every spatial location and the continuum of directions supplying the continuum of momentum-eigenvalues at every momentum. The fundamental theorem of measurement-theoretic spectra in orthodox QM — that position and momentum have continuous spectra — is in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework a *consequence* of the McGucken-Sphere structure of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ rather than a primitive of the kinematical formalism.

**Remark 10.10 (The “infinite” as the simple, beautiful, compelling idea behind dimensionality).** Wheeler’s 1986 \[144\] statement — *“behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, so compelling that when — in a decade, a century, or a millennium — we grasp it, we will all say to each other, how could it have been otherwise?”* — applies as much to the infinite-dimensionality of 𝓗 as to the foundational mathematical structures of quantum mechanics. The Hilbert space’s “infinite” is the cardinality of perpendicular x_4-radii — a Wheeler-grade simple geometric source for what was treated for a century as an abstract algebraic axiom.

The four-dimensional manifold Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ does not have a fixed four-dimensional Hilbert space attached to it; it has a function space whose cardinality is the continuum count of all perpendicular x_4-directions at all events. The “infinite” of quantum mechanics is the perpendicular x_4-content of the McGucken Spheres covering Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, made cascade-level explicit at the function-space level. each “dimension” of 𝓗 is one specific radius of one specific expanding spherically symmetric wavefront at one specific event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$; the wavefront’s intrinsic kinematic content — its wavelength, frequency, phase, and action — supplies the function-space content of 𝓗 at that cascade level; and the infinite-dimensionality of 𝓗 is the cardinality of the active wavefronts covering all of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. The wavefront-character of x_4-expansion that the McGucken Principle names (§2.1) is the geometric source of the infinite-dimensional Hilbert-space content, with the dynamics — Schrödinger evolution between slices, oscillatory phase along each radius, action accumulation per Planck-frequency oscillation — present in the premise from the start.

#### 10.6.4 Geometric continuity and action discreteness as complementary aspects of dx₄/dt = ic: the resolution of the discrete-vs-continuous debate

The discrete-vs-continuous debate over the foundational structure of spacetime has divided physics for a century. Two camps have emerged with mutually incompatible commitments. The discrete-spacetime camp — causal sets (Bombelli–Lee–Meyer–Sorkin 1987 and subsequent work by Sorkin, Dowker, Henson), loop quantum gravity (Rovelli–Smolin, Ashtekar 1986 and the LQG program), Regge calculus (Regge 1961), spin foams (Reisenberger–Rovelli 1997, Baez 1998) — has argued that spacetime must be fundamentally discrete at the Planck scale to regulate ultraviolet divergences, supply finite black-hole entropy, and provide a quantum-mechanical scale for the gravitational field. The continuous-spacetime camp — standard quantum field theory (Wightman, Glimm–Jaffe), high-precision tests of Lorentz invariance (Mattingly 2005 and the associated experimental program), the Wielandt–Wintner theorem (1948) forcing continuous spectra for canonical position and momentum, and the smooth-manifold structure presupposed by all of mainstream general relativity — has argued that spacetime must be continuous. Each program has confronted the other across decades of foundational dispute, with no resolution: discrete approaches struggle with Lorentz invariance (until the Dowker–Henson–Sorkin causal-set resolution via Poisson sprinklings, gr-qc/0311055); continuous approaches confront the ultraviolet divergences that motivated the discrete programs.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework resolves the debate by recognizing that geometric continuity and action discreteness are **complementary aspects of the same principle** dx₄/dt = ic, at different cascade-level positions in the dx₄/dt = ic framework. Geometry — spacetime points, McGucken-Sphere radii, position and momentum spectra, the Lorentzian metric — is continuous (preserving Lorentz invariance and the empirical record of high-precision tests). Action content — the action accumulated along any worldline through the geometric continuum — is discrete in units of ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance (preserving the quantum-mechanical character of every empirically observed quantum effect). The two are forced together by Proposition 2.2’s twin-constants reading of the McGucken Principle: c sets the rate of geometric (continuous) x_4-advance, ℏ sets the action quantum (discrete) per Planck-frequency oscillation. Neither continuity nor discreteness is bolted on as a separate axiom; both descend simultaneously from the same dx₄/dt = ic at the cogenerative-cascade level.

**Proposition 10.8 (Continuum-discrete duality: geometric continuity and action discreteness as complementary aspects of dx₄/dt = ic).** *The McGucken framework provides simultaneously the geometric continuity of spacetime structure and the action-quantization discreteness of quantum-mechanical content, at different cascade-level aspects of the single principle dx₄/dt = ic. Specifically:*

\*(i) (Geometric continuity is preserved at all cascade levels.) The spatial slice of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at parameter time t is a continuous 3-manifold (cardinality 2\^ℵ₀ for the spatial points; topologically ℝ³ with the standard Lorentzian-metric-induced smooth structure, Lemma 2.5). The McGucken Sphere 𝓜_E(t) at every event E ∈ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is a continuous 2-sphere with a continuum of perpendicular x_4-radii (Proposition 10.7 (i)–(ii)). The position and momentum operators q̂\_i, p̂\_i on 𝓗 have continuous spectra σ(q̂\_i) = σ(p̂\_i) = ℝ (Remark 10.9, Wielandt–Wintner 1948). The Lorentzian metric η_μν is a smooth tensor field on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (Lemma 2.5). All geometry of the dx₄/dt = ic framework is continuum-valued, with Lorentz invariance preserved exactly under the SO(1,3) action on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (Lemma 2.5, §10.6.7).\*

*(ii) (Action discreteness is forced at every Planck-frequency oscillation.) At every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, the x_4-advance along any radial direction of the local McGucken Sphere accumulates action in discrete units of ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation (Proposition 2.2 of the present paper). The discreteness is in *action accumulation\* per oscillation, not in the geometric position at which the oscillation occurs. Every quantum interference effect — double-slit fringes, Aharonov–Bohm, Bohm–Aharonov-like phases in mesoscopic conductors, neutron interferometry, atom interferometry, photon interferometry, Berry’s geometric phase — is the empirical record of this action quantization at the corresponding de Broglie wavelength λ = ℏc/E (Theorem 12.11 instance (9), the universal carrier exp(iS/ℏ) of the path-integral phase).\*

*(iii) (Fundamental wavelength hierarchy.) The natural discreteness scale of x_4-action at energy E is the de Broglie wavelength*

*λ_dB(E) = ℏc/E,*

*the spatial scale at which one full x_4-oscillation accumulates one action quantum ℏ. For a massive particle of rest energy mc², this specializes to the reduced Compton wavelength*

*λ_C(m) = ℏ/(mc),*

For the Planck mass m_P = √(ℏc/G) (where G is the gravitational coupling derived from dx₄/dt = ic via the Einstein field equations in the corpus GR papers \[54–57\]), the reduced Compton wavelength is
