**Remark 10.11 (Why prior continuum-discrete unifications fell short).** Three historically important attempts to combine continuum and discreteness deserve specific comparison.

*Bohr–Sommerfeld old quantum theory (1913–1916).* Bohr’s 1913 paper \[142\] introduced the quantization condition L = nℏ for hydrogen-atomic angular momentum, with continuous classical orbits and discrete action quanta at integer multiples of h. Sommerfeld’s 1916 generalization \[143\] extended this to multi-dimensional systems via ∮ p dq = nh. The action discreteness was correct in the asymptotic semiclassical limit (Maslov-corrected form ∮ p dq = (n + μ/4) h, Theorem 12.11 instance (5)), and the continuous classical content was kept intact. But Bohr–Sommerfeld did not connect the action discreteness to a geometric principle about a perpendicular fourth dimension. The discreteness appeared as a quantization condition imposed externally, not as an intrinsic property of an active geometric expansion. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the upstream principle: the action discreteness is the integer-count structure of ℏ-quanta per Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance (Proposition 2.2), with the McGucken-Sphere structure at every event supplying the geometric source of the oscillations.

*De Broglie matter waves (1924).* Louis de Broglie’s 1924 thesis \[160\] proposed that every massive particle has an associated wavelength λ = h/p, generalizing the Einstein–Planck photon relation to massive matter. The de Broglie relation is exactly the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s reading: λ is the spatial scale of one full x_4-oscillation at momentum p, with each oscillation carrying one ℏ-action quantum. De Broglie’s proposal was the first systematic recognition that matter has a wave character with action-quantized phase. But de Broglie did not connect the wavelength to a geometric principle about a perpendicular fourth dimension; the wave character was attached to the particle as an additional structure rather than as the spatial-slice projection of an active x_4-expansion. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the geometric source: de Broglie’s wavelength is the natural spatial scale at which the particle’s x_4-expansion completes one ℏ-action quantum of phase advance (Proposition 10.8 (iii)).

*Wheeler–Feynman absorber theory (1945).* John Archibald Wheeler and Richard Feynman’s 1945 paper \[161\] proposed a relativistic action-at-a-distance reformulation of electrodynamics, with forward (retarded) and backward (advanced) waves propagating on continuous spacetime and discrete emitter-absorber events supplying the empirics. The continuum-plus-discrete-events structure is in spirit similar to the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s continuum-plus-action-quantization structure, with the discrete events corresponding to the McGucken Wick-rotation events (Theorem 12.2 of the present paper). But Wheeler–Feynman did not connect the discrete events to a geometric reading of x_4 as the perpendicular advancing dimension; the events were absorber-emitter transactions on a passive Minkowski background. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the active-geometric reading: each Wheeler–Feynman absorber event is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, a head-on x_4-collision of two McGucken Spheres (Theorem 7.7), with both particles rotated out of x_4-expansion at the event (the physical Wick rotation of Theorem 12.2). The continuum geometric stage and the discrete absorber events are unified at the cascade level by the McGucken Principle.

The improvement of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework over each of these prior attempts is that **the continuum and the discreteness are two cascade-level aspects of one principle**. Bohr–Sommerfeld and de Broglie added discreteness as a quantization condition on top of continuous classical kinematics. Wheeler–Feynman added discrete absorber events as a separate dynamical postulate on top of continuous spacetime. The McGucken framework derives both from dx₄/dt = ic: c supplies the geometric continuity (rate of x_4-advance, isotropic expansion of McGucken Spheres at every event), ℏ supplies the action discreteness (one quantum per Planck-frequency oscillation), and both are forced simultaneously by the twin-constants reading of Proposition 2.2.

**Remark 10.12 (Comparison with contemporary discrete-spacetime programs).** Four contemporary programs have attempted to put discreteness into the geometric structure of spacetime itself, with varying degrees of success and varying confrontations with the continuum-tests of Lorentz invariance.

*Causal sets (Bombelli–Lee–Meyer–Sorkin 1987 \[162\], Sorkin, Dowker, Henson, and the CST program).* The causal-set program discretizes spacetime points themselves into a locally finite partially ordered set of “elements,” with the order relation supplying the causal structure and the count of elements supplying the volume. Lorentz invariance is recovered statistically via Poisson sprinklings (Dowker–Henson–Sorkin gr-qc/0311055, Bombelli–Henson–Sorkin gr-qc/0605006, “Discreteness without symmetry breaking”). The program is the most ambitious discretization of the geometric structure itself. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s relationship to causal sets: causal-set discreteness lives in the *spacetime-point cardinality* (countable elements rather than continuum); McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework discreteness lives in the *action accumulation along worldlines* (integer multiples of ℏ per oscillation). The two are not direct competitors — they place discreteness at different cascade-level positions. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework preserves the continuum at the spacetime-point level (Theorem 10.6 (iii), Proposition 10.7) while supplying discreteness at the action-accumulation level (Proposition 10.8 (ii)). Causal sets supply a discrete-spacetime model that recovers Lorentz invariance statistically; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies a continuous-spacetime model that maintains Lorentz invariance exactly and provides quantum discreteness via action quantization rather than via point cardinality.

*Loop quantum gravity (Ashtekar 1986 \[163\] with new connection-and-triad variables; Rovelli–Smolin canonical LQG 1990s; Rovelli 2004 \[159\]).* LQG discretizes geometric *operators* — the area operator on a 2-surface and the volume operator on a 3-region have discrete spectra in units of the Planck length squared and cubed respectively — while keeping the spacetime topology continuous. The discreteness is in the *spectra of geometric quantities*, not in the underlying spacetime points. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s relationship to LQG: LQG places discreteness in the geometric spectra (areas, volumes) while keeping the spacetime continuous; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework places discreteness in the action accumulation along worldlines while keeping the geometric spectra continuous (Proposition 10.8 (i), continuous σ(q̂) and σ(p̂)). The two programs make different empirical predictions in principle: LQG predicts geometric quantization observable in principle at the Planck scale (area gaps of order λ_P²); the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework predicts action quantization observable at the de Broglie scale (already empirically confirmed in every quantum interference experiment).

*Regge calculus (Regge 1961 \[164\]).* Regge calculus discretizes the spacetime manifold into a simplicial complex of flat 4-simplices joined at curvature concentrated on 2-dimensional sub-simplices. The discretization is geometric (simplicial complex vs smooth manifold), with Lorentz invariance broken at the lattice scale and recovered (approximately) in the continuum limit. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s relationship to Regge calculus: Regge calculus replaces the smooth manifold Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ with a simplicial approximation, breaking Lorentz invariance at the lattice; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework keeps Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ smooth (Lemma 2.5) and supplies the discreteness elsewhere (in action accumulation). The two are two distinct strategies for the same end (quantum-mechanical discreteness): Regge sacrifices the smooth manifold to discretize the geometry, McGucken keeps the smooth manifold and discretizes the action.

*Spin foams (Reisenberger–Rovelli 1997 \[165\], Baez 1998 \[166\]).* Spin foams discretize the *history* of a quantum-gravitational system into a 2-complex with group representations on edges and vertices, with each spin-foam configuration corresponding to a discrete quantum-gravitational history. The discreteness is in the *combinatorial structure of histories*, not in the underlying spacetime. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s relationship to spin foams: spin foams discretize histories combinatorially, with the geometry emergent from the combinatorial structure; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework keeps the geometry continuous (Proposition 10.8 (i)) and discretizes the action along each history (Proposition 10.8 (ii)). The path-integral structure that supplies the discreteness in both programs differs in where the discreteness lives: spin-foam histories are combinatorial structures; McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework histories are continuous worldlines with discrete action accumulation.

The pattern across all four contemporary programs: each places discreteness at some specific cascade-level position in the geometric or combinatorial structure, with confrontations with Lorentz invariance and other continuum properties of standard physics. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s distinct contribution is to place the discreteness at the *action-accumulation level* — preserving the geometric continuum at every cascade level while supplying the quantum-mechanical discreteness via ℏ per oscillation. This placement is novel against the contemporary literature and resolves the long-standing tension between Lorentz invariance (which demands a continuum) and quantum mechanics (which demands action quantization) by recognizing that the two demands operate at different cascade-level positions, not at competing positions on the same level.

**Remark 10.12bis (Why Planck-scale discreteness and Lorentz invariance coexist: discreteness in the invariant, contraction on the projection).** The trinity conflict catalogued in §1 (Sorkin 1991, 2009; Dowker–Glaser 2013; Belenchia et al. 2015) has a definite mechanical root, and stating it exactly shows why the McGucken placement escapes it. The objection is this: a 3-volume is not a Lorentz invariant. A cube of proper 3-volume $V_0$ measured in a boosted frame has volume $V_0/\gamma$, because one edge Lorentz-contracts by $1/\gamma$ while the transverse edges are unchanged. If the fundamental discreteness were a minimum 3-volume — a lattice of Planck cells, a minimal spatial region — then a sufficiently boosted observer would measure a volume below the supposed minimum ($\gamma$ is unbounded as $v \to c$), which either contradicts minimality or selects the preferred frame in which the cells are minimal, in violation of Lorentz invariance. The argument is sound, and it is fatal to any theory whose discrete objects are regions of a spatial slice.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework discretizes nothing on a spatial slice. What is discrete is the advance of $x_4$ along each worldline, in units of one action quantum $h$ per Compton substrate cycle (§2.2bis; Proposition 2.2; Proposition 10.8(ii)). The $x_4$-advance along a worldline is $X_4[\gamma] = ic\,\tau[\gamma]$ — proper time up to the factor $ic$ (Appendix A, (R4)). Proper time is a Lorentz scalar, and the number of Compton ticks accumulated along a worldline between two events is an invariant count, the same integer for every observer. The framework therefore discretizes an *invariant*; Einstein’s objection contracts a *projection*. The two do not meet: the 3-volume of a cube is a Channel-A coordinate reading of the spatial sector, it Lorentz-contracts by exactly $1/\gamma$ as special relativity demands (the spatial sector remains smooth and boost-covariant, Lemma 2.5), and nothing fundamental is stored in it. A boost mixes the spatial and temporal coordinate axes among themselves — acting on the projection of the $x_4$-advance onto the slice — while leaving the scalar tick count untouched. One cannot Lorentz-contract a scalar.

The logical shape is the same as ordinary angular-momentum quantization, which no one regards as breaking rotational invariance. The operator $\hat L_z$ has a discrete spectrum in integer units of $\hbar$, yet full $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ rotational invariance holds exactly, because what is discrete is the *spectrum of an invariantly-defined operator*, not a grid drawn on space; a rotation does not “contract” a spectrum. Here $x_4$-advance plays the role $L_z$ plays there: its increments are discrete ($h$ per cycle) while the geometry it advances through is continuous and boost-covariant. The paper’s own division of labour makes this precise — the position and momentum spectra $\sigma(\hat q)$, $\sigma(\hat p)$ are continuous (Proposition 10.8(i)); the action accumulated along the worldline is discrete (Proposition 10.8(ii)) — so the discreteness never touches a spatial or momentum *grid*, only the invariant action count.

Two Lorentz-side guarantees make this a theorem of the expansion rather than an assumption placed beside it. First, the metric and its isometry group $\mathrm{ISO}^+(1,3)$ are derived from the Sphere’s cone structure (Lemma 2.5; §17.5bis.1), and the null cone is the envelope of the expanding McGucken-Sphere wavefronts themselves; every boosted observer, re-slicing the same one family of Spheres, finds the same cone and the same $c$, because $c$ is the expansion rate, not a speed within a medium that a fast observer could overtake. Second, the distinguished foliation on which the expansion proceeds — the frame to which the tick count is naturally tied — is physically real (the cosmic-comoving frame, operationally the CMB rest frame) but dynamically cloaked: by the Cloaking Theorem (Theorem 39, Chapter 20), local ruler-and-clock metrology is built from $c$ itself and therefore reads the same physics in every frame, so the foliation the ticks ride is not locally detectable, which is exactly what the relativity of the observable content requires.

The reconciliation in one structure: the universe keeps a discrete pulse — Planck-stepped advance of the fourth dimension, one $h$ per Compton cycle, counted along worldlines — and keeps exact Lorentz invariance for everything measurable, because the pulse is counted in scalars (tick counts along worldlines, action per cycle, operator spectra) while contraction acts only on projections (lengths, 3-volumes, simultaneity slices). The programs that fell to the trinity objection made the projection fundamental and the invariant emergent; the McGucken Principle makes the invariant fundamental — the expansion $dx_4/dt = ic$ — and lets the projections transform as relativity requires.

**Remark 10.12ter (The same discreteness renders one-loop QED finite: the Brillouin-zone support theorem).** The $x_4$-discreteness of Remark 10.12bis has a direct consequence for the ultraviolet behaviour of quantum field theory, developed in the corpus papers \[MG-QFT\] (§3.7) and \[MG-Vanquishing\] (Theorem 1) and summarized here with its scope stated exactly.

*The mechanism.* If $x_4$ is discrete with spacing $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ (the Planck wavelength) while the three spatial directions remain continuous, the loop-integration measure is hybrid: $\mathbb{R}^3$ continuous, $(\ell_P\mathbb{Z})$ discrete along $x_4$. The configuration space is then the locally compact abelian group $G = \mathbb{R}^3 \times (\ell_P\mathbb{Z})$, and by Pontryagin duality its dual group — the momentum space — is $\hat G = \mathbb{R}^3 \times \mathbb{B}$, where the $x_4$-conjugate momentum is confined to the compact first Brillouin zone $\mathbb{B} = [-\pi\hbar/\ell_P, +\pi\hbar/\ell_P]$, of width $2\pi\hbar/\ell_P = 2\pi m_P c$. This is the **Brillouin-zone support theorem** (\[MG-QFT\] §3.7, Theorem III.2): the Fourier transform on the discretely-sampled $x_4$-axis is periodic in the conjugate variable with period $2\pi/\ell_P$, so the unique modes occupy the bounded interval $\mathbb{B}$ — exactly as crystal momentum in a solid-state lattice occupies a bounded Brillouin zone, and by the same Fourier/Plancherel argument (the compactness is a theorem of the discreteness, not an added cutoff). The spatial momenta $\mathbf{p}$ remain unbounded over $\mathbb{R}^3$; only the $x_4$-conjugate direction is bounded.

*The consequence for the one-loop vacuum polarization.* A four-momentum loop integral $\int d^4k\, F(k)$ whose divergence comes from the unbounded $k_4$-integration is rendered finite by structure: the $k_4$-integration runs over the compact $\mathbb{B}$, not over $\mathbb{R}$, so there is no ultraviolet divergence to subtract. For the one-loop photon vacuum polarization, \[MG-Vanquishing\] (Theorem 1) carries the computation through on the hybrid measure and obtains the closed form $I_{\mathrm{hyb}}(\Delta) = 2\pi^2\operatorname{arcsinh}(\pi\hbar/(\ell_P\sqrt{\Delta})) = 2\pi^2\log(2\pi\hbar/\ell_P) - \pi^2\log\Delta + O(\Delta\ell_P^2/\hbar^2)$, in which the standard logarithmic UV divergence is *absent* — not regulated and subtracted, but absent, because the integration domain was always finite. At scales far below the Planck scale the renormalized polarization reproduces the standard one-loop running $\Pi_R(q^2) \to (\alpha/3\pi)\log(q^2/m^2)$, with corrections of order $(m/m_P)^2 \sim 10^{-44}$ at the electron mass. The standard QED running coupling is recovered at every accessible scale; the Planck momentum $2\pi\hbar/\ell_P$ appears as the natural physical upper bound in place of infinity.

*Why this is consistent with Lorentz invariance.* The discreteness that bounds $\mathbb{B}$ is discreteness of the $x_4$-advance, which is proper time up to the factor $ic$ (Remark 10.12bis; Appendix A, (R4)); the spacing $\ell_P$ is therefore a proper-time spacing, a Lorentz scalar, the same in every inertial frame. The bound is on an invariantly-defined conjugate momentum, not on a spatial-momentum grid that a boost could shrink — the same reason, that a discrete angular-momentum spectrum coexists with exact rotational invariance (Remark 10.12bis). The mechanism is not one cutoff among the regulator choices (dimensional, Pauli–Villars, hard cutoff) that break and then restore symmetries by hand; it is a permanent, physical, derived feature of the substrate geometry.

*Scope, stated exactly.* Three boundaries are named honestly, as the source papers name them. First, the hybrid measure is not derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$ *alone*: fixing the spacing at $\ell_P$ requires $\hbar$ (through the one-action-quantum-per-cycle postulate) and $G$ (as an external dimensional input via Schwarzschild self-consistency $r_S = \lambda$ at the substrate scale); deriving the measure from the Principle without these auxiliary inputs is the central open problem recorded in \[MG-Vanquishing\]. Second, the finiteness demonstrated is at *one loop* for the vacuum polarization; higher-loop QED observables on the hybrid measure, and the closed-form reproduction of the running of $\alpha$ matched to the empirical record, are stated as open targets (\[MG-QFT\] (L6), (P1)). Third, whether the compact-$\mathbb{B}$ integration preserves the photon Ward identity $q_\mu\Pi^{\mu\nu} = 0$ term by term is not established in the present corpus and is left open; the finiteness result does not by itself supply the transversality proof. Within these bounds, the result stands: the $x_4$-discreteness that reconciles Planck-scale granularity with Lorentz invariance (Remark 10.12bis) is the same structure that removes the one-loop QED ultraviolet divergence, by bounding the $x_4$-conjugate momentum rather than by renormalization.

#### 10.12quater Relation to Palmer’s Rational Quantum Mechanics: two discrete-substrate programs, one empirical fork

The placement of discreteness in this framework can be sharpened by comparison with a contemporaneous discrete-substrate program that starts from the same Wheeler challenge and reaches an opposite prediction: Palmer’s *Rational Quantum Mechanics* (RaQM) \[Palmer 2026, arXiv:2510.02877v3\]. Both frameworks proceed from the physical conviction — Wheeler’s — that the continuum of Hilbert space conceals a discrete, information-theoretic substrate. Stating the overlaps at full strength first, then the divergences, isolates a clean experimental test that distinguishes the two.

*The shared platform.* Four convergences are real and are recorded in full. First, both programs are responses to Wheeler’s “it-from-bit” and “Law without Law” challenge: Palmer opens by crediting Wheeler’s assertion that continuum Hilbert space conceals an informational character; the present framework’s foundational anchor descends from the same Wheeler lineage (§1.6). Second, both build quantum structure from a *sphere*: Palmer discretizes Hilbert space by imposing rational-number constraints on the Riemann sphere of the Bloch qubit (rational $\cos\theta$ and $\phi/2\pi$); the present framework derives Hilbert space, the inner product, and the Born rule from the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$, the wavefront of the $x_4$-expansion (§7). Third, both hold that continuum Hilbert space is not fundamental but a limit: Palmer’s QM is the singular continuum limit of RaQM as the discretization index $L \to \infty$; the present framework’s Hilbert space is a derived structure cogenerated with Minkowski space from $dx_4/dt = ic$, not a primitive (§10). Both reject Hardy’s continuity axiom as foundational. Fourth, both make the Born rule emergent rather than axiomatic: Palmer reports that in RaQM the Born rule is emergent and not a separate axiom; the present framework derives it by five independent routes (Remark 7.17). This is a substantial shared platform, larger than either program shares with textbook quantum mechanics.

*First divergence: the ontology.* The present framework proceeds from a single physical postulate — the fourth dimension expanding at $c$ from every event, $dx_4/dt = ic$ — from which the discreteness (one action quantum $\hbar$ per Compton cycle of the $x_4$-advance) follows as the stepped character of that one expansion. RaQM’s discreteness is imposed as a number-theoretic admissibility constraint on the basis in which the state is defined, motivated by gravity but not derived from a single physical law. The open question the present framework would put to RaQM is what physical process the rational constraint expresses; the framework’s own answer is the quantized $x_4$-advance.

*Second divergence, and the crux: where the discreteness lives.* RaQM discretizes Hilbert space itself — the amplitudes, the state space, the qubit’s continuum degrees of freedom. The present framework discretizes the $x_4$-advance (proper time, action in units of $\hbar$) and keeps the operator spectra $\sigma(\hat q)$, $\sigma(\hat p)$ continuous (Proposition 10.8(i)), with the $x_4$-conjugate momentum bounded to the Brillouin zone (Remark 10.12ter). The distinction is the subject of Remark 10.12bis: discretizing a space that different observers slice differently invites a frame-dependence question, whereas discretizing the invariant $x_4$-advance (proper time along a worldline, a Lorentz scalar) does not. The question the present framework would put to RaQM is whether its discretized Hilbert space is Lorentz invariant or whether the rational-basis constraint distinguishes a preferred frame.

*On gravity and the scale.* Both programs locate the discreteness scale at gravity: Palmer proposes that the Hilbert-space discretization is due to gravity, with QM the $G \to 0$ limit; the present framework sets the $x_4$-spacing at the Planck length $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$, with $G$ entering through Schwarzschild self-consistency (Remark 10.12ter). The agreement that $G$ sits at the root of quantum discreteness is a genuine convergence. The present framework is explicit that it does not yet derive the Planck-scale measure from $dx_4/dt = ic$ alone (its central open problem); it credits RaQM for making the gravity–discreteness link a concrete, numerically scaled proposal.

*The empirical fork.* The programs part on their predictions, and the parting is testable. RaQM posits a finite qubit information capacity $N_{\max}$, estimated between roughly 200 and 1000, beyond which there is insufficient information to support the continuum degrees of freedom of an $N$-qubit state; RaQM therefore predicts that the exponential advantage of algorithms requiring maximal $N$-qubit superposition/entanglement saturates near $10^3$ perfect qubits, so a quantum computer will not factor a 2048-bit RSA integer — a predicted breakdown of quantum mechanics claimed testable within a few years. The present framework recovers standard quantum mechanics exactly at every accessible scale: its discreteness acts at the Planck scale, with fractional corrections of order $(m/m_P)^2 \sim 10^{-44}$ at laboratory energies (Remark 10.12ter), and imposes no ceiling on coherent large-$N$ superposition short of the Planck scale. The two programs thus make opposite predictions about the same experiment: RaQM predicts saturation of large-$N$ entanglement near $N_{\max} \sim 10^3$; the present framework predicts no such ceiling. The disagreement is decidable by the quantum-computing experiments RaQM identifies — which is the outcome Wheeler’s challenge would call for, two discrete-substrate programs made to differ on an observable.

#### 10.12quinquies The wider descent: general relativity, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, and cosmology as theorem chains from $dx_4/dt = ic$

The discreteness results above are one branch of a wider pattern: from the single physical postulate $dx_4/dt = ic$, the standard structures of four separate domains of physics descend as theorem chains, each link emanating from the Principle at the center rather than from an independent axiom. This subsection states the scope compactly, with each chain cross-referenced to where it is carried out; the point is that the same one expansion is the shared origin of all four.

*General relativity.* From $dx_4/dt = ic$ the framework recovers the relativity of simultaneity, the two postulates of special relativity (Theorem 2.4.5), and the three equivalence principles (weak, Einstein, strong; GR T3–T5). The Newtonian potential arises as the clock-rate gradient forced when the invariant $x_4$-expansion must bridge the proper spatial distance stretched near a mass; the geodesic equation follows from the Principle of Least Action (itself a theorem of the Principle) as the path of maximal proper time. The Einstein field equations descend by the null-surface (Jacobson) thermodynamic route on the McGucken manifold, and the Schwarzschild solution and the FLRW cosmological metric follow as particular geometries. The full development is the GR cascade of twenty-four theorems \[MG-GRChain\] and the physical-foundation treatment \[56\].

*Quantum mechanics.* From $dx_4/dt = ic$, read as Huygens-wavefront at every event (the McGucken Sphere), the framework derives the Hilbert-space inner product, the canonical commutation relation $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ (through the Hamiltonian and Lagrangian channels), the Born rule (five independent routes, Remark 7.17), and the Schrödinger equation as the wave equation of the $x_4$-advance. The present paper is itself the Minkowski–Hilbert cogeneration; the foundational mechanism is \[MG-MQF\] (*The Physical Mechanism Underlying Huygens’ Principle, the Principle of Least Action, Noether’s Theorem, and the Schrödinger Equation*, \[113\]). Both fundamental constants are the two dimensional parameters of the one expansion — $c$ its rate, $\hbar$ its action per cycle — rather than independent empirical inputs of quantum mechanics.

*Thermodynamics and the arrow of time.* The $+ic$ orientation of the expansion supplies a primitive time-orientation carried directly in the dynamics, below the statistical arrow. The second law and the entropic content of horizons descend by the same null-surface thermodynamics that yields the field equations, with the Hawking $1/4$ area coefficient recovered. The arrow of time is not imposed as a low-entropy boundary condition alone; it is the cascade-level expression of the substrate’s forward $+ic$ monotonicity.

*Cosmology.* Treating $\mathcal{M}_G$ as the source space generating the FLRW geometry, the framework produces a cosmological model with **zero free dark-sector parameters**: the dark-sector phenomenology follows from the asymmetry of $x_4$ expanding against the three spatial dimensions, not from tuned constants. The model is reported \[MG-Cosmology, 57\] to place first across twelve independent observational tests for dark-sector and modified-gravity frameworks in the combined empirical record, a ranking achieved without free dark-sector parameters — a parsimony distinguishing it from models that fit each observable with an adjustable constant.

*The unifying content.* That general relativity, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, and cosmology all descend from one geometric principle, with both fundamental constants $c$ and $\hbar$ derived as the expansion’s two dimensional parameters and the dark sector carrying zero free parameters, is the convergent-overdetermination signature of §10.9 read at the largest scale: not four independently-postulated theories later found consistent, but four theorem chains sharing the single origin $dx_4/dt = ic$. The recurrence of the same origin across domains that are usually axiomatized separately is the paper’s central evidence that the Principle is foundational.

#### 10.12sexies Wheeler’s four programs and the contribution of $dx_4/dt = ic$: geometrodynamics, geons, advanced/retarded waves, and it-from-bit

The framework’s placement of the physical primitive can be located precisely against the four major programs by which John Archibald Wheeler sought to reduce the fundamentals of physics — charge, mass, the quantum, and the arrow of time — to something deeper. Each program established a partial result and stalled at a definite obstacle; in each case the obstacle is traceable to the same feature, that Wheeler’s substrate was static, global, or under-specified, and in each case $dx_4/dt = ic$ addresses the obstacle by supplying a substrate that is a local dynamical rate. The four are set out with their achievements and their stalling points, since the contribution is only substantive if it meets the actual obstacle rather than the program’s slogan.

*(i) Geometrodynamics: charge without charge, mass without mass.* Building on Rainich’s 1925 result that the electromagnetic field can be recovered from its stress-energy contribution and hence from spacetime curvature, Misner and Wheeler (1957) developed the “already-unified” theory in which source-free Einstein–Maxwell on a nontrivially connected manifold reproduces particle properties: electric field lines threaded through a wormhole mouth present, to a distant observer, exactly the flux $q = \tfrac{1}{4\pi}\oint_S {\star F}$ of a point charge, with no charged matter present — charge as topology. As a mathematical demonstration this succeeds: a conserved, quantized-flux charge exists with no source term. It stalled on two obstacles. First, stability: the geon and wormhole configurations are dynamically unstable, the throats collapsing to form horizons that hide the multiply-connected topology, so the structures that were to be particles do not persist. Second, the program is classical throughout — it produces charge and mass-energy concentrations but no $\hbar$, no spin, and no discreteness of the charge spectrum, leaving the quantum entirely outside. The obstacle is that the substrate is *static topology*: a frozen handle has no dynamical reason to persist and carries no action scale. The present framework inverts the primitive from static geometry to the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$, from which the metric is derived rather than assumed (Lemma 2.5); charge is a conserved Noether current of the phase symmetry of the $x_4$-advance (§9.5.13.1) rather than a trapped flux in a frozen handle, so there is no throat to collapse, and the same advance that yields the metric carries the action quantum $\hbar$ per cycle (§2.3), reaching the quantum that geometrodynamics did not.

*(ii) Geons: mass without mass.* Wheeler’s geon (1955) was a configuration of electromagnetic or gravitational wave energy held together by its own gravitation, its inertial mass being nothing but the energy $E/c^2$ of the confined radiation — a concrete model of mass as a property of field configuration rather than of substance. The achievement is conceptual: mass is made potentially emergent. The obstacle is again stability — there is no stable geon in pure Einstein–Maxwell; a freely propagating wave resists gravitational confinement and the configuration disperses. The root of the recurring instability is that Wheeler attempted to confine a *traveling* wave using gravity alone. The present framework’s massive particle is not confined radiation but a standing wave in $x_4$: configuration (1) of the four-fold ontology (§2.4), a particle at spatial rest with its full four-velocity budget directed into the $x_4$-advance, oscillating at the Compton frequency $\nu_C = mc^2/h$. A standing wave with a fixed periodicity condition is stable for the reason any resonance is stable, and the periodicity is set by $\hbar$; mass emerges as Wheeler intended, as the frequency of a stable oscillation $m = \hbar\omega_C/c^2$, rather than as the energy of a metastable lump of trapped field.

*(iii) Wheeler–Feynman absorber theory: advanced and retarded waves.* To remove the divergent electron self-energy, Wheeler and Feynman (1945, 1949) made electrodynamics fully time-symmetric: an accelerated charge emits the half-sum of retarded and advanced Liénard–Wiechert fields, $\tfrac{1}{2}(F_{\text{ret}} + F_{\text{adv}})$, and the time-symmetric response of all future absorbers cancels the advanced components, leaving the observed retarded field and supplying the radiation-reaction force without a self-field. Two results stand: the radiation reaction is recovered finitely without self-energy divergence, and the electromagnetic arrow is correctly located — the field equations remain time-symmetric while the arrow enters through the absorber boundary condition, a global constraint, not through the dynamics. The theory stalled at the quantum level: with the discovery of the Lamb shift the self-interaction Wheeler and Feynman had removed proved physically necessary, and Feynman later conceded the theory failed to account for the electron self-energy; it was largely set aside. And the retarded selection was imposed as an external global absorber condition, not derived — the arrow was relocated to the boundary, not explained. The present framework derives the selection locally, from the sign of the expansion, and the two-atom double-slit construction (\[MG-TwoAtom\]) exhibits the derivation in the smallest system that can carry it. Strip the double-slit experiment to one atom $A$ on one side of the partition, one atom $B$ on the other, one excitation, and no room, screen, thermal bath, or detector: $A$ emits, the photon passes the slits, $B$ absorbs. Run it backward — $B$ emits — and the photon does not retrace its wave history. The field equations are $T$-symmetric (the wave, Maxwell, and Schrödinger equations each map to themselves under time reversal), and with a reflecting barrier the two-slit map is unitary and exactly invertible by phase-conjugate boundary data, so neither the equation nor the geometry is the source of the asymmetry: exact reversal would require the advanced solution $G_-$, an extended converging wavefront, whereas a point emitter produces only the outgoing retarded solution $G_+$, and the two agree at no point. The non-retracing therefore reduces to the selection of $G_{\text{ret}}$ over $G_{\text{adv}}$, which is a single sign: the retarded and advanced Green’s functions are the two boundary values $\omega \to \omega \pm i\varepsilon$ of one analytic function, and the arrow is the sign of that infinitesimal displacement. The framework fixes the sign by the chain $+ic \to +i\varepsilon \to G_{\text{ret}} \to$ outgoing emission: the $+$ of the advance in $dx_4/dt = ic$ fixes the orientation of the imaginary time displacement (the infinitesimal form of the Wick identification $t \to -i\tau$, $\tau = x_4/c$, of the Wick-necessity companion), which selects the retarded propagator, which is outgoing emission. The decisive contrast with Wheeler–Feynman is that this system contains *no absorbers beyond the two atoms* — no light-tight box, no cosmological absorber population — so the arrow cannot be the absorber response their theory invokes; it is the local $+ic$ orientation present at the single emission event. The result also sits below the Second Law, since two atoms and one excitation admit no ensemble, no coarse-graining, and no entropy count, so the irreversibility exhibited is present before thermodynamics begins. Wheeler and Feynman’s correct insight that the arrow lives in a boundary condition rather than in the equations is thus retained and its locus moved: from a global constraint on the totality of absorbers to a local ontological fact about each event. Because the framework does not attempt to eliminate the self-interaction — rendering it finite instead through the bounded $x_4$-conjugate momentum (Remark 10.12ter) — it does not incur the Lamb-shift objection that set the original aside.

*(iv) It-from-bit and “why the quantum”.* Wheeler’s final program (1989, 1990) held that every physical entity is information-theoretic in origin — “it from bit” — with the continuum of Hilbert space concealing a discrete, informational substrate, the delayed-choice experiment exhibiting the participatory role of measurement, and “law without law” extending this to the origin of the physical laws. The achievement is the identification of information as a foundational currency and the recognition, later made precise, that the finiteness of information is reflected in the quantum. The program never answered its own central question, “why the quantum”: it-from-bit asserted that reality is informational without deriving the specific structure of quantum mechanics — the complex Hilbert space, the Born rule, the value of $\hbar$ — from an information principle, and it left the participatory role of the observer an unexplained primitive. The present framework supplies the *it* beneath Wheeler’s *bit*, and does so in the precise sense established in §2.3 above: Wheeler held that the continuum of Hilbert space conceals discrete information, and the framework identifies what it conceals — the stepped $x_4$-advance, one action quantum $\hbar$ per Compton cycle, a discrete tick-count along each worldline, which both Minkowski space and Hilbert space freeze out as the two static integrals of the one advance. The bit is not free-floating information registered by an observer; it is the physical action quantum of the wavefront. What it-from-bit asserted the framework derives: the complex Hilbert space from the $x_4 = ict$ structure, the Born rule by five independent routes (Remark 7.17), and $\hbar$ itself as the action per cycle of the advance (§2.3), answering “why the quantum” with the physical expansion of $x_4$. And the observer ceases to be primitive: measurement is the Sphere-collision event at the detection point (§7), a physical process rather than an epistemic act. This is the step from “it from bit” to its converse — the information grounded in a physical process — which Wheeler suspected but did not derive.

*The common thread.* The four programs share one structure: each sought to derive a fundamental of physics from a deeper substrate — charge and mass from geometry, particles from confined fields, the arrow from a boundary condition, the quantum from information — and each stalled because the substrate was static (geometrodynamics and geons: frozen topology that collapses), global (absorber theory: a cosmological condition rather than a local fact), or under-specified (it-from-bit: a program without a derivation). The McGucken Principle pursues the same reductive aim with a substrate of a different kind: not static geometry, not a global constraint, and not abstract information, but a single local dynamical rate, $dx_4/dt = ic$, instantiated at every event. Because it is dynamical the structures it builds do not collapse; because it is local it requires no cosmological boundary condition; because it is a definite equation it derives rather than asserts. It is the continuation of Wheeler’s project — geometry and information unified in one expanding wavefront — carried out with the one ingredient the earlier programs lacked, a physical primitive that moves.

#### 10.12septies The two-atom double slit: a primitive time orientation below thermodynamics, derived in full from dx₄/dt = ic

The Wheeler–Feynman subsection above located the time-orientation contribution of $dx_4/dt = ic$ against absorber theory. This subsection gives the argument in full, self-contained, as the minimal exhibition of the Principle’s arrow: a two-atom system in which the retarded selection of a time-symmetric field equation is shown to be a single sign, and that sign is derived from $+ic$. The construction and all results transcribe the companion paper \[MG-TwoAtom\]; the theorems are renumbered here as 10.12S.1–10.12S.11 to avoid collision with the flagship numbering, and the equation labels are local to this subsection.

*The thought experiment.* Take the double-slit experiment and remove everything removable: the room, the glass, the screen, the thermal bath, the detector electronics. What remains is a partition with two apertures, one atom $A$ on side $M$, one atom $B$ on side $N$, and one excitation. Atom $A$ emits; the photon passes the partition; atom $B$ absorbs. Run it the other way — atom $B$ emits — and ask whether the photon retraces its path to $A$. Two readings must be separated: whether $A$ ever absorbs, and whether the forward process is run backward. It reaches $A$ with the forward interference weight (Theorem 10.12S.5) and retraces the forward wave history with probability zero. The system is minimal by construction: two degrees of freedom and one field, no ensemble, no coarse-graining, no entropy count. Whatever irreversibility survives here is present before thermodynamics begins, and the conclusion is that it is the choice of the retarded solution of a time-symmetric field equation, a sign on the time coordinate, and that $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the single statement from which that sign follows.

*Setup.* Let side $M$ be the half-space $z<0$, side $N$ the half-space $z>0$, and the partition the plane $z=0$ with aperture function $T(x,y) = 1$ on $S_1 \cup S_2$ (the two slits) and $0$ otherwise. Atom $A$ sits at $\mathbf{r}_A$ with $z_A<0$; atom $B$ at $\mathbf{r}_B$ with $z_B>0$. Work first with a scalar field for a monochromatic excitation, $\psi(\mathbf{r},t) = U(\mathbf{r})\,e^{-i\omega t}$, $k=\omega/c$; the spatial part obeys the inhomogeneous Helmholtz equation with the emitting atom as source,
$$(\nabla^2 + k^2)\,U(\mathbf{r}) = -\delta(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}_{\rm src}). \tag{S.1}$$
The analysis carries over verbatim to the vector Maxwell field and to the Schrödinger wave of a massive particle, each being time-reversal invariant in the sense of Theorem 10.12S.1 with retarded and advanced Green’s functions related as in (S.3). The barrier is reflecting in the first five theorems and absorbing in Theorem 10.12S.8; the two cases differ, and the difference is part of the content.

**Theorem 10.12S.1 (T-invariance).** *The wave equation $\square\,\psi = -4\pi\rho$, the source-free Maxwell equations, and the Schrödinger equation with real potential are each invariant under time reversal: if $\psi(\mathbf{r},t)$ is a solution, so is $\psi(\mathbf{r},-t)$ (wave; Maxwell with $\mathbf{B}\to-\mathbf{B}$) or $\psi^*(\mathbf{r},-t)$ (Schrödinger).*

*Proof.* For the wave equation $\partial_t^2$ is even in $t$. For Maxwell, the substitution $t\to-t$, $\mathbf{E}\to\mathbf{E}$, $\mathbf{B}\to-\mathbf{B}$, $\mathbf{j}\to-\mathbf{j}$ maps the equations to themselves. For Schrödinger, complex conjugation of $i\partial_t\psi = H\psi$ with $H$ real gives $-i\partial_t\psi^* = H\psi^*$, the original equation in $-t$. ∎

This is standard (Jackson §6.10; Sakurai §4.4); it is stated because the rest turns on it — the equation does not orient time, so whatever orients time is added to it. The Helmholtz equation (S.1) has two Green’s functions,
$$G_\pm(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r}') = \frac{e^{\pm ik|\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}'|}}{4\pi|\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}'|}, \tag{S.2}$$
which with the time factor $e^{-i\omega t}$ are the retarded (outgoing, $G_+$) and advanced (incoming, $G_-$) solutions, related by
$$G_-(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r}') = G_+(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r}')^*. \tag{S.3}$$
Both satisfy (S.1); the equation is indifferent between them. This is the Ritz–Einstein point of 1909.

**Proposition 10.12S.2 (Forward amplitude).** *Atom $A$ emits the retarded solution $U_A(\mathbf{r}) = G_+(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r}_A)$. With a reflecting barrier, the field on side $N$ is given by the Rayleigh–Sommerfeld integral over the aperture plane,*
$$U_A(\mathbf{r}_N) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\iint T(x,y)\,U_A(x,y,0^-)\,\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\!\left(\frac{e^{ikL_N}}{L_N}\right) dx\,dy, \qquad L_N = |\mathbf{r}_N - (x,y,0)|, \tag{S.4}$$
*and the probability that $B$ absorbs is proportional to $|U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)|^2$, the two-slit interference weight at $\mathbf{r}_B$.*

*Proof.* Kirchhoff–Rayleigh–Sommerfeld diffraction for an aperture in a plane screen (Born and Wolf §8.3); the restriction to $S_1 \cup S_2$ is the two-source coherence producing interference at $\mathbf{r}_B$. ∎

Denote the forward field on all of side $N$ by $U_A|_N$; it is an extended field determined on the entire half-space by the aperture data, and $U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)$ is one value of it.

**Theorem 10.12S.3 (Exact reversal requires the advanced solution).** *The time-reverse of the forward process is the solution $U_A^*$. On side $N$ it is the incoming, phase-conjugate field $U_A^*|_N$, which converges through the apertures onto $\mathbf{r}_A$; it is the advanced solution $G_-(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r}_A)$ restricted to the two-slit geometry.*

*Proof.* Apply Theorem 10.12S.1 to the forward solution: $\psi_A(\mathbf{r},t) = U_A(\mathbf{r})e^{-i\omega t}$ maps to $\psi_A(\mathbf{r},-t)$, spatial part $U_A^*(\mathbf{r})$; by (S.3), $U_A^* = G_-(\cdot,\mathbf{r}_A)$ filtered by $T$, incoming on $\mathbf{r}_A$. ∎

**Theorem 10.12S.4 (A point emitter produces the retarded solution).** *Atom $B$ re-emitting produces $U_B(\mathbf{r}) = G_+(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{r}_B)$, the outgoing spherical wave centered on $\mathbf{r}_B$, its restriction to the aperture plane $z=0^+$ having phase fixed by the distance from $\mathbf{r}_B$ to each point of $S_1\cup S_2$.* Which of $G_\pm$ describes emission is a property of the emitter, and it is the retarded one.

**Theorem 10.12S.5 (Non-retracing).** *With a reflecting barrier, the re-emission from $B$ does not retrace the forward path. The field on side $M$ is*
$$U_B(\mathbf{r}_M) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\iint T(x,y)\,U_B(x,y,0^+)\,\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\!\left(\frac{e^{ikL_M}}{L_M}\right)dx\,dy, \tag{S.5}$$
*an extended diffraction pattern over side $M$. The probability that $A$ absorbs is proportional to $|U_B(\mathbf{r}_A)|^2$, and by Helmholtz reciprocity $U_B(\mathbf{r}_A) = U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)$, so the return probability equals the forward interference weight at $B$, which is strictly less than the total weight over side $M$.*

*Proof.* By Theorem 10.12S.3, exact retracing requires the boundary data $U_A^*|_{z=0^+}$, the conjugate of the forward field, an extended converging wavefront. By Theorem 10.12S.4, $B$ supplies $U_B|_{z=0^+}$, the restriction of an outgoing spherical wave. The two agree at no point in general; the overlap of $U_B|_N$ with $U_A^*|_N$ is the single complex number $\langle U_A^*, U_B\rangle \propto U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)^{*}$, one component of the continuum exact reversal requires. The remainder of $U_B$ diffracts afresh through the apertures and spreads over side $M$ by (S.5); reciprocity $G_+(\mathbf{r}_A,\mathbf{r}_B) = G_+(\mathbf{r}_B,\mathbf{r}_A)$ gives the return amplitude. ∎

**Corollary 10.12S.6 (The asymmetry is not geometric).** *The map from the field on side $M$ to the field on side $N$ through a reflecting two-slit partition is unitary on the transmitted subspace and is inverted exactly by the conjugate boundary data of Theorem 10.12S.3. The double-slit geometry therefore does not produce the irreversibility; its role is to spread the boundary data exact reversal requires over an extended aperture, so the mismatch between the required incoming wavefront and the outgoing wavefront a point atom supplies is visible at every point of the aperture plane.*

*Proof.* The reflecting barrier conserves the field norm; transmitted and reflected components are orthogonal projections. Phase conjugation of the transmitted field, propagated back, reconstructs $U_A$ on side $M$ (Theorem 10.12S.3); this is realized experimentally by time-reversal mirrors (Fink 1992). ∎

The reading in which the partition “discards information” so that geometry alone forbids reversal is therefore wrong: with a reflecting barrier nothing is discarded, the blocked component returns into side $M$ and remains in the system, and reversal fails for one reason only — the emitter is oriented.

**Theorem 10.12S.8 (Absorption adds non-unitarity).** *If the barrier absorbs, the blocked component $U_A\,[1-T]$ leaves the two-atom-plus-field system. The forward evolution restricted to that system is non-unitary, and the reverse process initiated by $B$ has no access to the absorbed component; exact reversal then fails even with conjugate boundary data on side $N$.*

*Proof.* The absorbed component is transferred to barrier degrees of freedom outside the system; a reversal prepared on side $N$ alone reconstructs at most the transmitted component $U_A\,T$, and the reconstructed field on side $M$ differs from $U_A$ by the back-propagation of $U_A[1-T]$. ∎

Theorems 10.12S.5 and 10.12S.8 are independent: the first holds with a reflecting barrier and no absorption, the second with conjugate boundary data and no point-emitter restriction. Only the first survives when everything removable is removed, and it is the one the thought experiment isolates.

**Theorem 10.12S.10 (Retarded selection is a sign choice).** *The retarded and advanced Green’s functions of the wave operator are the two boundary values of the same analytic function,*
$$\tilde G(\mathbf{k},\omega) = \frac{1}{k^2 - \omega^2/c^2}, \qquad G_{\rm ret} \leftrightarrow \omega \to \omega + i\varepsilon, \quad G_{\rm adv} \leftrightarrow \omega \to \omega - i\varepsilon, \tag{S.6}$$
*and the choice between them is the sign of the infinitesimal imaginary displacement of the frequency, equivalently the sign of the imaginary part of the time coordinate in the Fourier kernel $e^{-i\omega t}$.*

*Proof.* The poles of (S.6) at $\omega = \pm ck$ are displaced into the lower half $\omega$-plane by $+i\varepsilon$, so the inverse transform vanishes for $t<0$ (retarded); the opposite displacement gives vanishing for $t>0$ (advanced). ∎

This is the exact location of the asymmetry: the equation is symmetric (Theorem 10.12S.1), emission is oriented (Theorem 10.12S.4), and the orientation is the sign in (S.6). Every account of irreversibility at the level of a single emission event must supply that sign, and the accounts differ in what they add to the field equation to supply it — Ritz (1908–1909) adds a rule, use $G_+$; Wheeler–Feynman (1945) adds a perfect-absorber boundary condition on the totality of absorbers; the standard thermodynamic account adds a low-entropy initial condition. None derives the sign from a prior kinematic fact about events.

**Theorem 10.12S.11 (The Principle selects the retarded propagator).** *Under $dx_4/dt = ic$, the Fourier kernel of time evolution acquires the imaginary displacement of Theorem 10.12S.10 with the sign fixed by the $+$ of $+ic$, so that the Green’s function selected is $G_{\rm ret}$. Emission from a point atom is therefore outgoing as a consequence of the Principle.*

*Derivation.* The Principle identifies the direction of advance in $x_4$ with the direction of increasing $t$ through $x_4 = ict$: as $t$ increases, $x_4$ moves in the $+i$ direction. The Wick substitution $t \to -i\tau$, $\tau = x_4/c$, is under the Principle the coordinate identification between $t$ and the advance in $x_4$ rather than an analytic continuation (Theorem 6 of the Wick-necessity companion \[MG-Wick\]). The $+i\varepsilon$ prescription of (S.6) is the infinitesimal form of that identification: displacing $\omega$ by $+i\varepsilon$ is equivalent to giving $t$ a small imaginary part of sign fixed by the orientation of $x_4$-advance, and $+ic$ fixes that orientation as $+$. With the displacement sign fixed, Theorem 10.12S.10 yields $G_{\rm ret}$, and a point source then emits the outgoing wave $G_+$, which is Theorem 10.12S.4. ∎

**Corollary 10.12S.12 (The two-atom double slit exhibits the Principle’s orientation).** *In the two-atom experiment, non-retracing (10.12S.5) follows from point emission being outgoing (10.12S.4), which follows from 10.12S.11, which follows from $dx_4/dt = ic$. The experiment therefore exhibits, in a single emission event with no environment and no statistics, the time orientation that the Principle yields.* Under the Principle the same $+ic$ that orients emission generates the expanding McGucken Sphere from every event, and the interference weight $|U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)|^2$ of Proposition 10.12S.2 is the Born weight carried by the SO(3)-Haar measure on that Sphere (Remark 7.17), so in this system the orientation of emission and the interference weight at $B$ have a common origin.

The comparison of accounts is set out in Table 10.12S.A, McGucken far-left.

*Unitarity: the operator and the realized process.* The system separates two claims the word “unitary” usually joins.

**Proposition 10.12S.15 (The evolution is unitary).** *With a reflecting barrier, the field evolution from any state on side $M$ to the corresponding state on side $N$ is norm-preserving and invertible (Corollary 10.12S.6).*

**Proposition 10.12S.16 (The realized process is not the unitary inverse of the forward process).** *The forward process ends with the excitation localized on $B$. The reverse process, initiated by $B$, ends with the excitation localized on $A$ with probability $|U_A(\mathbf{r}_B)|^2$ and elsewhere on side $M$ otherwise. In neither direction is the final state the image of the initial state under $U$ or $U^{-1}$: each process ends in a definite absorption, and the step from the extended field $U_B|_M$ to the excitation on one atom is a projection, not a unitary map.*

*Proof.* $U_B|_M$ is an extended field with support over side $M$ (S.5); absorption by a single atom takes it to a state supported on one atom, a projection onto that atom’s excited state with weight $|U_B(\mathbf{r}_A)|^2$, and a projection is not norm-preserving on the full field. ∎

Both propositions hold, and they are compatible: unitarity is a property of the evolution operator between emission and absorption, while the realized process contains two further steps, the oriented emission (Theorem 10.12S.4) and the localized absorption (Proposition 10.12S.16), neither of which is an instance of the unitary operator. Two quantities present at the start of the reverse process are absent at its end: the extended field $U_B|_M$ with its value at every point of side $M$ (after $A$ absorbs, those values are gone), and the advanced solution $G_-$ (of the two solutions the equation permits, one is realized and the other discarded before propagation begins). The two-atom system contains no environment into which to defer the projection: either the projection occurs and the field values on the rest of side $M$ are lost, or the excitation remains spread over side $M$ and $A$ has not absorbed.

**Proposition 10.12S.19 (The measured event is what exists).** *In the two-atom system the measurement is absorption at $A$. That event is oriented (Theorem 10.12S.4), definite (Proposition 10.12S.16), and not the reverse of the forward event (Theorem 10.12S.5); information is lost when it occurs. The unitary operator predicts the weight of the event and contains no orientation and no outcome. Under $dx_4/dt = ic$ the orientation of every event is fixed by law, and the measured orientation is a theorem (Theorem 10.12S.11).* Physics being defined by what is measured, and the measured event here being oriented, definite, and irreversible, the operator-level statement that evolution is unitary between emission and absorption holds of the operator and does not transfer to the realized process — the reversibility is a property of the mathematics, the irreversibility of the outcome is the physics. This is the minimal system in which the three components — unitary evolution, oriented emission, localized absorption — can be separated and named, and it exhibits the $+ic$ orientation with two atoms, one partition, one excitation, and one measurement.

#### 10.12octies Why dx₄/dt = ic derives what must otherwise be posited by hand: a reply to Kinney

> *The supreme task of the physicist is to arrive at those universal elementary laws from which the cosmos can be built up by pure deduction. There is no logical path to these laws; only intuition, resting on sympathetic understanding of experience, can reach them.* — A. Einstein, “Principles of Research,” for Max Planck’s sixtieth birthday, Berlin, 23 April 1918.
>
> *It can scarcely be denied that the supreme goal of all theory is to make the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible without having to surrender the adequate representation of a single datum of experience.* — A. Einstein, “On the Method of Theoretical Physics,” the Herbert Spencer Lecture, Oxford, 10 June 1933.

Will Kinney argues (X thread, 13 July 2025, https://x.com/WKCosmo/status/2076665681727099069) that three rules of physics are added by hand and cannot be derived from within a theory: (1) that the time direction in Minkowski space encodes causal order; (2) that the proper time along a worldline is the time a comoving clock reads; (3) the Born rule. He holds that to demand their derivation is a category error, since a formalism without a correspondence rule is mathematics rather than physics.

The premise is correct: a theory must posit its first principles. Newton posited $F = ma$ and universal gravitation; Einstein posited the constancy of $c$ and the equivalence of inertial and gravitational mass. A principle is a posit — that is what a principle is, and every theory has them. “You posit something by hand” is therefore true of all of physics and singles out nothing. What distinguishes theories is the count: how much observed physics is derived, from how few posits, which is the goal Einstein names in the second epigraph.

The primitive here is $dx_4/dt = +ic$, the physical expansion of the fourth dimension at the rate $c$ from every event, and Minkowski space and Hilbert space are derived from it — Minkowski as the integral $\int ic\,dt = ict$, Hilbert as the same advance with its modulus frozen (§2.3). Kinney’s three rules are external only in a different setting: when the primitive is a static object. A metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ is invariant under $t \to -t$ and fixes no future; a Hilbert space is a complex vector space and carries no probability rule. From those static primitives the three rules must be added, and Kinney is right. They are not the primitive here. Because $dx_4/dt = +ic$ already carries a direction and a rate, the three rules are properties of it, not additions to it.

*Causal order is the sign.* $dx_4/dt = ic$ — the fourth dimension physically expands at the rate $c$ from every event — is the geometric expansion of the McGucken Sphere from which time and all its arrows and asymmetries derive. The expansion carries a direction: increasing $t$ is the $+i$ direction of the advance. Integrating the oriented rate is a single act that yields three things at once: the coordinate $x_4 = \int ic\,dt = ict$, which is the fourth axis of Minkowski space (Lemma 2.5); the future orientation of that axis, since the $+$ of $+ic$ selects the future nappe of the light cone; and the causal ordering carried by that orientation. Minkowski space and its arrow are therefore not assembled separately and then linked — the same integration delivers the manifold already oriented, and the retarded-over-advanced choice follows from the same sign through the chain $+ic \to +i\varepsilon \to G_{\text{ret}}$ (Theorem 10.12S.11). This is the direct answer to the first of Kinney’s rules: the causal ordering is not added to Minkowski space after the fact, because it arrives with Minkowski space, in the one act of integrating the oriented rate. The causal arrow, the thermodynamic arrow, and the radiative arrow are three readings of the one oriented expansion.

*Proper time is the advance counted along a worldline.* Under $dx_4/dt = ic$, the expansion of $x_4$ at the rate $c$ is what a worldline accumulates and what a clock counts. A rest mass is a standing wave in $x_4$ at $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$; a clock counts those cycles; the accumulated advance is $X_4[\gamma] = ic\,\tau[\gamma]$, which is proper time up to the factor $ic$. “A clock reads proper time” is then “a counter of $x_4$-cycles counts $x_4$-cycles” — one physical quantity, not a bridge between a geometric arc length and a clock reading. This is the move statistical mechanics made in identifying temperature with mean molecular kinetic energy.

*The Born rule is the measure on the Sphere.* $dx_4/dt = ic$ generates the expanding McGucken Sphere at every event, and the Born rule is the unique SO(3)-invariant probability measure on that Sphere (Remark 7.17; Haar-uniqueness, Lemma 7.1.5). Measurement is the Sphere-collision at the absorbing event (§7, Proposition 10.12S.16), not an act requiring an outside observer.

Three independent posits — causal order, the proper-time rule, the Born rule — collapse to one, $dx_4/dt = +ic$: the sign gives the arrow, the rate gives the clock, the invariant measure on the generated Sphere gives Born. No datum of experience is surrendered.

Kinney supplies the test for a category error: it is made when one invokes quantities that cannot be measured even in principle. The inflationary multiverse fails the test, deriving unobservable universes and breaking when they are used in a calculation. $dx_4/dt = ic$ passes it, running the other way: the same $+ic$ fixes the retarded propagator (advanced radiation is never observed), sets $\hbar$ as the action per cycle (measured in the Compton frequency and the de Broglie wavelength), and gives an FLRW cosmology with zero free dark-sector parameters (twelve observational tests). It is tied to more measurement, not less.

*Scope.* All three cases are theorems of the framework. Causal order follows from the sign of the advance (Theorem 10.12S.11); the proper-time identity is established in §2.4 (proper time as the x₄-arc-length $X_4[\gamma] = ic\,\tau[\gamma]$), with a clock realized as a counter of Compton cycles; the Born measure is Theorem 7.2, established by five independent routes and the Haar-uniqueness Lemma 7.1.5. One item remains open, and it is narrower than the objection supposes: the Born theorem proves that any probability measure on the Sphere must be $|\psi|^2$ and locates the outcome in a physical collision event, but it does not by itself derive why an individual collision yields one definite outcome rather than another. That question is open. The claim of this subsection is one posit doing the work of three, each as a theorem, tested by the measurable content the posit forces — not physics from pure mathematics, which would be Kinney’s category error made real.

#### 10.12nonies A physical mechanism for nonlocality, entanglement, and time’s arrows: what the expansion distributes and what it orients

$dx_4/dt = ic$ — the fourth dimension physically expanding at the rate $c$ from every event — supplies a physical mechanism for three things that other frameworks take as primitive or leave unexplained: the nonlocality of entangled systems, the origin of entanglement itself, and the arrow of time. Each is a consequence of the expansion, and the consequences are different in kind: the expansion *distributes* what is local at a source into what appears nonlocal on a spatial slice, and it *orients* time by the sign of the advance. This subsection states the mechanism and marks precisely what is derived and what is posited.

*The expansion distributes locality into nonlocality.* Two systems co-emitted at an event $p_0$ ride the same expanding McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$. A photon has $v_{x_4} = 0$ — it is at rest in $x_4$ (§2.4, configuration 2) — so along each co-emitted worldline the accumulated $x_4$-advance is the same: $X_4(A) = X_4(B) = ic\,t_0$ for all later parameter values, independent of spatial separation. The two systems are therefore, in the fourth dimension, at one coordinate value forever, however far apart they move in the three spatial dimensions. What an observer reads on a spatial slice — a correlation between distant outcomes with no signal passing between them — is the three-dimensional projection of that four-dimensional coincidence. The correlation is not a signal distributed across space at emission and stored; it is the shadow, on the slice, of a coincidence the expansion carries forward in $x_4$. This is the content of the two nonlocality laws of the corpus (\[MG-Nonlocality\], \[MG-Equiv\]): first, that the $x_4$-coincidence of co-emitted systems persists at any spatial separation; second, that the measured Bell correlation is the spatial-slice projection of that persisting coincidence. Entanglement, on this reading, is not a correlation two systems carry independently — it is a single geometric fact about one shared Sphere, read on a slice that has separated the two systems in space while the expansion has kept them coincident in $x_4$.

*The mechanism supplies what “spooky action” names but does not explain.* The nonlocality of quantum mechanics is standardly stated and not mechanized: Bell’s theorem shows the correlations cannot come from local hidden variables, and the frameworks that take the correlations seriously (Bohmian mechanics, the various collapse and many-worlds readings) posit the nonlocal state and analyze its consequences rather than deriving where the nonlocality comes from. $dx_4/dt = ic$ gives the origin: the correlated systems share an $x_4$-coordinate because they share a Sphere, and the Sphere is the wavefront of the one expansion. The “action at a distance” is not action and not across a distance — it is coincidence in the fourth dimension, projected as apparent distance in the three. No influence propagates; the geometry was never separated in the dimension that carries the correlation.

*Causality is preserved because what is distributed is correlation, not signal.* The reduced state at either system is maximally mixed, so the marginal outcome distribution at $A$ is independent of the measurement setting at $B$: no choice at one end changes the statistics at the other, and no signal is sent (the no-signaling content of §6.6.8 and of \[MG-Nonlocality\]). This is the same structure the framework enforces elsewhere through the Dual-Cloaking Theorem 6.6.8.2: the $x_4$-advance is real and shared, and it is cloaked from local metrology, so the coincidence carries correlation without carrying a usable channel. The expansion distributes correlation, never signal — which is exactly the condition special relativity imposes and which the standard “spooky” language leaves as a coincidence to be marveled at rather than a consequence to be derived.

*Time and its arrows are oriented by the sign of the advance.* The same expansion that distributes the correlation orients time, and it does so by a different feature — not the sharing of the advance but its *sign*. $dx_4/dt = +ic$ has a direction built in; integrating the oriented rate gives Minkowski space already oriented (§10.12octies), and the retarded-over-advanced selection of radiation follows from the sign through the chain $+ic \to +i\varepsilon \to G_{\text{ret}}$ (the two-atom double-slit result, §10.12septies, Theorem 10.12S.11). The thermodynamic arrow follows from the same monotonic advance: the accessible phase-space volume grows as the McGucken Sphere expands, so entropy increases in the direction of the advance, and the Second Law is the statement that $x_4$ advances one way. The causal arrow, the radiative arrow, and the thermodynamic arrow are three readings of the one oriented expansion — not three independent facts to be separately postulated, but three projections of the sign of $+ic$. This is the physical mechanism for time’s asymmetries that a static block manifold cannot supply: a block universe with a $t \to -t$-symmetric metric has no oriented feature to distinguish past from future, and the arrow must be added by a low-entropy boundary condition (the Past Hypothesis); the oriented expansion carries the direction intrinsically, so the boundary condition is replaced by the sign of the rate.

*Why this is unique to a physical, expanding primitive.* The three results have a common requirement that only a physical, oriented, expanding primitive meets. Nonlocality distributed as a projection requires the correlated systems to be coincident in a real dimension that the spatial slice does not resolve — a static configuration-space state (wave-function realism) locates the correlation in a high-dimensional arena but has no expansion to distribute it and no mechanism relating the arena to the slice; a wormhole connection (ER=EPR) posits a static geometric link but no generating dynamics. The arrow of time oriented by the primitive requires the primitive to carry a sign — a static directed line (Maudlin’s Theory of Linear Structures) has an orientation posited as an axiom of the line, not derived, and generates no nonlocality at all. Only a rate with a direction — $dx_4/dt = +ic$ — both distributes the correlation (by expanding, sharing the advance across co-emitted worldlines) and orients time (by its sign), from the one posit. *Scope.* The $x_4$-coincidence of co-emitted systems (Theorem 10.12S.4 photon rest in $x_4$; the persistence law of \[MG-Nonlocality\]) and the no-signaling marginal (§6.6.8.2) are theorems. The identification of the measured Bell correlation with the spatial projection of the $x_4$-coincidence is the corpus’s central nonlocality claim (\[MG-Nonlocality\], \[MG-Equiv\]); it reproduces the singlet correlation and saturates the Tsirelson bound. What remains open is the same item flagged in §10.12octies — why an individual measurement yields one definite outcome — which is a feature of the measurement question, not of the nonlocality mechanism: the mechanism explains why the outcomes are correlated and why no signal passes, which is what “nonlocality” names.

#### 10.12decies A physical mechanism for holography and the emergence of space: the bulk dimension is the expansion

The holographic principle — that the information in a region is bounded by its boundary area, and that a bulk gravitational theory is encoded on a lower-dimensional boundary — is, in the standard treatment, a discovery without a mechanism. ’t Hooft and Susskind proposed it from black-hole entropy; Maldacena, Gubser–Klebanov–Polyakov, and Witten made it precise as AdS/CFT; but why holography holds, what the extra bulk dimension physically is, and what physically emerges when “space emerges” are left open. $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies the mechanism, and the mechanism is the same expansion that carries the nonlocality of §10.12nonies: the bulk dimension along which the boundary is holographically encoded is $x_4$, and its physical expansion is what does the encoding.

*The bulk radial dimension is the expansion.* In the AdS/CFT correspondence the boundary theory lives on the spatial directions and the bulk has one additional dimension, the radial coordinate $z$, along which bulk physics unfolds from the boundary. The corpus AdS/CFT paper (\[MG-AdSCFT\]) identifies this radial coordinate as the scaled $x_4$-advance: $z \propto L^2/x_4$, with the conformal boundary $z \to 0$ the asymptotic slice and the interior the region of small $x_4$-advance (its Proposition III.1). The “one extra dimension” of holography is therefore not a coordinate chosen to match symmetry groups; it is the physical fourth dimension of the McGucken Principle, and the “radial evolution into the bulk” that the standard account leaves physically unspecified is the $x_4$-expansion at rate $c$. This answers the question the standard treatment cannot: there is exactly one extra dimension to encode against because there is exactly one expanding dimension, $x_4$.

*The master equation is the $x_4$-path integral.* The GKP–Witten dictionary $Z_{\text{CFT}}[\varphi_0] = Z_{\text{AdS}}[\varphi|_\partial = \varphi_0]$ — the statement that boundary observables are computed by the bulk path integral with fixed boundary data — is, on this reading, the ordinary path integral of the framework rewritten as a boundary-to-bulk correspondence: the boundary spatial observables are computed by the $x_4$-advance path integral with the boundary values fixed at the asymptotic slice (\[MG-AdSCFT\], Proposition IV.1). The bulk-boundary equality holds because both sides compute the same physical process — the $x_4$-expansion from the boundary into the interior — read from two ends. The duality is not a conjecture matched by consistency checks; it is two parametrizations of one expansion.

*The area law and the Ryu–Takayanagi surface.* The reason information scales with boundary *area* rather than bulk volume is the reason of §10.12ter and the black-hole entropy derivations (\[MG-Bekenstein\], \[MG-Hawking\]): the horizon, and more generally any null hypersurface, supports one $x_4$-stationary mode per Planck area $\ell_P^2$, so the mode count on a bounding surface of area $A$ is $A/\ell_P^2$, giving $S = A/4\ell_P^2$ with the $1/4$ from the Euclidean cigar geometry of the McGucken–Wick rotation. The Ryu–Takayanagi formula $S(A) = \text{Area}(\gamma_A)/4G_N$ is then the statement that the entanglement entropy of a boundary region is the area of the minimal $x_4$-extremal surface anchored on its edge (\[MG-AdSCFT\], Proposition VIII.1) — the surface is the $x_4$-extremal bulk locus separating the region’s $x_4$-trajectories from its complement’s, and its area counts the $x_4$-modes crossing between them. The RT surface, left physically unidentified in the standard account, is a surface in the expanding fourth dimension, and its appearance as a nonlocality surface (§10.12nonies) is the same fact: the boundary entanglement it measures is the $x_4$-coincidence structure read across the bulk.

*Holography is the greater Huygens principle.* Underlying all of this is a single geometric identification the corpus makes explicit: Huygens’ principle — every point of a wavefront is a source of the next — is the holographic principle, with each point on the surface of a McGucken Sphere acting as a secondary source for the bulk wavefront, the count of surface points (one per Planck cell) giving the Bekenstein bound, and the encoding operating at every event rather than only at horizons or AdS boundaries (\[MG-Point\], Theorem 15.1; \[MG-AdSCFT\]). The bulk is generated by the boundary points expanding into the interior, event by event — this is the “generative” content the standard AdS/CFT dictionary, which relates two pre-existing theories without a generating mechanism, does not supply. AdS/CFT is recovered as the special case where the McGucken Sphere boundary lies at conformal infinity and the radial coordinate is the rescaled $x_4$.

*The emergence of space now has a mechanism, and it runs both ways.* The emergent-spacetime programme (Sakharov, Jacobson, Verlinde, Van Raamsdonk, Cao–Carroll–Michalakis, and Jacobson’s 2025 statement that the metric is not separately fundamental but encoded in the vacuum) has argued for sixty years that spacetime is emergent from a deeper substrate, but has supplied the direction (metric from vacuum) without the mechanism and without the reciprocal direction. $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies both: Minkowski space is the coordinate integral of the advance and Hilbert space is the modulus-frozen advance (§2.3), so the metric and the quantum state are two frozen readings of the one expanding primitive, each extractable from the other because both descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every event (\[MG-Point\], §1.10). “Space emerges” is, mechanized, “the expansion is integrated into a coordinate,” and the holographic encoding of a bulk on a boundary is “the expansion carries the boundary points into the interior.” The programme’s convergence — that seven independent emergent-spacetime approaches point at the same substrate — is what a correct mechanism predicts: they are reading, from different directions, the one expansion that generates the arena.

*Why only a physical expanding dimension supplies this.* The holographic extra dimension carries correlation and encodes a bulk, and it must do so without being a static re-description. A static emergent radial direction (the standard RG-scale reading of the AdS radial coordinate) is a translation of boundary data, not a physical process, and cannot say what the dimension *is* or why there is exactly one; a static wormhole (ER=EPR) carries the correlation but does not expand and cannot generate the bulk. The McGucken bulk dimension is a real dimension expanding at $c$: it is what the boundary points expand into, so it both *is* the extra dimension holography requires and *generates* the bulk holography encodes. This is the same reason, from §10.12nonies, that only an oriented expanding rate distributes nonlocality — holography and nonlocality are the same expansion read at two scales, the boundary-bulk encoding at the cosmological and horizon scale and the entanglement coincidence at the pair scale.

*Scope and the empirical fork.* The identification of the AdS radial coordinate with the scaled $x_4$-advance, the master equation as the $x_4$-path integral, and RT as the $x_4$-extremal-surface area are the theorems of \[MG-AdSCFT\] (Propositions III.1, IV.1, VIII.1); the black-hole entropy coefficient $1/4$ and the Hawking temperature are the theorems of \[MG-Bekenstein\] and \[MG-Hawking\]. What is inherited as input rather than derived is stated in those papers: the specific internal manifold ($S^5$ for the original Maldacena pair) and $G$ are not derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$ alone.
