The framework’s cosmological extension (\[MG-CosHolo\]) replaces the AdS bulk, which our universe does not have, with the FRW/de Sitter McGucken horizon, and yields a sharp empirical fork: the ratio of the McGucken horizon to the Hubble horizon at recombination is $\rho \approx 2.6$, so the cosmological holographic entropy differs from Hubble-horizon holography by $\rho^2 \approx 7$ — a quantitative signature in the early-universe entropy structure that distinguishes the McGucken mechanism from standard horizon holography, and that AdS/CFT, having no cosmological application, does not address.

#### 10.12undecies The uniqueness of the expanding fourth dimension as the 4D foundation of both general relativity and quantum mechanics

The preceding sections derive, from dx₄/dt = ic, the Lorentzian metric of general relativity (§2.3, §2.4.4) and the complex-projective and measure-theoretic structure of quantum mechanics (§7, §10.12nonies). This raises the question the framework is finally in a position to address: among all 4D geometric primitives, is the expanding fourth dimension the unique one that can underlie both theories, and is it the simplest? The answer has three parts of different logical status, stated here in order of strength, with the scope of each marked precisely.

*The removing-the-i result, on which the theorem rests.* The imaginary unit in dx₄/dt = ic is load-bearing, in a sense made exact by what its removal does. At the metric level, forming the four-coordinate line element ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² + dx₄² and substituting dx₄ = ic dt gives dx₄² = i²c²dt² = −c²dt², so ds² = dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² − c²dt², the Lorentzian signature (−,+,+,+); the single algebraic fact i² = −1 is the entire origin of the minus sign that distinguishes time from space and supplies causal structure (§2.3, Lemma 2.5). Replace the imaginary axis by a real coordinate w = cτ and dw² = +c²dτ², giving the Euclidean signature (+,+,+,+) — a static 4-geometry with no time direction, no light cones, no causality. At the dynamical level, the null relation (ict)² + r² = 0 gives r = ct, a real sphere expanding at c, because the negative x₄² from i² balances the positive r²; with the i removed, w² + r² = const is a static 4-sphere, not an expanding wavefront. At the quantum level, the i is the perpendicularity of x₄ to the three spatial dimensions (Theorem 5.1), and it is the same i that carries the quantum phase $e^{-iEt/\hbar}$ (§2.3), the commutator $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ (§5.2), the momentum operator $\hat{p} = -i\hbar\,\partial_x$, and the Kirchhoff quarter-wave factor (§4.3); removing it removes the complex phase (hence interference and the Born rule, which requires a complex ψ), the non-commutativity (hence the uncertainty relation and the quantum inner product), and the wavelength-carrying wavefront (hence ℏ). The controlled removal of the i is the Wick rotation t → iτ (\[MG-Wick\]), which carries the Lorentzian/quantum face (i present) to the Euclidean/statistical face (i removed). The result, stated once: the i is simultaneously the Lorentzian signature, the expansion-versus-static distinction, and the entire quantum structure; its removal collapses the framework to static 4D Euclidean space with no time, no causality, and no quantum.

*Part 1: uniqueness within the class of single-law 4D geometric primitives (a theorem).* Let a candidate 4D foundation be a geometric primitive consisting of a four-coordinate carrier with one dynamical law for the advance of a fourth coordinate relative to a parameter, subject to four conditions: (a) its integrated form induces a Lorentzian metric of signature (−,+,+,+) — the requirement that it be the arena of general relativity; (b) it carries a complex phase whose modulus-square is a normalizable, spatially isotropic measure — the requirement that it be the arena of quantum mechanics in the Born sense; (c) it is spatially isotropic, with no preferred spatial direction; (d) it has a single dynamical rate, not a family of rates.

**Theorem (uniqueness of the 4D foundation).** *Any geometric primitive satisfying (a)–(d) is dx₄/dt = ic, up to a positive scaling of c and the choice of future orientation.*

*Proof.* Write the candidate law as dx₄/dt = f, with the fourth coordinate x₄ a priori complex-valued and f to be determined. Four forcing steps fix f ≡ ic.

Condition (a) forces the imaginary direction. By the removing-the-i result, a Lorentzian induced metric of signature (−,+,+,+) requires dx₄² \< 0 on the constraint, i.e. dx₄² real and negative. Writing f = a + ib with a, b real, dx₄² = f²dt² = (a² − b² + 2iab)dt²; reality of the induced dt²-coefficient requires 2ab = 0, so a = 0 or b = 0, and negativity of the coefficient requires a² − b² \< 0. The case b = 0 gives f = a real and a² ≥ 0, violating negativity; hence a = 0 and f = ib with b ≠ 0. The fourth coordinate advance is therefore purely imaginary — the i is forced by the GR-arena condition, not assumed.

Condition (b) forces the wavefront and its wavelength. A complex phase with a normalizable, spatially isotropic modulus-square measure is a spherically symmetric wavefront carrying a periodic phase; the periodicity is a wavelength, and a wavelength on an advance at rate \|f\| = \|b\| carries an action per cycle, an ℏ. The QM-arena condition therefore requires the primitive to be an isotropic wavefront with a wavelength — consistent with, and reinforcing, the imaginary advance of (a), since the same i carries the phase whose modulus-square is the measure.

Condition (c) forces sphericity. Spatial isotropy is SO(3)-invariance of the law under rotations of the three spatial coordinates. By the spherical-symmetry argument (the vanishing of any spatial directional coefficient, §2.4.4, and Lemma 23 of \[MG-Reciprocal\]), the only SO(3)-invariant spatial vector is zero, so the advance has no spatial component and its wavefront cross-section is a round 2-sphere. The wavefront of the primitive is the McGucken Sphere.

Condition (d) fixes the magnitude and sign. With f = ib purely imaginary (a), an isotropic wavefront (b, c), and a single rate (d), the only remaining freedoms are \|b\| and the sign of b. The invariant propagation speed of the wavefront is \|f\| = \|b\|; identifying this with the invariant speed c gives \|b\| = c. The future-orientation of the advance (the requirement that the metric’s time direction be future-directed) selects b = +c over b = −c. Hence f = +ic.

Therefore any primitive satisfying (a)–(d) is dx₄/dt = ic up to the scaling of c (a unit choice) and the orientation sign (a convention), which is the statement of the theorem. *QED.*

This upgrades the uniqueness clause of the Reciprocal-Generation theorem (\[MG-Reciprocal\], Theorem 27), whose premises were the form of a first-order ODE, to a theorem whose premises are the arena-conditions of general relativity (a) and quantum mechanics (b) directly: the i is forced twice over, once by the Lorentzian signature and once by the complex Born measure, and the sphericity and rate follow from isotropy and single-law economy.

*Part 2: simplicity, in the precise sense of minimal posits (an argument, not a theorem).* Simplicity here means the fewest independent posits per derived phenomenon — the derivation ratio of §10.12octies. The primitive dx₄/dt = ic is one dynamical law (a rate, a sign, an isotropy), from which the Lorentzian metric, ℏ, the Born rule, and the arrow of time descend (§2.3, §7, §10.12nonies). The standard foundation posits Minkowski space, Hilbert space, the Born rule, ℏ, and a low-entropy boundary condition as separate inputs. Each alternative 4D-adjacent foundation in the literature adds ingredients beyond a single law: the Euclidean-relativity primitive removes the i and must reintroduce the quantum structure by hand; the qubit-Lorentz reconstructions posit the state-space sphere together with a selected inner product; the causal-set primitive posits a partial order together with a growth law. Among known 4D foundations, dx₄/dt = ic carries the minimal posit count and the highest derivation ratio — one law from which both arenas and their constants descend. This is a bookkeeping statement, verifiable by counting posits against derived results; it is not a proof that no simpler primitive can exist.

*Part 3: scope of the unconditional claim.* The theorem of Part 1 establishes uniqueness within the class of single-law 4D geometric primitives satisfying (a)–(d); it does not establish that no foundation of any other kind could underlie general relativity and quantum mechanics. An unconditional “only possible foundation” claim would require quantifying over all conceivable geometries, including ones not yet formulated, and no such proof exists for any foundational theory in physics — not for the Standard Model as the only possible particle content, nor for general relativity as the only possible theory of gravity at tested scales. The defensible statement is therefore the conjunction of Parts 1 and 2: dx₄/dt = ic is the unique single-law 4D geometric primitive satisfying the arena-conditions for both theories (Part 1, a theorem), and the minimal-posit, highest-derivation-ratio such primitive known (Part 2, an argument), with no alternative achieving the same unification from fewer or equal posits known. The claim is uniqueness within a precisely specified class together with minimality among known foundations, not unconditional sole possibility — which is both the strongest and the most defensible form the answer can take.

#### 10.12duodecies Gravity is the Born rule: both are the count of x₄-states on the expanding Sphere

Two connections are well established in the literature and are separately reproduced in this framework: gravity is entropy, and the Born rule is entropy. The first is the thermodynamic derivation of the field equations — Jacobson’s δQ = TδS on local causal horizons, Verlinde’s entropic force, Padmanabhan’s equipartition, the entanglement-equilibrium school (Jacobson 2015; Bueno–Min–Speranza–Visser; Alonso-Serrano–Liška), and the recent quantum-relative-entropy action of Bianconi (*Gravity from entropy*, Phys. Rev. D 111, 066001, 2025). The second is the identification of the Born rule with an entropy or information geometry — Zurek’s derivation from entanglement-assisted invariance (envariance) (Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 120404, 2003; Phys. Rev. A 71, 052105, 2005), Fivel’s derivation from information-entropy axioms with an entropy-reduction axiom (arXiv:1010.5300; Found. Phys. 42, 291, 2012), Ojima–Okamura–Saigo’s derivation from algebraic and statistical axioms on von Neumann algebras (arXiv:1304.6618), Chiribella–D’Ariano–Perinotti’s operational reconstruction from purification and information axioms (Phys. Rev. A 84, 012311, 2011), Carcassi and Aidala’s equivalence of the Born rule over pure states with the von Neumann entropy over mixed states (Assumptions of Physics, 2026), the derivation of the Born weights by relative-entropy minimization (“Born’s Rule from Contextual Relative-Entropy Minimization,” Entropy 27, 898, 2025), and the Fubini–Study = Fisher–Rao lineage from Wootters (1981) onward that makes the Born rule the unique map equating the state-space metric to the statistical metric. What no work in either literature does is close the triangle: gravity is entropy and the Born rule is entropy, but no established result states that gravity is the Born rule. The reason is derivational, and it is what the McGucken Principle removes.

*Why the triangle stays open in the standard treatment.* The two entropy-connections use two different, independently-posited entropies. The gravitational side uses a horizon or geometric entropy — Bekenstein–Hawking area entropy, or entanglement entropy across a causal diamond. The Born side uses a state-space entropy — von Neumann entropy of a density matrix, or relative entropy on the observable algebra. These are distinct objects living in distinct spaces (a horizon in spacetime; a density matrix in Hilbert space), related only by name. With two different entropies, the transitive step gravity = entropy = Born rule cannot be completed: the entropy on the left is not the entropy on the right. The single work that comes closest, Munkhammar’s “Is Holographic Entropy and Gravity the result of Quantum Mechanics?” (arXiv:1003.1262), inserts the Born density $|\psi|^2$ as a source for the holographic entropy in Verlinde’s construction, but uses the Born density as an input to entropic gravity rather than identifying the two, and leaves the relativistic origin open. Süzen (arXiv:1612.00288) similarly couples Verlinde’s entropic gravity to Diósi–Penrose gravity-induced collapse, relating the gravitational constant to the quantum state, again a coupling rather than an identification. In the opposite direction, Valentini (“Beyond the Born Rule in Quantum Gravity,” Found. Phys. 52, 2022) argues that at the fundamental Wheeler–DeWitt scale the Born rule does not hold and emerges only in the semiclassical regime — a position the present framework answers directly, since here the Born rule is the invariant measure of the Sphere at every event and holds wherever dx₄/dt = ic generates a Sphere, which is everywhere, with the semiclassical horizon regime being the integrated rather than the local reading of the same measure.

*The McGucken identification.* In this framework both entropies are one physical quantity: the count of x₄-advance states on the expanding McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$, generated at every event $p$ by dx₄/dt = ic and carrying the unique SO(3)-invariant Haar measure (Theorem 7.2). The Born rule is that Haar measure evaluated at the event: the Sphere-to-Hilbert cogeneration makes the inner product and the Born probability $p = |\langle\psi|\phi\rangle|^2$ the Haar measure of $\Sigma_+(p)$ read as a probability measure on rays, so $|\psi|^2$ is the measure of the Sphere restricted to the point-event. Gravity is the same Haar measure integrated over the horizon: the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy $S = A/4\ell_P^2$ is the count of Planck-scale Spheres tiling the horizon 2-surface (§10.12ter, §10.12decies; refs. \[MG-Bekenstein\], \[MG-Hawking\]), one x₄-stationary mode per Planck area, and the Hawking temperature is the near-horizon compactification of the Euclidean-section x₄-axis (the McGucken–Wick rotation, \[MG-Wick\]). Verlinde’s entropic gravity is then the horizon-scale statement of the same measure that gives the Born rule at the event scale. It would be an oversimplification to assign gravity to the Geometric Channel and the Born rule to the Algebraic Channel of the McGucken Duality, as though the identification were a cross-channel bridge — one physical fact reached by two mathematical routes that meet by external construction. Both channels derive both quantities, and this four-corner completeness is what places the identification below the channel decomposition, at the level of the Sphere itself. In the Geometric Channel, the Sphere gives gravity through its null hypersurfaces and the Jacobson relation δQ = TδS (Verlinde, Jacobson, Padmanabhan), and it gives the Born rule through the Fubini–Study metric on its rays, which Wootters identifies with the Fisher–Rao statistical distance. In the Algebraic Channel, the Sphere gives gravity through the metric read as a quantum operator whose quantum relative entropy is the gravitational action reducing to Einstein–Hilbert in the low-coupling limit (Bianconi), and it gives the Born rule through its SO(3)-Haar measure pulled back to Hilbert-space rays as $p = |\langle\psi|\phi\rangle|^2$. Each channel independently sees both facts from its own vantage; if a channel gave only one endpoint, gravity = Born rule would be a cross-channel coincidence, but the four-corner completeness shows both quantities are facts about the shared Sphere and its Haar measure, so every channel that accesses the Sphere sees both. The channel-independence is what places the equality at the Sphere level rather than at the channel level: gravity and the Born rule are the same fact about $\Sigma_+(p)$, before any channel decomposition, and the Duality’s two channels are two confirmations of it rather than its two halves. The entropy that links them is one entropy, $S = k\ln\Omega$, where $\Omega$ is the number of x₄-advance states the Haar measure distributes over — the same $\Omega$ whose horizon projection is the gravitational entropy. The chain closes:

$$\text{gravity} = \text{Haar measure of } \Sigma_+ \text{ integrated over the horizon} \;\longleftrightarrow\; S = k\ln\Omega \;\longleftrightarrow\; \text{Haar measure of } \Sigma_+ \text{ evaluated at the event} = \text{Born rule.}$$

Gravity is the Sphere’s Haar measure integrated over the horizon; the Born rule is the Sphere’s Haar measure evaluated at the event; both are measure-theoretic readings of the one physical fact dx₄/dt = ic at different scales of integration. This is the transitive step the literature cannot take, and the framework takes it not by a new postulate but because it has a single physical measure — the Haar measure of the Sphere at every event — where the standard treatment has two coincidentally-named entropies.

*Scope.* What is derived independently is each endpoint: gravity from the horizon mode-count (the Jacobson route on the Sphere, §10.12ter, with $S = A/4\ell_P^2$ from \[MG-Bekenstein\], \[MG-Hawking\]), and the Born rule from the surface invariant measure (Theorem 7.2). The identification gravity = Born rule is the transitive consequence of both being the same x₄-state count on the one Sphere — the gravitational entropy is the boundary reading and the Born measure the surface reading of a single $\Omega$. The claim is that the two entropy-connections of the literature, kept separate there by using two different entropies, are one connection here because the framework’s entropy is a single physical count; it is a unification of the two established results, not an additional posit.

#### 10.12terdecies The derived Hilbert space and the Carcassi–Lemos debate: physicality from a physical origin

A recent exchange bears directly on the object this paper derives. Carcassi, Calderón and Aidala argue in “The unphysicality of Hilbert spaces” (*Quantum Stud.: Math. Found.* 12, 2025; arXiv:2308.06669) that the completeness of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space forces in physically untenable elements: states with infinite expectation values, and transformations carrying finite expectations to infinite ones. Their concrete example pairs the Gaussian $\psi(x) = (e^{-x^2}/\sqrt{\pi})^{1/2}$, whose moments $\langle x^n\rangle$ are all finite, with $\phi(x) = (1/\pi(x^2+1))^{1/2}$, whose moments above the first diverge; the change of variables $y(x) = \tan(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\operatorname{erf}(x))$ maps $\psi$ to $\phi$, and a time-dependent version makes the expectation oscillate between finite and infinite in finite time. Since changes of variables are unitary, they conclude Hilbert space treats physically inequivalent states as equivalent, and propose Schwartz space — whose elements have all polynomial moments of position and momentum finite, and which is the unique space closed under Fourier transform — as the physically appropriate alternative. Lemos replied (“Are Hilbert Spaces Unphysical? Hardly, My Dear!,” *Found. Phys.* 55, 2025) that the argument conflates an active coordinate transformation with a change of basis: a change of basis transforms states and operators together and leaves expectation values invariant, so the position operator must be transformed alongside the state. Carcassi, Rozite and Aidala responded (arXiv:2507.09738) that the transformation is meant actively, in Shankar’s sense — states transform while operators are left alone, as in a genuine physical transformation such as time evolution — so the finite-to-infinite mapping stands.

The framework does not need to adjudicate the active-versus-passive dispute, because it removes the premise both sides share: that the starting object is a bare infinite-dimensional Hilbert space with completeness imposed and no physical governor on which states are admissible. Here the Hilbert space is not primitive; it is derived from dx₄/dt = ic (§2.3, §6.1), and the derivation fixes the physical domain that both the pathology and the debate turn on.

The physical states of the framework are not the whole completed space but the McGucken-derived Schwartz domain $\mathcal{S} \subset \mathcal{H}$: the Sphere wavefunctions of rapid decay that arise as finite Sphere superpositions with Gaussian source-event distributions (§6.4.5, Lemma 6.1.6; and the self-adjointness construction of §6.6.8, where $\hat q$ and $\hat p$ are established as essentially self-adjoint precisely on $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^3)$). This is exactly the space Carcassi proposes as the physical one — the Schwartz class, all polynomial moments finite, closed under Fourier transform — but here it is not chosen as a better axiom; it is the domain the physics delivers, because a Sphere wavefunction sourced by a Gaussian event distribution is Schwartz-class by construction. Carcassi’s runaway example lives outside this domain: $\phi = (1/\pi(x^2+1))^{1/2}$ has power-law rather than rapid decay and is not a Sphere wavefunction, so the transformation that manufactures it does not act within the physical states of the framework. The finite-to-infinite mapping is real on the bare completed space and excluded on the derived Schwartz domain, and the framework occupies the derived domain from the start.

The position this yields is a third one, distinct from both parties. Carcassi holds that Hilbert space is unphysical and should be replaced by Schwartz space; Lemos holds that the standard Hilbert-space formalism is sound as it stands. The framework grants Carcassi’s diagnosis — a bare complete space admits states and transformations with no physical governor, and the physically appropriate states are the Schwartz class — while declining his conclusion that Hilbert space must be discarded. Hilbert space is physical when it is derived from a physical primitive that carries its own domain of admissible states; taken as a free-standing complete space it lacks that governor, which is what Carcassi correctly detects and what the derivation supplies. The Schwartz domain that Carcassi reaches by proposing a better space, the framework reaches by deriving the space from dx₄/dt = ic: the Sphere wavefunctions are Schwartz-class because their sources are Gaussian, so the moment-finiteness Carcassi wants is a consequence of the physical origin rather than an additional mathematical requirement.

*Scope.* What the framework establishes is that its physical states form the derived Schwartz domain (§6.4.5, §6.6.8), which is the space Carcassi identifies as physically appropriate. It is a separate matter that the x₄-conjugate momentum is additionally bounded to the Brillouin zone by the x₄-discreteness (Remark 10.12ter); that bound is on the x₄-direction, not on the spatial moments of Carcassi’s example, and is not invoked here. The claim is the Schwartz-domain one: the physical restriction Carcassi proposes is, in this framework, derived rather than posited, which resolves his objection while retaining the Hilbert space Lemos defends — the space is kept, and given the physical domain whose absence generated the dispute.

#### 10.12quaterdecies Minkowski space and Hilbert space as higher-entropy readings that conceal the Sphere: the classical limit as loss of x₄-resolution

Carcassi, Landini and Aidala show that classical mechanics is the high-entropy limit of quantum mechanics (*Physica Scripta* 101, 065105, 2026; arXiv:2411.00972): high entropy masks quantum effects, and mixed states of sufficiently high entropy are approximated by classical distributions. Their mechanism is coarse-graining — a stretching map spreads a state over more phase-space cells, the concentric spheres of equal entropy in the Bloch ball crowd together, and distinguishable structure (interference, phase, non-commutativity) becomes unresolvable. Their key identity is that entropy is the logarithm of the count of states measured in units of $\hbar$, so the mathematical limit $\hbar \to 0$ is the same as setting the entropy of pure states to $-\infty$; physically $\hbar \to 0$ means $S \gg 0$. The result is explicitly independent of interpretation and of the mechanism that raises the entropy.

This limit has a direct reading in the framework, and it extends the concealment result of §2.3. There the two arenas are the two frozen integrals of the one cycling advance: Minkowski space is the coordinate integral $\int ic\,dt = ict$, which removes the ℏ-cycling by integrating it into a continuous coordinate, and Hilbert space in its measured face is the modulus-frozen advance, in which the Born-squaring annihilates the phase. Each arena is obtained from the McGucken Sphere by an operation that discards a distinguishable structure — the cycle-count in the Minkowski case, the phase in the Hilbert case — and discarding a distinguishable structure is, in Carcassi’s exact sense, raising the entropy of the description by the logarithm of the number of collapsed alternatives. The concealment of §2.3 and the high-entropy masking of Carcassi are therefore the same operation: the two arenas are higher-entropy readings of the Sphere, and the Sphere is the lower-entropy object both readings coarse-grain.

The correspondence is exact on Carcassi’s own state-counting. The entropy that hides the quantum is $S = k\ln\Omega$ with $\Omega$ the count of x₄-advance states in units of ℏ (§10.12duodecies), and the two concealments are two ways of summing over that count. Minkowski space sums over the x₄-cycles: integrating $ic\,dt$ into $x_4 = ict$ coarse-grains the individual ℏ-ticks into a continuous coordinate, so the cycle-structure is entropy-averaged away and the metric is the geometric high-entropy reading. Hilbert space in its Born face sums over the phase: the modulus-squaring discards the phase exactly as Carcassi’s maximally mixed two-slit state makes a mixture of phases indistinguishable from a mixture of paths (his §2.3), so the Born density is the probabilistic high-entropy reading. Both are the same $\Omega$ coarse-grained, read on the two channels of the McGucken Duality (§10.12duodecies): the geometric channel produces the Minkowski high-entropy reading, the algebraic channel the Hilbert one, and the fully-resolved low-entropy object beneath both is the expanding Sphere with its cycles and phase intact.

Carcassi’s $\hbar \to 0$ then has a geometric meaning the framework supplies. Since ℏ is the wavelength of the Sphere — the action per Compton cycle — $\hbar \to 0$ is the limit in which the Sphere’s wavelength shrinks below every resolved scale, so the discrete x₄-advance is coarse-grained into a continuum and the wavefront looks classical. This is Carcassi’s $S \gg 0$: the classical limit is the loss of x₄-resolution, the regime where the Sphere’s ℏ-cycles are too fine to distinguish. The McGucken Sphere is thus Carcassi’s low-entropy limit — the fully-resolved object of which classical mechanics, and with it the static Minkowski manifold and the phase-frozen Born density, are the high-entropy shadows.

*Scope.* Two entropies are in play and are identified here only where they coincide. Carcassi’s is the von Neumann entropy of mixed states; the §2.3 concealment is an information coarse-graining that integrates the cycles and freezes the phase. The two agree for these specific structures because the cycle-count and the phase are genuine distinguishable degrees of freedom whose loss is a state-count increase — the concealment is entropy-increasing in Carcassi’s sense because it sums over distinguishable x₄-structure. The claim is confined to this: the coarse-graining that produces Minkowski space and the Born density from the Sphere is entropy-increasing because it sums over the resolved x₄-cycles and phase, so both arenas are higher-entropy readings of the Sphere and the classical limit is the loss of x₄-resolution. It is not claimed that every concealment in the framework is thermodynamic entropy, only that these two are. Carcassi’s closing question — whether quantum mechanics is the only theory that recovers classical mechanics at high entropy — is the high-entropy face of the uniqueness result of §10.12undecies: within the class of single-law 4D geometric primitives, dx₄/dt = ic is the unique one whose fully-resolved structure yields both arenas and has the classical, high-entropy description as its coarse-grained limit.

#### 10.12quaterdecies-bis The QM–thermodynamics–classical triangle: the i as phase-preservation marker, Wick rotation as its analytic absorption, and the high-entropy limit as its coarse-graining, with the Sphere as a Compton-temperature KMS state

The classical limit of §10.12quaterdecies and the third-law/entropy-floor material of §10.12quindecies are two of three regimes joined to quantum mechanics, and the McGucken Principle organizes all three by the treatment of the single imaginary unit in dx₄/dt = ic. The i is the phase-preservation marker: it is what makes the Sphere’s expansion phase-carrying rather than amplitude-only, and phase is what distinguishes a pure state from a mixed one. Three operations remove or transform the i’s role, each yielding a different regime, and it is essential to keep straight that one of the three is a change of language while the other two are limits.

*The i explicit — quantum mechanics.* With the i present, the advance carries phase: the evolution is unitary, $e^{-iHt/\hbar}$; the path-integral weight is oscillatory, $e^{iS/\hbar}$; the commutator is $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$; the coordinate is $x_4 = ict$. Low entropy is possible; pure states ($S = 0$) exist. This is the fine-grained, phase-resolved reading of the Sphere.

*The i absorbed — thermodynamics, via Wick rotation.* The Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$, equivalently $x_4 = ict \to x_4 = c\tau$, absorbs the i into a real Euclidean coordinate. The Lorentzian signature $(-,+,+,+)$ becomes Euclidean $(+,+,+,+)$; unitary $e^{-iHt/\hbar}$ becomes contractive $e^{-H\tau/\hbar}$; the oscillatory weight $e^{iS/\hbar}$ becomes the convergent Boltzmann weight $e^{-S_E/\hbar}$; the Schrödinger equation becomes the heat equation. This is an exact analytic continuation, not a limit: the same physics described in real (Lorentzian) or imaginary (Euclidean) time. The i is not destroyed. It is reinterpreted — the phase $e^{iS/\hbar}$ becomes a statistical weight $e^{-S_E/\hbar}$, and the imaginary-time periodicity that the i now marks is the inverse temperature. At finite $\beta$ the natural state in the Euclidean description is thermal; the pure-state, zero-entropy case sits at the $\beta \to \infty$ boundary. Wick rotation converts phase into inverse-temperature periodicity; it does not abolish the pure states, it relocates them to the boundary of the thermal family. This is the McGucken-Wick rotation (\[MG-Wick\]) read as the QM-to-thermodynamics bridge.

*The i coarse-grained — classical mechanics, via the high-entropy limit.* Averaging over many Compton cycles washes out the sub-cycle phase resolution. This is Carcassi’s high-entropy limit (§10.12quaterdecies): the stretching map rescales the commutator to $[\hat X, \hat P] = i\hbar/\lambda$, and $\lambda \to \infty$ is mathematically $\hbar \to 0$, the Moyal-to-Poisson group contraction. The i’s phase role is not reinterpreted but coarse-grained away below the resolution scale. This is a limit, an approximation valid when observation does not resolve the one-cycle structure — the loss of x₄-resolution of §10.12quaterdecies.

*The triangle, and the two directions as one fact at two scales.* The three regimes are joined by three transitions of two kinds: QM and thermodynamics by the exact Wick rotation (a change of language), QM and classical mechanics by the high-entropy coarse-graining (a limit), and thermodynamics and classical mechanics by the high-temperature $\beta \to 0$ limit (a limit within the Euclidean theory — Carcassi’s Rayleigh-Jeans-from-Planck reduction, §3.1 of ref. \[222\]). Composing the two thermal operations, classical mechanics is the high-temperature Wick-rotated quantum mechanics. Two readings of the i’s role in the Sphere that appear opposed are one fact at two scales: at the many-Sphere ensemble scale (Direction A) the expanding Sphere distributes phase over a growing surface $4\pi c^2 t^2$ and is dissipative, generating entropy — the Second Law is the ensemble reading of the expansion; at the single-Compton-cycle scale (Direction B) the i preserves phase and supports the low-entropy pure state. The expansion dissipates at coarse scale precisely because the i preserves phase at fine scale; the two are the macro and micro readings of the one advance.

*The Sphere as a Compton-temperature KMS state.* The Kubo–Martin–Schwinger condition characterizes a thermal state by periodicity $i\beta\hbar$ in complex time — the Wick rotation read as a statement about states. The McGucken Sphere carries a natural periodicity at the Compton scale, $T_C = h/(mc^2)$ (the Compton clock of the matter orientation condition), so the Sphere is a KMS state at its own Compton temperature, $T_C^{\mathrm{temp}} = mc^2/k_B$. This is the same structure the framework already uses for the Hawking–Unruh effect — a thermal state at $T = \hbar a/(2\pi k_B c)$ seen by an accelerated observer is the KMS state of the Wick-rotated Rindler wedge — so the Hawking temperature and the Compton-clock periodicity are two readings of one KMS structure on the Sphere. The i that carries the phase at rate $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is the same i whose imaginary-time periodicity is the inverse Compton temperature.

*Carcassi’s closing question, answered twice.* Carcassi, Landini and Aidala close by asking whether quantum mechanics is the only theory that recovers classical mechanics at high entropy (ref. \[222\], §5). The framework answers with two conditionals, neither an unconditional “only possible theory.” First, class-conditional: within the class of single-law 4D geometric primitives, dx₄/dt = ic is the unique one whose fully-resolved structure has the classical high-entropy description as its coarse-grained limit (the uniqueness theorem of §10.12undecies). Second, premise-conditional: any theory that (i) recovers classical Hamiltonian mechanics at high entropy by a coarse-graining mechanism, (ii) supplies a physical unit-cell floor making the Boltzmann log $\ln(\Sigma/h)$ dimensionally consistent, and (iii) anchors $c$ by a mass-frequency relation, must supply the Compton-cycle structure as premise or theorem; dx₄/dt = ic supplies it as a theorem, and any competitor meeting (i)–(iii) must supply the same physical parent or be equivalent to it under redefinition. The first conditional fixes uniqueness within a specified class; the second names three physical premises that force the Compton parent. Both are conditionals with explicit antecedents, and both are defensible as such; neither claims that no other theory of any kind could exist.

This is the “cosmos built up by pure deduction from universal elementary laws” Einstein named the supreme task, read across three regimes: one premise, dx₄/dt = ic, with the i carrying the phase; and quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, and classical mechanics as the three consequences of what becomes of that i — held explicit, absorbed into imaginary time, or coarse-grained below the Compton scale — joined at the one Compton-cycle rate $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ of the Sphere at every event. Wheeler’s “idea so simple, so beautiful, so compelling that … we will all say to each other, ‘Oh, how could it have been otherwise?’” is here the single i, read three ways.

#### 10.12quindecies The third law, the classical uncertainty principle, and quantization as an entropy floor: the uncertainty principle and the third law as two readings of the Sphere’s one-cycle floor

The same lecture and program yield two further results that bear on the framework, and in both the McGucken Sphere supplies a physical scale that the entropy argument requires but does not itself fix. The full derivation of what follows, with the verbatim record of Carcassi’s four-step third-law argument, the physical origin of the classical-versus-quantum $2/e$ ratio in Sphere cycle-occupation geometry, and the two-bounds architecture mapped to the Duality’s channels, is Theorem 22.5 of \[MG-Thermo\] (*Thermodynamics Derived from the McGucken Principle: Chain of Theorems of dx₄/dt = ic*; ref. \[223\]); the present section summarizes that result and states its two load-bearing conclusions.

*The uncertainty principle and the third law are two readings of one floor.* Carcassi’s result is that the third law of thermodynamics forces a classical uncertainty principle: an entropy bounded below entails a phase-space uncertainty bounded below, the two sharing the scale $h$. Stated in his terms this is a formal entailment — one floor implies the other because they use the same constant. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework the entailment is explained rather than merely found, because the two floors are the same floor. The McGucken Sphere expands at $c$ and carries one quantum of action $\hbar$ per Compton cycle (§2.3, §4.3); its resolution bottoms out at a single cycle, and this one-cycle limit is read in two registers. The third law reads it as a bound on state-count: the entropy is the logarithm of the count of x₄-states (§10.12duodecies), and that count cannot fall below one cycle, so $S \geq 0$ (\[MG-Thermo\], Theorem 22.5). The uncertainty principle reads the same limit as a bound on phase-space area: the commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ is the projection of the x₄-advance onto the conjugate plane, its $\hbar$ the action per cycle, so the phase-space cell cannot fall below one cycle, $\sigma_q\sigma_p \geq \hbar/2$ (\[MG-Ontic\], *The Ontic Derivation of Quantum Mechanics from dx₄/dt = ic*, Theorems 8 and 13; ref. \[225\]). The entropy floor and the uncertainty floor are the one-Compton-cycle resolution limit of the expanding Sphere, read as a state-count and as a phase-space area respectively. This is why Carcassi finds each forces the other: they are not two floors with a shared constant but one floor — the Sphere’s single-cycle limit — expressed in two languages. The third law and the uncertainty principle do not stand in a provider–consumer relation over the scale $h$; they are co-consequences of dx₄/dt = ic, and their mutual entailment is the signature of their common origin.

*The floor as the integrability condition for the two arenas.* The same one-cycle floor has a further role: it is the measure-theoretic precondition that lets Minkowski space and Hilbert space be constructed as integrals of the advance. Both arenas are integrals of dx₄/dt = ic — Minkowski the coordinate integral $\int ic\,dt = ict$, Hilbert the modulus-frozen integral (§2.3) — and an integral is a sum over increments. Were the increments unbounded below, the sum would run over a true continuum of infinitesimal quantized expansions with no smallest cell, and the construction would inherit exactly the pathology the unphysicality-of-Hilbert-spaces debate identifies: with no smallest cell there is no well-defined measure, and a point carries zero measure while a region carries infinitely many points (§10.12terdecies; Carcassi’s dimensional-consistency observation is the same gap one level down — the entropy $\ln(\Delta x\,\Delta p/h)$ is undefined without a cell $h$). The one-cycle floor closes this: the advance is quantized in units of $\hbar$ per Compton cycle and cannot be resolved below a single cycle, so the integral that builds each arena is a sum over quantized increments with a well-defined smallest cell, and converges to a continuous space carrying a proper measure — the Lebesgue measure of the spatial slice and the Haar measure of the Sphere (Theorem 7.2) that the metric and the Born rule respectively require. In this reading the floor that makes the entropy well-defined and the floor that makes the integration well-defined are the same floor, doing the same job — supplying the quantum of measure — in the thermodynamic and the geometric constructions alike.

The order here is logical, not ontological. All three — the third law, the Lorentzian metric, and the Hilbert space — descend from dx₄/dt = ic; the floor is not upstream of the metric and the Hilbert space as a separate cause but is the co-descended feature that their construction requires. Its priority is the priority of a measure over the integral that needs it, the same priority Carcassi’s cell $h$ has over the entropy logarithm that needs it, not the priority of a source over what it generates. Stated precisely: dx₄/dt = ic is the single source; the one-cycle floor is the measure-theoretic precondition of the integration; and Minkowski space and Hilbert space are the two integrals that the floor renders constructible. This also sharpens why the derived Hilbert space is the physical one rather than the pathological completion (§10.12terdecies): it is the integral of a floored, quantized advance, hence the well-measured Schwartz-class object by construction, not the completed space whose infinities the floor never admits. Carcassi’s reading of quantization as the imposition of an entropy floor thereby acquires a construction-level meaning in the framework: the floor is not only what makes the theory quantum but what makes the arena integrable.

The distinction here is between formal existence and physical deducibility, and it is the distinction Einstein placed at the centre of the physicist’s task. The formal Lorentzian manifold and the formal $L^2$ space exist as mathematics for anyone, with no thermodynamic input: one may write a signature $(-,+,+,+)$ or complete a pre-Hilbert space without ever mentioning a floor. What the floor supplies is not their formal existence but their *deduction* from the single premise — their status as the coordinate and amplitude shadows that dx₄/dt = ic builds up, at every event, by the measure the Sphere carries. This is precisely the standard Einstein named: *“The supreme task of the physicist is to arrive at those universal elementary laws from which the cosmos can be built up by pure deduction”* (Einstein, “Principles of Research,” 1918), together with *“the supreme goal of all theory is to make the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible without having to surrender the adequate representation of a single datum of experience”* (Einstein, Herbert Spencer Lecture, 1933). The arenas are formal objects for anyone; they are *built up by pure deduction* from one premise only because the floor is the measure that links the integral to the Principle. The floor is therefore the deductive link, not a supplementary posit — the point at which the two arenas cease to be independent mathematical constructions and become deductions from dx₄/dt = ic, which is the whole of the Einsteinian task the program undertakes (§10.12octies).

*The classical uncertainty principle from the third law, and the scale the Sphere sets.* This result is derived in full in the corpus thermodynamics paper (\[MG-Thermo\], Theorem 22.5), which reads the same Carcassi lecture; it is reproduced here with its four steps because it bears directly on the flagship’s uncertainty and ℏ material. Carcassi observes that the standard classical statistical entropy is dimensionally ill-defined without a phase-space-area scale. Step 1 (dimensional consistency): $S = \ln(\Delta x\,\Delta p)$ takes the logarithm of a dimensioned quantity, which is not a number; the fix introduces a constant $h$ of action units, $S = \ln(\Delta x\,\Delta p / h)$, and a uniform distribution over a region of area $h$ has zero entropy, so $h$ is the area at which the entropy vanishes. Step 2 (Gaussian bound): at fixed uncertainty the entropy is bounded above by the Gaussian value $S \leq \ln(2\pi e\,\sigma_x\sigma_p / h)$, which rearranges to $\sigma_x\sigma_p \geq (\hbar/e)\,e^{S}$. Step 3 (third law): the third law of thermodynamics (Nernst 1906, Planck 1911) bounds the entropy below, $S \geq 0$. Step 4 (combine): with $e^{0} = 1$ the classical bound is $$\sigma_x\sigma_p \geq \frac{\hbar}{e} \approx 0.368\,\hbar,$$ which tightens to the quantum $\sigma_x\sigma_p \geq \hbar/2$ once pure states reach zero entropy. Carcassi notes he has not found this classical bound in the literature, and flags that the scale $h$ is introduced ad hoc: thermodynamics establishes that a scale must exist, not what sets it (Carcassi, Landini, Aidala, ref. \[222\]; and the CORE1 lecture, ref. \[224\]).

The framework supplies the scale, and this grounding is the content of \[MG-Thermo\] Theorem 22.5.3. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework $\hbar$ is the action per Compton cycle of the $x_4$-advance (§2.3, §4.3): for a particle of rest energy $mc^2$ Compton-coupled to the Sphere the Compton period is $T_C = h/(mc^2)$ and the action per cycle is $E\,T_C = h$, so the area scale $h$ Carcassi’s dimensional argument requires is not a free constant but the physical phase-space area of one wavefront cycle. The third law that Carcassi imposes as an axiom holds here for a physical reason: the entropy is the logarithm of the count of x₄-states (§10.12duodecies), and that count is bounded below by one cycle, so $S \geq 0$ is the statement that the wavefront cannot be resolved finer than a single Compton cycle. Going below $S = 0$ would mean resolving below one x₄-cycle, which is below the physical resolution of the Sphere, not merely below an axiomatic floor. Carcassi’s classical uncertainty principle is therefore, in the framework, the statement that no distribution can be resolved below one Compton cycle of the wavefront — a physical discreteness statement, not merely a thermodynamic one. The uncertainty principle is the entropy-floor bound read together with the geometric origin of the same $\hbar$: the commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ is the x₄-perpendicularity of Theorem 5.1, and its $\hbar$ is the cycle action whose floor gives the bound. What Carcassi grounds in the third law and the framework grounds in the x₄-cycle resolution are the epistemic and physical faces of the one $\hbar$.

*The 2/e ratio, physically.* The classical $\hbar/e$ and quantum $\hbar/2$ bounds differ by $2/e \approx 0.74$, and \[MG-Thermo\] Theorem 22.5.3 gives the physical mechanism the thermodynamic derivation leaves general. The classical bound corresponds to a distribution occupying one Sphere-cycle in position and in momentum *independently* (a rectangular phase-space cell), while the quantum bound corresponds to one Sphere-cycle occupied *jointly* in position and momentum; the factor $2/e$ is the ratio of these two cycle-occupation geometries. The joint, non-factorising occupation is forced because the Sphere’s Haar measure on rays is SO(3)-invariant and does not decompose into independent position and momentum measures (Theorem 7.2). So the numerical ratio between the classical third-law bound and the quantum Heisenberg bound, which Carcassi derives on general grounds without physical commitment, has in the framework a physical origin in the Sphere’s cycle-occupation geometry.

*Quantization as imposing an entropy floor.* Carcassi’s converse to the classical limit is that quantizing a classical theory is exactly imposing a lower bound on the entropy: every quantum effect — the uncertainty principle, entanglement, non-commutativity — follows from that floor, in the same way that everything in special relativity follows from the invariance of the maximum speed $c$; and the Moyal bracket is the unique one-parameter Lie-algebraic deformation of the Poisson bracket, so there is only one way to impose the floor. In the framework this floor is not imposed but physical: the Sphere’s Compton-cycle discreteness is the lower bound on the entropy, since the cycle-count cannot go below one. The ℏ-floor (quantum) and the c-ceiling (relativity) are then the two edges of the one Sphere’s parameter space — $c$ its rate, $\hbar$ its action per cycle — so Carcassi’s two bounds are the two parameters of $dx_4/dt = ic$. His Moyal-uniqueness of quantization is the algebraic counterpart of the framework’s uniqueness of the primitive (§10.12undecies): both state there is one way, one from the deformation side and one from the physical-primitive side, and both answer his closing question — whether quantum mechanics is the only fix for the low-entropy failure of classical mechanics — in the affirmative within their respective classes.

*States as ensembles.* Carcassi argues that entropy is a property of ensembles, that even pure states carry an entropy, and therefore that physical states must always be ensembles, with the regress of ensembles stopping at experimental controllability rather than at ontological constituents. In the framework the ensemble structure is native and physical: the Sphere at every event carries the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure (Theorem 7.2), so every state is a configuration on the Sphere’s orbit and is ensemble-structured by construction. Where Carcassi reaches “states are ensembles” as a philosophical necessity and lets the regress stop at controllability, the framework has it as a fact about the Sphere, and the regress stops at the Sphere — the ensembles all the way down are coarse-grainings of the one physical object (§10.12quaterdecies), and the ontological constituent Carcassi’s method declines to name is the expanding fourth dimension.

*Spacetime as an ensemble of Spheres; the arenas as its ensemble-average.* The previous paragraph can be given a physical, not merely philosophical, form. At its atomic level spacetime is an ensemble of expanding McGucken Spheres: every event generates a Sphere (§2.4.4, the Huygens point-source structure), and each carries the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure (Theorem 7.2). A dense population of these expanding wavefronts, each with a measure over it, is an ensemble in the precise sense — a collection equipped with a measure — and it therefore has entropic properties natively, the entropy being the logarithm of the count of x₄-states across the Spheres (§10.12duodecies). The atomic level of spacetime is thus ensemble-structured and entropy-bearing before any integration is performed.

Minkowski space and Hilbert space are this ensemble integrated into a continuum. Building the arenas sums the advance over the population of Spheres — the coordinate integral for Minkowski, the modulus-frozen integral for Hilbert (§2.3) — and the integration averages the ensemble: Minkowski space is what remains when the individual Spheres’ cycle-ticks are summed into a smooth manifold, and the Born face of Hilbert space is what remains when the phase is frozen. In this sense the arenas no longer resolve the ensemble of Spheres; the individual members are coarse-grained below the arena’s resolution, the one-cycle floor. This is the concealment of §10.12quaterdecies stated from the ensemble side: the arenas are the macrostate, the Sphere-population the microstate ensemble beneath it.

The loss is of resolution, not of the measure. What the integration averages away is the resolution of individual Spheres; what it retains is the ensemble’s measure, which becomes exactly the measures the arenas require — the Lebesgue measure of the spatial slice for the metric and the Haar measure on rays for the Born rule (Theorem 7.2). The arenas therefore see the statistics of the Sphere-population — its measure, hence geometry and probability — but not its individual members, precisely as a thermodynamic macrostate retains the entropy while not resolving the microstates. This is why the arenas appear continuous and deterministic-looking while the substrate is an entropic ensemble: each is the integrated, ensemble-averaged face of the Sphere-population, in which the population’s measure survives and its members do not. The same measure read two ways — integrated over the horizon it is the gravitational entropy, evaluated at the event it is the Born rule (§10.12duodecies) — is the measure of this one ensemble of Spheres, retained in the arenas and resolved only at the atomic level.

#### 10.12sedecies-bis The action principle and the rank-2 counting form as the classical shadow of the Sphere: Carcassi–Aidala’s geometric interpretation of stationary action

Carcassi and Aidala give a geometric and physical interpretation of the principle of stationary action (*Scientific Reports* 13, 12138, 2023; ref. \[228\]) that bears on the framework at its rank-2 heart. They prove that the principle of stationary action is equivalent to three physical assumptions — determinism/reversibility (DR), independence of degrees of freedom (IND), and kinematics/dynamics equivalence (KE) — and that its physics lies not in the Lagrangian or the action, which are gauge and “not uniquely defined,” but in two geometric objects: a divergence-free displacement field on extended phase space, and a rank-2 antisymmetric closed *state-counting form* $\varpi$. The variation of the action is the flow of the displacement field through the surface between a path and its variation; the action is stationary exactly when the path is a field line, because then the flow is tangent to that surface. They are explicit that this points beyond classical mechanics: “there is a unity among the different physical theories that begs to be brought to light. We are convinced that a version of this geometric understanding must exist in the quantum world.”

Three of their results are the classical-phase-space shadow of structures the present framework derives from dx₄/dt = ic, and stating the correspondence precisely closes the connection.

*The rank-2 counting form is the rank-2 that forces the Born exponent.* Carcassi and Aidala derive that the state-counting form must be rank two “as independent degrees of freedom are bi-dimensional (i.e. quantity plus conjugate).” This is, from the classical side, the same rank-2 structure that in this framework forces the Born rule to be degree two: the rank-2 character of the metric forces bilinearity in $(\psi, \psi^*)$ (Lemma 7.1, §7.7.2), so $|\psi|^2$ and not $|\psi|^p$ is the probability. Their counting form on phase space and the framework’s rank-2 Born structure are the same rank-2 — the two-dimensionality of a conjugate pair — read classically as the state-count over a phase-space parallelogram and quantum-mechanically as the bilinear measure on rays. In the framework both are the x₄-conjugate pairing: the quantity and its conjugate are the spatial coordinate and the x₄-advance projection (§5.2), so the “bi-dimensional” degree of freedom Carcassi and Aidala count is the spatial–x₄ pair, and the rank-2 form counting its states is the same object whose SO(3)-invariant measure on the wavefront is the Born rule (Theorem 7.2).

*The action-as-flux-through-the-surface is the classical shadow of Huygens propagation on the Sphere.* Their construction — the action variation is the flow of the displacement field through the path-variation surface, and a solution is a path to which that flow is everywhere tangent — is the phase-space form of the eikonal/Huygens condition that the framework carries as the propagation of the McGucken Sphere: the path integral is iterated Huygens projection onto the expanding wavefront, and the stationary path is the one along which successive wavefronts are tangent (\[MG-Reciprocal\], Theorem 51; \[MG-Feynman\], Proposition II.5). Their divergence-free displacement field is the classical, single-trajectory residue of the Sphere’s Huygens flow; the tangency that makes the action stationary is the wavefront-envelope tangency of the Huygens construction. Where they have a divergence-free flow in extended phase space, the framework has the expanding wavefront whose Huygens propagation that flow shadows.

*The canonical one-form is the differential of the x₄-advance.* Carcassi and Aidala note that their potential $H$, equation (19), is “remarkably similar to that of the relativistic four-momentum,” and leave the observation as a similarity. The full derivation of what follows is \[MG-Lagrangian\] §VIII.22 (*The Unique McGucken Lagrangian*; ref. \[229\]), which this paragraph summarizes. Their canonical one-form is $\theta = p_i\,dq^i - H\,dt = p_\mu\,dx^\mu$; substituting the momentum as the gradient of the accumulated x₄-advance, $p_\mu = \partial_\mu S = -mc\,\partial_\mu X$, gives, on the Lagrangian submanifold $L$ defined by a solution (the graph $p = \partial S/\partial q$),
$$\theta|_L = -mc\,dX.$$
The canonical one-form of Hamiltonian mechanics is the differential of the accumulated x₄-advance along the solution. On the full extended phase space the momenta are independent and $d\theta = -\varpi \neq 0$; on $L$ the momenta are determined by position, the counting form pulls back to zero, $\varpi|_L = 0$, and $\theta$ becomes exact with potential $-mcX$. The three statements $\theta|_L = -mc\,dX$, $\varpi|_L = 0$, and the kinematics/dynamics equivalence (KE) are one statement in three registers. The four-momentum resemblance Carcassi and Aidala observed but did not derive is therefore exact and physical: the conjugate variable of the counting form is the x₄-advance, the potential $H$ is the x₄-component of the momenergy, and the norm their four-momentum-like object would carry — $p_\mu p^\mu = -m^2c^2$, which their metric-free construction has no object to support — is the four-speed budget $u_\mu u^\mu = -c^2$, the covariant form of dx₄/dt = ic (§2.3). Their similarity is the shadow; the identity $\theta|_L = -mc\,dX$ is the object casting it.

*The action is physical, not unphysical; the gauge freedom is the zero-point of the advance.* Carcassi and Aidala conclude from the re-gaugeability of $\theta$ that the action is “an unphysical quantity,” with only its variation $\delta S$ physical. The framework reaches a different and weaker conclusion, and the weaker one is the true one. The identity $\theta|_L = -mc\,dX$ integrates to $\int_L \theta = -mc\int dX = -mc^2\,\Delta\tau$: the action is $mc^2$ times the accumulated x₄-advance, which is the standard free relativistic action, and only its zero-point is conventional. Their own construction supports this — they set the gauge $\theta = (p, 0, -H)$ “without loss of generality,” and that is precisely the gauge in which $\theta = -mc\,dX$. What they read as the action being unphysical is the action having no preferred origin: a gauge transformation $\theta \to \theta + df$ is a shift of $X$ by an additive function, and $X$’s additive freedom is the choice of x₄-origin — the phase of the advance. The Principle fixes the magnitude of the advance ($c$) and its direction ($+ic$, perpendicular) and fixes no origin, so the phase is unfixed and every functional built from the advance inherits exactly that freedom. Two distinct gauge freedoms are present in the free sector and should not be conflated: reparametrization invariance, fixed by the einbein elimination, and the x₄-phase, the additive origin of $X$; the Principle sources both, but they are different freedoms.

*The gauge hidden in $\theta$, and Carcassi’s conjecture that all Lagrangian theory is gauge theory.* Carcassi states the conjecture that “all Lagrangian theory have to be gauge theory in some sense,” pending the field-theory extension. In the framework the sense is named: the gauge hiding in $\theta$ is the x₄-phase indeterminacy, and it is the same indeterminacy that forces local gauge invariance. Every Lagrangian is built from the accumulated advance; the advance has no fixed origin; so every Lagrangian carries the phase freedom, and when the origin is allowed to vary from point to point, demanding insensitivity forces a connection — the gauge field. This is the route by which the Yang-Mills sector is forced (\[MG-SM\], Theorems 5, 10–11; \[MG-Lagrangian\], Proposition VI.2, ref. \[229\]) run in reverse: local gauge invariance is not an added demand but the consequence of the advance’s missing orthogonal reference in the plane perpendicular to $+ic$. The field-theory extension Carcassi flags as the open case is carried out in \[MG-QFT\]: the Lagrangian sectors are lifted to the field level by the hybrid measure $\mathbb{R}^3 \times (\ell_P \mathbb{Z})$ — continuous in the three spatial directions, discrete along x₄ at the Planck length — whose Pontryagin dual bounds the x₄-conjugate momentum to the compact Brillouin zone and thereby supplies a finite state count per finite spatial volume (the field-theoretic state count the programme’s record names as its open call, and the resolution of the Bekenstein/Deutsch information-storage pathology); the specific gauge group $G_{\mathrm{SM}} = U(1)_Y \times SU(2)_L \times SU(3)_c$ is derived from substrate-scale features rather than posited (SU(2)$_L$ from the Sphere’s SO(3) lift, SU(3)$_c$ from the non-commutation of the three spatial-direction operators, U(1)$_Y$ from the x₄-phase scalar); and the Maturity-Test Passage Theorem establishes that every standard presentation of quantum field theory — Lagrangian, Hamiltonian, Wightman, Haag–Kastler, lattice, bootstrap, scattering amplitudes — factors through the one substrate by an explicit extraction operation. The honest residue, stated in \[MG-QFT\]: the form of the gauge sector and the identity of the group factors are forced, while the numerical couplings, the three-generation structure, and the analytic resolution of confinement remain open. Carcassi conjectures that Lagrangian theory must be gauge theory and flags the field-theory extension as pending; the framework derives the gauge structure from x₄-phase indeterminacy and carries the extension out in \[MG-QFT\], with the specific group descending from the substrate and the numerical inputs marked as the remaining open work.

Their explicit conviction that a quantum version of this geometric, counting-form understanding “must exist in the quantum world” is answered by the framework in exactly those terms: the quantum counting form is the Sphere’s SO(3)-invariant Haar measure (Theorem 7.2), the quantum determinism-reversibility is unitarity (the norm-preserving x₄-flux, Theorem 9.2), and the classical–quantum bridge they seek through the counting form is the x₄-state measure read at the two levels (§10.12quaterdecies). As with the Reverse Physics results above, the relationship is one of shadow to object: Carcassi and Aidala reach the divergence-free flow and the rank-2 counting form from the classical side, deliberately without a mechanism; the framework supplies the physical object — the expanding Sphere and its x₄-conjugate pairing — of which their counting form is the classical phase-space shadow, and from which the quantum version they anticipate is derived.

#### 10.12sedecies Reverse Physics maps the masks; the McGucken Principle strikes through them: the heroic quest for the physical foundation

> *All visible objects, man, are but as pasteboard masks. But in each event—in the living act, the undoubted deed—there, some unknown but still reasoning thing puts forth the mouldings of its features from behind the unreasoning mask. If man will strike, strike through the mask! How can the prisoner reach outside except by thrusting through the wall?* — Herman Melville, *Moby-Dick*, Ch. 36 (Ahab).

The preceding sections (§10.12terdecies–quindecies) engaged the Reverse Physics programme of Carcassi, Aidala, and collaborators, which analyses the assumption-structure of the received formalism and exposes hidden equivalences among its conditions: that the Born rule, the von Neumann entropy, and orthogonality-as-mutual-exclusivity are one assumption in three guises; that the third law and the uncertainty bound press the same floor from two sides; that unitary evolution is deterministic-reversible information-conserving evolution; that classical mechanics is the high-entropy limit of the quantum. This is real and valuable work, and its achievement is precise: it shows that faces which looked distinct are the same face in different light. The masks rhyme.

Reverse Physics and the present framework are not two symmetric routes to one end, and it is worth stating the difference exactly, because it is the difference between two kinds of enterprise. Reverse Physics is meta-theoretic: it takes quantum mechanics as given and maps the logical dependencies among its conditions, deliberately declining to name a mechanism or an ontology — its regress, in its authors’ words, stops at experimental controllability, “not because we found the fundamental ontological constituents of the universe.” It is the cartography of the masks. The McGucken Principle is foundational physics in the older sense: it seeks the physical reality beneath the formalism — what the world is and by what law it unfolds — and offers dx₄/dt = ic, the fourth dimension expanding at c as a spherically symmetric wavefront, as that reality, from which the metric, the Hilbert space, the Born rule, ℏ, and the arrow are derived by pure deduction. Reverse Physics catalogues the resemblances among the masks; the McGucken Principle strikes through the mask to the reasoning thing whose single face they all wear.

That the masks rhyme is itself the decisive clue. When the Born rule and the entropy and the third law and the uncertainty bound and the classical limit all turn out to be one structure seen in different lights, the convergence is not a curiosity to be catalogued and set down; it is the fingerprint of a single physical reality pressing its features through every mask. Reverse Physics finds that the masks converge and, by principle, stops there. The convergence points, unavoidably, downward. In this framework the reason the masks rhyme is that they are the several faces of one object: the Born rule is the SO(3)-invariant Haar measure on the expanding Sphere read as probability (Theorem 7.2); the entropy is the same measure read as the logarithm of the x₄-state count (§10.12duodecies); the third law and the uncertainty bound are the Sphere’s one-Compton-cycle resolution floor read as a state-count bound and a phase-space-area bound (§10.12quindecies); the classical limit is the loss of x₄-resolution (§10.12quaterdecies). What Reverse Physics establishes as logical equivalences on the abstract state space, the Principle establishes as physical identities on one object — the crux of light (c, the rate), time (the advance), and dimension (the perpendicular i).

This is the quest to which the founders of the framework’s own lineage called. Wheeler — Bohr’s student, Einstein’s colleague, Feynman’s teacher, and the last figure of the heroic age, under whom the present principle was first formulated at Princeton (Historical Note) — set the charge plainly: *“Behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, so compelling that when—in a decade, a century, or a millennium—we grasp it, we will all say to each other, ‘Oh, how could it have been otherwise?’”* The task is to strike through to that idea, not to catalogue its masks. Eddington had already named the specific gap, in 1928: *“Something must be added to the geometrical conceptions comprised in Minkowski’s world before it becomes a complete picture of the world as we know it.”* Minkowski’s world is a mask — a frozen block in which, in Eddington’s words, “the events past and future lie spread out before us as in a map” with “no signboard to indicate that it is a one-way street.” The something that must be added is the motion: dx₄/dt = ic, the expansion that supplies the one-way street Eddington found missing. Bohr, on the quantum side, saw the shared $\sqrt{-1}$ of relativity and quantum theory and called it a “striking” analogy resting “essentially on the introduction of the conventional symbol $\sqrt{-1}$” (§5.2); the mask showed the same feature twice, and the reasoning thing behind it is the single perpendicular advance whose $i$ both faces wear.

The lineage is the lineage of striking through masks. Newton struck through the falling apple and the wheeling planets to one law, admitting “no more causes of natural things than such as are both true and sufficient to explain their appearances,” for “nature is pleased with simplicity.” Maxwell struck through electricity, magnetism, and light to one field. Faraday struck through action-at-a-distance to the field itself. Einstein struck through absolute space and time to the invariant interval, and through gravity-as-force to curvature, holding that “a physical theory can be satisfactory only if its structures are composed of elementary foundations” and that all knowledge of reality “starts from experience and ends in it.” Bohr struck through the classical atom; Wheeler struck through matter to information. Each refused the pasteboard mask; each thrust through the wall to the reasoning thing behind it. The present framework stands in that line: it strikes through the masks of Minkowski and Hilbert space to the expanding Sphere, and it earns the strike the only way the tradition allows — by deriving, from the one physical premise, what the masks display.

The physical tracer that reveals the reasoning thing is the photon. Relativity requires that the ageless, null-worldline photon be at rest in x₄ (State 2 of the four-fold ontology); quantum mechanics requires that the photon propagate as a spherically symmetric wavefront expanding at c; therefore x₄ itself is a spherically symmetric wavefront expanding at c. The photon, at rest in the fourth dimension and spreading at c in the three, is the instrument by which the fourth dimension’s motion is read off experience — the framework beginning and ending, as Einstein demanded, in what can be observed. The mask of the free particle, struck through, shows the expanding Sphere beneath.

Finally, the strike answers the sharpest result of the Reverse Physics programme on its own terms. Carcassi, Thrien, and Aidala prove (Reverse Quantum Mechanics, §6) that on the abstract Hilbert formalism QSTO:H the Born rule is an *independent* assumption — separable from the ensemble structure, requiring the extra postulate that mutually exclusive, single-shot-distinguishable states exist, which their entropy-cutoff Bloch-ball counterexample shows need not hold. The theorem is correct, and it is exactly the symptom of a formalism with no physical foundation beneath it: on a mask, the Born rule dangles as an unforced add-on. On the object beneath the mask it does not dangle. On the physical Sphere the measure is not assumed but forced — the unique SO(3)-invariant measure on the wavefront (Theorem 7.2), with orthogonality-as-mutual-exclusivity the antipodal structure of the Sphere (§6.2.12) and single-outcome definiteness the first contact of two expanding Spheres (§6.2.23). Carcassi’s independence result holds on the posited Hilbert space and fails on the derived one; that the Born rule is separable on the mask and forced beneath it is itself the argument for striking through. The mask leaves the rule hanging; the reasoning thing behind the mask holds it fast.

Truth, as Ahab said, hath no confines. A consistent formalism that declines the question “what is it, physically?” has accepted the pasteboard mask as the whole of reality, and that acceptance is the one move the tradition of Newton, Faraday, Maxwell, Einstein, Bohr, and Wheeler never made. Reverse Physics maps the mask with a rigor the tradition would honour and shows, invaluably, that all the masks are one mask in different light. The McGucken Principle strikes through the mask to the one physical reality that light is — dx₄/dt = ic, the expanding fourth dimension, the crux of light, time, and dimension — of which every mask the analysis has learned to read is a pasteboard face.

#### 10.12septdecies Two conceptions of the foundations of physics: the meta-theory of all models, and the one physical reality from which the laws deduce

The engagement with the Assumptions of Physics programme across §§10.12terdecies–sedecies-bis rests on a difference that its own authors state plainly, and it is worth naming directly, because it is a difference of aim rather than of rigor. In their 2025–26 overview, Carcassi describes the goal: to find not “the one true model that rules them all, but … a meta-theory for all the possible physical models,” on the model of the foundations of mathematics and computer science, where “nobody’s looking for the theorem of everything, the theorem that proves all the theorems.” He is explicit that, for his programme, “saying that the goal of physics is to find the true laws of the universe is not a very productive point of view.” Reverse Physics is therefore, by design, a meta-theory of physical models: it catalogues which physical assumptions yield which laws, across all admissible models, and declines to name a single physical primitive. This is a coherent and valuable methodological stance, and the results it produces — the equivalences of §§10.12terdecies–sedecies-bis — stand on their own.

The present framework takes the other conception, the one the founders of the discipline held. Its goal is the goal Einstein named the physicist’s supreme task: to find “those universal elementary laws from which the cosmos can be built up by pure deduction,” making “the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible.” Not a meta-theory of all possible models, but the one foundational, ontological, geometric reality of this universe — dx₄/dt = ic, the fourth dimension expanding at c in a spherically symmetric manner — from which the actual mathematical physics of the actual world is derived. From this single physical principle the framework derives, each as a theorem rather than a posit: the Lorentzian metric and general relativity (§2.3, §6; the Einstein field equations via \[MG-SM\], Theorem 12); quantum mechanics — the Hilbert space, the Born rule, the canonical commutator, the Schrödinger equation, the uncertainty principle (§2.3, §5.2, §7, §9); the symmetries and their conservation laws — the ten Poincaré charges from the uniformity, homogeneity, isotropy, and Lorentz-covariance of the x₄-advance, and the gauge charges from x₄-phase indeterminacy (\[MG-Noether\]; \[MG-SM\], Theorems 5, 10–11); the Lagrangians of all sectors — free-particle, Dirac, Yang-Mills, Einstein-Hilbert — forced by the four-fold uniqueness theorem (\[MG-Lagrangian\], Theorem VI.1, ref. \[229\]); thermodynamics — the strict Second Law from the signed $+ic$, the third law as the one-cycle floor, and the classical uncertainty bound (\[MG-Thermo\], §10.12quindecies); and time and all its arrows and asymmetries — thermodynamic, radiative, cosmological, quantum, and causal — unified by the single directionality of $+ic$ (§10.12nonies; \[MG-Entropy\]). This is the one true model in Einstein’s sense: not a framework within which many models may be posed, but the single physical reality of which the laws of this universe are the deductive consequences, in the tradition of Wheeler’s “idea so simple, so beautiful, so compelling that … we will all say to each other, ‘Oh, how could it have been otherwise?’”

The two conceptions are not competitors so much as different answers to the question of what the foundations of physics are for. The meta-theoretic answer maps the space of possible models; the physical answer strikes through to the one reality. But the choice is not without cost, and the cost falls on the meta-theoretic side in a specific way: one of the disadvantages of not looking for a foundational, physical model from which the mathematical physics derives is that one often does not find that which one is not looking for. The equivalences Reverse Physics catalogues — the Born rule with the entropy, the third law with the uncertainty bound, the metric with the Hilbert structure — are, in this framework, the visible signs of a single physical foundation pressing its features through the formalism; a programme that declines on principle to seek that foundation records the signs faithfully and, by that same principle, does not arrive at the reality they are signs of. The framework offered here is the record of what is found when one does look: one physical principle, dx₄/dt = ic, and the deductive descent from it of general relativity, quantum mechanics, the symmetries, the Lagrangians, thermodynamics, and time and all its arrows.

#### 10.12octodecies The cocyclic connection of relational quantum mechanics is the x₄-advance connection: François–Ravera’s $\exp\{-(i/\hbar)S\}$ as the phase of the McGucken Sphere

The most developed recent relational, bundle-geometric construction of quantum mechanics is the dressing-field/relational programme of François and Ravera, which extends the extraction of gauge-invariant content from general relativity and Yang–Mills theory to non-relativistic quantum mechanics itself (*Relational bundle geometric formulation of non-relativistic quantum mechanics*, arXiv:2501.02046, ref. \[232\]) and to mechanics treated as a general-relativistic gauge field theory with a relational account of quantization (*Mechanics as a general-relativistic gauge field theory, and Relational Quantization*, arXiv:2510.19845, ref. \[233\]). Their construction is not an adjacent programme to be catalogued: its central object is a connection built from a cocycle whose phase is, in this framework, exactly the x₄-advance of the expanding Sphere, so the demonstration below shows the most sophisticated relational reconstruction of quantum mechanics running on dx₄/dt = ic, with the two constants it inserts by hand — the imaginary unit and $\hbar$ — being the perpendicularity and the cycle-action the Principle derives.

*The construction.* On the configuration-spacetime bundle $\mathcal{C} \to \mathbb{T}$ with time as base, François and Ravera build the Schrödinger equation and the momentum operator as the two components of a single covariant-constancy condition $\bar D_0\psi = 0$, where the covariant derivative $\bar D_0 = d + \varpi_0$ carries a *cocyclic connection* $\varpi_0 = -(i/\hbar)\,dS$ built from the one-cocycle $C_\gamma = \exp\{-(i/\hbar)\,c_\gamma\}$. The horizontal (spatial) component of $\bar D_0\psi = 0$ yields the momentum operator $\hat p = -i\hbar\,\partial/\partial x$; the covariant-constancy (temporal) component yields the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$. The exponential $\exp\{-(i/\hbar)(\cdots)\}$ is the entire engine: it is what splits $\bar D_0\psi = 0$ into the momentum operator and the Schrödinger equation, unifying the two as components of one connection. The imaginary unit and $\hbar$ enter with the cocycle and the action-functional connection — the wave function being a ℂ-valued cocyclic tensorial 0-form and the connection the flat cocyclic connection the action functional induces — justified by the requirement that quantum mechanics be recovered; the construction does not derive why the cocycle must be the exponential of $i$ times the action divided by $\hbar$.

*Step 1: the cocyclic phase is the x₄-advance phase.* Their fundamental object is the phase $\exp\{(i/\hbar)S[\gamma]\}$ accumulated along a history $\gamma$. In this framework this is not a definitional choice but the physical wavefront phase of the expanding Sphere. For a particle of rest energy $mc^2$ Compton-coupled to the Sphere,
