$$\psi = \psi_0\,\exp\{\tfrac{i}{\hbar}S\} = \psi_0\,\exp\{\tfrac{i}{\hbar}\!\int mc^2\,d\tau\} = \psi_0\,\exp\{i\!\int \tfrac{mc^2}{\hbar}\,d\tau\} = \psi_0\,\exp\{i\,\omega_C\,\tau\},$$
with $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ the Compton frequency — the rate at which the Sphere advances in $x_4$ under dx₄/dt = ic, one cycle per Compton period. Their $S/\hbar$ is the accumulated x₄-advance measured in units of the cycle action, and their $i$ is the perpendicularity of the advance ($x_4 = ict$, Theorem 5.1). What they define as $\exp\{-(i/\hbar)c_\gamma\}$, the framework derives as the phase of the physical advance.

*Step 2: their connection is the advance-differential.* Their cocyclic connection $\varpi_0 = -(i/\hbar)\,dS$ carries $\hbar$ with no account of what fixes it. In the framework $\hbar$ is forced: it is the action per Compton cycle of the advance, $E\,T_C = (mc^2)(h/mc^2) = h$. Substituting the on-shell action $S = \int mc^2\,d\tau = -\int mc\,dX$ (with $X$ the accumulated x₄-advance, $dX = -c\,d\tau$ up to orientation),
$$\varpi_0 = -\tfrac{i}{\hbar}\,dS = -\tfrac{i}{\hbar}\,d\!\big(\!-\!\int mc\,dX\big) = \tfrac{i\,mc}{\hbar}\,dX,$$
so their connection is the differential of the x₄-advance, carried by the $i$ of perpendicularity and normalized by the cycle-action $\hbar$. This is the same object as the canonical one-form identity of §10.12sedecies-bis, $\theta|_L = -mc\,dX$: François and Ravera’s $\varpi_0 = -(i/\hbar)\,dS$ and the framework’s $\theta|_L = -mc\,dX$ are one connection — the differential of the accumulated x₄-advance — theirs wearing the factor $i/\hbar$, the framework’s exhibiting that factor as the perpendicular-advance-per-cycle-action of the Sphere. Their cocyclic connection is the connection form of the x₄-advance.

*Step 3: the two gauges are the two projections of the one advance.* The covariant-constancy condition $\bar D_0\psi = 0$ connects two structures that appear independent: the momentum gauge $\hat p = -i\hbar\,\partial_x$ (the horizontal, spatial component) and the energy gauge $i\hbar\,\partial_t\psi = \hat H\psi$ (the temporal, covariant-constancy component). In the framework these are the spatial and temporal projections of the one perpendicular advance: the suppression map $\sigma$ that relates $\partial_t$ and $\partial_{x_4}$ ($\partial_t = ic\,\partial_{x_4}$) projects the advance onto the time axis, giving the energy/Schrödinger gauge, and onto the space axis, giving the momentum gauge (§5.2, and \[MG-Ontic\] Theorem 8). Both projections carry the same $i$ (perpendicularity) and the same $\hbar$ (cycle action) because they are projections of a single advance perpendicular to both the space and the time axes. The gauge relationship François and Ravera construct — momentum gauge unified with energy gauge through one cocyclic connection — is the projection of dx₄/dt = ic onto the spatial and temporal axes, unified precisely because it is one perpendicular advance. Their $\bar D_0\psi = 0$ is the covariant-constancy of the x₄-advance phase; its two components are the two faces of the Sphere’s advance.

*The structure group and the physical role of vertical motion.* The verified content of the relational-QM paper (2501.02046) supports the reading in a further way. The structure group of the configuration space-time bundle is $H = \mathbb{R}^{3N}$, the particle translations, which the authors show captures exactly the extended Galilean transformations, and which decomposes as $H = H_{\mathrm{int}} \ltimes H_{\mathrm{ext}}$ — internal (physical relative changes of configuration) and external (global). They stress a point that distinguishes their bundle from a Yang–Mills one: vertical motion along the fibers is *not always pure gauge* — it “also contains genuine physical changes within the set of particles.” In the framework this is the statement that the advance along the fiber direction carries physics, which is what dx₄/dt = ic asserts: the fiber advance is the x₄-advance, physical, not gauge. Their observation that fiber motion is partly physical and partly gauge is, on the framework’s reading, the split between the physical x₄-advance and the gauge-redundant phase reference of §10.12sedecies-bis.

*The clock field as dressing field, and the deferred constant c.* The companion treatment of mechanics as a general-relativistic gauge field theory with relational quantization (2510.19845) makes the correspondence sharper. There the authors treat non-relativistic mechanics as a one-dimensional general-relativistic gauge field theory — Mechanical Field Theory — covariant under reparametrizations Diff(I), and show that its standard textbook formulation is recovered by the dressing field method when *the clock field is chosen as the dressing field*, the deparametrization condition $\dot t = 1$ being not a gauge-fixing but the identification of the clock as dressing field (their §4.2.2). The clock field $t$, monotonic ($\dot t > 0$) and serving as the physical reference against which the spatial fields evolve, is in the framework the x₄-advance clock of dx₄/dt = ic: making it the dressing field is making the x₄-advance the physical reference frame, and their result that “standard QM is the relational quantization of MFT” becomes, in the framework, that standard quantum mechanics is quantization relative to the x₄-advance clock. Their headline claim — that the standard QM path integral is *not* the analogue of the gauge-field-theory path integral on field space, but the dressed path integral on the moduli space $\mathcal{M} = \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{C})$ of relational histories — is, on this reading, the statement that quantum mechanics lives on the space of x₄-advance histories, not on the redundant parametrized field space.

Two verified specifics anchor this. First, the clock-field kinetic term: the authors state that a kinetic term for the clock field cannot be written without a velocity-dimensioned constant — “only with the help of a physical constant with the dimension of a velocity could we possibly write one … it hinges upon the introduction of what we should call the Einstein constant $c$ … (a.k.a. the ‘speed of light’)” (their §3.3, after Eq. (86)) — and they defer its treatment as leading to relativistic mechanics. That deferred kinetic term is dx₄/dt = ic: the clock field advancing at $c$ into $x_4$. The construction reaches for exactly the constant the Principle supplies, and defers precisely where the Principle begins. Second, the Hamiltonian constraint: their canonical momenta satisfy $p_t + \tfrac{1}{2m}\langle p_x, p_x\rangle + V = 0$ (their Eq. (90)), with $p_t = -H$ the energy conjugate to the clock. This is the non-relativistic form of the four-momentum norm $p_\mu p^\mu = -m^2 c^2$ — the four-speed budget $u_\mu u^\mu = -c^2$ that is the covariant statement of dx₄/dt = ic (§2.3). The constraint relating the clock-conjugate energy to the spatial momenta is the mass-shell condition of the x₄-advance, written on the mechanical field space.

*Scope.* François and Ravera construct relational, gauge-invariant non-relativistic quantum mechanics rigorously, by a bundle-geometric method of real generality, and the construction stands on its own as a derivation of the momentum operator and the Schrödinger equation from a single covariant-constancy condition. What the framework adds is the physical origin of the two constants their cocycle carries: the $i$ is the perpendicularity of the x₄-advance and the $\hbar$ is its cycle-action, so their cocyclic phase $\exp\{(i/\hbar)S\}$ is the phase of the expanding Sphere and their cocyclic connection $\varpi_0 = -(i/\hbar)\,dS$ is the advance-differential $\theta|_L = -mc\,dX$. The relationship is the one that recurs through this section: theirs is the rigorous relational structure taking the quantum constants as inputs; the framework supplies the physical advance those constants measure. The points at which their construction reaches for a velocity constant and a mass-shell constraint — the clock kinetic term requiring $c$, and the Hamiltonian constraint as the four-momentum norm — are exactly where dx₄/dt = ic supplies what the construction requires.

**Remark 10.13 (The de Broglie/Compton/Planck wavelength hierarchy as empirical anchor).** Proposition 10.8 (iii) supplies a three-level hierarchy of discreteness scales, each empirically anchored by independent experimental traditions of twentieth- and twenty-first-century physics.

*De Broglie wavelength scale* (λ_dB = ℏc/E). Empirically anchored by every quantum-mechanical interference experiment: electron-microscope diffraction patterns (since Davisson–Germer 1927), neutron interferometry (Rauch et al. 1975 \[138\], Werner et al. 1975 \[139\]), atom interferometry (since Estermann–Stern 1930, with modern atom-interferometer precision measurements of g and α), molecular interferometry (since Arndt–Zeilinger 1999 for C₆₀, with subsequent extensions to macromolecules), and Bose–Einstein condensate interference (since 1995). Every such experiment is an empirical measurement of the de Broglie wavelength scale of x_4-action discreteness.

*Compton wavelength scale* (λ_C = ℏ/(mc)). Empirically anchored by the Compton scattering experiment (Compton 1923, Nobel Prize 1927), pair production from photons (Anderson 1932 discovery of the positron at the predicted threshold 2 m_e c²), and the various Compton-wavelength-scale calculations in atomic physics (Lamb shift, hydrogen-spectrum fine structure, electron g-factor at the Compton scale).

*Planck length scale* (λ_P = √(ℏG/c³)). Not yet directly empirically anchored (the Planck length is 16 orders of magnitude below any directly probed scale), but bounded by the high-precision Lorentz-invariance tests (Mattingly 2005 \[167\] for the comprehensive review) which constrain any Planck-scale violation of Lorentz invariance to be smaller than what most discrete-spacetime programs naively predict.

The empirical force of Proposition 10.8 is that **the de Broglie wavelength scale is already empirically confirmed across the entire body of twentieth- and twenty-first-century quantum-mechanics experiments** — every interference fringe, every diffraction pattern, every quantum-mechanical phase measurement is a measurement of the same fundamental wavelength λ_dB = ℏc/E that the dx₄/dt = ic framework identifies as the discreteness scale of x_4-action. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework prediction is therefore the consolidation under a single principle of an enormous existing empirical body that the orthodox tradition treated as a collection of separate “quantum-mechanical phenomena.” the wavefront’s wavelength is the de Broglie wavelength, its frequency is the de Broglie / Compton frequency, its phase is the path-integral exp(iS/ℏ) phase, its action quantum is ℏ — and every quantum-mechanical experiment ever performed measures one or more of these intrinsic properties of the wavefront that the McGucken Principle names. The dynamics were in the premise (§2.1); the empirical record across a century of quantum-mechanical experimentation is the cascade-level confirmation that the wavefront-character of the active x_4-expansion is the geometry from which the entire quantum-mechanical AND Lorentzian spacetime formalism descends.

#### 10.6.5 The Lorentzian metric becomes the inner product

The rank-2 sesquilinear inner product on 𝓗 is the L²-functional rendering of the rank-2 Lorentzian metric η_μν on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. The correspondence is:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$                                                                                             𝓗
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  η_μν A\^μ B\^ν (rank-2 bilinear pairing of two vectors at a point)                    ⟨φ, ψ⟩ = ∫ φ\^\*ψ d³x (rank-2 sesquilinear pairing of two wavefunctions over space)

  ds² = η_μν dx\^μ dx\^ν (squared Lorentzian interval)                                                                   ‖ψ‖² = ⟨ψ, ψ⟩ = ∫

  (ict)² = -c²t² (Lemma 2.5: the metric’s signature from x_4-perpendicularity)    ψ\^\*ψ (Lemmas 7.1, 7.6: the Born density’s rank-2 character from the same x_4-perpendicularity)

  Lorentz isometries SO(1,3) preserving η_μν                                      Unitary transformations preserving ⟨·, ·⟩ generated by Stone’s theorem on the Lorentz generators

  Translations along x\^μ (Killing vectors)                                                Self-adjoint generators P̂\_μ = -iℏ ∂/∂x\^μ (canonical commutator, Theorem 5.1)

  Boosts (hyperbolic rotations in (x_4, x_i) planes)                                                   Boost operators K̂\_i (generated by p̂\_i, Remark 12.11)

The metric and the inner product are not two separate structures with an analogy between them. They are the same rank-2 sesquilinear object — the natural pairing supplied by the constraint surface of dx₄/dt = ic — at two cascade levels of representation. The squared content of the metric (Lemma 2.5: (ict)² = -c²t² producing the signature) becomes the squared content of the inner product (Lemmas 7.1, 7.6: ψ\^\*ψ producing the Born density). Both squarings remove the i-marker for x_4-perpendicularity at their respective cascade levels (§12.1). The function-space construction transfers the geometry of the manifold-level metric to the algebra of the Hilbert-space inner product without loss.

#### 10.6.6 The theorem: Hilbert space and Minkowski space as one geometric object

**Theorem 10.6 (Hilbert space and Minkowski space as one geometric object at two cascade levels of representation).** *The Hilbert space 𝓗 of quantum mechanics derived in Theorem 6.1 of the present paper and the Minkowski spacetime manifold $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ of special relativity supplied by Lemma 2.5 of the present paper are the same geometric object — the constraint surface where the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic holds locally — represented at two cascade levels:*

*(i) (Manifold-level representation.) Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is the point-set of the constraint surface, equipped with the Lorentzian metric η_μν of signature (−,+,+,+) supplied by Lemma 2.5 (the squared form (ict)² = -c²t² of dx₄/dt = ic, integrated and substituted into the four-dimensional line element).*

*(ii) (Function-space-level representation.) 𝓗 = L²(Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, η_μν) is the space of complex-valued square-integrable functions on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, equipped with the sesquilinear inner product ⟨φ, ψ⟩ = ∫ φ\^*ψ d³x supplied by the Minkowski metric via the canonical L²-functional construction (Lemma 7.1: rank-2 sesquilinearity inherited from the rank-2 metric).\*

*(iii) (Canonical bijection between manifold points and Hilbert-space basis.) The position eigenstates {\|x⟩ : x ∈ ℝ³} ⊂ 𝓗 at parameter time t are in canonical bijection with the spatial points of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at parameter time t, with the rigged-Hilbert-space inner product ⟨x \| y⟩ = δ³(x - y) reproducing in distributional form the spatial-distance content of the Minkowski metric on the slice.*

*(iv) (Function-space enrichments forced by the geometry.) The two features that distinguish 𝓗 from Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-as-point-set — complex linear superposition of states, and the non-commutative operator algebra \[q̂\_i, p̂\_j\] = iℏ δ_ij — are forced consequences of the geometry of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ under the McGucken Principle, not separate axiomatic additions. Superposition is forced by the perpendicular x_4-direction’s spatial-slice projection (Theorem 3.1, Definition 2.6, §12.2 (i)); the non-commutative algebra is forced by the x₁x₂x₃ vs x_4 perpendicularity at the operator level (Proposition 12.10), with the non-closure quantum iℏ supplied by Proposition 2.2 as the action quantum per Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance.*

*(v) (Both representations are pointwise instantiations of dx₄/dt = ic.) Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ contains dx₄/dt = ic literally at every point (Theorem 10.5 clause (i): in the rest frame of any massive particle at p ∈ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, the four-velocity normalization u\^μ u_μ = -c² reads dx₄/dt = ic). 𝓗 contains dx₄/dt = ic constructively in every element (Theorem 10.5 clause (ii): every ψ ∈ 𝓗 is built as the path-integral kernel over Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, with phase from x_4 = ict, with inner product the rank-2 pairing inherited from the metric, and with L² character forced by the rank-2 sesquilinearity via Lemmas 7.1 and 7.6). The two representations are the same geometry — the pointwise-instantiated principle dx₄/dt = ic — rendered at different cascade levels.*

**Proof.**

*(i)* By Lemma 2.5, integration of dx₄/dt = ic with the initial condition x_4 = 0 at t = 0 yields x_4 = ict; squaring gives dx_4² = (ic)² dt² = -c²dt²; substitution into the four-dimensional Euclidean line element ds² = dx_4² + dx_1² + dx_2² + dx_3² yields the Lorentzian line element ds² = -c²dt² + dx_1² + dx_2² + dx_3² with signature (−,+,+,+) on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. The constraint surface where dx₄/dt = ic holds locally is Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, and the Lorentzian metric is supplied by the squared form of the McGucken Principle.

*(ii)* By Theorem 6.1 (the four-step cascade dx₄/dt = ic → Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ → 𝓥 → 𝓗), the Hilbert space 𝓗 is constructed as the L²-Cauchy completion of the pre-Hilbert space 𝓥 of McGucken-wavefunctions ψ: ℝ³ → ℂ on the spatial slice. The inner product ⟨φ, ψ⟩ = ∫ φ\^\*ψ d³x is the L²-functional pairing on the spatial slice of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ with the Lebesgue measure d³x (which, for the spatial part of η_μν, agrees with √\|η\_{spatial}\| d³x = d³x for the spatial diagonal +1, +1, +1). The Minkowski metric’s contribution beyond the spatial slice (the temporal component −c²dt²) appears in the time-evolution operator Ĥ = -iℏ ∂\_t (Theorem 9.1) rather than in the slice inner product. The full Hilbert space is 𝓗 = L²(spatial slice of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at time t) at each fixed t, with Schrödinger evolution between slices governed by the temporal component of the metric. The L²-functional construction is therefore directly inherited from the Minkowski metric on $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, with the spatial part of the metric supplying the slice inner product and the temporal part supplying the time-evolution generator.

*(iii)* The position operators q̂\_i (multiplication by spatial coordinate x_i on the slice) have continuous spectra σ(q̂\_i) = ℝ. By the spectral theorem applied to commuting self-adjoint operators q̂\_1, q̂\_2, q̂\_3 with joint spectrum ℝ³, the simultaneous eigenstates \|x⟩ form a generalized (rigged-Hilbert-space) basis of 𝓗 indexed by x ∈ ℝ³. The map x ↔ \|x⟩ is a bijection between the spatial-slice points of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and the position-basis of 𝓗. The rigged-Hilbert-space inner product ⟨x \| y⟩ = δ³(x - y) is the spectral-theorem content: distinct spatial points have orthogonal position eigenstates (zero overlap), and a position eigenstate with itself is normalized to a delta function (the natural rigged-Hilbert-space normalization). The Minkowski metric on the spatial slice (the +1, +1, +1 part of η_μν) supplies the spatial distance \|x - y\|; the L²-functional construction transfers this to the inner product structure of the position basis.

*(iv)* The complex character of ψ ∈ 𝓗 is Theorem 3.1: forced by the perpendicularity of x_4 to x₁x₂x₃, with the imaginary unit i in ψ as the algebraic marker for the perpendicular direction along which the particle’s x_4-advance accumulates phase. Linear superposition is forced by the path-integral construction of ψ (Definition 2.6): ψ(x) = ∑\_paths exp(iS\[γ\]/ℏ) is by construction a linear superposition of contributions from distinct paths, with the complex weights summing in the algebra of ℂ. Without the perpendicular x_4-direction, no path-integral construction is possible (the wavefunction would degenerate to a real-valued density without phase), and without the linear sum over paths, no superposition structure exists. Complex superposition is therefore a forced consequence of the manifold-level perpendicularity of x_4.

The non-commutative algebra \[q̂\_i, p̂\_j\] = iℏ δ_ij is Theorem 5.1, with the operator-level interpretation supplied by Proposition 12.10: q̂ is in x₁x₂x₃ (pure spatial-slice operator, no i, no ℏ); p̂ is in x_4 (the i marks x_4-perpendicularity, the ℏ marks the action quantum, the spatial derivative reads off the x_4-phase rate per unit spatial step). The non-closure quantum iℏ in the commutator is the algebraic record of the geometric perpendicularity x₁x₂x₃ ⊥ x_4 at the operator level. Without the perpendicular x_4-direction, the commutator vanishes (the operators would all be in the same x₁x₂x₃ slice and would commute as multiplication operators on functions of x). The non-commutative algebra is therefore a forced consequence of the manifold-level perpendicularity of x_4 read at the operator level (Theorem 12.11 instance (1) of universal non-closure).

*(v)* By Theorem 10.5 clause (i), Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ contains dx₄/dt = ic literally at every point: in the rest frame of any massive particle at p ∈ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, the four-velocity normalization u\^μ u_μ = -c² reads dx₄/dt = ic. By Theorem 10.5 clause (ii), 𝓗 contains dx₄/dt = ic constructively in every element: every ψ ∈ 𝓗 carries the i as perpendicularity marker (algebraic), is built as the path-integral kernel over Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (constructive), participates in the rank-2 sesquilinear inner product structure (), and respects the L² completion forced by the rank-2 sesquilinearity (completion). The two cascade levels are therefore two renderings of the same pointwise-instantiated principle. Stripping dx₄/dt = ic from Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ destroys the manifold (the Lorentzian signature collapses); stripping dx₄/dt = ic from 𝓗 destroys the Hilbert space (the complex character, the inner product structure, the operator algebra all collapse together). The two structures are are constituted by the same upstream principle at every point. ∎

#### 10.6.7 Resolution of the orthodox “two-worlds” framing

The orthodox foundations program for quantum mechanics treated the Hilbert space and the spacetime manifold as two separate mathematical universes connected by external bridges (the wavefunction ψ as a “complex amplitude on spacetime”; the inner product as a “physically meaningful overlap”; the operators as “observables postulated to act on the Hilbert space”; the unitary time evolution as “the Schrödinger equation governing the wavefunction’s dynamics in time”). Each bridge was supplied by a separate axiom or postulate, with the foundational role of those axioms / postulates being to connect two structures that had been introduced as independent of each other.

Theorem 10.6 dissolves the two-worlds framing entirely. There is no separate Hilbert space “where quantum mechanics lives” connected by postulated bridges to a separate spacetime “where relativity lives.” There is one geometric structure — the constraint surface Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ where dx₄/dt = ic holds locally — and the Hilbert space is Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ in its function-valued representation. The wavefunction ψ is a complex-valued function on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$; the inner product ⟨φ, ψ⟩ is the L²-functional rendering of the Minkowski metric; the position operator q̂\_i is multiplication by the spatial coordinate function x_i on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$; the momentum operator p̂\_i = -iℏ ∂/∂x_i is the differential operator on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ that extracts the x_4-phase rate per unit spatial displacement; the Hamiltonian operator Ĥ = -iℏ ∂\_t generates the time-evolution between slices of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. Every feature of 𝓗 is a function-space rendering of a geometric feature of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, with the rendering canonical and the geometric features supplied by the upstream principle dx₄/dt = ic.

This dissolves, in one move, why nothing in the orthodox foundations program ever succeeded: every prior attempt (Mackey 1957, Piron 1964, Solèr 1995, Hardy 2001, Chiribella–D’Ariano–Perinotti 2011, Masanes–Galley–Müller 2019, and the twenty other programs surveyed in §6.2 of the present paper) tried to derive the Hilbert-space structure from axioms internal to the Hilbert space (operational, informational, lattice-theoretic, algebraic, categorical, etc.), missing that **the Hilbert space is the spacetime manifold in its function-valued representation, and its structure is forced by the geometry of the manifold supplied by dx₄/dt = ic**. The prior programs were all attempts to extract the Hilbert-space structure from within the Hilbert space; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies it from one cascade level upstream, where the Hilbert space and the spacetime manifold are revealed as the same geometric object.

#### 10.6.8 The relativistic case: 𝓗 as L² of the positive-mass-shell ⊂ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-dual

The non-relativistic Schrödinger-picture Hilbert space 𝓗 = L²(ℝ³, d³x) of Theorem 6.1 is the most direct manifold-level / function-space-level correspondence. The relativistic case — the one-particle Hilbert space of relativistic free fields, on which Wigner (1939) classified the unitary irreducible representations of the Poincaré group — exhibits the Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ ↔ 𝓗 identification even more transparently, because the relativistic Hilbert space is built *directly* from the geometry of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$.

For a relativistic free particle of mass m, the one-particle Hilbert space 𝓗\_{m, s} (where s is the spin) is, in the Wightman construction (ref. \[83\] of the present paper for the broader operational/categorical context; standard relativistic QFT references for the Wightman formulation):

𝓗\_{m, 0} = L²(H_m, dμ_m)

where H_m := {p\^μ ∈ `\mathbb{M}`{=tex}\_{1,3}-dual : p\^μ p_μ = -m²c², p\^0 \> 0} is the positive-mass-shell hyperboloid in the momentum-dual of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, and dμ_m is the Lorentz-invariant measure d³p / (2 E_p) with E_p = √(p² + m²c²). The mass-shell hyperboloid H_m is a 3-dimensional submanifold of the 4-dimensional Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-dual, embedded as the orbit of the Poincaré group acting on a fixed timelike momentum. The Hilbert space of relativistic one-particle states is therefore literally L² of a subset of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-dual — the Hilbert space is built directly from the geometry of the Minkowski manifold (via its dual).

For higher spin (s ≥ 1/2), the Hilbert space is the spin-s subspace of L²(H_m, dμ_m) ⊗ ℂ\^{2s+1}, with the spin index labeling a finite-dimensional internal vector space that the Lorentz group acts on. The construction extends the identification: 𝓗 is the L²-functional space over the Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-dual mass-shell, with internal indices for spin. Every feature is supplied by the geometry of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (via its dual): the mass-shell hyperboloid by the constraint p\^μp_μ = -m²c² in Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-dual; the Lorentz-invariant measure by the Minkowski metric on $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-dual; the spin representation by the little-group structure of the Lorentz subgroup that stabilizes a fixed timelike momentum (Wigner 1939). The Hilbert space and the Minkowski manifold are the same geometric object in the relativistic case as in the non-relativistic case, with the relativistic specialization making the identification cleaner because the Hilbert space is built directly from a submanifold of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-dual rather than from the spatial slice of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$.

#### 10.6.9 Historical context: prior programs that approached this identification

Several mathematical / foundational programs of the twentieth century approached the Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ ↔ 𝓗 identification without quite reaching it. Three deserve specific note.

The Wightman axioms for relativistic quantum field theory build the Hilbert space directly from the geometry of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$: the one-particle Hilbert space is L² of the positive-mass-shell (§10.6.8 above); the full multi-particle Hilbert space is the Fock space ⊕\_n S_n\[𝓗_1\^⊗n\]; the field operators are operator-valued distributions on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ acting on the Fock space. The Wightman construction is the closest the prior tradition came to recognizing the Hilbert space as a function-space rendering of the Minkowski manifold. But Wightman treated the Hilbert space as an abstract carrier space on which Poincaré representations act, with the geometry of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ supplying the *representation* but not constituting the *Hilbert space itself*. The McGucken reading is stronger: the Hilbert space *is* the Minkowski manifold in its function-valued representation, with the Poincaré symmetries being internal symmetries of this single geometric object rather than external transformations acting on a separate Hilbert space.

The Haag–Kastler axioms organize relativistic QFT around the local algebras 𝓐(𝓞) of observables in open regions 𝓞 ⊂ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, with the Hilbert space arising via the GNS construction from states on these algebras. The local-algebra structure makes the spatial-region content of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ explicit in the algebraic structure: each region of spacetime carries its own algebra, and the Hilbert space is built from states on the union of these algebras. Like Wightman, Haag–Kastler treats the Hilbert space as a carrier space for representations of structures indexed by Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ regions — closer to the Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ ↔ 𝓗 identification than the non-relativistic axiomatizations, but still with the Hilbert space as a separate object built over Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ rather than identified with it.

Connes’ spectral triple (𝓐, 𝓗, D) — a non-commutative algebra 𝓐, a Hilbert space 𝓗 on which 𝓐 acts, and a Dirac operator D — packages the geometry of a manifold (commutative case) or its non-commutative generalization (non-commutative case) into a single algebraic object. For a Riemannian spin manifold X, Connes’ theorem establishes that the spectral triple (C\^∞(X), L²(X, S), D_X) — with C\^∞(X) the algebra of smooth functions, L²(X, S) the L² space of spinor fields, and D_X the Dirac operator — reconstructs the manifold X from the algebraic data. Connes’ framework is the closest the prior tradition came to packaging the manifold and its Hilbert space as a single object. The McGucken reading agrees with Connes’ approach in identifying the manifold and the Hilbert space as two faces of the same geometric structure but goes further: in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the manifold *is* the Hilbert space’s point-set (via the position-eigenstate bijection of §10.6.2), and the Hilbert space *is* the manifold’s function space (via the L² construction of §10.6.1), with both representations pointwise instantiated by dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 10.5). Connes’ framework supplies the mathematical machinery for the Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ ↔ 𝓗 identification; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the upstream physical principle that makes the identification *forced* rather than merely *constructible*.

Three additional programs deserve brief mention. **Penrose’s twistor program (1967 onward)** attempts to encode the geometry of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ in algebraic / complex-geometric structures (twistors), with relativistic physics expressed in twistor space rather than in spacetime; the dx₄/dt = ic framework is a dual representation of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, parallel in spirit to the Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ ↔ 𝓗 identification but in a different mathematical setting. **The Atiyah–Singer index theorem (1963)** connects the analytic content of differential operators on a manifold (Hilbert-space operators on L² spaces of sections) to the topological content of the manifold itself — the strongest pre-McGucken statement that manifold-level topology and Hilbert-space-level operator structure are not independent. **’t Hooft’s holographic principle (1993)** and its later realization in AdS/CFT (Maldacena 1997) propose that the information content of a bulk spacetime region is encoded on its boundary; this is a related but different identification (bulk ↔ boundary, rather than manifold ↔ function-space-over-the-same-manifold).

None of these programs supplied the upstream physical principle from which the Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ ↔ 𝓗 identification descends as a forced theorem. The McGucken framework supplies that principle: dx₄/dt = ic with action quantum ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance (Proposition 2.2). With this principle in hand, the manifold and the Hilbert space are no longer two structures that mathematicians can show to be related; they are the same geometric object that physics has been describing in two different representations for a hundred years without recognizing the identification.

#### 10.6.10 The dissolution of “where does quantum mechanics live”

The deepest question that every century-long foundational program for quantum mechanics struggled with — *what kind of mathematical object is the Hilbert space, and how does it relate to the physical spacetime in which experiments occur?* — has, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, a one-line answer: **the Hilbert space is the spacetime, in its function-valued representation, with both supplied by the constraint surface where dx₄/dt = ic holds locally.**

The wavefunction ψ is the spatial-slice projection of a particle’s x_4-expansion (Definition 2.6), with the complex character supplied by x_4’s perpendicularity (Theorem 3.1) and the inner-product overlap of two wavefunctions being the L²-functional rendering of the Minkowski metric pairing (Lemma 7.1). The Hilbert space is the manifold of spacetime events at parameter time t, viewed as a complex-valued function space, with the position eigenstates labeling the spacetime points one-to-one (§10.6.2). The operator algebra is the spatial-slice vs. perpendicular-x_4 split of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ read at the operator level (Proposition 12.10), with the canonical commutator’s iℏ the algebraic record of the geometric perpendicularity (Theorem 12.11 instance (1)).

Every feature of the Hilbert space that the orthodox tradition treated as an independent axiomatic input — the complex character, the inner product, the position-momentum operator algebra, the unitary time evolution, the projection postulate, the Born density — is supplied by the geometry of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ under the McGucken Principle. The orthodox foundation’s axioms (Dirac–von Neumann, 1930s) treated 𝓗 as an arena requiring its own axiomatic justification; Theorem 10.6 establishes that 𝓗 has no separate existence as an arena and therefore needs no separate axiomatic justification. The arena and the manifold are the same. The principle that supplies the manifold (Lemma 2.5: dx₄/dt = ic squared and integrated gives Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ with its Lorentzian signature) supplies the arena (Theorem 10.6: the function space over Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ with the metric-induced inner product is 𝓗). One principle, one arena, two cascade-level representations of the same arena, with the McGucken Principle pointwise instantiated in both.

This is the central architectural fact of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, and the most direct consequence of Theorem 10.5’s pointwise-instantiation property: when a principle is locally instantiated at every point of every derived structure, the derived structures cannot be separate from one another — they are different cascade-level renderings of the same pointwise-instantiated principle. Quantum mechanics and special relativity, on this reading, are not two separate theories with a difficult relationship to be sorted out by future foundational work; they are two cascade-level renderings of dx₄/dt = ic, and the central foundational fact of physics is that the manifold of relativity and the Hilbert space of quantum mechanics are the same geometric object viewed at different levels.

#### 10.6.11 The orthodox view stated and superseded: a point-by-point diagnostic against the canonical historical sources

The orthodox pedagogical and foundational treatment of the Hilbert-space/Minkowski-space relationship — articulated across a century of mathematical-physics literature from Hilbert (1912) through Dirac (1930), von Neumann (1932), Wick (1954), Wigner (1960), Wheeler-DeWitt (1967), Penrose (1989), ’t Hooft (1993), Maldacena (1998), Rovelli (2004), Smolin (2001), and the contemporary foundations-of-quantum-mechanics literature — treats the two structures as fundamentally distinct mathematical universes whose relationship is an unresolved foundational problem. The present subsection states each canonical orthodox claim, cites the major historical sources where the claim was articulated, and exhibits the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s resolution.

The diagnostic is analogous to the diagnostic of §6.2 across twenty-three prior Hilbert-space-derivation programs (every program operated *inside* the postulated Hilbert space) and the diagnostic of §7.1 across fifteen prior Born-rule derivations (every program presupposed the Hilbert space as the arena). Both prior diagnostics established that the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework moves one cascade level upstream of all prior programs. The present diagnostic establishes the same architectural move at the higher level of the Hilbert-space-vs-Minkowski-space relationship itself: the orthodox view treats them as two structures requiring reconciliation; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework recognizes them as one geometric object at two cascade-level renderings (Theorem 10.6).

**Claim 1 (Orthodox): Quantum mechanics and special relativity are two pillars of modern physics with fundamentally distinct mathematical structures.**

*Canonical sources.* Dirac’s *Principles of Quantum Mechanics* (Oxford, 1930) \[13\] established the formal Hilbert-space framework as the mathematical foundation of quantum mechanics, separate from the relativistic spacetime framework. Von Neumann’s *Mathematische Grundlagen der Quantenmechanik* (Springer, 1932) \[14\] axiomatized this separation, with Hilbert space as the foundational object of quantum mechanics and spacetime as an external parameter. Wigner’s “The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Mathematics in the Natural Sciences” (*Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics* 13, 1–14, 1960) \[146\] treats quantum mechanics and relativity as separate mathematical theories whose joint applicability to nature is “unreasonable” — implying that no foundational identification was anticipated. Penrose’s *The Emperor’s New Mind* (Oxford, 1989) \[147\] frames the QM/relativity reconciliation as the central open problem of contemporary theoretical physics. Smolin’s *Three Roads to Quantum Gravity* (Basic Books, 2001) \[148\] presents the QM/GR reconciliation as the foundational challenge requiring three distinct programmatic approaches (string theory, loop quantum gravity, non-commutative geometry).

*McGucken supersession (Theorem 10.6).* The two structures are *not* distinct. They are the same geometric object — the constraint surface where dx₄/dt = ic holds locally — rendered at two cascade levels. Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is the point-set/manifold-level rendering; 𝓗 = L²(Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, η_μν) is the function-space-level rendering. The “fundamental distinctness” was an artifact of the orthodox treatment of 𝓗 as an abstract algebraic object disconnected from spacetime; once 𝓗 is recognized as L² over Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (§10.6.1), the distinctness disappears.

**Claim 2 (Orthodox): Hilbert space is an abstract state space, not a physical arena.**

*Canonical sources.* Von Neumann 1932 \[14\] established the abstract-state-space reading: Hilbert space is the carrier of quantum states, characterized algebraically by completeness, separability, and the inner product structure, with no intrinsic geometric connection to physical spacetime. Dirac 1930 \[13\] presented the bra-ket formalism as an abstract algebraic structure on the state space. Mackey’s *The Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics* (W. A. Benjamin, 1963; lectures delivered 1957) \[20\] developed the lattice-theoretic / orthomodular-poset axiomatization that abstracts away from any physical-spacetime content. Hardy’s “Quantum Theory from Five Reasonable Axioms” (arXiv:quant-ph/0101012, 2001) \[23\] reconstructs the abstract Hilbert space from operational axioms, treating it explicitly as a generalized-probability-theoretic state space with no spacetime referent. Chiribella–D’Ariano–Perinotti’s “Informational Derivation of Quantum Theory” (*Physical Review A* 84, 012311, 2011) \[24\] continues this abstract-operational tradition.

*McGucken supersession (§10.6.2).* Hilbert space *is* the physical arena, viewed in its function-valued representation. The position eigenstates {\|x⟩ : x ∈ ℝ³} are in canonical bijection with the spatial points of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at parameter time t: each spacetime point on the spatial slice corresponds one-to-one with a position eigenstate. The wavefunction ψ(x) = ⟨x\|ψ⟩ is a complex-valued function on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, with the position eigenstate at the physical spacetime point x supplying the basis label. The “state space” and the “physical arena” are the same set of objects — labeled by points in the manifold-level rendering and by position eigenstates in the function-space-level rendering.

**Claim 3 (Orthodox): ℂ vs ℝ is a fundamental contrast between the two structures.**

*Canonical sources.* Birkhoff and von Neumann’s “The Logic of Quantum Mechanics” (*Annals of Mathematics* 37, 823–843, 1936) \[58\] first systematically examined which division algebra (ℝ, ℂ, or ℍ) the quantum-logic structure admits, treating the choice as a fundamental algebraic question. Jordan, von Neumann, and Wigner’s “On an Algebraic Generalization of the Quantum Mechanical Formalism” (*Annals of Mathematics* 35, 29–64, 1934) \[17\] classified Jordan algebras and reached the three-way ℝ/ℂ/ℍ ambiguity. Stueckelberg’s “Quantum Theory in Real Hilbert Space” (*Helvetica Physica Acta* 33, 727–752, 1960) \[26\] developed real-Hilbert-space QM as a equivalent alternative. Adler’s *Quaternionic Quantum Mechanics and Quantum Fields* (Oxford, 1995) \[27\] developed quaternionic QM as a third alternative. Renou et al.’s “Quantum Theory Based on Real Numbers Can Be Experimentally Falsified” (*Nature* 600, 625–629, 2021; discussed in detail at §6.2.22 of the present paper) supplied the empirical experimental exclusion of the real-Hilbert-space alternative. The history of the ℂ-vs-ℝ-vs-ℍ debate confirms that the orthodox tradition treated the choice of number field as foundational and unexplained: nature requires complex numbers, but no prior program identified *why*.

*McGucken supersession (§§3, 4.1, 4.3, 4.5, §6.2.22).* The ℂ-vs-ℝ contrast is an artifact of two reading conventions for the same four dimensions. The all-real reading uses (ct, x₁, x₂, x₃) with Lorentzian metric η_μν of signature (−,+,+,+); the (ict)-reading uses (ict, x₁, x₂, x₃) with formal Euclidean metric where the i in x₄ = ict carries the perpendicularity information that the Lorentzian signature carries in the all-real reading. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework picks the second reading and recognizes the i in x₄ = ict as the algebraic marker for the perpendicularity of x_4 to x₁x₂x₃ (Theorem 3.1, §4.3, §4.5). The five canonical i’s of foundational physics (in x₄ = ict, in iℏ ∂\_t ψ = Ĥψ, in \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ, in exp(iS/ℏ), in the Feynman +iε prescription) are five appearances of one geometric fact, not five independent uses of a formal device (§4.4). The Frobenius theorem (§4.1) forces ℂ uniquely from the count of one perpendicular axis: one perpendicular axis → one imaginary unit → ℂ. Real QM fails empirically because it cannot encode the perpendicularity of x_4 (Renou et al. 2021); quaternionic QM fails because it would require three perpendicular axes where nature has one; ℂ works because the perpendicularity count of nature is exactly one. The ℂ-vs-ℝ contrast dissolves: ℂ *is* what ℝ⁴ with a perpendicular fourth dimension *is*, when the perpendicularity is made algebraically explicit.

**Claim 4 (Orthodox): Minkowski space is fixed at four dimensions; Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. The dimensional contrast is fundamental.**

*Canonical sources.* Dirac 1930 \[13\] developed the continuous position/momentum basis formalism with implicit infinite-dimensionality of the underlying Hilbert space. Von Neumann 1932 \[14\] gave the rigorous treatment of separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The standard modern functional-analytic treatment is Reed and Simon’s *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics* (Academic Press, 1972–1980) \[149\], the canonical textbook reference for the abstract Hilbert-space framework. The dimensional contrast (manifold dimension 4 vs Hilbert-space “dimension” ℵ₀) is presented in standard QM pedagogy from Dirac through current textbooks as a fundamental feature distinguishing the two structures.

*McGucken supersession (§10.6.2, Proposition 10.7 of §10.6.3).* The contrast between “4-dimensional Minkowski space” and “infinite-dimensional Hilbert space” is resolved at two complementary levels in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework. *First (the category-error correction):* the comparison compares two different quantities — the *topological dimension* of the manifold Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (= 4) and the *cardinality-as-vector-space* of the function space L²(ℝ³) (= 2\^ℵ₀ for the rigged-Hilbert-space basis). These are not directly comparable. Compared apples to apples — number of points in the spatial slice of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at parameter time t (continuum-many, 2\^ℵ₀) vs. number of position eigenstates of 𝓗 at parameter time t (continuum-many, 2\^ℵ₀) — the cardinalities coincide, with the bijection x ↔ \|x⟩ of §10.6.2 making the identification explicit. *Second (the positive geometric source):* Proposition 10.7 of §10.6.3 identifies the manifold-level geometric structure that *supplies* the infinite-dimensionality of 𝓗: at every event E ∈ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, the McGucken Sphere 𝓜_E(t) of §2.5 carries a continuum of perpendicular x_4-radii (one per direction on the sphere, parameterized by the solid angle), with each radius marked by the i-marker for x_4-perpendicularity (Theorem 3.1). The infinite-dimensionality of 𝓗 is the cascade-level expression of this manifold-level continuum: each “dimension” of 𝓗 is one specific perpendicular x_4-radius emanating from one specific past event and arriving at one specific spatial point at parameter time t. The continuum cardinality of the position basis of 𝓗 (Proposition 10.7 (v)) is the manifold-level count of perpendicular x_4-radii from McGucken Spheres throughout Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. The “4 vs ∞” framing therefore resolves into a positive geometric identification: **4 counts the spacetime dimensions of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at the manifold level; the cardinality 2\^ℵ₀ counts the perpendicular x_4-radii from McGucken Spheres at the function-space level. Same geometric structure, two cascade-level countings.** The “infinite-dimensionality” of 𝓗 was treated for a century as an abstract algebraic feature of L²(ℝ³); the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the simple geometric source — a continuum of perpendicular x_4-radii from McGucken Spheres at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$.

**Claim 5 (Orthodox): The inner product of 𝓗 (complex, positive-definite) and the Minkowski metric (real, indefinite) are fundamentally different bilinear pairings.**

*Canonical sources.* Hilbert’s *Grundzüge einer allgemeinen Theorie der linearen Integralgleichungen* (Teubner, 1912) \[150\] introduced the abstract Hilbert-space inner product as a positive-definite complex form. Riesz’s “Sur les systèmes orthogonaux de fonctions” (*Comptes Rendus de l’Académie des Sciences* 144, 615–619, 1907) \[18\] established the L² Hilbert-space structure. Minkowski’s “Raum und Zeit” address (Cologne, 21 September 1908; published in *Physikalische Zeitschrift* 10, 75–88, 1909) \[51\] introduced the indefinite Lorentzian metric. Von Neumann 1932 \[14\] axiomatized the abstract positive-definite inner product as foundational for quantum mechanics. The orthodox treatment presents the Hilbert-space inner product as a mathematical object derived from norm-completeness considerations and the Minkowski metric as a separate mathematical object derived from the invariance requirements of special relativity, with no intrinsic connection between the two.

*McGucken supersession (§10.6.5, Lemma 7.1).* The two pairings are the same rank-2 sesquilinear/bilinear pairing at two cascade levels. At the manifold level, η_μν A\^μ B\^ν is the rank-2 pairing of two tangent vectors at a point, producing a real scalar. At the function-space level, ⟨φ, ψ⟩ = ∫ φ\^\* ψ d³x is the rank-2 sesquilinear pairing of two wavefunctions over space, producing a complex scalar. Both are rank-2; Lemma 7.1 of the present paper makes this explicit, with the rank-2 of the Minkowski metric (Lemma 2.5) inherited by the rank-2 sesquilinear character of the L² inner product. The “indefinite vs positive-definite” distinction is resolved by noting that the indefiniteness lives in the temporal component (the −c²dt² piece), which feeds into the time-evolution operator Ĥ rather than the slice inner product; the spatial part of the metric (+1, +1, +1) is positive-definite and becomes the slice’s L² inner product. The L² inner product on the spatial slice is the spatial part of the Lorentzian metric rendered in function-space form (§10.6.5).

**Claim 6 (Orthodox): The Wick rotation is a formal mathematical bridge between the two structures, used as a computational device for convergent path integrals.**

*Canonical sources.* Wick’s “Properties of Bethe-Salpeter Wave Functions” (*Physical Review* 96, 1124–1134, 1954) \[151\] introduced the analytic continuation t → −iτ that bears his name. Schwinger’s selected papers on quantum electrodynamics (1958) \[152\] developed the Euclidean formalism. Symanzik’s “Euclidean Quantum Field Theory I” (*Journal of Mathematical Physics* 7, 510–525, 1966) \[153\] formalized Euclidean QFT. Osterwalder and Schrader’s “Axioms for Euclidean Green’s Functions” (*Communications in Mathematical Physics* 31, 83–112, 1973; II: 42, 281–305, 1975) \[154\] established the reconstruction theorem allowing Euclidean QFT to be recovered as Lorentzian QFT. Glimm and Jaffe’s *Quantum Physics: A Functional Integral Point of View* (Springer, 1981) \[155\] is the standard reference for Euclidean-rotation-based path-integral methods in mathematical QFT. The orthodox treatment is uniform: the Wick rotation is presented as a formal computational tool that rotates between the Lorentzian and Euclidean settings, with no intrinsic physics beyond convergence.

*McGucken supersession (Theorem 12.2, Theorem 12.4).* The Wick rotation is a *physical operation* with a real-world referent: the measurement event. Each measurement is a physical Wick rotation at a single particle (Theorem 12.2: the particle’s i-bearing wavefunction is rotated out of its participation in x_4-expansion when its forward x_4-expansion meets a localized absorber head-on, Theorem 7.7). The cumulative ensemble of measurements at total rate Γ_total ∼ 10³⁴ s⁻¹ realizes the macroscopic-scale Wick rotation as classical thermodynamics (Theorem 12.4); the standard mathematical Wick rotation t → −iτ that converts exp(iS/ℏ) into the Boltzmann weight exp(−S_E/ℏ) is the formal abstraction of this cumulative physical operation across the ensemble — *“the Wick rotation exalted Γ_total times per second by the ensemble’s Born rule events”* (Remark 12.5). The “bridge” reading is correct at the formal level; the *physics* of the bridge is the measurement event itself, and recognizing this content dissolves the framing of two structures requiring bridging.

**Claim 7 (Orthodox): The reconciliation of Hilbert-space quantum mechanics with Minkowski-space relativity remains an ongoing open problem at the heart of theoretical physics.**

*Canonical sources.* Wheeler and DeWitt’s “Quantum Theory of Gravity I: The Canonical Theory” (*Physical Review* 160, 1113–1148, 1967) \[156\] formulated the canonical quantization of general relativity, raising the “problem of time” — the failure of the standard QM time evolution to fit into a generally covariant framework — as central to the QM/GR reconciliation. Penrose’s *The Emperor’s New Mind* \[147\] presents the QM-GR reconciliation as the central open problem in contemporary theoretical physics. ’t Hooft’s “Dimensional Reduction in Quantum Gravity” (in *Salamfestschrift*, World Scientific, 1993; arXiv:gr-qc/9310026) \[157\] proposed the holographic principle as an approach to the reconciliation. Maldacena’s “The Large N Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity” (*Advances in Theoretical and Mathematical Physics* 2, 231–252, 1998; arXiv:hep-th/9711200) \[158\] established the AdS/CFT correspondence as a concrete realization of the holographic approach to QM-GR reconciliation. Rovelli’s *Quantum Gravity* (Cambridge, 2004) \[159\] developed loop quantum gravity as a non-perturbative approach to the reconciliation. Smolin’s *Three Roads to Quantum Gravity* \[148\] surveys the three major contemporary approaches (string theory, loop quantum gravity, non-commutative geometry) as competing strategies for the same reconciliation problem. The orthodox treatment is uniform across these sources: QM and SR/GR are separate theories, their reconciliation is unresolved, and the problem is the central open question of foundational theoretical physics.

*McGucken supersession (Theorem 10.6).* The “ongoing effort to reconcile” is not ongoing because the reconciliation has been accomplished by the recognition that the two structures are not separate. Quantum mechanics and special relativity are two cascade-level renderings of dx₄/dt = ic, with the manifold-level rendering (Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$) supplying the relativistic spacetime and the function-space-level rendering (𝓗 = L²(Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, η_μν)) supplying the quantum-mechanical formalism. The probabilistic character of “Hilbert space” is the spatial-slice projection of x_4-expansion’s nonlocality (Theorem 7.7: every event sends a spherically symmetric x_4-wavefront across the spatial slice, with the Born density being the head-on collision rate of two such wavefronts). The “geometric rigidity of Minkowski spacetime” is the four-velocity-budget constraint u\^μ u_μ = −c² (§2.3) supplying the Lorentzian metric via Lemma 2.5. Same principle, two renderings. The hundred-year “interpretation industry” (Copenhagen, Many-Worlds, Bohmian, QBist, relational) was attempting to bridge a gap that wasn’t there; the “measurement problem” was attempting to explain rotation out of x_4 using an ontology (Hilbert space disconnected from spacetime) that prevented the explanation; the “problem of time” in quantum gravity was attempting to reconcile two structures that already agree at every point on what time is doing.

#### 10.6.13 The McGucken Sphere as the shared geometric primitive at both cascade levels

The transposition of §10.6.12 — from “two pillars requiring reconciliation” to “one pillar at two cascade-level renderings” — calls for a concrete geometric carrier that lives at both cascade levels and whose properties supply the features of both Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$. **The McGucken Sphere $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ (Definition 2.3) is that carrier.** This subsection makes the dual existence fully explicit: it catalogs the Sphere’s properties at each cascade level, identifies the §10.6.5 manifold ↔ function-space correspondence as Sphere-mediated, and demonstrates that every feature of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and every feature of Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ is forced by a specific property of the McGucken Sphere. The architectural fact is that the dual existence of dx₄/dt = ic in both Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ is a fact about one shared geometric primitive — the Sphere — that lives at every event of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ as a wavefront-geometric object and at every point of Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ as a primitive vector.

##### 10.6.13.1 The Sphere’s foundational dual existence

The McGucken Sphere is defined by Definition 2.3 of the present paper as

$\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ = { p ∈ spacetime : ds²(E, p) = 0, x₄(p) − x₄(E) = ict },

the null wavefront of x₄-expansion from event E at parameter time t. This single definition has two derivationally distinct readings, both forced by the integrated form x₄ = ict of dx₄/dt = ic (Lemma 2.5):

(a) *Manifold-level reading.* $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ is a geometric subset of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ — specifically the future null cone Σ⁺(E) at event E, equipped with the SO(3) symmetry of x₁x₂x₃ about E (line 408 of the present paper). The Sphere lives in Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ as a definite point-set with metric content: every point p on the Sphere satisfies ds²(E, p) = 0 and x₄(p) − x₄(E) = ict. The Sphere is a geometric object of the Lorentzian manifold.

(b) *Function-space-level reading.* The same $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ generates the McGucken wavefunction ψ_E(x, t) (Definition 2.6 of the present paper) as the path-integral kernel ψ_E(B) = Σ_γ exp(iS\[γ\]/ℏ) over paths γ from E to B ∈ $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$. The wavefunction ψ_E is a primitive vector of Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ (§6.4.5 Step 1 of the present paper, line 1223: *“These McGucken-Sphere wavefronts are the primitive vectors of the Hilbert space construction — physical wavefronts arising from definite source events.”*). The Sphere lives in Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ as the element-level type from which the Hilbert space is constructed via Cauchy completion of finite Huygens–Fresnel–Kirchhoff superpositions (Theorem 6.1.5 of the present paper).

The two readings are not parallel-developments of two separate objects. They are the same object — the Sphere $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ — viewed at two cascade levels of representation. At the manifold level, the Sphere is the subset Σ⁺(E) ⊂ Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$; at the function-space level, the Sphere is the wavefunction ψ_E ∈ Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$. Same Sphere, same E, same t, same expansion at +ic; two cascade-level renderings of one geometric fact about dx₄/dt = ic.

This dual existence is what makes the §10.6.6 Theorem 10.6 identification Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ = Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-as-function-space rigorous rather than metaphorical. The Sphere is the explicit geometric carrier whose dual existence at both cascade levels constitutes the identification. Every feature of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is the manifold-level reading of a Sphere property; every feature of Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ is the function-space-level reading of the same Sphere property. The five tables below catalog this correspondence systematically.

##### 10.6.13.8 Summary

Theorem 10.6 of the present paper establishes that Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ and Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ are one geometric object at two cascade levels (line 3253): *“Stripping dx₄/dt = ic from Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ destroys the manifold (the Lorentzian signature collapses); stripping dx₄/dt = ic from Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ destroys the Hilbert space (the complex character, the inner product structure, the operator algebra all collapse together). The two structures are are constituted by the same upstream principle at every point.”* The present subsection identifies the concrete geometric carrier that realizes this constitutive principle at every point of every cascade level: **the McGucken Sphere**.

Three facts together constitute the closing reading.

*Fact 1 (Dual existence).* The Sphere lives at both cascade levels. At the manifold level, $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$ is a definite geometric subset of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ — the future null cone $\Sigma^+(E)$ with SO(3) symmetry and the active orientation $+ic$. At the function-space level, the same Sphere generates $\psi_E \in \mathcal{H}$ as a primitive vector of the Hilbert space. The two readings are not separate developments of two objects; they are the same Sphere viewed at two cascade-level renderings.

*Fact 2 (Forced axiomatization at both levels).* Every axiom of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ — Lorentzian signature, smooth-manifold structure, causal structure, light-speed invariance, Lorentz isometry group, Poincaré translation invariance, both SR postulates, mass-shell hyperboloid structure — is forced by a specific Sphere property (§10.6.13.6). Every axiom of Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ — complex vector space, inner product, sesquilinearity, conjugate symmetry, positive-definiteness, completeness, separability, continuous position and momentum spectra, infinite dimensionality, non-commutative algebra, Born-rule probability density — is forced by the same Sphere properties read at the function-space level (§10.6.13.5). The Sphere axiomatizes both structures simultaneously.

*Fact 3 (Pointwise instantiation at both levels).* By Theorem 10.5 reread Sphere-centrically (§10.6.13.7), the Sphere carries dx₄/dt = ic at every point of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ (literal), in every element of Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ (constructive), in every value of $|\psi|^2$ (evaluative), and in every term of $i\hbar \partial_t \psi = \hat{H}\psi$ (operatorial). The pointwise instantiation is a fact about the Sphere’s universal coverage of both cascade levels.

These three facts together establish the salient feature of the dx₄/dt = ic framework: **dx₄/dt = ic forces both Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ through one concrete geometric primitive — the McGucken Sphere — that lives at both cascade levels, axiomatizes both structures, and carries the principle pointwise in both renderings.** The orthodox question “does dx₄/dt = ic live in spacetime or in the Hilbert space?” is dissolved by the recognition that the Sphere is in both spacetime and the Hilbert space, with the same Sphere supplying the geometry of Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and the function-space content of Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ as two cascade-level renderings of the same geometric fact. The McGucken Sphere is what makes the architectural identity $\mathcal{H} = \mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ at the level of L² rendering (Theorem 10.6) carry concrete geometry at every point of both structures.

The dual-existence reading sharpens the projection-theorem reading of §16 (the McGucken Duality). The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel is foundational because the Sphere — the carrier of dx₄/dt = ic at both cascade levels — is a geometric object: a wavefront with definite center, radius, orientation, action-quantum content, and SO(3) symmetry. The Algebraic Channel is the $T$-invariant projection because the algebraic apparatus of Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ (operators, commutators, unitary groups, von Neumann axioms) is what survives when the Sphere’s $+ic$ orientation and point-set geometry are projected away by $\Pi_A$ (Lemmas 16.3.1, 16.3.2). The Sphere is in both Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$; the algebraic shadow of the Sphere is in $\Pi_A(\mathcal{H})$ alone, with the geometry stripped. This is why the §10.6 architectural identity $\mathcal{H} = \mathbb{M}_{1,3}$-as-function-space and the §16 projection-theorem reading $\mathcal{A} = \Pi_A(\mathcal{B})$ are the same fact viewed at two analytical levels: the Sphere lives in both spaces, and the Algebraic Channel sees only the Sphere’s sign-blind algebra while the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel sees the Sphere itself as the geometric primary.

### 10.7 Architectural significance of the four-sense pointwise instantiation (literal/constructive/evaluative/operatorial) of dx₄/dt = ic at every level of the cascade: foundational simplicity

The four-sense distinction (literal/constructive/evaluative/operatorial) captures what kind of foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic is: a recurring fact at every level of its descendant structures. The principle is *everywhere* in the formalism it generates.

This has no parallel in prior foundational programs for quantum mechanics. The Dirac–von Neumann axioms are upstream postulates: once stated, they do not appear “in” the theorems they entail. The Born rule does not contain the state axiom; the Schrödinger equation does not contain the observable axiom; the canonical commutator does not contain the measurement axiom. The axioms are starting points; the theorems are downstream products; the axioms are not pointwise present in the theorems. The same pattern holds for Mackey’s lattice axioms, Piron–Solèr’s constraints, Jordan–von Neumann–Wigner’s algebraic axioms, Hardy’s operational axioms, Chiribella–D’Ariano–Perinotti’s informational axioms, and every other foundational program in the prior tradition: all operate as upstream postulates that constrain the downstream formalism without being pointwise present in the formalism’s individual elements. A vector ψ ∈ 𝓗 in von Neumann’s axiomatization does not “contain” the Hilbert-space axiom; the axiom is a feature of 𝓗 as a whole, not a feature of each ψ individually.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s pointwise-instantiation property is therefore a distinct feature of dx₄/dt = ic as a foundational principle, with no parallel in the prior tradition. The principle is the fact instantiated at every point of every derived structure.

One cannot strip the McGucken Principle out of any derived structure without destroying that structure:

-   Strip the constraint Φ_M = x₄ − ict = 0 from Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and you destroy the spacetime manifold itself (clause (i)).
-   Strip the i out of any ψ ∈ 𝓗 and you destroy the wavefunction’s complex character (clause (ii) algebraic); replace the path-integral construction over Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ with a non-principle-derived construction and you destroy ψ’s content (clause (ii) constructive); replace the rank-2 inner product with a different sesquilinear form and you destroy 𝓗’s Hilbert structure (clause (ii)); replace L² with L\^p (p ≠ 2) and you lose the Hilbert character (clause (ii) completion).
-   Strip the geometric-overlap-of-x₄-expansions reading from P = \|ψ\|² and you lose the geometry; replace the exponent 2 with any other exponent and you violate both the rank-2 metric (Metric Route) and the L²-Hilbert character (Norm Route) — both routes to exponent 2 descending from the McGucken Principle (clause (iii)).
-   Strip the chain-rule operator identity ∂\_t = ic ∂/∂x₄ from the Schrödinger equation and you destroy the time-evolution operator; strip the perpendicularity-marker i and the action-quantum ℏ from iℏ ∂\_t and you destroy the LHS; strip ψ from either side and you destroy the equation entirely (clause (iv)).

The principle is therefore not removable from any derived structure because the structure is *constituted* by the McGucken Principle pointwise. This irreversibility is derivationally distinct from upstream-axiomatic dependence: removing the Hilbert-space axiom from von Neumann’s framework destroys the dx₄/dt = ic framework but does not destroy any particular wavefunction (a wavefunction without the Hilbert-space axiom is still a function); removing the McGucken Principle from the McGucken framework destroys every wavefunction in the dx₄/dt = ic framework because every wavefunction is constituted by the McGucken Principle.

Reciprocally, the McGucken Principle is recoverable from any derived structure by reading its local instantiation off the structure’s geometry:

-   From Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$: read the Lorentzian signature (−,+,+,+), recognize (ict)² = −c² t², unpack to x₄ = ict, differentiate to dx₄/dt = ic.
-   From any ψ ∈ 𝓗: read the imaginary unit i (perpendicularity marker), recognize x₄ = ict, recover the McGucken Principle.
-   From any value of P = \|ψ\|²: read the geometric overlap of forward and conjugate x₄-expansions, recover x₄ = ict and dx₄/dt = ic.
-   From any term of the Schrödinger equation: read the operator-form chain rule, recover dx₄/dt = ic; read the i and ℏ, recover the perpendicularity and action-quantization clauses of the McGucken Principle.

The principle is therefore recoverable from any derived structure in the cascade. The cascade is *invertible* in the sense that every derived structure carries enough information to recover the upstream principle. This is the correlate of the pointwise-instantiation property: if the McGucken Principle is locally readable at every point of every derived structure, then the McGucken Principle is recoverable from any one of them. Theorem 10.6 of the preceding subsection makes this recoverability fully explicit: Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and 𝓗 are the same geometric object at two cascade-level renderings of the same pointwise-instantiated principle, with the manifold-level rendering supplying the spacetime structure of relativity and the function-space-level rendering supplying the Hilbert-space structure of quantum mechanics.

Theorem 10.5 captures what it means for dx₄/dt = ic to be the foundational geometric principle of quantum mechanics: *constitutive* of the formalism at every level. The principle is *what the formalism is made of*. The cogenerative cascade is a identity between the McGucken Principle and the structures it generates: Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ is the constraint surface of the McGucken Principle, 𝓗 is the L²-closure of principle-built wavefunctions (and equivalently L²(Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$) by Theorem 10.6), P = \|ψ\|² is the overlap of principle-derived x₄-expansions, the Schrödinger equation is the operator-form expression of the McGucken Principle’s chain-rule identity on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$. In each case the derived structure is constituted by the McGucken Principle.

A hostile referee who claims the dx₄/dt = ic framework is “just” a derivation chain — that one can equally well derive the same formalism from any of a thousand other upstream principles — must answer the additional question raised by Theorem 10.5: why does *every* derived structure also contain dx₄/dt = ic pointwise? The pointwise-instantiation property is independent of derivational ancestry. Even granting all the derivations as mathematical-formal exercises, a referee must still account for why the McGucken Principle is locally readable in every output, and why Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$ and 𝓗 are the same geometric object at two cascade levels (Theorem 10.6). The pointwise-instantiation property therefore provides an independent line of evidence for dx₄/dt = ic as the right foundational principle: the McGucken Principle is the fact that recurs at every level of every derived structure, with the recurrence making the derived structures cascade-level renderings of one another rather than separate mathematical universes.

The principle is the constitutive structure of every output of the derivation, at every point, in one of four derivationally distinct senses corresponding to the four types of mathematical structure the dx₄/dt = ic framework generates, with the function-space-level structure (𝓗) and the manifold-level structure (Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$) revealed (Theorem 10.6) as the same geometric object at two cascade-level renderings of the same pointwise-instantiated principle.
