### 12.6 Two canonical illustrations: photon absorption and radioactive alpha detection

The dx₄/dt = ic framework’s reading of measurement as physical rotation out of the x₄-expansion is visible in two canonical experimental cases. The photon case is the purest: the photon’s existence as a photon is *constituted* by its participation in the x₄-expansion at exactly c, and absorption ends that participation absolutely, with no continuing photon. There is no “post-measurement photon at rest”; the photon is annihilated. The radioactive alpha case shows the same mechanism in a massive particle, where the rotation out of x₄ is the transition from free-particle participation in x₄-expansion (with the four-velocity budget partitioned between spatial and x₄ components per u\^μ u_μ = −c²) to bound-state absence of such participation. Both instantiate the same universal mechanism. The photon case makes it most transparent.

#### 12.6.1 The photon case: emission, propagation at c, and annihilation at a photographic grain

Consider an atom de-exciting from an excited state to a lower state, emitting a single photon of frequency ω. By rotational symmetry of the atomic transition (for isotropic emitters, or after averaging over orientations of an ensemble of identical emitters), the emitted photon’s complex amplitude is initially an outgoing spherical electromagnetic wave centered on the emission event.

The photon’s status in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework is ontologically more extreme than the massive particle’s. By the canonical ontology (clause 2), the photon is at *absolute rest in x₄* — dx₄/dτ = 0 on its null worldline — but rides the x₄-expansion wavefront at the universal rate c. The photon’s existence as a photon is constituted by its participation in the x₄-expansion at the boundary speed c: geometrically, a photon is an excitation of the electromagnetic field propagating along the null light cone, which is the wavefront of the active x₄-expansion. To call something a photon is to call it a participant in the four-dimensional active expansion at exactly the boundary speed c, with no spatial-rest representation available — there is no inertial frame in which a photon is at rest.

(i) **Spherical emission as projection of isotropic x₄-expansion.** The x₄-expansion from the emission event is isotropic in spacetime (canonical ontology, clause 3). The photon’s complex amplitude immediately after emission is an outgoing spherical electromagnetic wave centered on the emission event — the spatial-slice projection of the isotropic x₄-expansion wavefront. The initial spherical symmetry is the direct geometric record of the isotropic active expansion at the emission event.

(ii) **Propagation at c as riding the x₄-expansion wavefront.** The photon’s worldline is null: k\^μ k_μ = 0, where k\^μ is the photon’s four-momentum. In the (x₄ = ict, x₁, x₂, x₃) coordinate system, the photon’s spatial speed equals the x₄-rate in magnitude: it propagates at c along the spatial slice while x₄ advances at ic. The photon’s complex amplitude (the one-photon state in QED, or the classical EM field amplitude in the semi-classical limit) is i-bearing throughout this propagation, with the phase encoding the photon’s accumulated x₄-component along its null worldline and the modulus encoding the spatial-slice amplitude at each spacetime point. The photon, geometrically, *is* its participation in the x₄-expansion — there is no further substance to the photon beyond its propagating amplitude on the wavefront.

(iii) **Absorption at a photographic grain as physical annihilation of the photon.** The photographic emulsion contains discrete silver halide microcrystals (typically AgBr grains, of size \~ 0.5–1 μm). When the spherically spreading photon amplitude meets such a grain at some angle θ from the emission event, the absorption event occurs: the photon is *annihilated*, and its energy ℏω is transferred to a bound electron transition in the AgBr crystal, depositing a latent image that subsequent chemical development converts into metallic silver. The photon ceases to exist as a photon at this event. Unlike the massive-particle case, there is no question of “post-measurement photon state” because there is no post-measurement photon at all. The photon’s participation in the x₄-expansion ends absolutely at the absorption event. The rotation out of x₄ is, for the photon, total and unambiguous: the photon was a pure x₄-expansion participant, and now is not — because the photon as such no longer exists.

(iv) **Born rule probability as the algebraic signature of the photon’s annihilation.** The probability density that the grain at angle θ blackens is \|ψ_γ(θ, t_abs)\|² = ψ_γ\*(θ, t_abs) ψ_γ(θ, t_abs), where ψ_γ is the photon’s complex amplitude (the appropriate QED matrix element ⟨ x \| k, λ ⟩ for a one-photon state, or the classical EM field amplitude in the semi-classical limit). The modulus-squaring removes the i from the photon’s amplitude. This is the Wick rotation at the amplitude level (Theorem 12.2): the photon was an i-bearing participant in x₄-expansion; the squaring is the algebraic record of its annihilation, with the i removed because the photon — the i-bearing entity — has been removed. The exponent 2 is forced by the rank-2 character of the Minkowski metric (Lemma 7.1).

(v) **The film grain’s chemical reduction as macroscopic record on the spatial slice.** The AgBr crystal undergoes a photochemical reduction: Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag⁰, with the freed electron from the AgBr lattice’s valence band combining with an interstitial silver ion to form a metallic silver atom. With enough such reductions in a single grain (typically four silver atoms are needed for the grain to become developable), the grain becomes a developable latent image center. Subsequent chemical development reduces the entire grain to metallic silver, producing the visible black spot on the photographic plate. This chemical change is irreversible in any practical sense — the grain’s atomic structure has been altered, the photochemistry is one-way at ambient conditions, and the record exists purely on the spatial slice as a macroscopic configuration of silver atoms. The photon’s prior existence as a participant in the x₄-expansion leaves no trace in the post-absorption world except for this irreversible spatial-slice mark. The rotation out of x₄ is, in this case, complete: the photon is gone, the spatial-slice record remains.

The photon case exhibits the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s mechanism in its cleanest form. Pre-absorption, the photon is purely an x₄-expansion participant — there is no inertial-frame ambiguity about its “rest state” because no rest state exists. Post-absorption, the photon does not exist; the system that carries its deposited energy (the modified AgBr crystal) is at rest on the spatial slice, bound in the photographic emulsion’s chemistry, with no continuing participation in the x₄-expansion *as a free quantum*. The wavefunction’s i, which encoded the photon’s participation in the active expansion, is removed by the modulus-squaring because the participant — the photon — has been removed by the absorption.

Photographic detection of single photons is the historical foundation of quantum measurement: G. I. Taylor’s 1909 double-slit experiment with attenuated light, Einstein’s 1905 analysis of the photoelectric effect, Compton’s 1923 photon-electron scattering, the modern realization of single-photon detectors (avalanche photodiodes, superconducting nanowire detectors). Every photodetection event in the experimental record of twentieth- and twenty-first-century physics is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, a physical Wick rotation: a photon-as-x₄-expansion-participant is annihilated, the i-bearing amplitude is removed by the squaring, the spatial-slice record is established. The Born rule probability — squared because the underlying metric is rank-2 (Lemma 7.1) — is the algebraic signature of the physical annihilation event in every case.

#### 12.6.2 The radioactive alpha case: emission, spherical spreading, and detection

Consider a radioactive nucleus at rest, emitting an alpha particle by tunneling. The structure of the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s reading maps onto every stage of this canonical example, with the rotation-out-of-x₄ mechanism the same as in the photon case but with a massive-particle worldline replacing the null worldline.

(i) **Spherical wavefunction as projection of isotropic x₄-expansion.** The x₄-expansion from the emission event is isotropic in spacetime (canonical ontology, clause 3: from every event, the active expansion at ic proceeds symmetrically in all spatial directions). The spatial-slice projection of this isotropic expansion is a spherically symmetric outgoing wave centered on the emission event. The wavefunction’s initial spherical symmetry is the direct geometric record of the isotropic x₄-expansion structure, exactly as in the photon case.

(ii) **Spreading as surfing the x₄-expansion.** As proper time advances, the alpha particle’s worldline carries it forward along x₄ at the canonical rate ic per proper time, with the four-velocity budget partitioned between spatial motion and x₄-advance per u\^μ u_μ = −c² (Theorem 9.1 step 1). The wavefunction spreads over the spatial slice — at each later instant, the modulus is spread over a sphere of progressively larger radius. The spreading is the spatial-slice projection of the particle’s continuing participation in the x₄-expansion (Definition 12.1; §12.2). The wavefunction is complex-valued throughout: its phase encodes the accumulated x₄-component along the worldline, its modulus encodes the spatial-slice amplitude at each spacetime point. The difference from the photon case: the alpha’s worldline is timelike (u\^μ u_μ = −c², not 0), the alpha has a well-defined rest frame in principle, and the alpha’s spatial spreading speed is determined by its kinetic-energy distribution rather than by the universal c.

(iii) **Detection at angle θ as rotation out of x₄ and absorption into the detector.** When a detector at angle θ from the source registers the alpha particle, the particle is rotated out of x₄ at the detector’s spatial location and absorbed into the detector’s matter. The forward x₄-expansion ψ meets the detector’s localized conjugate x₄-image ψ\* at the detection event. The geometric meeting reorients the particle’s free-quantum participation in x₄-expansion into a bound, localized configuration in the detector’s matter. As with the photon, the post-detection alpha is no longer a free participant in x₄-expansion: it is absorbed, its kinetic energy deposited into ionization or excitation of the detector’s atomic structure, the free-particle wavefunction terminated. The “rotation out of x₄” is geometrically the same operation as in the photon case, applied here to a particle that had a (partial) x₄-participation rather than a (full) x₄-participation.

(iv) **Born rule probability as Wick rotation algebraic signature.** The probability of detection at angle θ is \|ψ(θ, t_det)\|² = ψ\*(θ, t_det) ψ(θ, t_det). The squaring is the algebraic signature of the rotation out of x₄: the i in the wavefunction’s phase (encoding x₄-perpendicularity) is removed by the modulus-squaring (the Wick rotation at the amplitude level, Theorem 12.2). The result is a real-valued probability density on the spatial slice — the spatial-slice observable that the laboratory records.

(v) **Collapse of unmeasured angles as completion of the rotation.** At the moment of detection at angle θ, the wavefunction at every other angle collapses to zero (Corollary 11.4). The dx₄/dt = ic framework’s reading: the alpha particle’s x₄-expansion is a single coherent four-dimensional structure; when the particle is rotated out of x₄ at one angle (the detector), the expansion structure terminates at that angle, and the spatial-slice projection at every other angle drops to zero because the underlying x₄-expansion no longer exists as a spreading entity. The particle has been rotated out of x₄ in toto across the entire spatial slice.

The alpha case differs from the photon case in two respects: the alpha has a timelike worldline (u\^μ u_μ = −c² rather than 0), and the absorbed alpha’s kinetic energy is deposited as ionization tracks in the detector’s matter (e.g., scintillator pulses, semiconductor electron-hole pairs, gas-proportional-counter ionization) rather than as a single bound-electron transition. The mechanism is the same: free-quantum x₄-expansion participant absorbed and bound into detector matter, the wavefunction’s i removed by the modulus-squaring because the free particle no longer exists.

#### 12.6.3 The universal mechanism

Both canonical cases instantiate the same mechanism. The wavefunction’s i is the imprint of the particle’s participation in x₄-expansion. The participation is full for photons (null worldline, rides the wavefront at c) and partitioned for massive particles (timelike worldline, x₄-component at rate ic per proper time). At measurement, the participation ends — the photon is annihilated, the massive particle is absorbed and bound into the detector. In neither case does the post-measurement system continue as a free quantum participating in x₄-expansion in the way the pre-measurement particle did. The i is removed from the description by the modulus-squaring because the i-bearing entity has been removed by the absorption.

The exponent 2 in the Born rule is the algebraic signature of this rotation. The rank-2 character of the Minkowski metric (Lemma 2.5, Lemma 7.1) forces the bilinear product ψ\*ψ as the unique sesquilinear invariant available for the probability density. Both squarings — the metric squaring of dx₄/dt = ic into ds² = −c²dt² + spatial (Lemma 2.5) and the amplitude squaring of ψ into \|ψ\|² (Theorem 7.4) — are the same geometric operation: removal of the i-marker for x₄-perpendicularity, applied at the kinematic level (rate squaring) and at the amplitude level (wavefunction squaring) respectively. Theorem 12.2 identifies the physical event at which the amplitude-level squaring occurs: the measurement event, at which the particle is physically rotated out of its participation in x₄-expansion.

The photon case makes the universality of the mechanism most visible because no rest-frame alternative is available for the photon. Whatever happens to a photon at absorption *cannot* be a Lorentz boost to a rest frame — there is no photon rest frame. The photon either participates in x₄-expansion at c or it does not exist as a photon at all. The mechanism the dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies for “what happens at measurement” must therefore be of a kind that applies equally to a particle with no rest frame (photon) and to a particle with a rest frame (alpha, electron, neutron). The rotation-out-of-x₄ reading meets this criterion: the photon’s full x₄-participation is removed at absorption; the massive particle’s partial x₄-participation is removed at absorption; in both cases the wavefunction’s i — the imprint of participation — is removed by the modulus-squaring; in both cases the spatial-slice record is established by the absorbing apparatus’s physical change.

This is the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s universal reading of measurement: the particle is rotated out of the x₄-expanding perpendicularity, the wavefunction’s i-bearing character is removed by the algebraic signature of the rotation (modulus squaring), and the spatial-slice record is established by the apparatus’s physical change. Every photodetection, every alpha track, every electron click, every photon registration in the empirical record of twentieth- and twenty-first-century physics is, in this reading, a physical Wick rotation — a particle annihilated or absorbed out of its participation in x₄-expansion, with the squared amplitude on the spatial slice the real-valued macroscopic record of that physical rotation.

### 12.7 The ensemble Born rule and the emergent disappearance of i: thermodynamics as the macroscopic-scale Wick rotation

§12.5 identified the single measurement event as the physical Wick rotation at a single particle (Theorem 12.2). §7.9 supplied the two-particle head-on x₄-collision mechanism for that single event (Theorem 7.7). In a macroscopic ensemble — a gas of N ∼ 10²³ particles undergoing on the order of 10⁹–10¹⁵ pairwise collisions per second per particle in a typical thermodynamic system — the head-on x₄-collision is occurring at a total rate Γ_total of order 10³²–10³⁸ events per second per macroscopic sample. Each event is a physical Wick rotation at the colliding pair. The cumulative effect on the macroscopic description of the ensemble is the emergent disappearance of the i-marker for x₄-perpendicularity: the post-collision spatial-slice records, accumulated across the ensemble, constitute a fully i-free real-valued macroscopic description — classical statistical mechanics and thermodynamics. The standard mathematical Wick rotation t → -iτ, which converts the quantum-mechanical path-integral weight exp(iS/ℏ) into the classical-statistical-mechanical Boltzmann weight exp(-S_E/ℏ), is in this reading the formal abstraction of the cumulative physical Wick rotation performed by the ensemble at rate Γ_total.

**Theorem 12.4 (Statistical-cumulative Wick rotation: thermodynamics as the macroscopic-scale physical Wick rotation).** *Let an ensemble of N free quantum particles of mass m, density ρ, and mean spatial speed v undergo pairwise McGucken-sphere head-on collisions at total rate Γ_total = (1/2) · N · ρ σ v, with σ the relevant scattering cross-section. By Theorem 12.2 and Theorem 7.7, each collision is a physical Wick rotation at the colliding pair, removing the i-marker for x₄-perpendicularity from both colliding particles’ descriptions and depositing a real-valued spatial-slice configuration record at the collision event. Then for sufficiently large N · T (the thermodynamic limit, with T the time interval of observation), the cumulative macroscopic spatial-slice configuration record is:*

*(i) i-free and real-valued (the i-marker for x₄-perpendicularity has been removed at every collision event, with the cumulative description over all Γ_total · T events being entirely real-valued);*

*(ii) governed by classical statistical-mechanical equations — Boltzmann’s H-functional H = ∫ f log f d³v decreasing monotonically toward equilibrium, Maxwell-Boltzmann velocity distribution at equilibrium, the second law dS/dt ≥ 0 — with the irreversibility supplied by the one-way character of the rotation-out-of-x₄ at each collision (Theorem 12.2);*

*(iii) the macroscopic-scale physical realization of the standard mathematical Wick rotation t → -iτ; the latter is performed once on the path integral as a coordinate substitution, the former is performed Γ_total times per second across the ensemble as a sequence of physical events.*

**Proof.**

(1) By Theorem 12.2 (steps (5)–(6)), each measurement event removes the i from the participating particle’s amplitude by the modulus-squaring ψ → ψ\^\*ψ. By Theorem 7.7 (clause (iii)), each measurement event is the head-on x₄-collision of two McGucken spheres, with the x₄-momenergy cancelling and being redeposited as 3-spatial momenergy at the collision point. The amplitude-level i-removal of Theorem 12.2 and the geometric rotation-out-of-x₄ of Theorem 7.7 are two descriptions of the same single physical event.

(2) For an ensemble of N particles at density ρ with mean speed v and pairwise collision cross-section σ, the per-particle collision rate is ν_coll = ρ σ v (the standard mean-free-path collision rate from kinetic theory). The total ensemble collision rate is Γ_total = (1/2) N ν_coll = (1/2) N ρ σ v (the factor 1/2 because each collision involves two particles). For air at STP (N ∼ 6 × 10²³ per mole, ρ ∼ 2.5 × 10¹⁹ molecules per cm³, v ∼ 5 × 10⁴ cm/s, σ ∼ 4 × 10⁻¹⁵ cm² for N₂-N₂ collisions), Γ_total ∼ 10³⁴ collisions per second per mole.

(3) Each collision deposits a spatial-slice configuration record (the two-particle outgoing momenta and positions on the spatial slice at the collision event, with the post-collision momenta determined by the elastic-collision kinematics). The record is i-free: the post-collision particles’ four-velocity budget has been rotated from x₄-dominated to spatial-dominated (Theorem 7.7 (iii)), with the i-marker for x₄-perpendicularity removed by the modulus-squaring (Theorem 12.2 (5)).

(4) Over time T, the cumulative spatial-slice configuration record across the ensemble is the time-integrated histogram of all Γ_total · T collision outcomes. In the limit N · T → ∞ (the thermodynamic limit), this histogram converges to the equilibrium statistical-mechanical distribution. For a dilute gas of identical particles with two-body elastic collisions, the convergence is the content of Boltzmann’s H-theorem: H = ∫ f log f d³v decreases monotonically, with the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution f(v) = (m/(2π k_B T))\^{3/2} exp(-mv²/(2k_B T)) the equilibrium attractor at which H ceases to decrease. The Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution is i-free and real-valued, observable as the velocity distribution of the macroscopic gas — establishing (ii).

(5) The second law of thermodynamics, dS/dt ≥ 0 along the macroscopic time-evolution (with S = -k_B ∫ f log f d³v the Gibbs-Boltzmann entropy), is the statement that the cumulative configuration record approaches equilibrium and remains there once attained. The irreversibility is supplied by the one-way character of each collision’s rotation-out-of-x₄: once two free quanta have collided and been deposited as a spatial-slice record, no reverse process within the ensemble’s microscopic Schrödinger dynamics can recover the pre-collision free-quantum state — because the post-collision particles are no longer free participants in x₄-expansion in the way the pre-collision particles were. The arrow of time at the thermodynamic level is the cumulative arrow of these collision events.

(6) The standard mathematical Wick rotation t → -iτ, acting at the path-integral level, converts exp(iS/ℏ) → exp(-S_E/ℏ). The transformed path integral defines classical statistical mechanics with Boltzmann weights — the very statistical mechanics that steps (4)–(5) realized as the macroscopic limit of the ensemble. The mathematical Wick rotation is therefore the formal abstraction of the cumulative physical Wick rotation performed by the ensemble. A single coordinate substitution at the formalism level corresponds to Γ_total · T physical events at the ensemble level; the formalism’s “single coordinate change” is the empirical “ensemble-amplified Born rule” performed across all colliding pairs at rate Γ_total — establishing (iii). ∎

**Remark 12.5 (the Wick rotation “exalted Γ_total times per second”).** The standard mathematical Wick rotation is a single coordinate substitution, performed once at the path-integral level. The physics of this substitution — removal of the i-marker for x₄-perpendicularity from the action — is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the physics of a single measurement event (Theorem 12.2). In a macroscopic ensemble, the same physical operation is performed by every collision event at total rate Γ_total ∼ 10³⁴ s⁻¹ per macroscopic sample. The macroscopic appearance of thermodynamics — its complete absence of i in any equation, its real-valued thermodynamic potentials, its real-valued entropy, its real-valued Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution — is the cumulative effect of this ensemble-amplified physical Wick rotation. Thermodynamics is, in this reading, **the Wick rotation exalted Γ_total times per second** by the ensemble’s Born rule events. The well-known correspondence between Wick-rotated quantum mechanics and classical statistical mechanics is restated here with a physical mechanism for the correspondence: each Born rule event at every collision in the ensemble is itself a physical Wick rotation, and the macroscopic statistical mechanics is the cumulative effect of all of them.

**Remark 12.6 (resolution of the “two arrows of time” puzzle).** A long-standing question in the foundations of thermodynamics: why is there a macroscopic arrow of time (entropy increases monotonically) when the underlying microscopic equations (the Schrödinger evolution of Theorem 9.1, the unitary Schrödinger flow of Theorem 9.2, Hamilton’s equations for the classical limit) are time-symmetric? The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s answer: the microscopic time-symmetric evolution is the description *between* measurements. Each measurement event is irreversible — the rotation-out-of-x₄ at a collision (Theorem 7.7, Theorem 12.2) deposits a spatial-slice record that cannot be undone by reversing the Schrödinger equation, because the post-collision state is no longer a free quantum participating in x₄-expansion in the way the pre-collision state was. The thermodynamic arrow of time is therefore the cumulative arrow of all measurements in the ensemble. The second law’s increasing-entropy direction is the direction in which more measurements have accumulated — equivalently, the direction in which more physical Wick rotations have been performed. The “two arrows” — the time-symmetric microscopic dynamics and the time-asymmetric macroscopic thermodynamics — are reconciled: the latter is the macroscopic record of the former’s interruption by measurement events, with the interruptions one-way (rotation-out-of-x₄ is irreversible) and the cumulative count of interruptions growing monotonically with parameter time.

**Remark 12.7 (spherically symmetric emission as direct evidence of x₄-expansion nonlocality).** That a radioactive sample emits its decay products spherically symmetrically in space — equally probable in every spatial direction, with no preferred axis once the sample’s orientation is averaged or the emitter’s orientation is isotropic by construction — is direct empirical evidence of the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s reading. The spherical symmetry is the spatial-slice projection of the isotropic x₄-expansion (canonical clause 3, §2.4) from the emission event. The nonlocal character of the pre-detection wavefunction — its spread over a sphere of progressively larger radius as proper time advances — is the spatial-slice projection of the particle’s continuing participation in the active x₄-expansion. The probability distribution of detection events across many emissions reproduces the spherical symmetry of the x₄-expansion exactly: equally many detections per unit solid angle in every direction, with the probability per unit volume at radius r decreasing as 1/r² (geometric thinning of the spherical wavefront) as the wavefront expands. Each individual detection is one Born rule event — one head-on x₄-collision (Theorem 7.7) — and the cumulative statistics of many such detections is the empirics of the wavefunction’s \|ψ\|² density.

### 12.8 Boost and measurement as the two physical realizations of rotation with respect to x₄

The McGucken framework’s unification of GR and QM through dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 10.5) admits, in light of Theorem 7.7 and Theorem 12.2, an explicit physical reading at the level of operations on a single particle. In both theories, the operation of changing a particle’s spatial state arises from a rotation involving x₄. In relativity, this rotation is the Lorentz boost — a continuous hyperbolic rotation in the (x_i, x_4) plane that mixes a spatial direction with x_4 = ict, changing the particle’s spatial velocity. In quantum mechanics, this rotation is the measurement event — a discrete rotation in the (x_4, \[spatial direction at E\]) plane that takes the particle’s four-velocity from x_4-participation to x₁x₂x₃-localization at E, changing the particle’s spatial position from spread-out to localized. The two operations are the two physical realizations of rotation with respect to x_4, both descending from the same upstream principle dx₄/dt = ic.

**Proposition 12.8 (Boost-measurement parallel: the two physical rotations with respect to x_4).** *The Lorentz boost in relativity and the measurement event in quantum mechanics are the two physical realizations of rotation in a plane containing x_4 = ict:*

*(i) (Boost.) The Lorentz boost in a (1+1)D plane (t, x_i) is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, a hyperbolic rotation in the (x_4, x_i) plane with x_4 = ict — specifically a rotation of rapidity ξ with tanh ξ = v/c, mapping (x_4, x_i) → (x_4 cosh ξ - (i x_i / c) sinh ξ · c, x_i cosh ξ - (x_4 / c) sinh ξ · c) and equivalent in real Minkowski coordinates to the standard boost (ct, x_i) → ((ct - (v/c) x_i) γ, (x_i - v t) γ) with γ = cosh ξ = 1/√(1 - v²/c²). The effect: the particle’s spatial velocity changes from 0 (initial rest in the original frame) to v (final spatial velocity in the boosted frame). The particle’s four-velocity budget is reallocated: some x_4-component is rotated into spatial-component, with the total magnitude c preserved (u\^μu_μ = -c² is invariant under the rotation).*

*(ii) (Measurement.) The measurement event at E is, by Theorem 12.2, the rotation in the (x_4, \[spatial direction at E\]) plane that takes the particle’s four-velocity from the pre-measurement x_4-dominated configuration (worldline tangent “surfing the wavefront,” phase encoding accumulated x_4-component) to the post-measurement spatial-direction-dominated configuration (worldline tangent committed to a definite spatial position at a definite t, with the i-marker for x_4-perpendicularity removed by the modulus-squaring at the head-on x₄-collision; Theorem 7.7). The effect: the particle’s spatial position is localized at E, with its x_4-participation ended.*

*(iii) (Common geometry.) Both operations are rotations in a plane containing x_4. The boost (i) is a continuous rotation parameterized by rapidity ξ, with continuous one-parameter family of outcomes (velocities from 0 to c). The measurement (ii) is a discrete rotation at the head-on x_4-collision event, with the outcome being one of the eigenvalues of the measured observable. Both operations descend from dx₄/dt = ic: the boost from the rotation symmetry of the Lorentzian metric (Lemma 2.5, descended from (ict)² = -c²t²); the measurement from the head-on x_4-collision mechanism (Theorem 7.7, descended from the bilinear pairing Lemma 7.1, descended from the rank-2 metric Lemma 2.5, descended from dx₄/dt = ic).*

**Proof.**

*(i)* The Lorentzian metric arises from the squared form of dx₄/dt = ic (Lemma 2.5): (ict)² = -c²t², giving the signature (-, +, +, +) on `\mathbb{M}`{=tex}\_{1,3}. The isometry group of this metric is SO(1,3); its boost subgroup acts on the (x_4, x_i) coordinates as the hyperbolic rotation in that plane. In the (x_4 = ict, x_i) coordinate frame, this is geometrically a rotation in the plane containing the perpendicular x_4 direction and the spatial direction x_i — the angle of rotation being the rapidity ξ with tanh ξ = v/c. The particle’s worldline tangent, initially aligned with x_4 in its rest frame (full four-velocity budget in x_4 with magnitude ic per proper time), rotates by ξ to make angle (in the analytic-continuation sense after Wick rotation, or in the hyperbolic-rotation sense in Lorentzian signature) corresponding to spatial velocity v with x_4-component-magnitude reduced to ic cosh ξ. The reallocation of the four-velocity budget across the rotation preserves u\^μu_μ = -c² (the four-velocity magnitude is the Lorentz invariant).

*(ii)* Theorem 12.2 establishes that the measurement event rotates the particle from x_4-participation (worldline tangent dominated by x_4-component, phase encoding accumulated x_4-component) to x₁x₂x₃-localization at E (worldline tangent committed to a definite spatial position at a definite t, with the i-marker for x_4-perpendicularity removed). The rotation is geometrically of the same character as the boost — rotation in a plane containing x_4 — but with three differences from (i): (a) the rotation is discrete (the head-on x_4-collision of Theorem 7.7 is an event, not a continuous transformation parameterized by ξ); (b) the rotation is at the amplitude level (the i is removed from the wavefunction, with the coordinate-level Wick rotation x_4 → ct the formal correlate performed once on the formalism); and (c) the rotation is irreversible (the post-measurement state is no longer a free quantum participating in x_4-expansion, and no continuous parameter exists by which the rotation can be undone).

*(iii)* Both transformations are rotations in a plane containing x_4 = ict. The boost is the continuous, unitary, reversible version (parameterized by rapidity ξ, with the boost subgroup forming a one-parameter family connected to the identity). The measurement is the discrete, non-unitary, irreversible version (occurring at the head-on collision event, with no continuous parameter). Both are physical operations on the same geometric structure — the (x_4, spatial) plane in a Minkowski frame. The shared upstream principle dx₄/dt = ic supplies the x_4 in both cases: in the boost, as the perpendicular direction whose rotation mixes with spatial directions to change velocity; in the measurement, as the perpendicular direction whose participation is ended by the head-on collision with another McGucken sphere. ∎

**Remark 12.9 (a unifying physical reading of boost and measurement).** The boost is what happens to a free particle when it is accelerated in space — its spatial velocity changes because some of its x_4-momenergy has been rotated into spatial momenergy, with the rotation continuous and reversible (the particle remains a free participant in x_4-expansion, just with a reallocated four-velocity budget). The measurement is what happens to a free particle when it collides head-on with a localized absorber — its spatial position changes from spread-out to localized because all of its x_4-momenergy at the collision moment has been cancelled by the absorber’s opposing x_4-momenergy and redeposited as 3-spatial momenergy at the collision point, with the rotation discrete and irreversible (the particle ceases to be a free participant in x_4-expansion). The boost is a *partial* rotation (some x_4-component remains, the particle continues to participate in x_4-expansion at a reduced rate per spatial axis); the measurement is a *total* rotation (no free x_4-component remains, the particle is no longer a free participant). Both are operations on the same geometric structure — the four-dimensional configuration where x_4 = ict is the perpendicular dimension — differing in continuity/discreteness, reversibility, and totality but sharing the same underlying mechanism: rotation involving x_4.

The dx₄/dt = ic framework’s unification of GR and QM through dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 10.5) is therefore a physical statement that the boost (the central operation of relativity) and the measurement (the central operation of quantum mechanics) are the same kind of physical operation, partial-and-continuous in the relativistic case, total-and-discrete in the quantum case, both rotations involving x_4 = ict. The boost-measurement parallel completes the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s reading of the four-dimensional structure of physics: the Lorentzian metric (Lemma 2.5) is the squared rate-form of dx₄/dt = ic; the Born density (Theorem 7.2) is the squared amplitude-form of the wavefunction; the boost (relativity’s continuous rotation involving x_4) and the measurement (QM’s discrete rotation out of x_4) are the two operations that rotate a particle’s free four-velocity budget with respect to x_4. All four — metric, density, boost, measurement — are downstream consequences of the one principle dx₄/dt = ic.

### 12.9 Position in x₁x₂x₃ and momentum in x₄: the operator-level statement of the boost-measurement parallel

Proposition 12.8 of the previous subsection established the boost-measurement parallel at the geometric level: both are rotations in a plane containing x_4 = ict, with the boost continuous-reversible-partial and the measurement discrete-irreversible-total. The present subsection descends this parallel one cascade level: the *operator-level* statement of the same x₁x₂x₃/x₄ split shows up directly in the structure of the canonical commutation relation \[q̂\_i, p̂\_j\] = iℏ δ_ij of Theorem 5.1. The position operator q̂\_i has its content entirely in x₁x₂x₃ — pure spatial-slice multiplication, with no factor of i and no factor of ℏ. The momentum operator p̂\_i = -iℏ ∂/∂x_i has its content entirely in x_4 — the i marks x_4-perpendicularity (Theorem 3.1, §4.3), the ℏ marks the action quantum of x_4-oscillation (Proposition 2.2), and the spatial derivative ∂/∂x_i extracts how the wavefunction’s x_4-phase accumulates per unit displacement in spatial direction x_i. The canonical commutator’s structure — its non-zero magnitude, its imaginary unit, its action quantum, and its Kronecker delta — records exactly this split.

**Proposition 12.10 (Canonical commutation relation as algebraic statement of the x₁x₂x₃ / x_4 split).** \*The canonical commutation relation \[q̂\_i, p̂\_j\] = iℏ δ_ij of Theorem 5.1 is the operator-level algebraic statement of the geometric perpendicularity x₁x₂x₃ ⊥ x_4 that the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic forces on the constraint surface `\mathbb{M}`{=tex}\_{1,3} (Lemma 2.5). Specifically:\*

\*(i) (q̂ in x₁x₂x₃.) The position operator q̂\_i acts on ψ by multiplication by the spatial coordinate x_i. Its content is entirely in the spatial slice x₁x₂x₃ — no factor of i, no factor of ℏ, no derivative. q̂\_i is a pure spatial-slice operator.\*

\*(ii) (p̂ in x_4.) The momentum operator p̂\_i = -iℏ ∂/∂x_i acts on ψ by extracting the rate of x_4-phase accumulation per unit displacement in spatial direction x_i. The factor i marks the perpendicularity of x_4 to x₁x₂x₃ (Theorem 3.1, §4.3); the factor ℏ marks the action quantum carried by one Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance (Proposition 2.2). Both i and ℏ in p̂\_i descend from x_4, not from x₁x₂x₃. p̂\_i is the operator whose action on ψ reads off the wavefunction’s x_4-content, parameterized by the rate at which that content varies across the spatial slice.\*

\*(iii) (Non-zero commutator as operator-level non-closure.) The non-zero commutator \[q̂\_i, p̂\_i\] = iℏ records the infinitesimal non-closure between “translation by ε in x_i” and “translation by δ in x_4-phase-rate.” A round trip in the (q̂, p̂)-plane around an infinitesimal parallelogram of area εδ — apply q̂\_i, then p̂\_i, then -q̂\_i, then -p̂\_i — fails to close by exactly iℏ · εδ. The non-closure magnitude is one action quantum ℏ (in the perpendicular direction marked by i), recording that q̂\_i and p̂\_i access orthogonal cascade-level directions of the four-dimensional structure (x_i in x₁x₂x₃ and x_4 respectively).\*

\*(iv) (Kronecker δ_ij as direction-specific perpendicularity.) The Kronecker δ_ij records that x_4-perpendicularity attaches to a specific spatial direction. The operator q̂\_i (multiplication by x_i) and p̂\_j with i ≠ j (the x_4-phase-rate per unit step in x_j ≠ x_i) access different spatial-direction projections of the four-dimensional structure: q̂\_i is in the spatial direction x_i; p̂\_j is in the (x_j, x_4)-plane perpendicular pair with x_j ≠ x_i. These two operators do not share a common (spatial-direction, x_4-perpendicular-direction) pair, and their commutator vanishes. Only when i = j do q̂\_i and p̂\_j share the (x_i, x_4)-perpendicular pair, and only then does the commutator carry the non-closure quantum iℏ.\*

*(v) (Position eigenstates and momentum eigenstates as the two complementary limits of x_4-participation.) A position eigenstate \|x₀⟩ ∝ δ(x - x₀) is fully localized in x₁x₂x₃ at x₀, with zero x_4-participation remaining at the localization event — total rotation out of x_4 at x₀ (the limiting case of the measurement event of Theorem 12.2 with infinitely sharp localization). Its momentum is completely undetermined because no x_4-phase-rate information exists at a perfectly localized x₁x₂x₃ event. A momentum eigenstate \|p⟩ ∝ exp(ip · x / ℏ) is fully extended over x₁x₂x₃ as a plane wave with constant amplitude and pure x_4-phase; its x_4-participation is maximal and uniform across the spatial slice. Its position is completely undetermined because the wavefunction has no spatial-slice peak. The two eigenstate families are the two complementary limits of x_4-participation: zero x_4-content with full x₁x₂x₃-localization (position eigenstates) vs full x_4-content with full x₁x₂x₃-delocalization (momentum eigenstates).*

*(vi) (Fourier conjugacy as the algebraic shadow of x₁x₂x₃ ⊥ x_4.) The Fourier-conjugate relation ⟨x \| p⟩ = (1/√(2πℏ)\^{n/2}) exp(i p · x / ℏ) between position and momentum bases is the algebraic shadow of the geometric perpendicularity x₁x₂x₃ ⊥ x_4. The exponential kernel exp(i p · x / ℏ) is the x_4-phase that a momentum-eigenstate plane wave accumulates per unit spatial displacement x — precisely the Compton-de Broglie content reading exactly as the Lagrangian-channel form of dx₄/dt = ic over a spatial step. Fourier conjugacy in QM and geometric perpendicularity in the spacetime structure are not analogous; they are the same fact at different cascade levels of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework.*

**Proof.**

*(i)* By Theorem 6.1’s construction of 𝓗 as L²(`\mathbb{M}`{=tex}\_{1,3}), the position operator q̂*i is multiplication by the i-th spatial coordinate function x_i on the spatial slice. The spatial coordinate functions x₁, x₂, x₃ are pure real-valued labels on the spatial slice of `\mathbb{M}`{=tex}*{1,3}; they carry no x_4-content (the x_4-direction is perpendicular to the spatial slice by Theorem 3.1 and §4.3) and no action-quantum content (Proposition 2.2’s ℏ attaches to x_4-oscillation, not to spatial-slice coordinate labels). Therefore q̂\_i is a pure spatial-slice operator, free of i and free of ℏ.

*(ii)* By Theorem 5.1’s derivation, p̂\_i = -iℏ ∂/∂x_i is the spatial component of the four-momentum operator in the rest frame. The full four-momentum operator is P̂\_μ = -iℏ ∂/∂x\^μ with the temporal component P̂\_4 carrying x_4-content (the time component in the (x_4 = ict, x_1, x_2, x_3) coordinate frame). The spatial component p̂\_i = P̂\_i = -iℏ ∂/∂x_i acts on ψ by extracting how ψ’s x_4-phase varies per unit spatial displacement: applied to a plane wave ψ = exp(i k · x), p̂\_i ψ = ℏk_i ψ — yielding the spatial component of the four-wavevector ℏk_i, which is by the Compton-de Broglie relation the spatial-slice projection of the particle’s x_4-phase advance per unit spatial step. The i and the ℏ in p̂\_i are therefore both attached to x_4: i is the perpendicularity marker (Theorem 3.1, §4.3), ℏ is the action quantum per Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance (Proposition 2.2).

*(iii)* By direct calculation on a test wavefunction ψ ∈ 𝓗,

\[q̂\_i, p̂\_i\] ψ = q̂\_i (-iℏ ∂ψ/∂x_i) - p̂\_i (x_i ψ) = -iℏ x_i ∂ψ/∂x_i - (-iℏ)(ψ + x_i ∂ψ/∂x_i) = iℏ ψ,

establishing \[q̂\_i, p̂\_i\] = iℏ as an operator identity on 𝓗. Geometrically, this is the infinitesimal-loop non-closure: applying the four operations (q̂\_i, p̂\_i, -q̂\_i, -p̂\_i) in sequence does to (1 + iℏ/\[something\]) ψ at infinitesimal order, with the non-closure proportional to the loop’s signed area in (q, p)-space and to the action quantum ℏ in the perpendicular (i-marked) direction. The non-closure occurs because q̂\_i and p̂\_i access orthogonal cascade-level directions of the four-dimensional structure: q̂\_i accesses x_i in x₁x₂x₃; p̂\_i accesses the x_4-direction (via the x_4-phase rate that p̂\_i reads off). The non-closure quantum is exactly iℏ — one perpendicularity-marker times one action-quantum — because that is the minimum content of one Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance perpendicular to the spatial slice.

*(iv)* By analogous direct calculation, \[q̂\_i, p̂\_j\] ψ = -iℏ x_i ∂ψ/∂x_j - (-iℏ) ∂(x_i ψ)/∂x_j = -iℏ x_i ∂ψ/∂x_j + iℏ (δ_ij ψ + x_i ∂ψ/∂x_j) = iℏ δ_ij ψ. The Kronecker δ_ij thus emerges as the algebraic record that q̂\_i (in spatial direction x_i) and p̂\_j (the x_4-phase rate in spatial direction x_j) share their (spatial, x_4-perpendicular) pair only when i = j. For i ≠ j the two operators access different spatial-direction projections of the (spatial, x_4-perpendicular)-structure, and their non-closure vanishes — the round trip in the (q̂\_i, p̂\_j) plane closes exactly when i ≠ j because no shared (spatial direction, x_4-perpendicular direction) pair is involved.

*(v)* A position eigenstate \|x₀⟩ ∝ δ(x - x₀) has support concentrated at the spatial point x₀ on the spatial slice; its wavefunction has no spatial extension and therefore no x_4-phase variation across space (the phase exists only at the single point x₀ and has no rate-of-change content). This is the limiting case in which the particle has been fully rotated out of x_4 at x₀ — the rotation-out-of-x_4 of Theorem 12.2 in its infinitely-sharp-localization limit. The momentum eigenvalue is correspondingly undetermined: the Fourier transform of δ(x - x₀) is exp(-i p · x₀ / ℏ), which has constant modulus across all p-values — the momentum is uniformly distributed across all possible values. A momentum eigenstate \|p⟩ ∝ exp(i p · x / ℏ) has uniform modulus across all of x₁x₂x₃; its x_4-phase varies linearly across the spatial slice at rate p/ℏ per unit spatial displacement; its spatial localization is correspondingly absent (modulus is constant everywhere). The position eigenvalue is undetermined: the Fourier transform of exp(i p · x / ℏ) is δ(x’ - x) localized in p-space, not in x-space. The complementarity of \|x₀⟩ and \|p⟩ is the complementarity of “zero x_4-content, full x₁x₂x₃-localization” and “full x_4-content, full x₁x₂x₃-delocalization” — the two opposite limits on a particle’s four-velocity-budget allocation (§2.3, §9.2 step 1).

*(vi)* The Fourier kernel ⟨x \| p⟩ = (1/√(2πℏ)\^{n/2}) exp(i p · x / ℏ) is exactly the x_4-phase carried per unit spatial displacement x for a momentum-eigenstate plane wave: the phase exp(i p · x / ℏ) is the integral of the x_4-phase rate p/ℏ across the spatial displacement, with the i in the exponent the perpendicularity marker for x_4 and the ℏ in the denominator the action quantum per oscillation. The Fourier conjugacy between (x \| basis) and (p \| basis), which in textbook QM is presented as an abstract algebraic relation, is in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework the algebraic record of the geometric perpendicularity x₁x₂x₃ ⊥ x_4 of the four-dimensional structure: the position-basis records spatial-slice content; the momentum-basis records x_4-content (as x_4-phase rate across the spatial slice); the Fourier transform exchanges the two by integrating the (Compton-de Broglie) x_4-phase against the spatial coordinate. ∎

**Remark 12.10 (Why p̂ is Hermitian despite carrying i: the same frame-relational i of Theorem 7.7).** The momentum operator p̂ = -iℏ ∂/∂x carries an explicit imaginary unit, but is required to be Hermitian for momentum to be a measurable real-valued observable. Hermiticity holds because integration by parts shifts the derivative from one factor to the other, with the resulting sign change exactly compensating the explicit i in p̂’s definition: ⟨φ \| p̂ψ⟩ = -iℏ ∫ φ\^\* (∂ψ/∂x) dx = +iℏ ∫ (∂φ\^*/∂x) ψ dx = ∫ (-iℏ ∂φ/∂x)\^* ψ dx = ⟨p̂φ \| ψ⟩, using the fact that the i in p̂ satisfies i\^\* = -i. This algebraic fact — that i\^\* = -i — is the same frame-relational complex conjugation that Theorem 7.7 (i) and (ii) identified as the absorber’s outgoing x_4-direction appearing antiparallel from the emitter’s frame. The operator-level Hermiticity of p̂ and the geometric-level frame-relational antiparallelism of the head-on x_4-collision are the same fact: x_4-perpendicularity is preserved under conjugate frame-swap, with the i and -i exchanging roles consistently.

**Remark 12.11 (Why p̂ generates rotations involving x_4: the boost-measurement parallel descends to the operator level).** Proposition 12.8 established the boost-measurement parallel at the geometric level: both are rotations in a plane containing x_4 = ict. At the operator level, the boost generator is essentially the momentum operator: the Lorentz boost K_i in spatial direction i is generated by p̂\_i (up to normalization by c and rest-mass content). This is the operator-level expression of the boost-measurement parallel: the same operator p̂\_i that generates the continuous-reversible boost (Lorentz transformation) is the operator whose eigenvalues are read off at the discrete-irreversible measurement (momentum measurement). Both operations are operations on the wavefunction’s x_4-content, and both are realized by the same operator at the operator level. The boost extracts x_4-content continuously (rotating some x_4-component into spatial-component, with the particle remaining a free quantum); the momentum measurement extracts x_4-content discretely (reading off the x_4-phase rate and reducing the wavefunction to a momentum eigenstate). q̂ and p̂ are the operator-level instantiations of “spatial-slice operations” (q̂) and “x_4-rotation operations” (p̂), with their non-commutation being the algebraic record of the geometric perpendicularity that the boost-measurement parallel exhibits.

\*\*Remark 12.12 (Classical limit and the ensemble Wick rotation: how \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ becomes \[q, p\]\_PB = 1).\*\* In classical mechanics, position and momentum are real-valued functions on a real-valued phase space, and they commute as functions: q · p = p · q. The transition from quantum \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ to classical Poisson bracket {q, p}\_PB = 1 is the Dirac correspondence (i/ℏ) \[·, ·\] ↔ {·, ·}\_PB. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, this correspondence is the algebra of the ensemble-amplified Wick rotation of Theorem 12.4: in the classical limit, the i-marker for x_4-perpendicularity has been removed by the ensemble’s cumulative Born rule events, the ℏ action-quantum has been integrated out into the real-valued phase space (the cumulative ℏ-quanta become a real-valued Liouville measure dq dp), and the operator non-commutation iℏ becomes the function commutativity 0. The Dirac correspondence (i/ℏ) \[·, ·\] ↔ {·, ·}\_PB is the Wick-rotation factor (i and ℏ both removed by integration over the cumulative ensemble’s i-removals at every collision). Where Theorem 12.4 established that thermodynamics is the ensemble-amplified Wick rotation of QM, this remark adds: the entire Hamiltonian-mechanics structure of classical phase space — including \[q, p\]\_PB — is the same ensemble-amplified Wick rotation applied to the operator-level structure \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ. The classical limit is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the Wick-rotation-amplified-by-the-ensemble of the operator-algebraic core of quantum mechanics.

### 12.10 The universal non-closure quantum: ℏ across foundational physics

The non-closure of round-trip rotations involving x_4 is not confined to the canonical commutator. The McGucken framework’s reading of dx₄/dt = ic with action quantum ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation (Proposition 2.2) supplies a single physical mechanism by which **any closed loop in physics that involves a round-trip through x_4 cannot close more tightly than the action quantum ℏ.** This minimum-non-closure principle is the upstream physics of a list of independently celebrated results across foundational physics — the canonical commutator (Theorem 5.1), the Robertson uncertainty bound σ_q σ_p ≥ ℏ/2 (Theorem 8.2), the Berry geometric phase (Berry 1984), the spin-1/2 4π closure requirement (the SU(2) double-cover of SO(3), confirmed empirically by Rauch–Werner–Colella–Overhauser 1975), the Bohr–Sommerfeld quantization with Maslov ½-correction, the Aharonov–Bohm phase (Aharonov–Bohm 1959; confirmed by Tonomura et al. 1986), the Dirac magnetic monopole quantization eg = (n/2) ℏc (Dirac 1931), the Wigner rotation from non-parallel boost composition (Wigner 1939; Thomas 1927), and the universal path-integral interference exp(iS/ℏ) of Feynman’s formulation. Each of these has been treated historically as a separate empirical fact requiring its own derivation; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework places all nine under a single upstream principle and identifies the universal minimum quantum ℏ as the action carried by one cycle of x_4-advance.

#### 12.10.1 Historical context: nine separate threads, never unified

The history of these non-closure results is the history of nine separate threads, with partial unifications among subsets but no overall connection to the canonical commutator and to a common upstream physical principle.

**Pancharatnam (1956)** introduced the polarization-state phase that bears his name in *Generalized theory of interference and its applications*, *Proceedings of the Indian Academy of Sciences* A 44, 247–262. Pancharatnam observed that transporting a polarization state around a closed loop on the Poincaré sphere of polarization states accumulates a phase equal to half the solid angle enclosed by the loop. This was the first instance of what would later be called a geometric phase. Pancharatnam did not connect this to the canonical commutator or to any other quantum-mechanical non-closure, and his work remained largely uncited for nearly three decades.

**Dirac (1931)** in *Quantised singularities in the electromagnetic field*, *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* 133, 60–72, established that the wavefunction of a charged particle in the presence of a magnetic monopole must be single-valued, which requires eg = (n/2) ℏc for some integer n. Dirac’s derivation was topological: the Dirac string is unobservable iff the round-trip phase around it is a multiple of 2π. Dirac did not connect his quantization condition to the canonical commutator or to any broader non-closure structure; he viewed it as a constraint on charge values necessary for consistency of QED with monopoles.

**Aharonov and Bohm (1959)** in *Significance of electromagnetic potentials in the quantum theory*, *Physical Review* 115, 485–491, established that a charged particle going around a region of confined magnetic flux Φ acquires a phase exp(ieΦ/ℏ) even though the magnetic field along its trajectory is zero. The phase is observable in interference experiments. Aharonov and Bohm noted the topological character of the result but did not connect it to the canonical commutator or to the uncertainty principle.

**Bohr (1913)** and **Sommerfeld (1916)**, in the old quantum theory, posited the quantization condition ∮ p dq = nh for closed classical orbits. **Maslov (1965)** and **Arnold (1967)** corrected the rule to ∮ p dq = (n + μ/4) h, where μ is the Maslov index counting caustic / turning-point traversals. The ½-correction was understood by Arnold as a topological invariant of Lagrangian submanifolds. Neither Maslov nor Arnold connected the ½-quantum correction to the canonical commutator’s iℏ or to the geometric phase.

**Rauch, Werner, Colella, Overhauser** (and independently Werner et al.) demonstrated the 4π-closure of spin-1/2 in 1975, in two simultaneous papers (\[Rauch et al., *Physics Letters* 54A, 425–427; Werner et al., *Physical Review Letters* 35, 1053–1055\]), using neutron interferometry with magnetic-field-induced spin precession. The result was understood as the empirical confirmation of the SU(2) double cover of SO(3), itself known mathematically since Cartan. Rauch–Werner et al. did not connect 4π-closure to the canonical commutator or to the geometric phase.

**Tonomura et al. (1986)**, in *Evidence for Aharonov–Bohm effect with magnetic field completely shielded from electron wave*, *Physical Review Letters* 56, 792–795, achieved the definitive empirical confirmation of the Aharonov–Bohm effect using shielded superconducting magnetic flux and electron holography. Tonomura’s group did not connect their result beyond the Aharonov–Bohm framework.

**Yang (1974)**, in *Integral formalism for gauge fields*, *Physical Review Letters* 33, 445–447, recognized that the Aharonov–Bohm phase, the Dirac monopole quantization, and the general structure of gauge invariance live in a common framework of “nonintegrable phase factors” — line integrals of the gauge connection along closed paths. Yang’s framework was extended in **Wu and Yang (1975)**, *Concept of nonintegrable phase factors and global formulation of gauge fields*, *Physical Review D* 12, 3845–3857, which identified the Aharonov–Bohm phase factor and the Dirac monopole quantization condition as manifestations of a single mathematical structure: the holonomy of a connection on a U(1) principal fiber bundle over spacetime. Wu and Yang’s paper is the most ambitious pre-Berry unification of the gauge-theoretic non-closures. It connected Aharonov–Bohm, Dirac monopoles, and the general non-Abelian generalization (Yang–Mills theory) under one geometric umbrella — but did not extend to the canonical commutator, the uncertainty principle, the spin-1/2 4π closure, the Bohr–Sommerfeld–Maslov, the Wigner rotation, or the Pancharatnam phase. It was a gauge-theory-internal unification, not a foundational physical unification.

**Souriau (1970)**, in *Structure des systèmes dynamiques* (Dunod, Paris), and independently **Kostant (1970)**, in *Quantization and unitary representations* (Springer Lecture Notes in Mathematics 170), developed the dx₄/dt = ic framework of geometric quantization. They showed that the integrality condition for a symplectic manifold to admit a pre-quantum line bundle (the Souriau–Kostant prequantization condition) connects the Bohr–Sommerfeld quantization, the Dirac monopole quantization, and the magnetic flux quantization to a single cohomological condition: the symplectic 2-form’s integral over closed 2-cycles must be quantized in units of h. This was a unification at the symplectic-geometric level, more general than Wu–Yang. But geometric quantization did not connect to the canonical commutator’s iℏ as a foundational physics; the iℏ was treated as the input from which the dx₄/dt = ic framework began, not as a derived quantity of an upstream physical principle. Geometric quantization gave a mathematical framework in which several non-closures live together; it did not provide an upstream physical reason why ℏ should be the universal quantum.

**Berry (1984)**, in *Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes*, *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* 392, 45–57, identified the geometric phase γ_B = ∮ A · dℓ as a universal feature of adiabatic quantum evolution — picked up by any quantum state transported around a closed loop in parameter space, depending only on the geometry of the loop and not on its timing. **Simon (1983)**, in *Holonomy, the quantum adiabatic theorem, and Berry’s phase*, *Physical Review Letters* 51, 2167–2170, identified Berry’s phase as the holonomy of a connection on a principal U(1) bundle over parameter space, completing the mathematical formulation. **Wilczek and Zee (1984)**, in *Appearance of gauge structure in simple dynamical systems*, *Physical Review Letters* 52, 2111–2114, extended Berry’s framework to non-Abelian gauge structures and degenerate adiabatic evolution.

Berry-Simon-Wilczek-Zee represent the most extensive pre-McGucken unification of geometric-phase-type non-closures. The Berry framework explicitly subsumes Pancharatnam (polarization-state phase = Berry phase for the photon polarization Hilbert space), the Aharonov–Bohm phase (= Berry phase for the U(1) gauge fiber), and at least implicitly connects to the Wu–Yang gauge-theoretic non-closures (Berry phase = abelian gauge holonomy, non-abelian Wilczek–Zee phase = non-abelian gauge holonomy). The Berry framework provided the geometric language in which gauge-theoretic non-closures, polarization non-closures, and adiabatic-quantum non-closures could all be discussed using the same mathematical objects (connection, curvature, holonomy on fiber bundles).

But — and this is the gap that no prior program closed — the Berry-Simon-Wilczek-Zee unification, even at its widest, did not connect the geometric phase to (a) the canonical commutator \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ, (b) the Robertson uncertainty bound σ_q σ_p ≥ ℏ/2, (c) the spin-1/2 4π closure of SU(2) → SO(3), (d) the Bohr–Sommerfeld + Maslov ½-quantum correction, or (e) the Wigner-Thomas rotation from non-parallel boost composition. The geometric-phase framework treats ℏ as the input to quantum mechanics; it does not provide an upstream physical reason why the geometric phase, the canonical commutator, the uncertainty bound, the spin-1/2 closure, the Bohr–Sommerfeld semiclassical limit, and the Wigner rotation should all share the same minimum non-closure quantum ℏ as their lower bound. The geometric phase is recognized as one instance of round-trip non-closure; it is not recognized as part of a broader principle that includes the canonical commutator’s iℏ and the uncertainty bound’s ℏ/2 as instances of the same upstream fact.

The closest a prior program came to a comprehensive unification was the **Yang–Wu (1975)** + **Berry–Simon–Wilczek–Zee (1983–1984)** combined corpus — gauge-theoretic non-closures plus adiabatic-quantum non-closures, mathematically unified through fiber-bundle holonomy. The reach of this combined framework covers items (3), (6), (7) of the list in the next subsection. The remaining items — (1), (2), (4), (5), (8), (9) — were not connected. **No prior program unified all nine items under a single upstream physical principle.**

The McGucken framework supplies the missing principle: dx₄/dt = ic with action quantum ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance (Proposition 2.2). With this principle in hand, all nine items become instances of the same physical fact — any round-trip involving x_4 cannot close more tightly than one action quantum ℏ, because x_4 is always advancing in quanta of ℏ at every event.

#### 12.10.2 The universal non-closure theorem

**Theorem 12.11 (Universal non-closure quantum of x_4-involving rotations).** \*Let R denote any physical operation involving rotation through the perpendicular x_4-direction of the McGucken constraint surface `\mathbb{M}`{=tex}\_{1,3} (a quantum-mechanical operator action involving x_4-phase via the operator i; a closed loop in phase space; a closed loop in parameter space for adiabatic transport; a closed spatial loop around a region of gauge curvature; a closed orbit traversing classical turning points; a composition of non-parallel Lorentz boosts; or any other process whose round-trip closure depends on the integrated x_4-content along the trajectory). Then the round-trip non-closure of R is bounded below by the action quantum ℏ supplied by Proposition 2.2:\*

*non-closure(R) ≥ ℏ × (topological coefficient determined by the operation’s structure)*

*with the topological coefficient ranging from 1 (for the infinitesimal canonical-commutator case) down to 1/2 (for the Robertson uncertainty bound, the Bohr–Sommerfeld Maslov correction, the spin-1/2 4π closure relative to 2π, and the Dirac monopole minimum quantization), or up to large integers determined by the topology of the operation (winding number for Aharonov–Bohm and Dirac monopole; Chern number for Wigner–Zee non-abelian; etc.). The universal lower bound across all instances is supplied by Proposition 2.2: ℏ is the action quantum carried by one Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance, and any round-trip involving x_4 cannot resolve a phase difference finer than this quantum because x_4-advance occurs in discrete units of ℏ per oscillation.*

*Specifically, the following nine canonical non-closures are all instances of this universal principle:*

*(1) Canonical commutator (Theorem 5.1): \[q̂\_i, p̂\_j\] = iℏ δ_ij.* The infinitesimal-loop non-closure of (q̂, p̂)-rotation, with non-closure quantum ℏ (in the perpendicular direction marked by i). q̂ is in x₁x₂x₃; p̂ is in x_4 (Proposition 12.10); the round-trip in the (q̂, p̂)-plane around an infinitesimal parallelogram does not close because q̂ and p̂ access orthogonal cascade-level directions of the four-dimensional structure. The non-closure magnitude iℏ records one action quantum of x_4-oscillation traversed by the loop.

*(2) Uncertainty principle (Theorem 8.2): σ_q σ_p ≥ ℏ/2.* The statistical version of (1): no quantum state can have both position-uncertainty and momentum-uncertainty arbitrarily small. The minimum product is exactly half the non-closure quantum, with the ½ supplied by Cauchy–Schwarz on the commutator’s iℏ (Robertson 1929). Geometrically: a state cannot be both fully localized in x₁x₂x₃ (zero σ_q, requiring full rotation out of x_4) AND fully localized in the x_4-perpendicular direction (zero σ_p, requiring zero x_4-content variation), because the combined operation would close two round-trips into x_4 with zero non-closure, which is impossible since each costs ℏ/2.

\*(3) Berry geometric phase (Berry 1984): γ_B = ∮\_C A · dℓ.\* The global non-closure of an adiabatic loop in parameter space. *(4) Spin-1/2 4π closure (SU(2) double cover of SO(3); Rauch et al. 1975, Werner et al. 1975).* A spin-1/2 particle rotated by 2π in physical space picks up a phase factor of exp(iπ) = -1, requiring a full 4π rotation for closure. *(6) Aharonov–Bohm phase (Aharonov–Bohm 1959; Tonomura et al. 1986): exp(ieΦ/ℏ).* The closed-loop phase of a charged particle around a region of confined magnetic flux Φ, with the field zero along the trajectory. #### 12.10.3 Architectural significance

The unification of these nine results under one upstream physical principle is, the most far-reaching content of the McGucken framework’s reading of dx₄/dt = ic. Prior unifications had reached subsets — gauge-theoretic via Wu–Yang–Berry–Simon–Wilczek–Zee, symplectic-geometric via Souriau–Kostant — but no prior program connected the canonical commutator (1) and the uncertainty bound (2) to the geometric / topological / semiclassical / relativistic non-closures (3)–(8) as instances of a single foundational physical principle. The path-integral case (9) was understood by Feynman to involve all of the others (every path interference is an action-difference in units of ℏ), but the upstream physics of “why exp(iS/ℏ) is the universal carrier” was never identified — Feynman’s i and ℏ were inputs to the formalism, not derived quantities of an upstream principle. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the missing physics: i and ℏ are twin properties of one geometric flow (Proposition 2.2), and every non-closure that involves x_4 (which is essentially every non-closure in foundational physics) inherits the iℏ structure as its algebraic signature.

The architectural significance is that **the empirical universality of ℏ across these nine independently-celebrated results is the empirics of Proposition 2.2 itself, measured nine different ways**. Every interferometer, every monopole-search experiment, every neutron-spin rotation, every adiabatic quantum transport, every semiclassical Bohr–Sommerfeld orbit, every relativistic Thomas precession measurement, and every quantum interference experiment is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, a measurement of the same physical quantity — the action carried by one cycle of x_4-advance — instantiated at the cascade level appropriate to the experimental setup. The agreement of all these measurements on the same numerical value of ℏ is therefore the same empirics measured by different probes.

The dx₄/dt = ic framework’s prediction is that the universal non-closure quantum will continue to emerge in any future foundational physics experiment that involves rotation through x_4 — and that the mathematical machinery for handling each such non-closure (gauge theory, fiber bundles, Maslov indices, holonomy, geometric phases) will continue to converge on the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework as the upstream physical reading of why all of these mathematical structures share the same ℏ.

This unification echoes Wheeler’s 1986 articulation of the foundational-physics aspiration that drove the present line of inquiry across the four-decade arc of the McGucken corpus. In *How Come the Quantum?* — Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, Volume 480, 1986 — Wheeler wrote:

> *Behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, so compelling that when — in a decade, a century, or a millennium — we grasp it, we will all say to each other, how could it have been otherwise?*

The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, with action quantum ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation of x_4-advance (Proposition 2.2), is offered as the candidate that satisfies Wheeler’s aspiration. From this one principle the entire formalism of quantum mechanics cascades as theorems (this paper, §§2–11), the canonical structures of general relativity cascade as theorems (\[54–57\]), the second law of thermodynamics emerges as the cumulative ensemble Wick rotation (Theorem 12.4), the boost-measurement parallel unifies relativity’s and QM’s central operations (Proposition 12.8), the position-momentum operator structure records the geometric perpendicularity x₁x₂x₃ ⊥ x_4 (Proposition 12.10), and the universal non-closure quantum ℏ across nine independently-celebrated foundational results emerges as the same physics measured at different cascade levels (Theorem 12.11). The idea is simple. The geometric beauty is the perpendicular fourth dimension expanding at the velocity of light with action ℏ per oscillation. The empirical force is the agreement of the entire body of foundational-physics experiments across the twentieth and twenty-first centuries on the predictions that descend from it.

### 12.11 Summary

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s reading of quantum measurement, in one sentence: **a measurement is the physical rotation of a quantum particle out of the x₄-expanding perpendicularity into a definite spatial event in x₁x₂x₃, with the wavefunction’s i-bearing complex character — the imprint of its participation in x₄-perpendicularity — removed by the modulus-squaring that the Born rule prescribes.**

The key identifications are:

-   **Lorentzian metric and Born density as the same operation at two cascade levels.** The metric is the squared-rate form of dx₄/dt = ic; the Born density is the squared-amplitude form of the wavefunction. Both squarings remove the i-marker for x₄-perpendicularity. Both produce a real-valued spatial-slice quantity. The rank-2 character of the Minkowski metric (Lemma 2.5) forces both exponents at 2.

-   **The wavefunction’s complex character as imprint of x₄-perpendicularity.** Between measurements, the particle is participating in x₄-expansion; its wavefunction is i-bearing because the phase encodes x₄-position along the perpendicular direction. The “imaginariness” of the wavefunction is the geometry of x₄’s perpendicularity to x₁x₂x₃.

-   **Measurement as physical Wick rotation.** Theorem 12.2 identifies the measurement event as the physical realization of the standard mathematical Wick rotation x₄ = ict → ct, performed at the particle’s worldline at the measurement event. The Born rule’s modulus-squaring is the algebra of this rotation at the amplitude level, exactly as the metric squaring is the algebra at the rate level.

-   **The photon case as the cleanest illustration.** The photon, having no rest frame, is constituted entirely by its participation in the x₄-expansion at c. Absorption at a photographic grain (or any single-photon detector) annihilates the photon absolutely; the rotation out of x₄ is total and unambiguous; the i-bearing amplitude is removed by the modulus-squaring because the i-bearing entity — the photon — has been removed by the absorption. The dx₄/dt = ic framework’s mechanism is most transparent in this case because no rest-frame alternative is available: whatever happens to a photon at measurement cannot be a Lorentz boost to a rest frame.

-   **The universal mechanism across particle types.** The radioactive alpha case shows the same mechanism in a massive particle, whose timelike worldline participates in x₄-expansion partially (four-velocity budget partitioned per u\^μ u_μ = −c²) rather than fully. Detection rotates the alpha out of its free-quantum x₄-participation by absorption into the detector’s matter. Both cases instantiate the same universal mechanism: free quantum’s x₄-participation ended by absorption, i removed from the description by modulus-squaring, spatial-slice record established by the apparatus’s physical change.

-   **The head-on x₄-collision mechanism (Theorem 7.7).** The Born rule’s bilinearity is, mechanistically, the algebraic record of two McGucken spheres meeting head-on in x₄ at the detection event. From the emitter’s frame, the absorber’s outgoing x₄-expansion appears antiparallel (dx₄/dt = -ic where the emitter’s is +ic) — this antiparallelism is the frame-relational physics of complex conjugation. The two x₄-momenta cancel at the head-on meeting, and by four-momentum conservation the cancelled x₄-momenergy reappears as 3-spatial momenergy, localizing both particles at the collision point. The single-particle Born rule P = ψ\^\*ψ is the localized-absorber limit of this head-on collision picture.

-   **Thermodynamics as the macroscopic-scale Wick rotation (Theorem 12.4).** A macroscopic ensemble undergoes head-on x₄-collisions at total rate Γ_total ∼ 10³⁴ s⁻¹ per macroscopic sample. Each collision is a physical Wick rotation (Theorem 12.2) at the colliding pair. The cumulative spatial-slice configuration record across the ensemble is i-free, real-valued, and governed by classical statistical mechanics — Boltzmann’s H-theorem, the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, the second law. The standard mathematical Wick rotation t → -iτ, which transforms exp(iS/ℏ) into exp(-S_E/ℏ), is the formal abstraction of this cumulative physical Wick rotation performed by the ensemble. Thermodynamics is, in this reading, the Wick rotation exalted Γ_total times per second by the ensemble’s Born rule events. The thermodynamic arrow of time emerges as the cumulative arrow of measurements, with the irreversibility of each rotation-out-of-x₄ giving the macroscopic second law.

-   **Boost and measurement as the two rotations involving x_4 (Proposition 12.8).** The Lorentz boost (relativity) and the measurement event (QM) are the two physical realizations of rotation in a plane containing x_4 = ict, both descending from dx₄/dt = ic. The boost is continuous, reversible, and partial (some x_4-component remains; the particle continues to participate in x_4-expansion at a reallocated rate); the measurement is discrete, irreversible, and total (no free x_4-component remains; the particle ceases to be a free participant in x_4-expansion). Both are operations on the same geometric structure, differing in continuity, reversibility, and totality but sharing the same underlying mechanism: rotation involving x_4. The unification of GR and QM through dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 10.5) is therefore a physical statement at the level of operations on a single particle: the boost (relativity’s central operation) and the measurement (QM’s central operation) are the same kind of operation — partial-continuous in one case, total-discrete in the other — both rotations involving the perpendicular x_4 dimension that dx₄/dt = ic supplies.

-   **q̂ in x₁x₂x₃ and p̂ in x_4 — the CCR as operator-level statement of the perpendicularity (Proposition 12.10).** The canonical commutation relation \[q̂\_i, p̂\_j\] = iℏ δ_ij records the x₁x₂x₃ / x_4 split at the operator level. q̂\_i is a pure spatial-slice operator (multiplication by x_i, no i, no ℏ); p̂\_i = −iℏ ∂/∂x_i is a pure x_4-content operator (the i marks x_4-perpendicularity, the ℏ marks the action quantum per Planck-frequency x_4-oscillation, the spatial derivative reads off the x_4-phase rate per unit spatial step). The non-zero commutator is the operator-level non-closure of the (q, p) round-trip — the round trip fails to close because q̂ and p̂ access orthogonal cascade-level directions of the four-dimensional structure. The Kronecker δ_ij records that x_4-perpendicularity attaches to a specific spatial direction (the commutator vanishes for i ≠ j because q̂*i and p̂*{j ≠ i} access different spatial-direction projections). Position eigenstates and momentum eigenstates are the two complementary limits of x_4-participation: zero-x_4-content with full-x₁x₂x₃-localization vs full-x_4-content with full-x₁x₂x₃-delocalization. Fourier conjugacy between (x \| basis) and (p \| basis) is the algebraic shadow of the geometric perpendicularity x₁x₂x₃ ⊥ x_4. The boost-measurement parallel of Proposition 12.8 descends to the operator level: p̂\_i is (up to normalization) the generator of the Lorentz boost in spatial direction i, with the same operator generating both relativity’s continuous boost and QM’s discrete momentum measurement.

-   **The universal non-closure quantum ℏ across foundational physics (Theorem 12.11).** Nine independently-celebrated foundational-physics results share their minimum non-closure quantum because all nine involve round-trips through x_4: (1) the canonical commutator \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ, (2) the Robertson uncertainty bound σ_q σ_p ≥ ℏ/2, (3) the Berry geometric phase, (4) the spin-1/2 4π closure of SU(2) → SO(3), (5) the Bohr–Sommerfeld + Maslov ½-quantum, (6) the Aharonov–Bohm phase, (7) the Dirac monopole quantization eg = (n/2) ℏc, (8) the Wigner rotation from non-parallel boost composition, and (9) the universal path-integral interference exp(iS/ℏ). Prior unifications (Wu–Yang 1975 for gauge-theoretic items (6), (7); Berry–Simon–Wilczek–Zee 1983–1984 for (3) and gauge items; Souriau–Kostant 1970 for symplectic items including (5), (6), (7)) reached subsets but never connected the canonical commutator (1) and the uncertainty bound (2) to the geometric / topological / semiclassical / relativistic non-closures (3)–(8). ## 13.
