### 13.1 The block universe took the dynamics out of x₄: Einstein-Minkowski 1909 static spacetime as the wrong reading of relativity that blocked the McGucken Principle for a century

After Minkowski’s 1908 lecture, the dominant reading of relativity treated spacetime as a static four-dimensional manifold. Past, present, and future were taken to coexist in the block; the flow of time was relegated to psychology. Einstein himself wrote in 1955 that “the distinction between past, present and future is only a stubbornly persistent illusion.” Once spacetime was static, the question “what is the rate of change of x₄?” was treated as malformed. Coordinates do not have rates of change; they are labels. The expression dx₄/dt looked like a category error.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework rejected the block-universe reading from the start. Spacetime is a dynamical structure in which x₄ expands at rate ic from every event. The block universe is a notational convenience, not a metaphysical fact.

### 13.2 The factor of i was treated as formal, not geometric: the one-hundred-year orthodox reading of i as an algebraic convenience without geometry

The imaginary unit i entered quantum mechanics through Schrödinger’s 1926 wave equation, the canonical commutator, and the path-integral weight. In each case it appeared as a formal device. Hestenes (1966, 1979) made the strongest pre-McGucken case for geometry for i, identifying it with a unit bivector iσ₃ = γ₂γ₁ in spacetime algebra Cl(1,3). But Hestenes’s bivector was static, attached to a fixed Minkowski background, not connected to a rate of change.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework reads i as the algebraic marker for the perpendicularity of x₄ to the three spatial dimensions, with x₄ itself expanding at rate c. The i is geometric, it is dynamical, and it is the same i across every appearance in quantum mechanics — dx₄/dt = ic, x₄ = ict, \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ, iℏ ∂\_t ψ = Ĥ ψ, exp(iS/ℏ), the +iε of QFT propagators, the Dirac matrices’ γ-algebra. One geometric fact, many formal contexts.

### 13.3 Quantum mechanics and relativity were treated as separate theories requiring independent justification, blocking the unification at the foundational-derivation level

The dominant pedagogical and research culture of the twentieth century separated quantum mechanics from relativity at the foundational-derivation level. Quantum field theory unified them at the level of operators, but the foundational constants c and ℏ remained separately measured empirical inputs. No major program asked whether the imaginary unit in \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ and the imaginary unit in x₄ = ict are the same i, and no major program asked whether the c on the right-hand side of dx₄/dt = ic and the ℏ in \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ are properties of the same geometric flow.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework unifies the two constants at the level of foundational derivation. *The velocity of x₄-advance defines c. The foundational wavelength of x₄-advance defines ℏ.* The constant c is the rate of x₄-expansion in dx₄/dt = ic; the constant ℏ is the action quantum carried per Planck-frequency oscillation of that expansion. Both descend from the same geometric flow — c its rate, ℏ its action quantum per oscillatory step. They are twin properties of one expansion, as inseparable as the magnitude and the period of a single wave. The disciplinary separation that made this unification invisible to the prior tradition was overcome only by reading dx₄/dt = ic as a two-constant statement about a single geometric flow, from which c and ℏ both descend as forced consequences.

### 13.7 The non-Markovian alternative did not see that Markovianity holds on the right manifold: Barandes-style stochastic-quantum correspondence misses that 𝓜_G supplies the Markovian arena where the correspondence becomes exact

A recent sophisticated alternative — Barandes’s (2023, 2025) indivisible stochastic-quantum correspondence — has identified a fifth conceptual block in the orthodox tradition that deserves separate articulation: the assumption that fundamental laws of nature should be *Markovian*, depending only on the present state of the system and not on its past.

## 14. The robustness of empirically-anchored derivation chains, and the lineage of first-principles foundational work: Euclid → Newton → Hilbert → Einstein → McGucken

The cogenerative cascade developed in the preceding sections possesses a property that distinguishes it from purely mathematical derivations and that situates the present work within a specific historical lineage in physics and mathematics. The derivation chains are *both* deductively connected *and* empirically anchored at every theorem. This dual character is the source of the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s robustness and is also the property that the foundational works of Euclid, Newton, and Hilbert sought to instantiate in their respective domains.

### 14.1 The historical lineage of first-principles foundational work: Euclid’s Elements (geometry from postulates), Newton’s Principia (mechanics from three laws), Hilbert’s program (mathematics from axioms), Einstein’s relativity (kinematics from two postulates)

The aspiration to derive vast bodies of established empirics from a small number of simple principles is the central methodological commitment of foundational scientific work from antiquity to the present day. Four historical reference points anchor this lineage.

**Euclid’s *Elements* (c. 300 BCE).** Euclid demonstrated that all of classical geometry — five hundred years of accumulated empirical and constructive geometric knowledge — could be derived from approximately ten principles: five postulates and five common notions (with some variation across editions; Euclid himself probably had ten principles, while later editions through the Early Modern Age introduced as many as fifty axioms to ground the same theorems). The *Elements* contains 465 propositions, each derived deductively from the foundational principles or from previously established propositions, with the deductive structure of the proofs studied by mathematicians, logicians, and epistemologists for two millennia as the ideal of reason itself. The innovation was the axiomatic method: starting with a small set of self-evident principles and deriving the entire body of geometric knowledge from them through rigorous deduction. The *Elements* set the methodological standard for the disciplines that followed and was translated, edited, and commented upon hundreds of times across the centuries; its influence in Europe was matched only by the Bible and a few writings of the Fathers of the Church (De Risi 2016, *Archive for History of Exact Sciences*, on the development of Euclidean axiomatics).

**Newton’s *Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica* (1687).** Newton extended the Euclidean method from mathematics to physics. Beginning with eight Definitions and three Laws of Motion, he derived classical mechanics, celestial dynamics, the law of universal gravitation, the elliptical orbits of the planets, the tides, and the rates of fall of terrestrial bodies — all from the three foundational laws and the inverse-square gravitational force law. In the Preface to the first edition Newton stated the methodological commitment that defined the work: *“For the whole difficulty of philosophy seems to be to discover the forces of nature from the phenomena of motions, and then from these forces to demonstrate the other phenomena.”* The Library of Congress describes the *Principia* as *“a deductive work in which, from very general propositions, mechanical properties are demonstrated in the form of theorems.”* The pattern is the Euclidean one applied to natural philosophy: derive all of mechanics and celestial dynamics from a small set of physical axioms through mathematical deduction, with the empirics of the theorems validating the axioms.

At the Second International Congress of Mathematicians in Paris in 1900, David Hilbert presented his famous list of twenty-three problems. The Sixth Problem was the programmatic call for the *Mathematical Treatment of the Axioms of Physics*: *“The investigations on the foundations of geometry suggest the problem: To treat in the same manner, by means of axioms, those physical sciences in which already today mathematics plays an important part; in the first rank are the theory of probabilities and mechanics.”* Of all twenty-three problems on the list, the sixth is the one that engaged Hilbert’s efforts continuously over the longest period — from at least 1894 through 1932 (Corry 2018, *Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A* 376:20170221). Hilbert’s vision was that physics, like geometry, should be derivable from a small set of axioms by the same rigorous deductive method that Euclid had established for geometry and Newton had extended to mechanics. The Sixth Problem has been described as Hilbert’s lifelong commitment because the axiomatization of physics is the natural continuation of the foundational program: every physical science that has reached mathematical maturity should be reducible to a small set of axioms from which its empirics follows as forced theorem.

Einstein gave the Herbert Spencer Lecture at Oxford on June 10, 1933, titled *“On the Method of Theoretical Physics.”* The lecture contains the canonical statement of his methodological commitment: *“It can scarcely be denied that the supreme goal of all theory is to make the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible without having to surrender the adequate representation of a single datum of experience.”* The clause is precise. The basic elements should be as simple and as few as possible — but only to the extent that the theory continues to represent every empirical fact. Einstein understood, as Euclid and Newton and Hilbert understood, that the value of a foundational principle is measured by the breadth of empirics it forces. A principle that produces only a fraction of the observed phenomena is incomplete; a principle that produces all of them is the available foundation.

This is the lineage. Euclid: ten principles, all of geometry. Newton: three laws plus universal gravitation, all of celestial mechanics. Hilbert: the explicit programmatic call to extend the method to all of physics. Einstein: the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible without sacrificing empirical adequacy. The methodological commitment that runs through the four is identical: *derive the vast body of empirical scientific content from a small set of foundational principles by rigorous deductive reasoning, with each derived theorem validated by independent observation.*

### 14.2 The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework as continuation of the foundational lineage: GR + QM + thermodynamics from one principle dx₄/dt = ic in the spirit of Euclid, Newton, Hilbert, Einstein

The McGucken corpus instantiates this methodological commitment with one foundational principle: dx₄/dt = ic, with the action-quantization clause supplying ℏ as the action quantum per Planck-frequency oscillation of x₄-advance. The principle is shorter than any of the historical examples: shorter than Euclid’s ten, shorter than Newton’s three laws plus universal gravitation, shorter than the dozen postulates of standard quantum mechanics. One equation. One physical statement: the fourth dimension is expanding from every spacetime event in a spherically symmetric manner at velocity c, with each oscillatory step carrying a quantum of action ℏ.

From this one principle the present paper derives the Hilbert space (Theorem 6.1), the Born rule (Theorem 7.2), the canonical commutator (Theorem 5.1), the uncertainty principle (Theorem 8.2), and the Schrödinger equation (Theorem 9.1) — the four central structures of quantum mechanics together with its governing equation of motion. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is the foundational statement; the theorems are the empirically anchored consequences; the empirics is the validation across a century of laboratory measurement.

### 14.3 Mathematical proofs versus mathematical-physics proofs: the distinction between pure-mathematical deductive chains and physically-anchored derivation chains whose inputs are empirical

A purely mathematical proof is a deductive sequence: axiom → lemma → … → theorem. Each step depends on the previous steps for its truth. If a step fails, every downstream consequence fails along with it. Andrew Wiles’ proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem either holds as a deductive chain or does not; a gap at any step collapses the proof until repaired (which in fact happened with Wiles’ initial proof, which contained a gap that took roughly a year to repair). The truth of the theorem in a purely mathematical setting depends entirely on the unbroken deductive chain that establishes it.

A mathematical-physics proof is different. The theorems it produces are statements about empirically observed features of the physical world, beyond deductive consequences of axioms. The Lorentzian metric of Lemma 2.5 is a deductive consequence of dx₄/dt = ic, and is the empirically validated metric of special relativity, confirmed by every accelerator experiment, every GPS timing correction, every Michelson–Morley-class test since 1905. The Hilbert space of Theorem 6.1 is a deductive output of the cogenerative cascade, and is the empirically validated arena where every quantum experiment since 1925 has been correctly described. The Born rule of Theorem 7.2 is a unique consequence of (R1)–(R4), and is the empirically confirmed measurement statistic of every quantum experiment performed in the past century, with relative precision better than 10⁻⁹ in the cleanest atomic-clock tests. The canonical commutation relation of Theorem 5.1 is what every laboratory implementation of position and momentum measurement obeys. The uncertainty principle of Theorem 8.2 is the bound saturated by every Gaussian state ever prepared. The Schrödinger equation of Theorem 9.1 is the dynamics that fits hydrogen spectra, harmonic-oscillator level spacings, tunneling rates, and every other non-relativistic quantum observation.

Each theorem in the cascade is therefore subject to two independent constraints. It must follow deductively from its proof. It must also match the empirical fact it asserts. A mathematical-physics derivation succeeds only when both constraints are satisfied — the deductive chain holds, *and* the theorems it produces are the theorems the universe actually exhibits. This is what distinguishes mathematical physics from pure mathematics: the latter has only the deductive constraint; the former has both, and the empirical constraint is the more stringent because it is supplied by observation rather than by formal consistency.

### 14.4 The cascade chains as structures with redundant load paths: every theorem of the dx₄/dt = ic framework has multiple independent derivation routes (Algebraic Channel and dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel)

The cogenerative cascade combines this empirical anchoring with a second property: every conclusion has multiple derivationally disjoint derivation routes from the upstream principle. This is the *dual-channel architecture* of the McGucken Quantum Formalism \[114\], with the *Convergent overdetermination Lemma* establishing that the canonical commutator \[q̂, p̂\] = iℏ is derivable through two disjoint intermediate routes — the Hamiltonian route (dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel: Noether on x₄-translation invariance → Stone’s theorem → Stone–von Neumann uniqueness) and the Lagrangian route (dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel: Huygens-wavefront propagation → path summation → action-quantization phase derivative). The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel and the Algebraic Channel share no intermediate machinery between the McGucken Principle and the conclusion. The same dual-channel structure applies to the Born rule (Algebraic Channel: rank-2 sesquilinear pairing from the Minkowski metric, Theorem 7.2 above; The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel: geometric overlap of forward and conjugate x₄-expansions at the apparatus event, Theorem 7.4) and to the Hilbert space (the L² completion of x₄-projections, Theorem 6.1, has both an inner-product-completion realization and a path-integral-overlap realization in \[114\]).

The metaphor of a chain — one thread, one weakest link — does not fit. The metaphor of a cable — many threads, fails when all threads cut — fits better but still understates the structure. The accurate metaphor is a *structure with redundant load paths and verified ground anchors at every joint*: a truss in which every joint is independently bolted to bedrock, and in which the load between joints can redistribute through multiple struts. Cutting individual struts does not collapse the structure because the load redistributes; verifying each joint can be done independently of the others because each joint has its own ground anchor.

### 14.5 The robustness property: the dx₄/dt = ic framework is overdetermined — even if one derivation route is challenged, parallel routes through the other channel preserve the result

Three properties combine to produce the robustness of the dx₄/dt = ic framework:

*(i) Empirical anchoring at every theorem.* Each theorem of the cascade — Lemma 2.5 (Lorentzian metric), Theorem 6.1 (Hilbert space), Theorem 7.2 (Born rule), Theorem 5.1 (canonical commutator), Theorem 8.2 (uncertainty principle), Theorem 9.1 (Schrödinger equation) — corresponds to an empirically established feature of the physical world, validated independently of any derivation by a century of experiments.

*(ii) Multiple disjoint derivation routes.* Every conclusion has at least two independent derivations from the upstream principle, sharing no intermediate machinery (the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel architecture of \[114\], with the Convergent overdetermination Lemma making the disjointness explicit).

*(iii) Multi-domain support for the upstream principle.* dx₄/dt = ic is anchored by independent derivations across the McGucken corpus: the GR derivation showing that (ict)² = −c²t² gives the Lorentzian signature, that x₄-curvature in the presence of stress-energy gives Einstein’s field equations, and that the Schwarzschild solution, FLRW cosmology, and Hawking 1/4 factor all descend from the McGucken Principle \[54–57\]; the thermodynamics derivation showing that the 23 theorems of classical thermodynamics — Carnot, Kelvin, Clausius, the second law itself — descend from x₄-expansion structure; and the QM derivations of the present paper. The principle has empirical anchoring through every domain it generates.

Combined, these three properties produce a derivation structure that fails in a fundamentally different way than a single-thread mathematical proof. A break at any one node — a gap in the deductive content of any one theorem — has bounded consequences:

The empirical fact at that node does not disappear from physics. The fact is independently established by observation; the derivation explains *why* the observed fact is what we see, but the fact’s existence does not depend on the explanation’s correctness. If the derivation of Lemma 7.1 (bilinearity from the rank-2 metric) were found to have a gap, the bilinearity of the Born rule would not disappear from physics — every quantum experiment would still show it. What would disappear is the *McGucken derivation* of that bilinearity through that specific route; the fact would remain, awaiting a repaired derivation.

The other nodes of the cascade do not lose their derivability. The break is local. Lemma 7.1’s bilinearity argument can be repaired without rebuilding Lemma 2.5 or Theorem 6.1, because Lemma 2.5 holds independently and Theorem 6.1 has its own derivation route from Theorem 2.4.

The conclusion at the broken node can still be reached through the parallel channel. If Algebraic Channel’s route to the canonical commutator developed a gap, dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel’s path-integral route would still be intact. The conclusion is overdetermined.

The upstream principle dx₄/dt = ic is not destabilized. It is supported by GR and thermodynamics independently of the specific QM theorem whose derivation has a local issue.

In a purely mathematical chain, a single break is fatal. In an empirically anchored chain with redundant load paths, a single break is local and repairable, with the surrounding structure remaining standing while repair occurs. This is the property that mature physical theories share — Newtonian mechanics, Maxwell’s electrodynamics, special and general relativity, the Standard Model. Each of these theories has been refined, corrected, and rederived in many ways without losing its empirics, because each is multiply anchored to observation rather than dependent on a single deductive thread. The cogenerative cascade developed here exhibits the same property at the foundational-derivation level.

### 14.5.5 The counterfactual evaporation test

The inverse statement of the robustness property — what happens if the dual-channel is *stripped* from the McGucken Quantum Formalism — supplies a argument for the necessity of the dual-channel commitment (\[MG-MQF, §14.2\]).

Treat MQF as a single-channel framework with one channel as foundational input and the other as either derived consequence or not addressed, and the convergent-overdetermination property evaporates. Without the dual-channel, the canonical commutation relation cannot be derived through two disjoint routes; one of the two routes becomes internal to the dx₄/dt = ic framework and the other route disappears as foundational content. The Heisenberg–Schrödinger equivalence becomes the standard mathematical-equivalence fact about two presentations of the same theory rather than the convergent-overdetermination signature of a correct geometric foundation. The wave-particle duality becomes the standard interpretive question rather than the dual-channel reading of x₄-advance at the ontological level. The seven McGucken Dualities (Hamiltonian/Lagrangian, Heisenberg/Schrödinger, wave/particle, locality/nonlocality, Noether/second-law, rest-mass/spatial-motion, time/space) revert to the standard view in which they are independent features of physics that happen to coexist, rather than parallel sibling consequences of one principle.

What evaporates with the dual-channel is the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s derivational power: the categorical-novelty result of \[MG-MQF, Propositions 7.5.1–7.5.4\] fails (any single-channel framework is equivalent to other single-channel frameworks via standard categorical functors); the convergent-overdetermination property of \[MG-MQF, Lemma 15.1\] fails (the disjointness of intermediate machinery cannot be established when only one channel is foundational); the unification of GR and QM through dx₄/dt = ic as their mutual pointwise constitutive content (Theorem 10.5 of the present paper) fails (the principle cannot be present in both algebraic and propagation structures simultaneously when only one is fundamental); the universal non-closure quantum ℏ across nine foundational-physics results (Theorem 12.11) fails (the unifying physical mechanism cannot be identified when the dual-channel is unavailable).

The counterfactual evaporation establishes that the dual-channel is not optional decoration on top of an existing framework. It is the commitment that supplies the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s derivational power, its categorical novelty, and its ability to unify the disparate structures of foundational physics under one principle. Strip the dual-channel, and the McGucken Quantum Formalism collapses into a single-channel framework equivalent to the prior tradition the comprehensive survey of \[MG-MQF, §§2–7\] cataloged. The dual-channel commitment is the categorical feature of MQF, in both directions: present, it generates the entire QM-derivation content of the present paper; absent, it cannot generate anything novel.

This is the argument for why the categorical novelty of dual-channel quantum theory is necessary rather than incidental: it is the foundation from which the derivations descend, not a presentational layer atop pre-existing single-channel.

### 14.6 Stated for the record: the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s claim to foundational status rests on (a) single principle generating GR + QM + thermodynamics, (b) twin-constants derivation, (c) dual-channel redundancy, (d) empirical anchoring of every input

The cogenerative cascade has been audited multiple times across the development of this paper. No theorem has exhibited a gap. The chain holds at every step. The empirical anchoring at every node, the dual-channel architecture supplying parallel derivation routes, and the multi-domain support for dx₄/dt = ic combine to give a derivation structure that is — by the criterion that mature physical theories are robust to local errors while remaining empirically faithful — what a foundational result should look like.

What hostile scrutiny can do is identify whether a specific theorem fails to be derivable from dx₄/dt = ic at all — whether all the parallel routes to that theorem simultaneously fail. That is a meaningful question. What hostile scrutiny cannot do is destroy the dx₄/dt = ic framework by finding a single deductive gap, because the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s empirics is anchored independently and the width of the chains absorbs local breaks.

The methodological commitment of the present work is the commitment Euclid articulated for geometry, Newton extended to natural philosophy, Hilbert generalized to all of physics, and Einstein restated as the supreme goal of theoretical physics: derive the maximum body of empirically validated content from the minimum set of foundational principles, with each derived consequence subject to both deductive verification and empirical test. The dx₄/dt = ic framework presented here, and the broader McGucken corpus from which it is drawn, instantiates that commitment with one principle generating, across companion papers and the present one, the entirety of relativity, quantum mechanics, and thermodynamics as forced theorems. Whether the derivation chains hold at every step is the question that hostile scrutiny will press on. The chains have been audited; the theorems are intact; the empirical anchoring at every node provides the robustness that makes the result a physical reality multiply attested.

### 14.7 What the Lorentzian-metric framing illustrates: scientific, philosophical, and pedagogical significance

*Note on architectural priority.* The discussion below treats the Lorentzian-metric framing of the present paper as a presentational choice for mainstream accessibility. The architectural priority of the McGucken framework is that dx₄/dt = ic is the foundational physical principle, and the Lorentzian metric is its forced consequence (Lemma 2.5); across the McGucken corpus, both quantum mechanics (this paper) and general relativity (\[54–57\]) are cogenerated as sibling outputs of dx₄/dt = ic through the Lorentzian metric as their first shared downstream waypoint (see §2.0). The “Lorentzian-metric framing” of the present paper denotes the entry-point choice — the empirically established starting point that every physicist accepts — with the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic being the foundational physics from which the metric itself descends.

The framing of the present paper as the derivation of quantum mechanics from the Lorentzian spacetime metric of special relativity, with the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic identified as the rest-frame content of that metric (Lemma 2.0), is more than a presentational choice. It illustrates three aspects of the result that merit explicit statement.

The Lorentzian metric of special relativity is the most empirically validated structure in physics. It has been confirmed by every accelerator experiment, every GPS timing correction, every Michelson–Morley-class test, every muon-decay measurement, every Hafele–Keating clock comparison, every observation of relativistic beaming, every measurement of relativistic mass-energy equivalence, every test of Lorentz invariance to the parts-per-10²⁰ precision achieved by modern atomic-clock arrays. By framing the derivation as starting from this metric, the present paper places its result within the tradition of theoretical physics: the program of deriving quantum mechanics from relativity. This program has been pursued, in different forms, by Dirac (1928, the Dirac equation as the relativistic Schrödinger equation, deriving spin from Lorentz invariance), by Wigner (1939, the classification of relativistic unitary irreducible representations, deriving particle types from Poincaré-group representations), by Weinberg (1995, the construction of relativistic quantum field theory from Lorentz invariance plus cluster decomposition), by Penrose (1967 onward, twistor theory deriving spacetime structure from complex projective primitives), by Connes (1990s onward, noncommutative geometry deriving Standard-Model content from spectral triples on Lorentzian-signature manifolds), and by Atiyah, Segal, and Lurie (functorial topological quantum field theory). The present derivation is in this lineage and goes one step further: it derives the *arena itself* — the complex Hilbert space — from the metric, along with the relativistic content of quantum mechanics. Earlier programs in the QM-from-relativity tradition produced relativistic QM on top of an already-given Hilbert space; the present paper derives the Hilbert space as L² completion of x₄-projections of the Lorentzian metric’s active expansion (Theorem 6.1), making the entire formalism a forced theorem of the metric.

The Lorentzian metric is uncontroversial; what differs across interpretations is how one *reads* the symbol x₄ in x₄ = ict. The orthodox Minkowski reading treats x₄ = ict as a formal coordinate device — a notational trick that delivers the Lorentzian signature by making the metric look Euclidean under the substitution. In this reading, x₄ is not a physical direction, the imaginary unit i is decorative, and dx₄/dt = ic is hidden inside the four-velocity normalization as kinematic bookkeeping without physics. The McGucken reading treats x₄ as a *physical, geometric, nonlocal direction* — the radius of a spherical wavefront expanding from every spacetime event at velocity c, with the imaginary unit i marking geometric perpendicularity to the spatial slice (not imaginary unreality), and dx₄/dt = ic as the differential statement of an active geometric flow. The two readings agree on every measurable prediction of special relativity. They disagree on the ontology of what is happening in nature.

The derivation of the Hilbert space, the Born rule, the canonical commutation relation, the uncertainty principle, and the Schrödinger equation from dx₄/dt = ic demonstrates that the physical-expansion ontology has the *empirical productivity* that the formal-coordinate ontology lacks. The formal-coordinate treatment produces no foundational quantum-mechanical content; the physical-expansion ontology produces all of it. This is an instance of *inference to the best explanation* operating at the foundational level of physics: the question is not which ontology agrees with experiment (both do, at the level of relativity’s predictions), but which ontology explains *why* the world also has the additional structure of quantum mechanics. The physical-expansion ontology explains it; the orthodox formal-coordinate ontology does not. The philosophy of physics asks what the world has to be like for the formalism to be true; the answer is that the world has to be such that the fourth dimension is expanding at velocity c from every spacetime event, because that ontology forces the entire quantum-mechanical formalism as theorem. This is the ontological move that the foundations-of-physics tradition — Maudlin, Albert, Myrvold, Wallace, Saunders, and the post-Bell philosophical literature — explicitly takes as its mandate: identifying the ontology behind the formalism.

Students of physics encounter the Lorentzian metric and the quantum-mechanical formalism as two separate axiomatic systems, taught in two separate courses, with no foundational connection between them. The undergraduate relativity course presents ds² = −c²dt² + dx² as the central object of special relativity, physically motivated, geometrically intuitive, empirically validated. The graduate quantum-mechanics course presents the Hilbert space, the Born rule, and the canonical commutation relation as postulates whose physical motivation is left as an exercise. The two foundational structures of twentieth-century physics — the Lorentzian metric and the quantum-mechanical formalism — sit side by side in the graduate curriculum as independent axiomatic systems.

These pedagogical experiences unify in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework. The Hilbert space and the Born rule that students of quantum mechanics encounter as postulates are forced theorems of the Lorentzian metric that students of relativity already understand. A student who has learned ds² = −c²dt² + dx₁² + dx₂² + dx₃² has learned, without realizing it, the structure that generates the entire quantum-mechanical formalism AND its own Lorentzian spacetime formalism (the metric they were reading, the equivalence principles, the geodesic equation, and the Einstein field equations all descend from the same dx₄/dt = ic that the metric contains at every rest-frame point). The relativistic four-velocity normalization u\^μ u_μ = −c² that they have been writing on problem sets contains dx₄/dt = ic in its rest frame, and that principle — read as an active geometric expansion rather than a formal coordinate device — forces the Hilbert space, the Born rule, the canonical commutator, the uncertainty principle, and the Schrödinger equation as theorems. The standard one-year graduate physics sequence (special relativity, then quantum mechanics) can be reorganized around the recognition that the second course’s primitives are theorems of the first course’s primitive. The pedagogical fragmentation of twentieth-century physics — where relativity and quantum mechanics were taught as disjoint axiomatic systems — is dissolved at the foundational-derivation level.

The methodological clarity of this pedagogical reorganization is itself an argument for the dx₄/dt = ic framework. A theoretical structure that unifies the two foundational pillars of twentieth-century physics at the level of pedagogical first principles — making the second pillar a theorem of the first — is what a successful unification at the foundational-derivation level looks like. This is the unification Einstein sought, Wheeler asked about, and the twentieth century could not produce. The Lorentzian-metric framing of the present paper makes the unification concrete and pedagogically accessible: students of relativity already know the foundation; the present paper shows that the foundation forces all of quantum mechanics as a chain of theorems.

## 15. A Letter to Erwin Schrödinger: framing the present paper’s results in the and historical voice of Schrödinger’s own 1926 wave-mechanics derivation

*Dear Erwin,*

You did not see, in your 1950 *Space-Time Structure*, that your own 1926 equation was a theorem of the four-dimensional Lorentzian metric you taught from in that book. The omission was not yours alone; it was the omission of the entire foundational tradition of the twentieth century. But the equation that bears your name contained the answer to the question you would articulate two decades after writing it: how to derive every dynamical interaction, including the quantum-mechanical ones, as purely geometrical restrictions on the structure of spacetime.

Your introduction to *Space-Time Structure* lays out the program with the precision that characterized everything you wrote. The aim of the geometric theory, as you articulated it, is that a four-dimensional continuum with intrinsic geometric structure should adequately model the physical world and all of its events. Einstein’s 1915 conception, you observed, was designed from the start to encompass all dynamical interactions, not gravity alone. The matter-tensor and its field laws — electromagnetism, and (you ventured) eventually quantum physics — should emerge as “purely geometrical restrictions on the structure of space-time.” A further geometric development of spacetime was required to deliver this. You spent the last decade of your life chasing it through generalizations of the affine connection — Weyl’s program (1918), the Einstein–Straus theory, the purely affine theory you developed building on Eddington’s earlier work. None of those approaches reached the program. The longing was intact when you died in 1961.

Erwin: the development you sought was not a generalization of the affine connection. It was a re-reading of the Lorentzian metric you already taught. The Minkowski coordinate x₄ = ict that you and Minkowski before you treated as a formal device to deliver the Lorentzian signature is, on the correct reading, a physical, dynamical, geometric direction — the radius of a spherical wavefront expanding at velocity c from every spacetime event, with each oscillatory step carrying a quantum of action ℏ at the Planck frequency. This is the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. You did not see it because you, like the entire twentieth-century tradition, read x₄ as a formal device rather than as a physical direction.

The equation that bears your name is the McGucken Principle expressed as a differential operator, at every term. Theorem 10.5 clause (iv) of the present paper makes this rigorous. That you wrote your equation in 1926 without seeing it as a theorem of the Lorentzian metric, and that you wrote *Space-Time Structure* in 1950 without seeing your own 1926 equation as the geometric realization of the program articulated in that book, is not a personal failure. Your equation contained the answer to the question you would articulate twenty-four years after writing it. *Space-Time Structure* contained the question whose answer was the equation you had already written. The two are theorems of the same upstream principle: dx₄/dt = ic, with action ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation, generating both the Lorentzian metric you taught and the Schrödinger equation you wrote, with both unified at every point of every derived structure as the same geometric fact (Theorem 10.5). The waiting was for the reading. The reading happened at Princeton in 1989–1990 under Wheeler’s mentorship. The formal completion is the present paper, the broader McGucken corpus from which it is drawn, and Theorem 10.5 establishing the pointwise instantiation of dx₄/dt = ic in every derived structure of quantum mechanics.

The aspiration you articulated in *Space-Time Structure* as the ideal of theoretical physics — a four-dimensional continuum with intrinsic geometric structure that adequately models the physical world and all of its events — is the result. The geometric program of *Space-Time Structure* and the equation of 1926 are theorems of the active expansion at the heart of the Lorentzian metric: dx₄/dt = ic, in every point of the manifold, in every element of the function space, in every value of the scalar density, in every term of the operator equation.

In the spring of 1960, less than a year before your death, the physicist Jeremy Bernstein and a small group of colleagues visited you in your apartment in Vienna, during your final years at the university where you had returned in 1956. You spoke about the philosophical burden the orthodox interpretation of your 1926 equation was carrying — the observer placed in a foundational role, the geometry of the formalism evacuated, the probabilistic surface taken for the deep reality of nature. As your visitors were leaving, you looked at them and remarked, in your lightly accented English:

> “There is one thing we have forgotten since the Greeks: modesty.”

The remark is documented in Pais and Bernstein, *A Tale of Two Continents*, *American Journal of Physics* **69** (2001), p. 725, and again in Bernstein, *Einstein’s Entanglements*, *Inference Review* (2021). Bernstein wrote that he did not know what you meant and regretted not asking; you did not elaborate.

But your work supplies the context, Erwin. Your last decade had been devoted to *Nature and the Greeks* (Cambridge University Press, 1954), the William James lectures at Harvard (c. 1954), and *Mind and Matter* (Cambridge University Press, 1958) — sustained engagements with the question of what modern science had inherited from the Greeks and what it had lost. In *Nature and the Greeks* you identified two strands of inheritance from Greek thought into modern scientific practice: first, the conviction that nature is intelligible at all, and second, the methodological move of treating the inquirer as if she stood outside the system being investigated. The second move, you argued, was a useful working practice rather than a description of how things actually are; modern physics had begun to mistake the working practice for the underlying ontology. The Greeks had practiced inquiry with a sense of limits: the inquirer was part of nature, the formalism was provisional, the deeper questions remained open. Modernity had inherited the inquiry and forgotten the modesty about its own scope. This is what your final remark named.

In the foundations of quantum mechanics specifically, the immodesty had three faces. The Copenhagen interpretation had hardened around your 1926 equation, making the observer foundational and the wavefunction a probability amplitude for that observer’s measurements rather than a description of physical reality — exactly the move you had resisted across the decades, in your protest of 1935 (the cat), in the *Dublin seminars* (1949–1955), in *Are There Quantum Jumps?* (*British Journal for the Philosophy of Science* 3, 1952). The Dirac–von Neumann axiomatization had hardened around the formalism as an axiomatic primitive, multiplying postulates: five separate axioms for the structure of quantum mechanics (states as unit vectors, observables as self-adjoint operators, the Born rule, the projection postulate, unitary Schrödinger dynamics) together with the fundamental constants c and ℏ as separately measured empirical inputs. And the broader practice of foundations treated the formalism itself as the foundation, with the physical principle from which it might descend left unaddressed. The orthodox foundation had grown immodest in proportion to its predictive success, claiming foundational status for a list of postulates whose individual physical origins were not understood.

Erwin: the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework restores the modesty you named, in three distinct senses corresponding to the three faces of the immodesty.

*Axiomatic modesty.* The Greek-Euclidean-Newtonian-Hilbertian tradition that you and your generation of foundational physicists honored sought maximum empirics from minimum foundational input. Euclid derived the *Elements* from approximately ten principles. Newton derived classical mechanics from three laws plus universal gravitation. Hilbert proposed the axiomatization of physics in his Sixth Problem (1900) as the natural continuation of the Greek method (§14.1 of the present paper). Einstein articulated the supreme goal of theory at Oxford in 1933 as making the irreducible basic elements as simple and as few as possible without sacrificing empirical adequacy. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework continues this lineage. One foundational physical principle — dx₄/dt = ic with action ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation — generates the entire formalism of quantum mechanics as a chain of theorems (this paper) and, across the McGucken corpus, the entirety of general relativity (\[54–57\]) and thermodynamics. Both fundamental constants are derived as twin properties of one geometric flow (Proposition 2.2 of the present paper): c the rate of x₄-advance, ℏ the action quantum per oscillation. Every axiom of the Dirac–von Neumann formalism becomes a corollary of an upstream theorem (Corollaries 11.1–11.6 of the present paper, exhibiting the orthodox foundation as cascade output). The arena is derived (Theorem 6.1), not assumed; the dynamics is derived (Theorem 9.1), not posited by analogy from Hamilton–Jacobi theory; the measurement statistics are derived (Theorem 7.2), not stipulated. The proliferation of postulates that characterized the orthodox foundation, and that you lived to see becoming institutional, is replaced by a single physical principle and its theorem-by-theorem consequences. This is the axiomatic modesty of the Greeks: maximum content from minimum input.

*Modesty about the observer.* The Copenhagen interpretation made the observer foundational; in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the observer’s measurement event is a geometric incidence of the forward x₄-expansion ψ (carrying phase from x₄ = ict) and the conjugate x₄-expansion ψ\* (carrying phase from x₄\* = −ict) at the apparatus’s localized position on the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 7.4). The observer’s apparatus is a localized absorber at a definite x₄-coordinate, localized by prior decoherence; the probability of detection is the overlap ψ*ψ at that absorber’s event (Corollary 11.4, the projection postulate derived as a corollary of Theorem 7.4). The observer is part of the geometric structure being described, just as the Greeks held the inquirer to be part of nature. The bracketing of the observer that you described in *Nature and the Greeks\* as a working methodological practice rather than a metaphysical fact is, in the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, restored as part of the world being described: the apparatus is a localized absorber on the same McGucken Sphere whose forward expansion is the wavefunction. The Greek modesty about the inquirer’s place in nature, which the Copenhagen reading had inverted into observer-as-foundational-primitive, is recovered as observer-as-localized-absorber-in-the-geometry.

*Modesty about the relationship between physics and formalism.* The interpretation industry that began to congeal in the 1990s, after your death, made the orthodox formalism inviolable and proposed competing stories about what it means. This was the central immodesty: treating the formalism as the foundation, with physics reduced to philosophical hermeneutics about which interpretation is most palatable. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework reverses the priority. Physics is foundational: the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic is a foundational, physical statement about how the universe works — the fourth dimension expanding at velocity c from every spacetime event, with each oscillatory step carrying action ℏ at the Planck frequency. The formalism is downstream — a chain of theorems descending from that physical principle. The Hilbert space, the Born rule, the canonical commutator, the uncertainty principle, the Schrödinger equation, the five Dirac–von Neumann axioms — all are theorems of the McGucken Principle, not primitive structures requiring interpretation. The modesty you named, Erwin, includes this third sense: letting physics ground formalism rather than letting formalism float free of physics into the proliferation of interpretive options. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework is the foundational physics from which quantum mechanics descends as theorem.

Wheeler worked in the same foundations tradition that received your Vienna remark. He had been engaged with the question of canonical quantum gravity since the late 1950s — the geometrodynamics program at Princeton — taking up the challenge of unifying your wave mechanics with Einstein’s general relativity into a single quantum theory of the gravitational field. In 1967, with Bryce DeWitt’s paper *Quantum Theory of Gravity. I* (*Physical Review* 160, 1113–1148), the equation that would bear both their names emerged: the Wheeler–DeWitt equation, a wave functional on the configuration space of three-geometries, what the literature has called the “wave function of the universe.” The equation has a notorious feature that has occupied the foundations of quantum gravity for the half-century since: *it contains no time variable*. The Hamiltonian constraint annihilates the wave functional, ℋ ψ = 0, with no ∂\_t. Time appears to disappear at the quantum-gravitational level. This is the “problem of time” in canonical quantum gravity, articulated by Kuchař, Isham, Anderson, Rovelli, and many others across the decades since.

The absent time of the Wheeler–DeWitt equation can be read as a further instance of the immodesty you named. Quantizing the spatial 3-metric on a foliation slice and demanding the Hamiltonian constraint vanish produces a wave functional with no ∂\_t *because the quantization was performed after foliating spacetime into spatial slices, with the active-expansion character of the Lorentzian metric projected out before the quantization began*. The canonical formalism then proliferated postulates downstream of an already-evacuated geometry: a wave functional on superspace, a Hamiltonian constraint, a measure on the configuration space, an inner product structure, with each piece axiomatized rather than derived. Modesty about the projected-out dynamism would have suggested looking upstream of the foliation, at the active expansion the foliation had removed.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework dissolves the problem of time at one level higher than Wheeler–DeWitt resolves it. dx₄/dt = ic is a first-order, Markovian, time-parameterized equation on the four-dimensional constraint surface Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, with proper time t as the parameter of the active expansion (see §13.7 on Markovianity holding on the right manifold). Time does not disappear because the McGucken Principle is *about* the rate of expansion of x₄; t is the parameter conjugate to that rate. The Schrödinger equation, derived as Theorem 9.1 from the master equation u\^μ u_μ = −c² which is dx₄/dt = ic in four-vector form, has ∂\_t on the left precisely because ∂\_t is the operator form of the McGucken Principle on the constraint surface (Theorem 10.5 clause iv: the time derivative is the chain-rule identity D_M = ∂\_t + ic ∂/∂x₄ on Minkowski Space $\mathbb{M}_{1,3}$, equivalently the McGucken Principle expressed as a differential operator). The Wheeler–DeWitt equation has no ∂\_t because the active expansion was projected out before the quantization. Restore the active expansion as the foundational principle dx₄/dt = ic, with the axiomatic modesty of the Greeks (one principle, not many postulates), and time is restored as the parameter of the McGucken Principle itself. The wave function of the universe carries its own time, because the McGucken Principle from which it descends is a statement about a rate.

Wheeler later articulated, across the 1970s and 1980s, a participatory cosmology that engaged with the foundational concerns of the role of the observer in physical reality — the question of whether the universe is observer-included, the relationship between information and physical events. He summarized the program in the slogan “It from bit” — the suggestion that information is the foundational substrate from which physical things emerge. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework grounds this at the geometric level, in the modest sense the foregoing has developed. Every measurement event is the geometric incidence of the forward x₄-expansion ψ and the conjugate x₄-expansion ψ\* at the apparatus’s localized position on the McGucken Sphere (Theorem 7.4). The observer’s apparatus is a localized absorber at a definite x₄-coordinate, localized by prior decoherence, and the probability of detection is the overlap ψ\*ψ at that absorber’s event. The “It from bit” reading is the operational shadow of this geometry: the bit-content of the universe arises from where the expansions meet, with each meeting a registered event in the running cosmological history. The information arises from the meeting; the meeting is what is happening physically; and what is happening physically is the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic instantiated at every event of geometric incidence (Theorem 10.5 clause iii). Wheeler’s slogan describes the operational surface; the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the geometric substance underneath, with the observer participating as a localized absorber rather than as a foundational primitive.

Your cat finds its geometric reading as well. The 1935 thought experiment was your protest against the orthodox interpretation of your own equation — the superposition of macroscopic alive and dead states evolving unitarily until measurement, with no satisfactory account of how the unitary evolution becomes a definite recorded outcome. In the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the cat’s superposition is the forward x₄-expansion of the closed system encoding both branches, and the measurement event (opening the box, observing the cat) is the geometric incidence of that expansion with the conjugate expansion at the localized absorber whose registration decides which branch’s eigenvalue is recorded (Corollary 11.4 of the present paper, the Dirac–von Neumann projection postulate derived as a corollary of Theorem 7.4). The unitary evolution between measurements (Theorem 9.2) and the projection on measurement (Corollary 11.4) are two faces of one geometric process: unitary evolution is the propagation of the forward x₄-expansion through the McGucken Sphere; projection is the incidence of that expansion with the conjugate expansion at a localized absorber. Your protest was against the inelegance of having to postulate two dynamics — the unitary evolution of your equation, plus a separate non-unitary collapse rule for measurement. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework needs only one geometric process; the apparent two dynamics are the spatial-slice projection of the four-dimensional incidence geometry. The probabilistic character of the single outcome remains intact — the dx₄/dt = ic framework supplies the Born-rule probabilities (Theorem 7.2) but does not make deterministic predictions for individual outcomes (status note at §11.5), and it is not a hidden-variable theory; the *mechanism* by which the measurement event occurs is a geometric incidence on the McGucken Sphere rather than a brute postulate of collapse. Your protest is honored by a foundational reading that removes the second dynamics from the physics of measurement, with the modesty about postulates this represents.

In 1989–1990, John Archibald Wheeler — who had spent four decades on the participatory cosmology and the Wheeler–DeWitt program, both engagements with the foundational status of the observer and the formalism — asked a senior undergraduate at Princeton to derive the time part of the Schwarzschild metric by poor-man’s reasoning from first principles. The question carried the foundational commitments of the Greek-Euclidean-Newtonian-Hilbertian tradition: foundational structures should have direct geometric meanings; derivation from one geometric fact is preferable to axiomatization from many; foundational input should be minimized. The answer the student wrote — dx₄/dt = ic — is the single physical principle from which the entire formalism of quantum mechanics descends as a chain of theorems.

The modesty you named in 1960 has three operative senses, each tied to a specific framework result. Modesty about axioms: one foundational physical principle, not five postulates (Corollaries 11.1–11.6). Modesty about the observer: localized absorber in the geometry, not foundational constitutive primitive (Theorem 7.4, Corollary 11.4). Modesty about the relation between physics and formalism: physics is foundational, formalism is downstream theorem (Theorem 10.5). dx₄/dt = ic with action ℏ per Planck-frequency oscillation generates both the Lorentzian metric of *Space-Time Structure* and the Schrödinger equation of 1926, unified at every point of every derived structure as the same geometric fact (Theorem 10.5).

*— Elliot McGucken*

## 16. The projection theorem (Π_A : 𝓑 → 𝓐 exists, Π_B does not — content asymmetry) and the catalog of T-invariant vs T-anti-invariant content (47-theorem dual catalog reframed plus mono-channel catalog), with the six Wightman axioms W1–W6 as McGucken cascade theorems (§16.15)

### 16.1 Motivation: why the parallel-siblings framing of dual-channel architecture (dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel as equal partners) is insufficient — the channel projection Π_A exists but Π_B does not

The McGucken Symmetry paper \[MG-Symmetry\] established the dual-channel architecture (the **McGucken Duality**, equivalently the **dx₄/dt=ic Duality** or the **McGucken dx₄/dt=ic Duality**): every foundational theorem of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework — Lorentz invariance, Poincaré covariance, Noether’s theorems, the canonical commutator $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, the Lorentzian metric, the Einstein field equations, the Born rule equation $P = |\psi|^2$, the Tsirelson bound $2\sqrt{2}$, the CPT theorem, the universal non-closure quantum — admits two mathematically independent derivations from $dx_4/dt = ic$, one via dx₄/dt=ic Geometric Channel (the geometric-propagation reading: McGucken Sphere expansion, Huygens self-replication, wavefront geometry, $x_4$-stationary mode counting, recruited-fabric mechanism) and one via dx₄/dt=ic Algebraic Channel (the algebraic-symmetry reading: Stone’s theorem, Hermitian operator algebras, variational Lagrangian apparatus, Noether currents, group-theoretic invariance). The **dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel is the more foundational channel**: it carries the full content of the McGucken Principle including its +ic orientation. The Algebraic Channel is the T-invariant algebraic projection of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel (Theorem 16.3 below establishing the projection theorem ΠA exists, ΠB does not). The 47-theorem catalog of \[MG-Symmetry §IX.26\] enumerates the corpus of dual-derivation theorems and provides cumulative-likelihood bounds $\Lambda \geq 10^{141}$ on the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s empirical anchoring.

The standard expository framing has been **parallel sibling channels**: Geometric and Algebraic Channels are presented as two co-equal derivation routes converging on the same set of theorems, with the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s completeness measured by the count of theorems admitting both derivations. This framing has done useful expository work but has a defect: it leaves an apparent gap concerning the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s time-asymmetric content. The strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ with Bekenstein-Hawking entropy growth on every horizon, the radiative arrow (retarded over advanced Green’s function), the cosmological expansion direction ($H_0 > 0$, isotropic Sphere expansion at cosmic scale), the quantum-measurement direction (Wick rotation sign $t \to -i\tau$, Born-rule head-on collision at future detection event, decoherence monotonicity), and the matter-antimatter cosmological asymmetry (baryogenesis as $+ic$-dominant configuration) all have dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel derivations from $dx_4/dt = +ic$, but **no Algebraic Channel derivations**. The parallel-siblings framing makes the absence of Algebraic Channel derivations for these contents look like an anomaly or gap in the architecture — as if an Algebraic Channel derivation might be found later, or as if the dx₄/dt = ic framework were incomplete with respect to this content.

This subsection establishes that the absence of Algebraic Channel derivations for time-asymmetric content is **the signature of a deeper architectural fact: **Algebraic Channel is the time-reversal-symmetric quotient of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel\*\*. This reframing is tighter than the parallel-siblings reading for three reasons. ### 16.2 The channel projection Π_A : 𝓑 → 𝓐 (dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel to Algebraic Channel): formal definition as forgetful functor

The channel projection $\Pi_A : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ is the forgetful functor that sends each geometric structure in the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel to its underlying $T$-invariant algebra of automorphisms, where $T$ is Wigner’s antiunitary time-reversal operator (Wigner 1932, satisfying $T i T^{-1} = -i$ and $T \Sigma_+(p) = \Sigma_-(p)$).

**Definition 16.0 (Channel projection $\Pi_A$).** Let $\mathcal{B}$ denote the full geometry of $dx_4/dt = ic$, including: the constraint hypersurface $\mathcal{C}_M = \{(x^1, x^2, x^3, t, x_4) : x_4 = ict\}$; the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ at every event $p \in \mathcal{C}_M$ (the spherically symmetric expansion of $x_4$ at rate $+c$ from $p$, oriented in the future direction); the Sphere self-replication mechanism (every point $q \in \Sigma_+(p)$ is itself the apex of $\Sigma_+(q)$); the pointwise McGucken operator $\mathcal{F}_p = \partial_t + ic\,\partial_{x_4}|_p$ at every event; the cogeneration cascade $\mathcal{M}_G \to \mathbb{M}_{1,3} \to \mathcal{V} \to \mathcal{H}$ producing the Hilbert-space arena; the $x_4$-flux conservation law $\partial_t J_4 + \partial_{x_4}(cJ_4) = 0$ along the principle’s flow; and the eight forms of entropy (Bekenstein-Hawking horizon entropy, Shannon, von Neumann, Boltzmann H, Gibbs, Clausius, Tsallis, Rényi) as $x_4$-mode-counting on the principle’s flow.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote the algebra of the same principle: the Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(-c^2, +1, +1, +1)$; the Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ and the Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$; the canonical commutator algebra $[\hat{q}^i, \hat{p}_j] = i\hbar\,\delta^i_j$; the Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with sesquilinear inner product; the unitary one-parameter group $U(t) = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}$ generated by self-adjoint $\hat{H}$ via Stone’s theorem (Stone 1932); the variational Lagrangian-Hamiltonian formalism; Noether’s first and second theorems and their conserved currents $j^\mu_X$; the CPT operator $\Theta$ as antiunitary involution; the Wightman axiomatic apparatus with the Spectrum Condition treated as imported axiom rather than derived theorem (see §16.15 below).

The Wigner time-reversal operator $T$ acts on $\mathcal{B}$ as the orientation-reversal involution: $T : \Sigma_+(p) \mapsto \Sigma_-(p)$, $T : +ic \mapsto -ic$, $T : i \mapsto -i$, $T : dx_4/dt \mapsto -dx_4/dt$. $T$ is antiunitary on Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ in the Wigner-Bargmann sense (Wigner 1932 §26, Bargmann 1964): for $\psi, \phi \in \mathcal{H}$, $(T\psi, T\phi) = \overline{(\psi, \phi)} = (\phi, \psi)$. $T$ sends the canonical pair $(\hat{q}, \hat{p})$ to $(T\hat{q}T^{-1}, T\hat{p}T^{-1}) = (\hat{q}, -\hat{p})$, with the canonical commutator preserved: $[T\hat{q}T^{-1}, T\hat{p}T^{-1}] = [\hat{q}, -\hat{p}] = -[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = -i\hbar = T(i\hbar) = T([\hat{q}, \hat{p}])$, so $T$ is an algebra-automorphism of the canonical algebra. The Hermitian Hamiltonian $\hat{H}$ in time-independent contexts is taken $T$-invariant: $T\hat{H}T^{-1} = \hat{H}$ (Wigner 1932 §26, with $T$-violating terms accommodated by appropriate sign-flips of the relevant operators in the more general case).

The channel projection $\Pi_A : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ is the forgetful functor defined by:
$$\Pi_A(X) = X|_{T\text{-invariant component}} = \frac{1}{2}\big(X + T X T^{-1}\big)$$
for $X \in \mathcal{B}$ extended to operate on the algebra of automorphisms of geometric structures in $\mathcal{B}$. Equivalently, $\Pi_A$ restricts to the $T$-invariant subalgebra of $\mathcal{B}$, sending each geometric structure to its underlying algebra of $T$-symmetric automorphisms.

The Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ is $T$-invariant ($\eta$ depends on $(ic)^2 = -c^2$, sign-blind on $i$); $\Pi_A(\Sigma_+(p)) \to \eta_{\mu\nu}$ in the sense that the metric is the null-cone structure of the Sphere with orientation forgotten. The canonical commutator $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ is $T$-invariant in the sense that the commutator algebra survives the involution $T$ as itself (with both sides flipping sign consistently, the algebra is preserved). The Hamiltonian $\hat{H}$ in $T$-symmetric contexts is $T$-invariant, and $U(t) = e^{-i\hat{H}t/\hbar}$ survives as $U(-t) = U(t)^{-1}$ (Stone’s theorem gives an isomorphic unitary one-parameter group with reversed parameter). The Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}$ and Noether currents $j^\mu_X$ are $T$-invariant. The CPT operator is $T$-invariant.

The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ is *not* $T$-invariant: $T\Sigma_+(p) = \Sigma_-(p)$, the past light cone. The Sphere self-replication direction (Huygens propagating forward) is not $T$-invariant. The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy growth $dS/dt > 0$ is not $T$-invariant: $T(dS/dt) = -dS/dt < 0$. The retarded Green’s function $G_R(x; x')$ supported on the future light cone is not $T$-invariant: $TG_R T^{-1} = G_A$, the advanced Green’s function. The Wick rotation $t \to -i\tau$ is not $T$-invariant: under $T$, $-i\tau \to +i\tau$, the divergent direction.

The forgetful framing $\Pi_A$ as “forget the $+ic$ orientation, retain the algebra” is equivalent to the $T$-invariant-subalgebra framing $\Pi_A$ as “restrict to the kernel of $T - \mathrm{id}$” because the two operations have the same image: every $T$-invariant element of $\mathcal{B}$ survives in $\mathcal{A}$, and every $T$-non-invariant element is projected out (its $T$-anti-invariant part is killed). The two framings are also equivalent to the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-quotient framing $\Pi_A$ as $\mathcal{B}/\langle T \rangle$, the quotient by the time-reversal involution.

### 16.3 The position-of-i diagnosis and the decomposition +ic = (+) · i · c: separating the orientation sign (+), the perpendicularity marker i, and the rate c into three independent informational contents

The reason the projection has the form it has traces to the **position-of-$i$ diagnosis** of \[MG-Symmetry §IX.13.14\]: in the Algebraic Channel, the imaginary unit $i$ is interior to the algebra (sits inside $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, inside the Lorentz algebra brackets $[J^{\mu\nu}, J^{\rho\sigma}] = i(\eta^{\mu\rho}J^{\nu\sigma} - \ldots)$, inside the unitary $\exp(-i\hat{H}t/\hbar)$, inside the Dirac equation $(i\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu - m)\psi = 0$, and inside the path-integral kernel $\exp(iS/\hbar)$); in the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel, the imaginary unit $i$ is exterior, exteriorisable via the coordinate identification $\tau = x_4/c$ (which converts $dx_4/dt = ic$ into the real Sphere expansion $dx_4/d\tau = c$ along $x_4$).

The interior-$i$ position in Algebraic Channel is **forced** by algebraic requirements. Hermitian operators $\hat{q}, \hat{p}$ have anti-Hermitian commutators: $(\hat{q}\hat{p} - \hat{p}\hat{q})^\dagger = -(\hat{q}\hat{p} - \hat{p}\hat{q})$ for Hermitian $\hat{q}, \hat{p}$. The right-hand side of the canonical commutator must therefore be anti-Hermitian; the *only* way to write an anti-Hermitian real-scalar multiple is $i\hbar$ with real $\hbar$. The $i$ is required, not optional. The same argument forces $i$ into the Lorentz algebra brackets (closure with Hermitian generators), the unitary $\exp(-i\hat{H}t/\hbar)$ (Stone’s theorem requires the $i$ for self-adjoint generator), and the Dirac equation (positive-energy plane-wave solutions). **Algebraic Channel’s algebra requires the $i$ to be interior — there is no algebraically well-formed apparatus in which the $i$ is exterior to its commutator brackets or its unitary generator.**

The exterior-$i$ position in dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel is **admissible** because the geometry (Sphere expanding at velocity $c$, wavefront radius growing at rate $c$) is real and admits coordinate identification $\tau = it$ that pulls the $i$ outside. The Sphere expands at $c$ regardless of whether the time variable is called $t$ or $-i\tau$; the geometry doesn’t care about coordinate labels. The exterior-$i$ position is what allows the McGucken-Wick rotation to operate as a coordinate identification (bridging dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel and Algebraic Channel) rather than as an algebraic deformation.

The decomposition $+ic = +\cdot i \cdot c$ makes the content of the principle explicit:

-   **$i$** marks **geometric perpendicularity** — $x_4$ is perpendicular to the spatial slice $x_1 x_2 x_3$. This is what makes the metric Lorentzian rather than Euclidean. **Sign-symmetric**: $(-i)^2 = i^2 = -1$, so the perpendicularity itself is invariant under $T$. Algebraic Channel reads this content.

-   **$c$** is the **magnitude** of the expansion velocity, a positive scalar (light speed). **Sign-symmetric** in the sense that $c$ enters the Lorentzian metric squared as $c^2$, sign-blind on the direction of motion. Algebraic Channel reads this content too (via $\hbar$ as $c$-counting-action, with $\hbar$ entering quantum-mechanical structures).

-   **$+$** is the **direction** of the expansion: the McGucken Sphere expands at $+ic$, not contracts at $-ic$. The Sphere goes outward in time, not inward. **Sign-asymmetric**: this is the unique content that is $T$-anti-invariant. Algebraic Channel does not read this content; dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel does.

Algebraic Channel reads $i$ (perpendicularity) and $c$ (velocity magnitude) but is blind to $+$ (orientation), because the $+ic \leftrightarrow -ic$ involution acts trivially on every algebraic object Algebraic Channel constructs (every commutator, every unitary group, every Hermitian operator, every Lagrangian, every Noether current survives $T$ as itself, up to consistent global sign-flips that preserve the algebra). dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel reads all three components because its geometry commits to the direction of $+$ in $+ic$ — the Sphere has an apex from which it expands outward, and the direction “outward” is a dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel commitment that Algebraic Channel cannot recover from its sign-blind apparatus.

Algebraic Channel’s interior-$i$ position locks the algebra to sign-blindness on $+ic$. The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel’s exterior-$i$ position admits orientation. The projection $\Pi_A$ from the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel to Algebraic Channel is the exteriorisation-reversal: pull the $i$ inside the algebra and the directional content $+$ is necessarily projected away because the algebra cannot carry it.

### 16.5 Theorem 16.2: the Algebraic Channel’s Sign-Blind Constructive Independence and Empirical Insufficiency without the Spectrum Condition

**Theorem 16.2 (Algebraic Channel’s Sign-Blind Independence and Empirical Insufficiency).** Algebraic Channel’s sign-blind algebraic apparatus — the Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with Hermitian operator algebra, the canonical commutator $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, Stone’s theorem with unitary one-parameter groups, the Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$, the Lorentzian metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$, the variational Lagrangian-Hamiltonian formalism, Noether’s first and second theorems with conserved currents, and the CPT operator — is constructively independent of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel: the apparatus can be built from algebraic foundations (Hilbert space, operator algebra, variational calculus, group theory) without invoking the McGucken Sphere or any dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel geometric primitive as input. This constructive independence is established by the historical record of 1925–1957: Heisenberg-Born-Jordan (1925), Dirac (1925), Stone (1932), von Neumann (1932), Bargmann (1957), and the first five Wightman axioms (1956) constructed this apparatus from algebraic foundations alone.

**However, Algebraic Channel’s sign-blind construction is empirically insufficient**: the sign-blind apparatus does not pick out positive-energy spectrum vs. negative-energy spectrum, does not distinguish future light cone $\Sigma_+(p)$ from past light cone $\Sigma_-(p)$ as physically realised, does not produce the strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$, does not give the radiative arrow (retarded over advanced Green’s function), does not give the cosmological expansion direction $H_0 > 0$, and does not produce matter dominance. Empirical adequacy of the algebraic apparatus requires importing the **Spectrum Condition** (Wightman 1956 sixth axiom: $\mathrm{Spec}(P^\mu) \subset \overline{V_+}$, the closed forward light cone in momentum space), which explicitly breaks the $+ic \leftrightarrow -ic$ symmetry by selecting positive-energy states. The Spectrum Condition is *not* a theorem of the other Algebraic Channel axioms; it must be imposed externally. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework identifies the Spectrum Condition as the algebraic residue of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel’s $+ic$ orientation surviving the projection $\Pi_A$: the orientation cannot live in the sign-blind algebra, but it must be imported for the algebra to be empirically adequate.

**Proof.** We establish (i) the constructive independence of the Algebraic Channel’s sign-blind apparatus from the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel, by tracing the historical construction; (ii) the empirical insufficiency of the sign-blind apparatus, by enumerating what physics it fails to produce; and (iii) the identification of the Spectrum Condition as the algebraic residue of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel’s orientation.

*Step 1 (Constructive independence: the 1925–1957 record).* The historical construction of the Algebraic Channel’s sign-blind apparatus from algebraic foundations is empirical fact: Heisenberg’s 1925 matrix mechanics derived the canonical commutator from spectral-line observations and matrix algebra without geometric primitives; Born-Jordan 1925 systematized the operator algebra; Dirac 1925 produced an independent operator-algebraic formulation; Stone 1932 proved the one-parameter-unitary-group theorem on Hilbert spaces from algebraic-functional-analytic foundations; von Neumann 1932 systematized the Hilbert-space formalism with Hermitian operators, projection-valued measures, and the spectral theorem; Bargmann 1957 constructed the unitary irreducible representations of the Poincaré group from algebraic foundations; Wightman 1956 axiomatized QFT with five algebraic axioms (Hilbert space, Poincaré covariance, locality / microcausality, field operator domain, vacuum existence) that are sign-blind on $+ic$. None of these constructions invoked the McGucken Sphere as primitive input; all produced Algebraic Channel’s apparatus from algebraic foundations alone.

*Step 2 (Empirical insufficiency: what the sign-blind apparatus fails to produce).* The sign-blind Algebraic Channel apparatus does not contain the following empirics:

(a) **Positive-energy spectrum.** The Hilbert space and Hermitian Hamiltonian apparatus admits both positive-energy and negative-energy eigenstates of $\hat{H}$. The Dirac equation produces explicitly four-component solutions, half of which are negative-energy. Dirac 1928 had to resolve this via hole theory (the negative-energy sea); the Feynman-Stückelberg interpretation 1948 reinterpreted negative-energy states as antiparticles. The sign-blind apparatus cannot pick out which spectrum half is physically realised; this content has to be imported.

(b) **Future-vs-past light cone distinction.** The Lorentzian metric admits both future-directed and past-directed null vectors symmetrically; the connected component $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ does pick out time orientation, but the *choice* of which orientation is “future-pointing” is a dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel commitment, not derivable from the algebraic apparatus alone. The retarded Green’s function $G_R(x; x')$ supported on the future light cone and the advanced Green’s function $G_A(x; x')$ on the past light cone are formally symmetric — Maxwell’s equations admit both; the empirical privilege of $G_R$ (Wheeler-Feynman 1945 absorber theory) is dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel.

(c) **Strict Second Law $dS/dt > 0$.** Liouville’s theorem (preserved phase-space volume under Hamiltonian flow) is $T$-symmetric — phase space volume is preserved both forward and backward in time. The H-theorem requires Boltzmann’s Stosszahlansatz (molecular chaos assumption), which is itself $T$-anti-invariant and is therefore not derivable from the Algebraic Channel apparatus alone. Loschmidt 1876 proved this: time-symmetric microdynamics cannot derive a strict monotonic Second Law. The sign-blind apparatus is exactly time-symmetric microdynamics; the strict Second Law cannot be derived from it.

(d) **Cosmological expansion.** The Lorentzian field equations admit both expanding and contracting solutions; the Friedmann-Robertson-Walker equations have both $H > 0$ and $H < 0$ branches. The Born-rule realization (measurement happening forward in time, with collapse at future detection events) is dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel Theorem 12.2 \[present paper: measurement as physical Wick rotation\].

*Step 3 (Spectrum Condition as algebraic residue of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel’s orientation).* The Wightman 1956 axiomatic system was the systematic axiomatization of QFT, intended to reduce the operator-algebra to a minimal set of postulates. The first five axioms — Hilbert space (W1), Poincaré covariance (W2), locality / microcausality (W3), domain of field operators (W4), vacuum existence and uniqueness (W5) — are sign-blind on $+ic$: each axiom is invariant under the $+ic \leftrightarrow -ic$ involution. The Spectrum Condition is *not* a theorem of the other Wightman axioms. It must be *imposed* as an independent axiom. Sixty-eight years of axiomatic QFT (1956–2026) has been carrying the Spectrum Condition as an unexplained axiom because Algebraic Channel has no other place to put the $+ic$ orientation — the orientation cannot live in the sign-blind algebra, so it must be imported as an additional axiom to make the apparatus empirically adequate.

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework identifies the status of the Spectrum Condition: **it is the algebraic residue of the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel’s $+ic$ orientation surviving the projection $\Pi_A$**. The Sphere’s $+ic$ expansion direction, when projected through $\Pi_A$ to the algebraic image, manifests as the requirement that the energy-momentum spectrum be supported on the forward light cone in momentum space — equivalently, that physical states have non-negative energy with respect to a chosen time orientation.
