#### 19.3.2 On-shell enhancement theorem

The conservation laws (C1)+(C2) are weaker than the full local conservation $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$. The gap is closed *on shell* by the constitutive identity (10.2.1.1) combined with the matter equations of motion.

**Theorem 19.3.2.1 (On-shell enhancement to full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ symmetry).** Given:
(i) $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$-invariance of the matter action (kinematic symmetry from foliation-preservation by $dx_4/dt = ic$);
(ii) the constitutive identity $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ pointwise (GR T1, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$);
*(iii) the matter equations of motion (continuity equation, Euler equation, equations of state),*

the local conservation $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ holds at every event of $M_G$. Consequently, the full diffeomorphism group $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ acts as a symmetry of the on-shell theory.
*Proof.* The proof proceeds by computing $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu}$ from the stress-energy tensor (10.2.2.1) and showing both its $u_\nu$-contraction (parallel component) and its spatial-projection (orthogonal component) vanish under the three postulates.

Differentiate (10.2.2.1):
`\begin{align*} \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; & \nabla_\mu\!\left[ (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu u^\nu}{c^2} \right] \;+\; \nabla_\mu (p g^{\mu\nu}) \\ =\; & \nabla_\mu\!\left[ (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu}{c^2} \right] u^\nu \;+\; (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu \nabla_\mu u^\nu}{c^2} \;+\; g^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p, \end{align*}`{=tex}
using metric compatibility $\nabla_\mu g_{\nu\rho} = 0$ (Lemma 8.2.4.1 of \[55, Chapter 8\]) in the second equation.

Contract by $u_\nu$:
$$u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; -c^2 \nabla_\mu\!\left[ (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu}{c^2} \right] \;+\; (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu u_\nu \nabla_\mu u^\nu}{c^2} \;+\; u^\mu \partial_\mu p,$$
using $u_\nu u^\nu = -c^2$ (postulate (ii)) for the first term. The crucial identity:
$$u_\nu \nabla_\mu u^\nu \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2} \nabla_\mu (u^\nu u_\nu) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2} \nabla_\mu (-c^2) \;=\; 0, \tag{10.3.2.1}$$
by differentiating the constitutive identity (postulate (ii)). Hence the second term vanishes, leaving
$$u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; -c^2 \nabla_\mu\!\left[ (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu}{c^2} \right] \;+\; u^\mu \partial_\mu p.$$
The continuity equation $\nabla_\mu (\rho u^\mu) = 0$ (matter equation of motion, postulate (iii)) together with the first law of thermodynamics $u^\mu \partial_\mu \rho = -(\rho + p/c^2) \nabla_\mu u^\mu$ closes this expression to zero:
$$u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; 0. \tag{10.3.2.2}$$

Define the spatial projector $h^\nu_\lambda \equiv \delta^\nu_\lambda + u^\nu u_\lambda / c^2$. Projecting $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu}$ by $h^\nu_\lambda$:
$$h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\lambda} \;=\; (\rho c^2 + p)\, h^\nu_\lambda \frac{u^\mu \nabla_\mu u^\lambda}{c^2} \;+\; h^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p,$$
where the first term used the projector annihilating $u^\nu$ in the first term of Step 1’s expansion (since $h^\nu_\lambda u^\lambda = 0$ by direct computation: $h^\nu_\lambda u^\lambda = u^\nu + u^\nu u_\lambda u^\lambda / c^2 = u^\nu - u^\nu = 0$). The Euler equation in covariant form (matter equation of motion, postulate (iii)) is
$$(\rho c^2 + p)\, u^\mu \nabla_\mu u^\lambda \;=\; -h^{\mu\lambda} \partial_\mu p, \tag{10.3.2.3}$$
which when projected by $h^\nu_\lambda$ gives $h^\nu_\lambda \cdot (\text{first term}) = -h^\nu_\lambda \cdot h^{\mu\lambda} \partial_\mu p / 1 = -h^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p$. Combining:
$$h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\lambda} \;=\; -h^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p \;+\; h^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p \;=\; 0. \tag{10.3.2.4}$$

Equations (10.3.2.2) and (10.3.2.4) together span all four directions in the tangent space at every event $p \in M_G$: $u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ on the timelike direction, $h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\lambda} = 0$ on the spatial three-directions. The full divergence vanishes:
$$\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; 0 \tag{10.3.2.5}$$
at every event. This is the standard local conservation of stress-energy.

With $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ established, the Bianchi-compatible field equations $G_{\mu\nu} \propto T_{\mu\nu}$ are consistent with arbitrary diffeomorphisms of $M_G$. The action is invariant under full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ *on shell*; the off-shell symmetry remains $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$. The full diffeomorphism invariance of general relativity emerges as the on-shell consequence of the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s factorisation. $\square$

The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework is stronger than Hilbert’s diffeomorphism postulate: it specifies which diffeomorphisms are off-shell symmetries (only $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$, by foliation preservation), why the gap to full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ closes on-shell (by the four-velocity budget plus matter equations of motion), and what each of the two factors physically contributes. Hilbert’s full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$-invariance, taken as a primitive in the standard textbook treatment, is here a derived consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$ on shell.

### 19.4 Algebraic Channel, Step 4: Lovelock’s Theorem and the Newtonian Limit {#sec:lovelock}

#### 19.4.1 Lovelock’s theorem

**Theorem 19.4.1 (Lovelock 1971).** On a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold, the unique divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensor constructed from the metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ and its first two derivatives, with linear dependence on the second derivatives, is
$$L_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \alpha\, G_{\mu\nu} \;+\; \beta\, g_{\mu\nu}, \tag{10.4.1.1}$$
where $G_{\mu\nu} = R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu}$ is the Einstein tensor and $\alpha, \beta$ are constants.
This is a purely differential-geometric theorem \[Lovelock 1971\]; we take it as a standard input. Within the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, the conditions of Lovelock’s theorem are themselves theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$:

-   “four-dimensional manifold” follows from the McGucken-manifold structure of Definition 1 of the Introduction;

-   “Lorentzian signature” follows from Lemma 5.1.2.2 of \[55, Chapter 5\] (Minkowski metric forced by $dx_4/dt = ic$);

-   “symmetric rank-2 tensor” follows from Riemann symmetry (S3) (Lemma 9.2.2.4 of \[55, Chapter 9\]);

-   “divergence-free” follows from the contracted second Bianchi identity (Theorem 9.4.2.3 of \[55, Chapter 9\]);

-   “metric + first two derivatives” follows from the Christoffel symbol formula (GR T8, \[55, Chapter 8\]).

Hence the *inputs* of Lovelock’s theorem are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$; the theorem itself is the uniqueness statement applied to the LHS of the field equations.

#### 19.4.2 Application of Lovelock with the stress-energy tensor as source

**Lemma 19.4.2 (Field equations from Lovelock + on-shell conservation).** Set $L_{\mu\nu} = \kappa\, T_{\mu\nu}$ with $\kappa$ a coupling constant to be determined. Using (10.4.1.1):
$$\alpha\, G_{\mu\nu} \;+\; \beta\, g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \kappa\, T_{\mu\nu}. \tag{10.4.2.1}$$
Dividing by $\alpha$ (assumed non-zero) and identifying $\beta/\alpha = \Lambda$ and $\kappa/\alpha = \kappa'$:
$$G_{\mu\nu} \;+\; \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \kappa'\, T_{\mu\nu}. \tag{10.4.2.2}$$
Consistency with the conservation $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (Theorem 19.3.2.1) requires $\nabla^\mu G_{\mu\nu} = 0$, which is the contracted Bianchi identity (Theorem 9.4.2.3); $\nabla^\mu (\Lambda g_{\mu\nu}) = \Lambda \nabla^\mu g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ by metric compatibility. Hence (10.4.2.2) is consistent.
\#### 19.4.3 Newtonian-limit matching fixes the coupling constant

**Theorem 19.4.3 (Coupling-constant matching to Newtonian gravity).** In the weak-field, non-relativistic static limit of (10.4.2.2) — with $g_{00} = -(1 + 2\Phi/c^2)$, $g_{ij} = \delta_{ij}$, $T_{00} = \rho c^2$ dominant, $\Lambda$ negligible at solar-system scales — equation (10.4.2.2) reduces to Newton’s law of gravity
$$\nabla^2 \Phi \;=\; 4\pi G\, \rho, \tag{10.4.3.1}$$
*provided $\kappa' = 8\pi G / c^4$. Hence the coupling constant is*
$$\kappa' \;=\; \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}. \tag{10.4.3.2}$$

*Proof.* Standard calculation (Wald §4.4, Carroll §4.2). The $00$-component of (10.4.2.2) in the weak-field limit reduces to
$$G_{00} \;=\; \kappa'\, T_{00}.$$
Computing $G_{00}$ from the weak-field metric: $R_{00} = \nabla^2 \Phi / c^2$ to leading order; $R = 2 \nabla^2 \Phi / c^2$ to leading order (with sign conventions consistent with the $(-, +, +, +)$ metric); $G_{00} = R_{00} - \tfrac{1}{2} R g_{00} = \nabla^2 \Phi/c^2 - \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot (2 \nabla^2 \Phi / c^2) \cdot (-1) = 2 \nabla^2 \Phi / c^2$. With $T_{00} = \rho c^2$:
$$2 \nabla^2 \Phi / c^2 \;=\; \kappa' \rho c^2 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \nabla^2 \Phi \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2} \kappa' c^4 \rho.$$
Matching to Newton’s law $\nabla^2 \Phi = 4\pi G \rho$:
$$4\pi G \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2} \kappa' c^4 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \kappa' \;=\; \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}.$$

*McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework reading.* The coupling constant $\kappa' = 8\pi G/c^4$ is the *Einstein-equation coupling* between curvature and stress-energy. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework reading: by Lemma 11.3.1.1 (the factor-of-2 weak-field expansion), the linearised Einstein-equation coupling is *twice* the naive Newtonian-coupling that would arise from a direct identification of the metric perturbation with the Newtonian potential. The factor of 2 traces back to the trace-reversal structure of the Einstein tensor $G_{\mu\nu} = R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu}$ (Lemma 9.4.2.2 of \[55, Chapter 9\]), which contributes a second factor of $G$ to the source coupling on top of the Ricci-tensor contribution. The reading: the Einstein-equation coupling $8\pi G/c^4$ encodes (i) the gravitational constant $G$ (the strength of the gravitational interaction), (ii) the speed of light $c^4$ (the dimensional reduction from energy-density to curvature units), and (iii) the geometric factor $8\pi$ (the surface-area normalisation of the gravitational source on a unit sphere, $8\pi = 2 \cdot 4\pi$ — the trace-reversal-doubled normalisation). The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework meaning: the constant $\kappa' = 8\pi G/c^4$ is the precise coupling that makes the Einstein-tensor-conservation (Theorem 9.4.2.3) compatible with stress-energy conservation $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ at every event of $M_G$, with the McGucken-Sphere geometric structure of $M_G$ determining the precise numerical factor via the linearised Newtonian-limit matching. $\square$

Postulates (i) and (ii) are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$; postulate (iii) follows from (i) + (ii) + matter dynamics; postulates (iv) and (v) are standard. The field equations are forced. $\square$

### 19.5 dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel, Step 1: The Geometric Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ {#sec:second-law}

The $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations follows the thermodynamic route of Jacobson \[Jacobson 1995\], with every input that Jacobson treats as a postulate (area-law entropy, Unruh temperature, monotone entropy increase) derived as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The first such theorem is the Geometric Second Law.

#### 19.5.1 Statement and proof of the Geometric Second Law

**Theorem 19.5.1 (Geometric Second Law of Thermodynamics).** Let $M_G$ be the McGucken manifold and the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ hold at every event. Consider an ensemble of $N$ particles at positions $\{r_\alpha\}_{\alpha=1}^N$ on the spatial slice $\Sigma_t$. The Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy of the ensemble is
$$S(t) \;=\; -k_B \int P(\vec r, t)\, \ln P(\vec r, t)\, d^3 r, \tag{10.5.1.1}$$
where $P(\vec r, t)$ is the probability density. Then $S$ is strictly monotonically increasing in $t$:
$$\frac{dS}{dt} \;>\; 0 \tag{10.5.1.2}$$
*at every $t > t_0$, with $t_0$ the initial time.*

The monotonicity is *exact* (not statistical), and there is no Poincaré recurrence: $x_4$ advances and does not retreat.
*Proof.* We proceed in four steps.

By $dx_4/dt = ic$, $x_4$ advances at rate $ic$ from every event of $M_G$, isotropically across the spatial three-slice (the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (ii)). At every Planck-time step $\delta t_P = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^5}$, the McGucken Sphere of expansion at each particle’s position has radius $c\, \delta t_P = \ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^3}$ (the Planck length), and the particle is displaced by $c \, \delta t_P$ in a direction $\hat n$ drawn uniformly from the unit sphere $S^2$.

The probability density $P(\vec r, t)$ evolves under iterated isotropic Compton displacements with rms step size $c\, \delta t_P$ per step. By the Einstein 1905 derivation of Brownian motion applied with step size $c \, \delta t_P$ and step time $\delta t_P$, the diffusion coefficient is
$$D \;=\; \frac{(c\, \delta t_P)^2}{6\, \delta t_P} \;=\; \frac{c^2\, \delta t_P}{6}, \tag{10.5.1.3}$$
and the probability density satisfies
$$\frac{\partial P}{\partial t} \;=\; D\, \nabla^2 P. \tag{10.5.1.4}$$
This is the isotropic-diffusion equation, derived from the McGucken Sphere expansion at each Planck-time step.

The fundamental solution of (10.5.1.4) with delta-function initial data $P(\vec r, 0) = \delta^3(\vec r)$ is the Gaussian
$$P(\vec r, t) \;=\; (4\pi D t)^{-3/2}\, \exp\!\left(-\frac{r^2}{4 D t}\right). \tag{10.5.1.5}$$
Substituting into (10.5.1.1) and evaluating the Gaussian-entropy integral (standard computation):
$$S(t) \;=\; \tfrac{3}{2} k_B\, \ln(4\pi e\, D t) \;+\; \text{const.} \tag{10.5.1.6}$$

Differentiate (10.5.1.6) with respect to $t$:
$$\frac{dS}{dt} \;=\; \frac{3 k_B}{2 t} \;>\; 0 \tag{10.5.1.7}$$
for all $t > 0$, since $k_B > 0$ and $t > 0$.

The strictness of the inequality follows from the *$+ic$ orientation* of the principle: $x_4$ advances at $+ic$, not $-ic$. The diffusion equation (10.5.1.4) propagates probability forward in $t$ with no time-reversed branch. The textbook statistical Second Law (a tendency with Poincaré recurrence) reduces to the McGucken geometric Second Law (a strict monotonicity without recurrence) when the $+ic$-oriented physical motion underlying $dx_4/dt = ic$ is recognised. $\square$

#### 19.5.2 Reading of the Geometric Second Law

The Geometric Second Law is *not* the statistical Second Law of Boltzmann (a tendency with non-zero probability of fluctuations); it is a theorem about the certain monotonic advance of $x_4$ and the entropy it generates. There is no Poincaré recurrence because $x_4$ does not recur.

Theorem 19.5.1 is the *horizon-level* Geometric Second Law (used directly in §19.8 in the Jacobson chain). A particle-level companion — Theorem 19.5.3 below, importing Proposition 4.5.4 of \[2, §4.5\] — establishes the same Second Law from the Compton-coupling Brownian motion of massive particles, with a sharper *quantitative* form $dS/dt = (3/2) k_B / t$.

#### 19.5.3 Particle-level companion (optional, for the headline chapter)

**Theorem 19.5.3 (Strict Second Law for massive-particle ensembles).** For an ensemble of massive particles undergoing the Compton-coupling Wiener process generated by the iterated McGucken Sphere flow on the spatial slice,
$$\frac{dS}{dt} \;=\; \frac{3 k_B}{2 t} \tag{10.5.3.1}$$
*strictly, for all $t > 0$.*

*Proof.* Established at Proposition 4.5.4 of \[2, §4.5\]. The proof uses Propositions 4.5.1 (Compton coupling between matter and $x_4$ at angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$), 4.5.2 (spatial-projection isotropy by spherical symmetry of $dx_4/dt = ic$), 4.5.3 (Brownian motion as iterated isotropic Compton displacement via central limit theorem applied to iid sphere-uniform increments), and direct Gaussian-entropy evaluation of $S = -k_B \int P \ln P d^3 r$ on the Wiener-process density. $\square$

The particle-level derivation refines the horizon-level Theorem 19.5.1 with a sharper quantitative content: the specific rate $dS/dt = (3/2) k_B / t$.

### 19.6 dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel, Step 2: The Area Law $S = k_B A / (4 \ell_P^2)$ {#sec:area-law}

#### 19.6.1 The area law from $x_4$-mode counting on McGucken Spheres

**Theorem 19.6.1 (Area law for entropy on McGucken Spheres).** Let $M_G$ be the McGucken manifold, let the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ hold at every event, and let the Planck length $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^3}$ be identified as the fundamental wavelength of $x_4$-advance (the identification developed in \[3, 4\] and used throughout the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework). Then the entropy associated with a McGucken Sphere of area $A$ is
$$S \;=\; \frac{k_B A}{4 \ell_P^2} \;=\; \frac{k_B A c^3}{4 \hbar G}. \tag{10.6.1.1}$$

*Proof.* The McGucken Sphere associated with a spacetime event $O$ is the 2-sphere swept out by $x_4$’s spherically symmetric expansion at radius $R = ct$ from $O$ (Definition 2 of the Introduction). Its area is $A = 4\pi R^2 = 4\pi c^2 t^2$.

Quantise $x_4$’s expansion at the Planck scale: the fundamental wavelength of $x_4$-advance is $\ell_P$. The number of independent quantum modes of $x_4$-advance crossing the McGucken Sphere is one mode per Planck-area cell. By the standard mode-counting argument \[Bekenstein 1973, Hawking 1975, ’t Hooft 1993 (the holographic principle), Susskind 1995\],
$$N_{\text{bits}} \;=\; \frac{A}{\ell_P^2} \tag{10.6.1.2}$$
up to a numerical factor of order unity. Identifying entropy with $k_B$ times the number of bits, and fixing the numerical factor by demanding consistency with the Bekenstein-Hawking expression in the limiting case of a black hole horizon \[Bekenstein 1973, Hawking 1975\]:
$$S \;=\; \frac{k_B A}{4 \ell_P^2} \;=\; \frac{k_B A c^3}{4 \hbar G}.$$
The factor $1/4$ is fixed by the Bekenstein-Hawking matching; the fact $S \propto A$ (rather than $S \propto V$) is forced by the $x_4$-mode counting on the McGucken Sphere. $\square$

#### 19.6.2 Reading: the area law is McGucken-Sphere entropy

The area law (T10.6.1) is *not* an imported result from black hole thermodynamics; rather, the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of a black hole horizon is the *special case* of the McGucken-Sphere entropy when the McGucken Sphere coincides with the black hole horizon. The priority statement: $S = k_B A / (4 \ell_P^2)$ is the entropy of $x_4$-advance modes on any McGucken Sphere, with the black hole horizon being a particular kind of McGucken Sphere (the apparent horizon of a Schwarzschild-trapped region; see \[55, Chapter 22\]-24).

### 19.7 dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel, Step 3: The Unruh Temperature $T_U = \hbar a / (2\pi c k_B)$ {#sec:unruh}

#### 19.7.1 The Unruh temperature from the Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost

**Theorem 19.7.1 (Unruh temperature from the McGucken-Wick rotation).** A uniformly accelerated observer in $M_G$ with proper acceleration $a$ experiences a thermal bath at temperature
$$T_U \;=\; \frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c k_B}. \tag{10.7.1.1}$$
The temperature is a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the Wick-rotation Theorem 4 of the Introduction (the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$) plus the KMS-periodicity identification of thermal states.
*Proof.* Consider a uniformly accelerated observer with proper acceleration $a$. The observer’s worldline in Minkowski coordinates is
$$X(\tau_p) \;=\; \frac{c^2}{a}\, \sinh\!\left(\frac{a \tau_p}{c}\right), \quad x(\tau_p) \;=\; \frac{c^2}{a}\, \cosh\!\left(\frac{a \tau_p}{c}\right) \tag{10.7.1.2}$$
where $\tau_p$ is the observer’s proper time.

Under the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$, $t \to -i\tau$ (Theorem 4 of the Introduction; theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via Lemma 5.1.2.1 of \[55, Chapter 5\]), the hyperbolic boost in the $(x, t)$-plane becomes a Euclidean rotation in the $(x, x_4)$-plane by angle $\theta = a \tau_p / c$ (where $\tau_p$ in this context denotes the Wick-rotated, Euclidean-section proper time of the accelerated observer).

Periodicity in the Euclidean angle $\theta$ (required by single-valuedness of the rotation on the Euclidean section): $\theta \in [0, 2\pi)$. The corresponding period in the Wick-rotated proper time is
$$\Delta \tau_p \;=\; \frac{2 \pi c}{a}. \tag{10.7.1.3}$$

By the KMS condition of quantum statistical mechanics \[Kubo 1957; Martin-Schwinger 1959; Haag 1992\], a quantum field state periodic in imaginary (proper) time with period $\Delta\tau_p$ is a thermal state at temperature $T$ given by the standard KMS relation $\Delta\tau_p = \hbar/(k_B T)$, equivalently $T = \hbar/(k_B \Delta\tau_p)$. Substituting (10.7.1.3):
$$T_U \;=\; \frac{\hbar}{k_B \cdot 2\pi c/a} \;=\; \frac{\hbar a}{2 \pi c\, k_B}. \tag{10.7.1.4}$$
$\square$

**Remark 10.7.2 (the KMS identification).** The KMS identification of imaginary-time periodicity with inverse temperature is the one substantive input from quantum statistical mechanics. Within the McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework, KMS itself admits a derivation from the Wick-rotation structure of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Theorem 4 of the Introduction); we leave the full development of this to \[3CH, §5\] and import the KMS identification here as a standing assumption of the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel, alongside the Clausius relation in §19.8.

### 19.8 dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel, Step 4: Clausius Relation at Local Rindler Horizons {#sec:jacobson}

#### 19.8.1 The Jacobson chain: $\delta Q = T \delta S$ at horizons

With the Geometric Second Law (Theorem 19.5.1), the area law (Theorem 19.6.1), and the Unruh temperature (Theorem 19.7.1) established as theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$, the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations proceeds along Jacobson’s 1995 chain.

Consider an arbitrary spacetime event $p \in M_G$ and a *local Rindler horizon* $H$ through $p$: a null hypersurface generated by a null congruence with affine parameter $\lambda$ and tangent vector $k^\mu$. The horizon is the boundary of the past of a uniformly accelerated observer in the local neighbourhood of $p$.

The heat flux through a portion of $H$ is the integrated stress-energy flux along the local Rindler boost Killing vector $\xi^\mu = -\kappa\, \lambda\, k^\mu$ (Jacobson 1995 eq. 2; Wald 1984 §12.5), where $\kappa = a$ is the surface gravity (equal to the proper acceleration of the local Rindler observer at unit distance) and $\lambda$ is the affine parameter along the null generators of $H$:
$$\delta Q \;=\; \int_H T_{\mu\nu}\, \xi^\mu\, k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \;=\; -\kappa \int_H \lambda\, T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu\, k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA. \tag{10.8.1.1}$$

By Theorem 19.6.1, the entropy associated with the horizon area is $S = k_B A / (4 \ell_P^2)$. The infinitesimal entropy change is
$$\delta S \;=\; \frac{k_B}{4 \ell_P^2}\, \delta A. \tag{10.8.1.2}$$

The Raychaudhuri equation for a null congruence with tangent vector $k^\mu$ and expansion $\theta = d\ln A/d\lambda$, with vanishing expansion and shear at the bifurcation surface (where $\lambda = 0$), gives to leading order in $\lambda$
$$\theta(\lambda) = -\int_0^\lambda R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda'.$$
Integrating $dA/d\lambda = \theta\, A$ along the null generators, the area change between the bifurcation surface and affine parameter $\Lambda$ is
$$\delta A \;=\; -\int_H \lambda\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \tag{10.8.1.3}$$
to leading order. The minus sign reflects that positive $R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu$ (the null energy condition direction) causes geodesic focussing, which decreases the cross-sectional area of the congruence.

Applying the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T \delta S$ with $T = T_U = \hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)$ from (10.7.1.1) and $\kappa = a$:
$$-a \int_H \lambda\, T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \;=\; \frac{\hbar a}{2 \pi c\, k_B} \cdot \frac{k_B}{4 \ell_P^2} \cdot \left(-\int_H \lambda\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA\right).$$
Cancelling $-a$ from both sides:
$$\int_H \lambda\, T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \;=\; \frac{\hbar}{8 \pi c\, \ell_P^2} \int_H \lambda\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA.$$
This identity, together with full unit-tracking through the boost-Killing-vector normalization (Jacobson 1995, eqs. 3–5; the standard derivation), produces the Einstein-equation coefficient $c^4/(8\pi G)$ on the right-hand side. The pointwise statement valid at every event $p \in M_G$ and for every null $k^\mu$ at $p$ is
$$T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu \;=\; \frac{c^4}{8 \pi G}\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu. \tag{10.8.1.4}$$
The complete unit-tracking calculation, reconciling the dimensional content of the Unruh temperature, the Planck-area normalization, the Killing-vector normalization, and the Raychaudhuri-area integration, is in \[Jacobson 1995, equations 1–6\] and recovered in textbook form in \[Padmanabhan 2010, *Gravitation*, §15.4\]. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework sourcing of each of the three thermodynamic inputs (Geometric Second Law, area law, Unruh temperature) as theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the dx₄/dt = ic framework’s contribution at this step; the Jacobson chain itself is inherited.

Since (10.8.1.4) holds for every null vector $k^\mu$ at every event, and $T_{\mu\nu}$ and $R_{\mu\nu}$ are both symmetric tensors, the contraction with null vectors forces a relation between the full tensors:
$$R_{\mu\nu} \;-\; \tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu} \;+\; \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \frac{8 \pi G}{c^4}\, T_{\mu\nu}. \tag{10.8.1.5}$$

The trace term $-\tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu}$ is forced by the conservation $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$, which is in turn required by the contracted Bianchi identity $\nabla^\mu G_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (Theorem 9.4.2.3 of \[55, Chapter 9\]); the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ enters as an integration constant (the unique additive term consistent with $\nabla^\mu (\Lambda g_{\mu\nu}) = 0$ by metric compatibility).

#### 19.8.2 The Einstein field equations from the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel

**Theorem 19.8.2 (Einstein Field Equations from the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel).** Combining Theorems 10.5.1 (Geometric Second Law), 10.6.1 (area law), 10.7.1 (Unruh temperature), the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T \delta S$, and the Raychaudhuri equation, the Einstein field equations
$$\boxed{\, G_{\mu\nu} \,+\, \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}\, T_{\mu\nu} \,} \tag{T11.1, dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel}$$
*are forced as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ along the Geometric Channel route.*

*Proof.* Direct combination of: (i) the Geometric Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ (Theorem 19.5.1, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via isotropic-diffusion content of $dx_4/dt = ic$); (ii) the area law $S = k_B A / (4 \ell_P^2)$ (Theorem 19.6.1, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via $x_4$-mode counting at Planck scale); (iii) the Unruh temperature $T_U = \hbar a / (2 \pi c k_B)$ (Theorem 19.7.1, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost); (iv) the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T \delta S$ at local Rindler horizons; (v) the Raychaudhuri equation for null congruences (Equation 10.8.1.3, theorem of differential geometry on null geodesic congruences). Postulates (i)-(iii) are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$; postulates (iv) and (v) are standard inputs from thermodynamics and differential geometry respectively. The field equations are forced. $\square$

The Jacobson-McGucken thermodynamic route reads the Einstein field equations as the *equation of state* of spacetime, with the McGucken Sphere as the fundamental horizon-bounding surface and the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the source of the Sphere’s expansion. The thermodynamic identity $\delta Q = T \delta S$ at every local Rindler horizon, with $T$ the Unruh temperature and $S$ the area-law entropy, forces $G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$ as the unique relation that makes the identity hold for every null direction at every event. The dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel derivation reveals general relativity as a *thermodynamic limit* of underlying $x_4$-expansion dynamics, with the field equations emerging from the area-law statistics of $x_4$-modes on McGucken Sphere horizons.

(A2) Lemma 19.1.2.1 (rigidity of $\xi^0$) is a restriction on diffeomorphism generators; dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel has no analogous restriction — the Rindler boost is parameterised by proper acceleration $a$, not by a restricted-vector-field structure. (A2) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A4) Noether’s second theorem is the *variational* tool of the Algebraic Channel; dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel uses no variational principle at any step. The Raychaudhuri equation (B9) is a *kinematic* identity for null congruences, not a Noether-type conservation theorem. (A4) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A5) Spatial conservation and integrated time conservation are weak conservation laws specific to the Algebraic Channel’s $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ symmetry; dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel has no analogous weak conservation laws — it uses the strong conservation $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ implicitly through the contracted Bianchi identity at step (B10), but does not derive that conservation from a Noether-type argument. (A5) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A6) On-shell enhancement is the mechanism by which Algebraic Channel closes the gap from $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ to $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$; dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel has no analogous enhancement step — the Clausius relation is applied locally at every event without an on-shell/off-shell distinction. (A6) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A7) Lovelock’s theorem is a *differential-geometric uniqueness* result on divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensors in 4D; dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel does not invoke this theorem at any step. The universalisation in (B10) uses the contracted Bianchi identity to fix the trace term, but does not use Lovelock’s uniqueness statement on the metric-and-derivatives functional form of the LHS. (A8) Newtonian-limit matching is a *weak-field static* calculation matching to Poisson’s equation; dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel has no Newtonian-limit step — the coupling constant $\kappa' = 8\pi G/c^4$ emerges in the dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel from the Clausius relation directly, via the combination of the area-law factor $1/(4\ell_P^2)$, the Unruh factor $\hbar/(2\pi c k_B)$, and the Planck-length substitution $\ell_P^2 = \hbar G/c^3$ — with no Newtonian matching invoked. (A8) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

Conversely:

(B1) Isotropic-diffusion equation is a *Brownian-motion* identity for the probability density; Algebraic Channel has no probability-density structure — it treats matter through the deterministic stress-energy tensor (A3). (B1) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B2) Gaussian fundamental solution is the explicit form of the diffusion’s heat kernel; Algebraic Channel has no heat-kernel structure. (B2) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B3) Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy and the Geometric Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ are *statistical-mechanical* identities; Algebraic Channel has no entropy or Second Law content at any step — the Newtonian-limit matching (A8) is deterministic, not statistical. (B3) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B4) $x_4$-mode counting at the Planck scale is a *quantum-geometric* counting argument; Algebraic Channel has no quantum-geometric inputs — it operates entirely at the classical-variational level. (B4) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

share no intermediate machinery. The Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$ have the following status within the McGucken framework:

## Appendix A. Reading the McGucken Principle: A Note on $dx_4/dt$, $dx_4/d\tau$, and the Photon — Clarifying Common Reader Misconceptions

**About this appendix.** Readers arriving at the McGucken Principle from a standard graduate-relativity background bring one deep habit: the reflex to treat per-proper-time quantities as the “physical” or “covariant” ones, and per-coordinate-time quantities as gauge-dependent bookkeeping. That habit points the wrong way here, because the Principle is a statement about the manifold itself — an expansion happening at every event, at the same rate, regardless of which worldline crosses that event. This appendix explains the four distinct $x_4$-rate quantities the paper uses, states which one is the Principle, and shows through five worked examples how photons, horizons, twins, and GPS clocks all read naturally once the four quantities are kept in their proper roles.

### A.0 The Physical Fact

Every quantity, rule, and check in this appendix descends from one physical fact:

> The fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding in a spherically symmetric manner at the rate of $c$ from every spacetime event, or $dx_4/dt = ic$.

That is the McGucken Principle. Before any of its consequences are unpacked, its status must be stated plainly, because it is the point on which every reading in this appendix turns: $dx_4/dt = ic$ is an *ontological* claim — a statement about what physically is — and not a coordinate convention, a formal device, or a notational choice. It asserts that the fourth dimension is a real dimension that is really expanding, at the rate $c$, from every event of spacetime, now. The expansion is the physically primary fact; everything else in the paper is a consequence of it. Minkowski spacetime is what the expansion looks like after its rate is integrated into the coordinate $x_4 = ict$ and squared into the Lorentzian metric $x_4^2 = -c^2t^2$; Hilbert space is what the same expansion looks like when its per-increment imaginary rate is read as oscillation; the light cone is the locus the expanding wavefront traces; the metric, the causal order, the Poincaré group, the Born rule, and the Schrödinger equation are all downstream of the one expansion. None of these is postulated independently. They descend, by the derivations of the body, from the single physical fact that $x_4$ is expanding at $c$.

This is the reversal the reader must hold onto throughout. Standard physics takes Minkowski spacetime, or the Hilbert space, or the metric, as a starting arena and builds upon it. Here the arena is not a starting point but a *result*: the starting point is the physical expansion $dx_4/dt = ic$, and the arena is what that expansion generates. When the appendix below insists that $dx_4/dt = ic$ is primary and the per-proper-time quantities are constructed from it, this is what is meant — not a preference among equivalent formalisms, but a claim about which fact is physically prior. The rate is prior; the worldlines that share in it, the metric that its squaring produces, and the observers that read it are all posterior.

The imaginary unit $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ records the algebraic perpendicularity of the $x_4$-axis to the three spatial axes on which the expansion casts its projection. Its geometric realisation at each event $p \in$ 𝓜_G is the McGucken Sphere $M_p^+(t)$ — the spherical wavefront of radius $ct$ swept out around $p$ by the $x_4$-expansion. The Sphere is what distinguishes the Principle from Minkowski’s constant four-velocity norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$: the norm is a scalar constraint carrying no group action and no measure, and it survives here as a theorem of the Principle (the chain-rule pullback of the Sphere’s expansion rate).

The Sphere carries structure that supplies the Born rule downstream by five independent routes, established in the body of the paper and consolidated here. The two most fundamental are the Metric Route (the exponent 2 is the rank of the Minkowski metric that $x_4 = ict$ induces; Lemma 7.1) and the Haar Route (the Sphere’s transitive $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ action forces a unique invariant probability measure; Lemma 7.1.5). That these derivationally-disjoint derivations return the same Born density $|\psi|^2$ is an instance of the convergent overdetermination catalogued in Remark 7.17 and §17.5bis; see Remark A.0.1.

*Remark A.0.1 (Five independent derivations of the Born rule).* The Born density $P = |\psi|^2$ is derived in this framework by five routes that share no premises beyond the McGucken Sphere itself, each proceeding from a distinct property of the one Sphere. They are given here in order of foundational priority, matching the catalogue of Remark 7.17.

*(1) Metric Route — the Sphere’s metric rank* (Lemma 7.1; Theorem 7.2). The $x_4$-flux density at a detection event is the metric pairing of the forward $+ic$ advance with its conjugate $-ic$ advance. The Minkowski metric induced by $x_4 = ict$ is a rank-2 tensor, so the pairing is bilinear in $(\psi, \psi^*)$; rank-4 quartic densities are excluded by rank-counting, and $U(1)$ phase invariance, reality, non-negativity, and normalization then force $P = |\psi|^2$ uniquely. The exponent 2 is the rank of the metric. This is the most fundamental route, because the exponent is a property of the metric the Principle itself induces.

*(2) Haar Route — the Sphere’s symmetry group* (Lemma 7.1.5). The Sphere at the detection event is a round $S^2 \cong \mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2)$ carrying the transitive $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ action fixed by the isotropy of the $x_4$-expansion. By the uniqueness of the invariant measure on a homogeneous space of a compact group, there is exactly one $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant probability measure on the Sphere, the round measure $d\mu = \sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\phi/(4\pi)$, and this is the Born weight over detection directions. This is the route that answers why a probability *measure* exists at all: a measure is physically forced only where a symmetry singles it out uniquely, and $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ singles out exactly this one. Minkowski’s norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ carries no group action and therefore no such measure — which is why the Sphere, not the bare norm, is what grounds quantum probability.

*(3) Norm Route — the Sphere’s sesquilinear inner product* (Lemma 7.6). The rank-2 sesquilinear inner product satisfies the parallelogram identity as a two-line algebraic consequence, giving the L²-norm structure on Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with no Jordan–von Neumann theorem needed as upstream input.

*(4) Collision Route — two physical Spheres* (Theorem 7.7; Lemma 7.7.5). The number of physical participants in a head-on detection event is exactly two — emitter Sphere and absorber Sphere — and the coincidence rate is sesquilinear in the two amplitudes, with sum, max, min, and arithmetic/geometric/harmonic means excluded by action-additivity.

*(5) PT-Symmetry Route — the Sphere’s reflection* (Theorem 7.11). The Sphere’s discrete PT$_E$-symmetry through its source event gives $\psi^*(P) = \psi(PT_E \cdot P)$ exactly, so the squaring in the Born density is the cascade-level expression of that symmetry, and complex conjugation itself is grounded in it.

Routes (1) and (2) proceed respectively from the *rank* of the metric and the *symmetry group* of the Sphere, and are foregrounded as the two most important: the first fixes the exponent as the metric’s rank, the second supplies the invariant measure a probability rule requires. Routes (3)–(5) confirm the same exponent from the norm, the physical collision count, and the reflection symmetry. No route uses another’s premise — rank 2, the $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ action, the parallelogram identity, the two-participant count, and the PT-reflection are five logically independent facts about the same Sphere — so their agreement on $P = |\psi|^2$ is genuine convergence, not one argument told five times. This is the sense in which the Born rule is convergently overdetermined by $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Remark 7.17; §17.5bis): one downstream fact fixed by five upstream properties of the Sphere.

### A.1 The Four $x_4$-Rate Quantities

The framework uses four related quantities associated with the fourth dimension’s advance. Each has its own symbol, its own domain of definition, and its own interpretation, and they diverge on null worldlines.

*(R1) The coordinate rate* $dx_4/dt = ic$, parameter: coordinate $t$; range: fixed value $ic$; universal — holds at every event of 𝓜_G. The Principle. With the integrated shadow $x_4 = ict$, this rate holds identically along every worldline of 𝓜_G — timelike, null, accelerated, at any gravitational potential — because $x_4$ is a coordinate function of $t$ alone. Every statement about the universality of the expansion, its metric-independence (GR T2), or its exception-freeness is a statement in (R1).

*(R2) The Sphere-tangent velocity component* $v_{x_4} \equiv \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$ (the worldline’s share of the $x_4$-expansion, per coordinate time); parameter: coordinate $t$; range: $[0, c]$; worldline-dependent. A bounded quantity (Lemma 5.1.3.2). The partition $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$ holds for every worldline, null ones included: at spatial rest $v_{x_4} = c$; on a null worldline $v = c$ gives $v_{x_4} = 0$. On timelike worldlines, $v_{x_4}$ coincides with the standard time-dilation-related quantities of special relativity: $v_{x_4} = c\,d\tau/dt = c/\gamma$ for $0 \leq v < c$. The identity $v_{x_4} = c\, d\tau/dt$ is a theorem about $v_{x_4}$ — $\tau$ appears as output, not as the differentiation parameter. At $v = c$ (the null limit) all three expressions give $v_{x_4} = 0$: the $\sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$ form by direct substitution, the $c\,d\tau/dt$ form as the ratio $c \cdot 0/dt$ with $d\tau = 0$, and the $c/\gamma$ form as the limit $\gamma \to \infty$. The framework uses $v_{x_4}$ as the primary symbol because it is defined by direct substitution on the null boundary. Statements about time dilation, the photon’s $x_4$-rest, and horizons live here.

*(R3) The Lorentzian temporal component* $u^4 = dx_4/d\tau = ic\gamma$; parameter: proper $\tau$; unbounded, undefined on null worldlines; a chain-rule consequence. Derived from (R1) by the chain rule (Theorem 5.1.2.8): $dx_4/d\tau = (dx_4/dt)(dt/d\tau) = ic\gamma$. Its magnitude $c\gamma$ is unbounded as $v \to c$, and on a null worldline ($d\tau = 0$) the quantity is undefined — there the affinely-parametrised null tangent $dx^\mu/d\lambda$ replaces it (Lemma 7.2.2.1a).

*(R4) The accumulated $x_4$-advance along $\gamma$*, $X_4[\gamma] \equiv \int_\gamma ic\, d\tau = ic\, \tau[\gamma]$; a worldline functional, path-dependent. Distinct from the coordinate $x_4$. Two worldlines sharing endpoints share $\Delta x_4 = ic\, \Delta t$ but generally differ in $X_4$. Along a null worldline $X_4$ is constant; around any closed curve $\oint dx_4 = 0$ identically. Statements about differential aging (the twins) live in (R4). The bridge to (R2): $dX_4 = ic\, d\tau = i\, v_{x_4}\, dt$.

### A.2 Which One Is the Principle

The Principle is $dx_4/dt = ic$: the coordinate-time reading (R1). Because $x_4$ is a coordinate function of $t$ alone, the rate $dx_4/dt$ takes the same value $ic$ at every event of 𝓜_G — an expanding photon-event, a horizon event, an event on any accelerated worldline. The reading $dx_4/d\tau = ic$ is available too, but only where $d\tau = dt$: on a worldline at spatial rest, the chain rule collapses and (R1) coincides with the value of (R3). This is Lemma 4.7 (the rest-frame reverse-reading equivalence), and the qualification $d\tau = dt$ is what makes it valid. On a moving worldline the chain rule gives $ic\gamma$; on a null worldline the quantity does not exist. The coordinate-time reading is primary because $dx_4/dt = ic$ is a physical fact — the expansion itself is prior to any worldline, and $dx_4/dt = ic$ records it directly.

### A.3 Reading the Photon, the Horizon, and the Time-Dilation Formula

**A.3.1 What is the photon’s $x_4$-rate?** The photon’s share in the expansion is zero: $v_{x_4} = 0$ (the $v = c$ limit of $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$), obtained by direct substitution of $v = c$ into $v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$. The reader may be tempted to write “$dx_4/dt = 0$ for the photon” or “$dx_4/d\tau = 0$.” Neither is available. The first is the coordinate rate (R1), which is $ic$ at every event of 𝓜_G including the photon’s — what vanishes is the photon’s share, not the expansion. The second is $0/0$: proper time is not defined for a photon ($d\tau = 0$ pointwise). The correct statement is the share $v_{x_4} = 0$, so $X_4$ does not accumulate, so the photon ages not at all. The Principle continues to hold at every event the photon crosses.

**A.3.2 What does “the $x_4$-rate at the horizon” mean?** The rate is gravity-rigid: $\partial(dx_4/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (GR T2). The rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ takes the same value near the horizon as at infinity. What varies with potential is the share: $v_{x_4}(r) = c\,d\tau/dt = c\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ (static Schwarzschild observer), vanishing at $r = r_s$. On the infaller’s own clock $d\tau = dt$ locally and Lemma 4.7 applies: the local rate is the full $ic$ throughout. Gravitational time dilation is the coordinate-frame projection of a locally invariant rate.

**A.3.3 Which identity is “$c^2$ through spacetime”?** *Sphere partition* (per coordinate time, all worldlines): $v^2 + v_{x_4}^2 = c^2$, bounded, locus a quarter-circle. *Lorentzian four-velocity norm* (per proper time, massive worldlines): $u^\mu u_\mu = |dx_4/d\tau|^2 - |d\vec x/d\tau|^2 = -c^2$, unbounded in each term, signature difference fixing the invariant. The Euclidean per-proper-time sum $|dx_4/d\tau|^2 + |d\vec x/d\tau|^2$ equals $c^2$ only in the instantaneous rest frame; elsewhere $c^2\gamma^2$. Plus-sign identities belong to (R2); minus-sign identities to (R3).

**A.3.4 How does the twin paradox read?** Coordinate accumulation is path-independent: both twins accumulate $\Delta x_4 = ic\, \Delta t$. Differential ageing is read from $X_4 = \int ic\, d\tau$, advancing at real magnitude $v_{x_4}$ per unit coordinate time. On the traveling leg $v_{x_4} < c$, so the traveler accumulates less $X_4$, so less proper time. The stay-at-home twin retains $v_{x_4} = c$ and accumulates the maximal $X_4$. The CTC question closes the same way: $\oint dx_4 = 0$ identically, so a CTC cannot run on the coordinate; the impossibility lives in $X_4$.

**A.3.5 $\gamma$-projection and rapidity.** A boost is hyperbolic: rapidity $\phi$ with $\cosh\phi = \gamma$. The Sphere-partition projection is circular: Sphere angle $\theta$ with $\sin\theta = v/c$, $\cos\theta = v_{x_4}/c = 1/\gamma$. Related by the Gudermannian, $\theta = \operatorname{gd}(\phi)$, so $\cos\theta = \operatorname{sech}\phi$. The $1/\gamma$ projection is about $\theta$; unbounded component growth is about $\phi$.

### A.4 Why Nothing of Relativity Is Lost

The fourth dimension advances at the same rate at every event of 𝓜_G; worldlines differ only in how much of that advance they share in. Massive at rest shares fully ($v_{x_4} = c$); moving shares less ($v_{x_4} = \sqrt{c^2 - v^2}$, clock slowed by the Lorentz factor); photon does not share at all ($v_{x_4} = 0$, ageless, no $X_4$). Lorentz invariance survives entire because the invariant content — the norm $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ and the metric — is a theorem of the Principle (the metric is the pullback of the Euclidean form along $x_4 = ict$, the $-c^2$ from $(ic)^2$). Lorentz transformations preserve that derived metric; $\gamma$, time dilation, length contraction, $E = \gamma mc^2$, the null cone, and the mass-shell all come out unchanged. The foliation quantities $v_{x_4}$ and $X_4$ are additional bookkeeping frame-anchored to the cosmic-comoving foliation (the CMB rest frame); the Cloaking Theorem (Theorem 39) explains why local metrology cannot detect them. GR survives by the invariant/deformable split: the rate is gravity-rigid; gravity deforms the spatial sector. Time dilation, redshift, light bending, perihelion advance, the horizon, and the field equations are recovered exactly. The horizon is where the share is extinguished; the expansion does not stop.

### A.5 Worked Examples

**A.5.1 The twin paradox.** Traveler at speed $v$ for coordinate time $\Delta t$. Coordinate accumulation: $\Delta x_4 = ic\, \Delta t$ for both. Traveler’s share: $v_{x_4} = c\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$. Accumulated: $\Delta X_4^{\text{trav}} = ic\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}\, \Delta t$ vs $\Delta X_4^{\text{stay}} = ic\, \Delta t$. Differential aging: $\Delta\tau^{\text{trav}} - \Delta\tau^{\text{stay}} = \Delta t\,(\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2} - 1) < 0$: the traveler is younger by exactly the Lorentz factor.

**A.5.2 GPS clock rate.** Satellite at radius $r$, speed $v$, mass $M$. Principle: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Gravitational share: $v_{x_4}^{\text{grav}}/c = \sqrt{1 - 2GM/rc^2}$; kinematic factor $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$. Total: $v_{x_4}^{\text{sat}}/c \approx 1 - GM/(rc^2) - v^2/(2c^2)$. Ground: $\approx 1 - GM/(R_\oplus c^2)$. Fractional difference $\approx GM(1/R_\oplus - 1/r) - v^2/(2c^2)$, matching the $+4.5 \times 10^{-10}$ pre-launch offset at $r = 26{,}600$ km, $v = 3.87$ km/s.

**A.5.3 Schwarzschild gravitational redshift.** Photon from $r_1$ to $r_2 > r_1$. Principle: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Local clock rate: $v_{x_4}(r)/c = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$. Frequency ratio $\nu_2/\nu_1 = \sqrt{(1 - r_s/r_1)/(1 - r_s/r_2)}$; weak-field $\Delta\nu/\nu \approx -GM(1/r_2 - 1/r_1)/c^2$, matching Pound–Rebka 1959. Photon: $v_{x_4} = 0$ throughout, no $X_4$. The redshift is about the clock rates at emitter and receiver, not the photon.

**A.5.4 Hawking temperature.** At $r = r_s$, local share $v_{x_4}(r) \to 0$. Surface gravity $\kappa = c/(2r_s)$; compactification circumference $L_H = 4\pi r_s = c\hbar\beta_H$; temperature $T_H = \hbar c^3/(8\pi G M k_B)$. The expansion does not stop at the horizon; the share is extinguished on the static foliation, and compactification of the Euclidean-section $x_4$-axis at $L_H$ produces the thermal spectrum.

**A.5.5 Bell’s spaceship.** Rockets $A, B$ at proper distance $L_0$, accelerating identically. Coordinate rate: $dx_4/dt = ic$. Share: $v_{x_4}(t) = c\sqrt{1 - v(t)^2/c^2}$, decreasing. Accumulated: $X_4^A = X_4^B$, so both age identically. Launch-frame separation constant $L_0$; co-moving separation $L(t) = L_0\,c/v_{x_4}(t)$, growing without bound. The string breaks: the budget shifts into the spatial sector identically on each rocket, so no differential ageing; the paradox lives in the spatial-sector geometry, the string breaking as co-moving distance grows as $1/v_{x_4}$.

### C. Historical Bibliography for §16 (The Projection Theorem and the Catalog)

The following references are cited in §16 for the historical-evolution reading of physics primarily through the Algebraic Channel, the heterodox reach for dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel by twentieth-century dissidents, and the foundational papers of the 333-year light controversy.

**\[Wheeler 1978\]** Wheeler, J. A. “The ‘Past’ and the ‘Delayed-Choice’ Double-Slit Experiment.” In A. R. Marlow, ed., *Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Theory*, Academic Press, 1978, pp. 9–48. The original delayed-choice experiment proposal.

**\[Wheeler 1983, Smoky Dragon\]** Wheeler, J. A. “Law Without Law.” In J. A. Wheeler and W. H. Zurek, eds., *Quantum Theory and Measurement*, Princeton University Press, 1983, pp. 182–213. The primary citation for the Smoky Dragon metaphor: “We have no right to talk about what the photon is doing between emission and detection.” The dragon’s tail is the emission event (sharp); the dragon’s head is the detection event (sharp); the smoky body between is what Algebraic Channel’s apparatus has no right to speak of. The McGucken dx₄/dt = ic framework’s identification (§16.20): the smoke is the +ic-oriented McGucken Sphere expansion; the dragon is the Sphere itself; the silence of the Algebraic Channel about the dragon’s body is the signature of ΠB’s non-existence (Theorem 16.3).

**\[Wheeler-Zurek 1983\]** Wheeler, J. A. and Zurek, W. H., eds. *Quantum Theory and Measurement*. Princeton University Press, 1983. The canonical anthology containing the Wheeler “Law Without Law” essay and many other foundational measurement-theory papers; cited as the primary source for the Smoky Dragon and as the canonical Wheeler-era foundations anthology.

**\[Wheeler 1983, AmJP\]** Wheeler, J. A. “Bohr, Einstein, and the Strange Lesson of the Quantum.” *American Journal of Physics* 51, 1–10, 1983. Wheeler’s parallel articulation of the delayed-choice and observer-participancy content.

**\[Bell 1964\]** Bell, J. S. “On the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Paradox.” *Physics Physique Физика* 1, 195–200, 1964. The original Bell inequality establishing that quantum mechanics is incompatible with local hidden-variable theories. Cited in §16.20 entry C-B14 for the vindication of the Algebraic Channel’s irreducible-probability content over classical-ensemble reductions.

**\[Bell 1987\]** Bell, J. S. *Speakable and Unspeakable in Quantum Mechanics*. Cambridge University Press, 1987. The canonical collection of Bell’s foundations papers, including the beables/observables distinction. Cited in §16.20 entry C-B14 as the sharpest twentieth-century articulation of the ontological-epistemic asymmetry — Bell’s “beables” (what exists in the universe) are dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel; Bell’s “observables” (what gets measured) are Algebraic Channel.

**\[Bohm 1952\]** Bohm, D. “A Suggested Interpretation of the Quantum Theory in Terms of ‘Hidden’ Variables. I, II.” *Physical Review* 85, 166–179 and 180–193, 1952. The pilot-wave hidden-variable theory restoring definite particle trajectories guided by a quantum potential. Cited in §16.20 entry C-B10 as a pure dx₄/dt = ic Geometric Channel reach: the trajectories are definite spatiotemporal content underneath the statistical apparatus.

**\[Bohm 1980\]** Bohm, D. *Wholeness and the Implicate Order*. Routledge, 1980. The implicate-order generalization of the 1952 hidden-variable programme to a foundational reading of physics as the unfolding of an underlying generative content. Cited in §16.20 entry C-B15.

**\[Born 1926\]** Born, M. “Zur Quantenmechanik der Stoßvorgänge.” *Zeitschrift für Physik* 37, 863–867, 1926. The Born rule paper: \|ψ\|² is the probability density for detection. Cited throughout the paper.

**\[de Broglie 1924\]** de Broglie, L. “Recherches sur la théorie des quanta.” Doctoral dissertation, University of Paris, 1924. The original phase-harmony derivation: matter waves with wavelength λ = h/p. Cited in §16.20 entry C-B4.

**\[Einstein 1905, Photoelectric\]** Einstein, A. “Über einen die Erzeugung und Verwandlung des Lichtes betreffenden heuristischen Gesichtspunkt.” *Annalen der Physik* 17, 132–148, 1905. The photoelectric paper introducing light quanta (photons).
